# cpmdc documentation (full text export)

Site: https://cpmdc.rgoswami.me

## File: docs/orgmode/contributing/developer/release.org

# Versioning
`cpmdc` uses semantic versioning on the public C ABI and Cap'n Proto schema
fields.
Additive Cap'n Proto fields and new ABI entry points are minor; breaking field
renumbers or ABI signature changes are major.
The public C ABI is the
`CPMDC_API` declarations of `include/cpmdc.h` and `include/cpmdc_features.h`;
`libcpmdc` exports nothing else, so hiding a symbol no public header declares
changes neither the version nor the soversion.
The version is the single line of the root `version.txt`, and no other file
carries a hand-written copy.
Meson reads it with `files()`, and `docs/source/conf.py` reads it for the Sphinx
`version` and `release`.
`pixi run version-sync` regenerates the cog copies in `pixi.toml`,
`CITATION.cff`, `README.md`, `include/cpmdc.h`, the Doxygen configuration, and
the first-energy tutorial.
`pixi run release-assert` fails when one of them differs from `version.txt`.
The first cocogitto pre-bump hook writes the new version to `version.txt` and
then regenerates the copies.

# Checklist
1. Run `meson test -C build --print-errorlogs` on the default parser/session
   configuration.
2. Run `pixi run -e docs sphinxbld` after documentation or public header
   changes.
3. Run the OpenCPMD archive suite when the release changes the embed path:
   `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=/path/to/PP_LIBRARY meson test -C build-cpmd --print-errorlogs`.
4. Confirm `cpmdc_feature_table()` exposes any new ABI, schema, section, or
   keyword capability.
5. Add a fragment `docs/newsfragments/+NAME.TYPE.md` for each user-visible
   change, with `TYPE` one of the types in `towncrier.toml`; `cog bump` runs
   towncrier, which moves the fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`, and
   `pixi run towncrier-draft` previews the result.
6. Tag `vX.Y.Z` when publishing.


## File: docs/orgmode/contributing/index.org

Bug reports, fixes, tests, documentation, and new typed keywords for the input
deck are welcome.
Report a problem or propose a change on the
GitHub issue tracker (https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/cpmdc/issues).
Send the change itself as a pull request to the
cpmdc repository (https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/cpmdc) on GitHub.
The sections below list the checks to run first and the files that each kind of
change touches.

# Development Checks
Run the default parser, socket, and stub checks before changing the ABI, schema,
renderer, or session runtime:

meson setup build -Dwith_tests=true
meson compile -C build
meson test -C build --print-errorlogs

Use focused suites while iterating, then run the default suite before pushing a
public change:

| Contract | Command |
|----------+---------|
| Full default ABI and parser suite | `meson test -C build --print-errorlogs` |
| Cap'n Proto decode and deck rendering | `meson test -C build --suite cmocka --print-errorlogs` |
| Session, topology, result sizing, and unit conversion | `meson test -C build --suite e2e --print-errorlogs` |
| Generated feature inventory | `meson test -C build feature-inventory --print-errorlogs` |
| Base `&CPMD` keyword inventory | `meson test -C build cpmd-base-keyword-inventory --print-errorlogs` |
| Top-level `CPMDParams` feature rows and duplicate inventory lists | `meson test -C build cpmd-params-field-inventory --print-errorlogs` |
| Public C ABI inventory | `meson test -C build cpmd-public-abi-inventory --print-errorlogs` |
| Stub ABI feature rows | `meson test -C build stub-abi-symbol-coverage stub-abi --print-errorlogs` |
| Shared library ABI exports | `meson test -C build shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage shared-dlopen-abi --print-errorlogs` |
| `CPMDCpmdSection` render mappings | `meson test -C build cpmd-schema-render-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Inline option token coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-option-token-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Typed render field coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Long-tail directive section coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Escape-hatch carrier coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Embedding docs coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-embedding-docs-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Public header docs coverage | `meson test -C build cpmd-public-header-docs-coverage --print-errorlogs` |
| Public host example docs | `meson test -C build examples-documented --print-errorlogs` |
| README and build-and-test navigation | `meson test -C build readme-navigation --print-errorlogs` |
| Reference contract of every public name, no hidden names in the docs | `meson test -C build reference-contract public-api-docs --print-errorlogs` |
| LLM index files match Org sources | `python3 scripts/generate_llms_txt.py --check` or `meson test -C build llms-txt --print-errorlogs` |
| Public inventory JSON coverage report | `python3 scripts/docs_coverage_inventory.py` or `meson test -C build docs-coverage-inventory --print-errorlogs` |
| Every README and Org code block runs, compiles, or names why not | `meson test -C build docs-examples --print-errorlogs` |
| OpenCPMD archive build | `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=/path/to/PP_LIBRARY meson test -C build-cpmd --print-errorlogs` |

`scripts/ci/fetch_pseudopotentials.sh pp` writes the pseudopotentials that suite reads into `pp`, `Si_MT_BLYP.psp` from `PP_LIBRARY/pseudo`
included; point `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` there.
On one core the OpenCPMD build runs `python-pytest` in about half an hour.

Params render coverage lives under `tests/cmocka/` and uses cmocka assertions on
generated Cap'n Proto types (`read_CPMDParams`, deck substrings) only.
Session tests use encoded `CPMDParams` and `ForceInput` fixtures from
`tests/*.capnp.txt`.
`feature-inventory` ties the generated JSON inventory to the schema, public
feature table, docs, public headers, ABI symbol list, and optional `CPMD_ROOT`
parser section probe.
`cpmd-base-keyword-inventory` requires every base `&CPMD` keyword in
`schema/inventory/cpmd_cp_keywords.txt` to resolve to a `catalog.cpmd.*` row.
`cpmd-params-field-inventory` requires every top-level `CPMDParams` schema field
to resolve to a
`params.*` feature row and rejects duplicate inventory IDs/lists and C feature table duplicates before set comparisons can hide them. `cpmd-public-abi-inventory` requires every public `cpmdc_*`
header function to resolve through
`abi_symbols` and the feature table, then verifies the native `src/cpmdc.c`, stub `src/cpmdc_stub.c`,
or shared
`src/cpmdc_features.c` implementation that exports it. `stub-abi-symbol-coverage` requires the standalone stub test to assert every `abi_symbols` feature row is present and stub-applicable. `shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage` requires the shared-library `dlopen` test to load every `abi_symbols` entry from `libcpmdc.so`. `cpmd-schema-render-coverage` and `cpmd-option-token-coverage` keep typed `CPMDCpmdSection` fields and fixture inline tokens tied to render coverage. `cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage` requires typed `cpmd`, `system`, `dft`, and `atoms` fields to appear in render fixtures or render assertions. `cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage` requires every `CPMDDirectiveSection` union arm to appear in the long-tail fixture, render assertions, and option reference. `cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage` requires `inputBlocks`, `generic`, `set`, and `raw` carriers to stay covered by schema, fixtures, render tests, and option docs. `cpmd-embedding-docs-coverage` requires the embedding how-to to name the public ABI feature IDs plus the typed, long-tail, and escape-hatch `CPMDParams` carrier IDs used by host authors. `cpmd-public-header-docs-coverage` requires the public header and generated C API docs to describe the serialized `CPMDParams` input surface. `examples-documented` requires public docs to point at the runnable `examples/host_step.c` host program. `readme-navigation` keeps the README and build-and-test how-to focused on entry paths, work-loop labels, and current wording. `reference-contract` requires every function, type, enum constant, and macro of `cpmdc.h`, `cpmdc_features.h`,
and
`cpmdc_restart.h` in the C ABI reference (file:../reference/c-abi.org), each function with its parameter list in a table row, an `__all__` in every `python/cpmdc` module that lists its public functions and classes, each of those names and each public member of an exported class in the Python reference (file:../reference/python.org), and no `cpmdc_`
name in the README or the Org pages that no public header declares.
`docs-examples` classifies every code block of the README and the Org pages.
It runs the blocks the default build can run, compiles the C fragments against
`include/`, and lists the rest in `tests/test_docs_examples.py`: blocks that
need OpenCPMD in `OPENCPMD`, whose surrounding text must say so, and the others
in `SKIP` with the tool or input they need.
Every shell block, run or not, must name meson options, pixi tasks, meson tests
and suites, repository paths, and build outputs that exist.
A new block fails the test until it is classified.

# NumPy preflight
`tests/python/conftest.py` multiplies small matrices with `@` and with a loop
before collecting any test (`tests/python/blas_probe.py`), and stops the session
with exit status 3 when they differ by more than 1e-12 of the scale of the
product. The references of the GROMACS and ASE tests use `@`, which NumPy gives
to OpenBLAS, and OpenBLAS chooses its kernel from the CPU it detects. Under
`qemu-user` 8.2 with `-cpu max` on aarch64 the detected core is `armv9sme`,
and 195 of 385 product shapes then come out wrong, with one OpenBLAS thread, by
the size of the result,
so a NumPy reference sums nothing and every comparison with the library fails
far from the cause; whether the emulation of SME or the kernel is at fault was
not settled. On such a machine set `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE` to an older core,
`ARMV8` on aarch64, or run the emulator with `QEMU_CPU=max,sme=off`.

# GROMACS tests
`tests/python/test_gromacs.py` runs under Meson's `python-pytest`.
Without GROMACS it still checks the library through `ctypes`:

- the unit factors against GROMACS' `units.h`;
- the energy and forces of the whole system against `CPMDCCalculator` to 1e-10,
  in a cubic and a triclinic box;
- unwrapping across the boundary, and the whole QM region with `CELL NONE`;
- the mechanical embedding against an independent NumPy Ewald sum in a cubic and
  a triclinic box, its convergence with the precision, a finite difference of
  its forces, and the direct sum without a box;
  both sides sum the same terms, so the energy agrees to `1e-12` Ha and a force
  element to `1e-12` Ha plus `1e-10` relative, against a rounding bound of
  6e-16 Ha and measured differences of at most 4e-17 Ha on x86-64 and aarch64;
  the splitting parameters `rcut` and `alpha` that the shim logs agree to
  `1e-14` relative, against the 1.5e-15 that the two determinants of the box
  leave;
- the stress of `cp2k_get_stress_tensor()`, as ASE's stress: with
  `CELL PERIODIC` against `CPMDCCalculator` to 1e-13 and ASE's central
  difference under a 1e-6 strain of the cell to 1e-8 of its largest element;
  with `CELL NONE`, with and without the mechanical embedding, against the same
  difference of the library's own energy; each in a cubic and a triclinic box,
  and the box of GROMACS 2026 read the same as that of 2024;
- no stress without a box or for an isolated periodic deck;
- the error for each refused input.

With `gmx_d` from `CPMDC_GMX` or on `PATH`, it also runs `grompp` and `mdrun`:

- one step of two QM waters, the whole system, in a cubic and a triclinic box:
  `Quantum En.` against `CPMDCCalculator` to 1e-10 relative and equal to
  `Potential`, and the forces to 1e-10 relative, read with `gmx energy -dp` and
  from the double-precision `.trr`;
- one QM water among three MM waters with PME: `Quantum En.` and the QM atom
  forces against the reference evaluator plus the NumPy Ewald sum;
- 2000 NVE steps of each system: the total energy stays within 2e-3 and 5e-3 of
  the swing of the potential energy;
- the virial and pressure of step 0 from rest with `md-vv`, two QM waters in a
  cubic and a triclinic box: `Vir` equals `0.5 V sigma` of `CPMDCCalculator`'s
  ASE stress to 1e-9 relative, and `Pres` equals `-sigma`;
- one QM water among three MM waters with PME, in a cubic and a triclinic box:
  each element of `Vir` equals half the central difference of `Potential` under
  a 1e-5 strain of the box and positions, to 1e-8 of its largest element, so the
  QM, QM-MM, and classical terms all enter it;
- generated input, `EMBEDDING ELECTROSTATIC`, and charged MM atoms without an
  embedding each stop `mdrun` with the reason.

With `gmx_mpi_d` from `CPMDC_GMX_MPI`, a double-precision GROMACS built with
`-DGMX_MPI=ON`, launched by `CPMDC_MPIEXEC` (default `mpiexec`):

- 20 NVE steps of 64 waters in a 2.4 nm box, one of them QM with its atoms
  across the periodic boundary in x and y, on 2 and 4 ranks with
  `QM_RANKS ALL` and on 4 with `QM_RANKS 1`: `Quantum En.`, `Potential` and
  `Total Energy` of every step and the positions and forces of steps 0, 10 and
  20 match the one-rank run to 1e-10, and the virial and pressure of every step
  to 1e-9 of their largest element, so the QM virial enters once.
  The pair list is rebuilt every step without a buffer (`nstlist = 1`,
  `verlet-buffer-tolerance = -1`), so that every decomposition sees the same
  pairs;
- `-npme 1` stops `mdrun` with GROMACS' refusal of separate PME ranks.

`tests/test_installed_pkgconfig_consumer.py` builds a libcp2k client from an installed `libcp2k.pc` alone and runs it without `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. After the prefix is moved it rejects an installed shared library or executable whose run path points at the build tree or the original prefix, then runs the pkg-config, libcp2k, and CMake consumers from that tree. `cpmdc-ipi-c` is run the same way, without the prefix on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

The CI job `gromacs-qmmm` builds GROMACS 2025.5 three ways and fails if any of
its tests skips:

| Route | GROMACS | Tests |
|-------+---------+-------|
| `build` | thread-MPI, against `build/tools/gromacs` | the one-rank tests and the Meson suite |
| `installed` | thread-MPI, against the `libcp2k.pc` of `meson install` into `build/prefix` | the same, with `libcpmdc` and `libcpmdc_gromacs` from the prefix |
| `mpi` | `-DGMX_MPI=ON` with the Open MPI of the pixi environment | the domain decomposition tests |

The reference evaluator of a build without OpenCPMD is a well about the origin.
Two consequences show in the tests: the mdp sets `comm-mode = None`, because
removing the centre-of-mass motion of a system with a net external force takes
energy out of NVE, and the QM/MM NVE run gives the QM hydrogens a small
Lennard-Jones repulsion, because the well does not bind them to their oxygen.
An OpenCPMD energy needs neither.

# LAMMPS tests
`tests/python/test_lammps.py` runs both routes under Meson's `python-pytest` and
checks:

- energy, forces, and virial against `CPMDCCalculator` to 1e-10, in a cubic and
  a triclinic box and without a cell, under `metal`, `real`, and `electron`;
- each of the six virial components against a central difference of the energy
  under strain on the triclinic box;
- the type-to-element map, unwrapping across the boundary, and `press` against
  the virial trace;
- energy drift of a short NVE run and of the extended energy of an NPT run;
- the error for each refused input and a failed step;
- two ranks against one, under `mpiexec`.

The module skips with a reason when the `lammps` module cannot start, and the
plugin cases skip when `cpmdcplugin.so` is not built.
The reference evaluator of a build without OpenCPMD is a harmonic well about the
origin, which is not translation invariant; NPT runs on it need
`fixedpoint 0 0 0`, which an OpenCPMD energy does not.

# Add a typed CPMD keyword
Use a typed field when a CPMD control has stable structure, affects ordinary
host inputs, or should be discoverable through `cpmdc_feature_find()`.
Use `directives`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` for rare literal
deck fragments that should stay text.

Start from the test surface:

| File | Required change |
|------+-----------------|
| `tests/test_params_cp_dft_render.c` | Add catalog coverage and rendered-token checks |
| `tests/test_features_cmocka.c` | Add `catalog.cpmd.*` and `params.inputSections.cpmd.*` expectations |
| `tests/params_*.capnp.txt` | Add a fixture value that exercises the new field |

Run the focused failure before adding production code:

CPMD_ROOT=OpenCPMD-cpmdc meson test -C build \
  params-cp-dft-render features-cmocka feature-inventory \
  cpmd-base-keyword-inventory cpmd-params-field-inventory \
  cpmd-public-abi-inventory cpmd-schema-render-coverage \
  stub-abi-symbol-coverage \
  shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage \
  cpmd-option-token-coverage cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage \
  cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage \
  cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage \
  --print-errorlogs

Then update the production and docs surface in one change:

| File | Required change |
|------+-----------------|
| `schema/Potentials.capnp` | Add the `CPMDCpmdSection` field with the next field number |
| `src/cpmdc_params.c` | Render the exact `&CPMD` deck spelling accepted by OpenCPMD |
| `src/cpmdc_features.c` | Add catalog and parameter feature table rows |
| `schema/inventory/cpmd_features.json` | Add matching inventory metadata |
| `schema/inventory/cpmd_cp_keywords.txt` | Add a base `&CPMD` keyword when the parser accepts it as a top-level control |
| `docs/orgmode/reference/cpmd-options.org` | Document every writable field ID |

Re-run the focused command, then run:

meson test -C build --print-errorlogs
pixi run -e docs sphinxbld

For parser coverage audits, compare OpenCPMD
`control_utils.mod.F90` `keyword_contains(line, ...)` branches against
`catalog.cpmd.*` rows.
Treat context-specific branch tokens as covered by their structured parent when
the schema field renders the accepted deck form, such as
`LBFGS_NTRUST` for `LBFGS NTRUST` or `NOSE_IONS_LOCAL` for `NOSE IONS LOCAL`.

# Source Layout

| Path | Ownership |
|------+-----------|
| `schema/Potentials.capnp` | shared RPC and direct-call wire contract |
| `include/cpmdc.h` | public C ABI and session result entry points |
| `include/cpmdc_features.h` | runtime feature discovery ABI |
| `include/cpmdc_export.h` | `CPMDC_API`, the mark on every exported function |
| `include/cpmdc_restart.h`, `src/cpmdc_restart.c` | `libcpmdc_restart`, the RESTART file reader and writer |
| `src/cpmdc_params.c` | Cap'n Proto decode, effective config, CPMD deck rendering |
| `src/cpmdc.c` | session lifecycle, topology guard, unit conversion, result writing |
| `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90` | Fortran `iso_c_binding` bridge and OpenCPMD archive path |
| `tests/` | encoded fixtures and C/cmocka contract tests |

# Documentation
Documentation source lives under
`docs/orgmode` (authoritative prose), with light/dark logos in
`docs/source/_static/` and `branding/logo/`.
Build docs (exports Org to RST, Doxygen XML, Sphinx HTML with Antics analytics):

pixi run -e docs docbld

Link between pages with Org file links, `text (file:../howto/mpi.org)`.
The default export is `ox-rst`.
A file link whose target ends in `.org` becomes a Sphinx `:doc:` role, so the
same link works on the forge and in the built site.
Set `CPMDC_ORG_EXPORT=pandoc` to export with pandoc instead.
That path applies `docs/org-links.lua` and makes the same `:doc:` rewrite.
Generated `docs/source/**/*.rst` is not committed.

When a page moves, leave a short page at the old path that starts with an
`:orphan:` export block and links to the new page, as
`docs/orgmode/tutorials/quickstart.org` does.
The old address then keeps working, and `readme-navigation` does not ask the
README to link that page.

Regenerate RST after editing Org sources:

pixi run -e docs mkrst

Regenerate the LLM index files (`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`) after editing
`docs/orgmode/` or `schema/inventory/cpmd_features.json`:

python3 scripts/generate_llms_txt.py

The generator writes deterministic output without timestamps or host paths.
Verify that committed index files match the sources with
`python3 scripts/generate_llms_txt.py --check` or
`meson test -C build llms-txt --print-errorlogs`; when a file is stale or
missing, the check names the file, prints the regeneration command above, and
shows a short unified diff head.

Check the links in the README, the Org sources, and the newsfragments:

pixi run -e docs lychee

The task runs lychee (https://lychee.cli.rs) 0.24.2 from the `docs` Pixi
environment with `.lychee.toml`, which also checks the anchor of a link such as
`README.md#citation`.
A link to a file on the `main` branch fails until that file lands there.

The Sphinx theme injects
`antics-api.turtletech.us/antics.js` via `docs/source/_templates/partials/extra-head.html`, and the footer credit lives in `docs/source/_templates/partials/site-foot.html`
(same pattern as `rgpot`).

## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/architecture.org

# Why a C ABI around CPMD
OpenCPMD is a Fortran program.
Its state lives in module variables, its input is a deck of `&SECTION`
blocks read from a file, and its normal life is one run per process.
A host that wants many energies and forces, such as a minimiser, a saddle
search, or a nudged elastic band, needs something else: a library it can
call repeatedly, from C, C++, Rust, or Python, without writing decks or
starting processes.
`cpmdc` is that library.
It follows the pattern of `nwchemc`: Cap'n Proto messages on the boundary, a
small C ABI, and a Fortran `iso_c_binding` layer that drives the engine as a
library.

# Layers

| Layer | Files | Owns |
|-------+-------+------|
| Public C ABI | `include/cpmdc.h`, `include/cpmdc_features.h`, `include/cpmdc_export.h` | the functions, the result structs, the feature table types, the `CPMDC_API` export mark |
| Messages | `schema/Potentials.capnp` | `CPMDParams`, `ForceInput`, `PotentialResult`, `PotentialConfig`, `Capabilities` |
| Decode and render | `src/cpmdc_params.c`, generated `capnp-c` readers | reading messages, rendering the CPMD deck, unit factors |
| Sessions | `src/cpmdc.c` | session lifecycle, topology guard, unit conversion, result messages |
| Calculator index | `src/cpmdc_adopt.c` | rank and size of an adopted communicator, and the calculator index of an aligned block |
| Fortran decode | `src/cpmdc_embed_apply_params.f90`, generated `capnp-fortran` readers | the scalar method knobs, read on the Fortran side |
| Engine bridge | `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90` | `bind(C)` entry points; the reference evaluator, or with `CPMDC_HAS_CPMD` the calls into OpenCPMD |
| Support | `src/cpmdc_memfd.c`, `src/cpmd_stop_intercept.c` | the in-memory deck file and working-directory switch; the `stopgm` catch |
| Host helpers | `src/cpmdc_embed_host.c`, declared in `src/cpmdc_embed_host.h` | the pseudopotential directory (`CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR`, else `CPMD_PP_LIBRARY_PATH`) and the map that returns species-block gradients to atom order; the same header declares the working-directory switch of `src/cpmdc_memfd.c`, which enters the pseudopotential directory while CPMD reads the files and returns to the host directory, and the note of an embed failure for the C result path, which `src/cpmdc.c` defines |
| Discovery | `src/cpmdc_features.c`, `src/cpmdc_capabilities.c` | the feature table and the `Capabilities` message |
| Stub | `src/cpmdc_stub.c` | the same symbols for link checks; calls that need OpenCPMD fail, and `cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm` still returns the calculator index when MPI is linked |

The C side never includes CPMD headers, and the Fortran side never sees a
Cap'n Proto type it did not decode itself.
Everything that crosses between them is a C array, a scalar, or a
null-terminated string.

# Two messages, two lifetimes
`CPMDParams` carries the method: functional, cutoff, the typed deck sections,
and literal blocks.
A host builds it once per session.
`ForceInput` carries one geometry: positions, atomic numbers, an optional
cell, and the units the host wants back.
A host builds one per step.
Keeping them apart is what lets a warm step skip CPMD's setup.

# What one evaluation does
1. `cpmdc_session_create()` copies the `CPMDParams` bytes, renders the deck in
   C, writes it to `CPMDC_DECK_OUT` when set, and hands the bytes and the deck
   to the Fortran side, which decodes the functional, cutoff, charge, and
   multiplicity with `capnp-fortran`.
2. `cpmdc_session_calculate_result()` decodes the `ForceInput`, converts
   positions and the cell to Angstrom, and sizes the result buffer.
   `session_accept_topology` fixes the topology after that call passes its
   argument checks and collective orbital preflight. A rejected preflight
   leaves it configurable. All of that is before any CPMD work.
3. On a cold evaluation, the bridge composes the full deck from the method
   deck and the step geometry, writes it to an anonymous `memfd` exposed as
   `/proc/self/fd/N`, and runs OpenCPMD's own setup on it (`control`,
   `dftin`, `sysin`, `ratom`, `setsys`, `rinit`, and the rest), then the SCF
   through `wfopts`.
4. On a warm step, the bridge writes the new positions into `coor%tau0`
   (Angstrom to Bohr), recomputes the structure factors with `phfac`,
   restores the saved orbitals, and runs `wfopts` again.
5. After the SCF, the bridge reads `ener_com%etot` and `coor%fion`, copies
   the energy components, charges, dipole, and stress into the session, and
   reports failure when the orbitals did not converge.
6. `cpmdc.c` negates the gradient into forces, scales energy and forces to
   the requested units, and writes the `PotentialResult`.

No deck is written to disk unless `CPMDC_DECK_OUT` names a file.
The only input file CPMD opens is the in-memory deck, and a library force
call writes no `RESTART.1`, `LATEST`, `GEOMETRY`, or `GEOMETRY.xyz`;
`cpmd.x` on the same deck writes them.

# Where the deck comes from
The deck is rendered from `CPMDParams` for three reasons: CPMD's own parsers
already turn every keyword into module state, so no C setter per keyword is
needed; the rendered deck is what `cpmd.x` would read; and `CPMDC_DECK_OUT`
can show it to a person.
Typed fields render the keywords the schema models, `directives` carry keywords
without a typed field, and `set`, `generic`, `raw`, and `inputBlocks` carry
text that must pass through unchanged.
The geometry never goes into `CPMDParams`: the bridge writes `&ATOMS` from the
step on a cold evaluation and moves atoms through `tau0` on a warm step.

# Sessions, topology, and state
`session_accept_topology` fixes the topology after an evaluation call passes
its argument checks and collective orbital preflight, because the species
tables, the plane-wave setup, and the stored orbitals are sized for one
composition. A rejected preflight leaves it configurable.
A reordering of those elements stays on the session.
Coordinates may change freely. A changed cell runs setup again, except a
constant-cutoff cell that stays within `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE`.
OpenCPMD's module state is one per process, so one session at a time owns it.
A different session with the same functional, deck, cutoff, cell, charge,
multiplicity, and elemental composition reuses the stored orbitals.
A different method or composition runs setup again on the next evaluation.
Wavefunction state (file:wavefunction-state.org) follows the orbitals from call to call,
and the MPI model (file:mpi-model.org) covers ranks and calculator groups.

# Three builds, one ABI

| Build | `cpmdc_available()` | Evaluator | `cpmdc_last_energy_components()` |
|-------+---------------------+-----------+----------------------------------|
| stub (`libcpmdc_stub.a`) | 0 | none; every call fails | returns -1 |
| default `libcpmdc.so` | 0 | reference function, harmonic in the positions and scaled by atomic number | `etot` only |
| OpenCPMD `libcpmdc.so` (`-Dwith_cpmd=true`) | 1 | OpenCPMD `wfopts` with ionic forces | `etot`, `ekin`, `epseu`, `enl`, `eht`, `exc` |

The reference build exists so the ABI, the parser, sessions, units, and
result sizing can be tested on any machine.
Its energies are deterministic and have no physical meaning.

# The file route it replaces
Before the library, a host ran `cpmd.x` once per force call and exchanged
decks, restart files, and `GEOMETRY` through the file system.
The route comparison (file:routes.org) measures what each approach costs and what each one
has to guard against.


## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/constant-cutoff-npt.org

This page explains why NPT dynamics on a fixed plane-wave cutoff gives liquid water the wrong density, and measures the density that `CPMDCCalculator` gives with and without the constant-cutoff functional.
The steps that turn the functional on are in Relax a cell at a constant cutoff (file:../howto/constant-cutoff.org); the GROMACS NPT runs of a QM water in classical water are in cpmdc inside MD engines (file:md-engines.org).

# Why a fixed cutoff compresses the liquid
Without the functional, every new cell is a new setup of the deck at its cutoff, and the stress is the derivative of the energy at the plane waves of that setup.
A larger cell holds more plane waves at the same cutoff, so the energy of the setups falls with the volume faster than that stress says.
The difference is the Pulay stress.
The barostat holds the stress at the target pressure, which holds -dE/dV of the setups above the target by the Pulay stress, so the liquid settles denser than the volume where -dE/dV is the target.
A basis that keeps its plane waves as the cell moves, as Parrinello-Rahman dynamics in a plane-wave code does, has a stress that follows its energy, but its effective cutoff falls as the cell grows, which raises the energy of the larger cells and biases the volume the same way.

The constant-cutoff functional of Bernasconi et al. (reference 1) removes both.
The energy belongs to the constant cutoff E0, which stays below the cutoff of the deck in every cell that the run visits, and the stress is the derivative of that energy.

# The runs
`bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py` integrates hydrostatic NPT with ASE's `LangevinBAOAB`, whose cell follows the Langevin-Hoover equations of Quigley and Probert (reference 2): the Martyna-Tobias-Klein barostat with a Langevin piston, and Langevin dynamics of the atoms.
ASE added that integrator in 3.27, so `run` needs ASE 3.27 or newer.
`start` thermalizes momenta with `thermalize_momenta` on ASE 3.29 and with `MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution` on earlier releases, and the module imports on ASE 3.23.
Each step evaluates the energy, the forces, and the stress through `CPMDCCalculator` once.
Every run shares these settings:

- 32 waters, from the box that `start` writes: a 9.8555 Angstrom cube at 1000 kg/m^3, after 10 ps of a classical flexible TIP3P model at 350 K.
- PBE with the Troullier-Martins pseudopotentials `O_MT_PBE` and `H_MT_PBE` of the CPMD library (reference 3), orbital convergence 1e-5, and orbitals predicted by ASPC of order 4.
- 350 K and 1 bar, a thermostat time `--t-tau` of 100 fs, 1 fs steps, and deuterium masses on the hydrogens.
  The density counts each molecule as H2O, 18.015 u, so that it compares with light water.
- OpenCPMD on 7 or 8 ranks of one node, as the cost table gives, with `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1`, and `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE=0.01`, which keeps the plane waves of a constant-cutoff setup through every cell within 1% strain of it.
- E0 = 85 Ry and sigma = 4.25 Ry on the 100 Ry deck, and E0 = 102 Ry and sigma = 5.1 Ry on the 120 Ry deck, with the default A of 50 times the deck cutoff, so that E0 + 2 sigma stays below the deck cutoff.

`bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.org` names each run by its record:

| Run | Basis | P_tau, fs | Start | Steps |
|-----+-------+-----------+-------+-------|
| relax100 | 100 Ry, E0 85 Ry | 500 | box32.xyz | 470 |
| cc100 | 100 Ry, E0 85 Ry | 100 | relax100.state.npz, 0.47 ps into relax100 | 700 |
| cc100b | 100 Ry, E0 85 Ry | 100 | cc100.final.state.npz, 0.7 ps into cc100 | 50 |
| off100 | 100 Ry, no constant cutoff | 100 | cc100.final.state.npz, 0.7 ps into cc100 | 50 |
| off120 | 120 Ry, no constant cutoff | 100 | cc100.final.state.npz, 0.7 ps into cc100 | 50 |
| cc120 | 120 Ry, E0 102 Ry | 100 | cc100.final.state.npz, 0.7 ps into cc100 | 100 |

`relax100` starts from the box with a barostat time `--p-tau` of 500 fs.
ASE sets the piston mass from that time with a heuristic fitted to aluminium, and on 32 waters that mass gives a slow swing of the volume: in 0.43 ps the density falls from 1000 to 761 kg/m^3, where it turns.
`cc100` continues from the state of `relax100` at 0.47 ps with `--p-tau 100`, which divides the piston mass by 25 and multiplies its friction by 5, and keeps the strain rate of the state.
The other four runs start from the last state of `cc100` with the same seed, so they draw the same noise for the thermostat and the piston, and the differences between them come from the basis.

# The stress of one configuration
`constant_cutoff_npt.py pressure` evaluated the last state of `cc100`, at 763.9 kg/m^3 (1253.21 Angstrom^3), at six bases with orbital convergence 1e-6 and wrote `bench/results/constant_cutoff_pressure.org`.
The atomic pressure is the virial of the forces on the atoms; the molecular pressure is the virial of the forces on the molecular centres of mass, which leaves out the intramolecular forces.
Neither holds the kinetic term, which is the same at every basis:

| Cutoff, Ry | E0, Ry | A, Ry | sigma, Ry | Energy, eV | Atomic pressure, kbar | Molecular pressure, kbar | Wall, s |
|------------+--------+-------+-----------+------------+-----------------------+--------------------------+---------|
| 100 |  |  |  | -15014.0713 | -29.21 | -19.98 | 39.3 |
| 100 | 85 | 5000 | 4.25 | -14997.8313 | -5.99 | -2.24 | 42.3 |
| 120 |  |  |  | -15015.7523 | -14.99 | -5.47 | 42.1 |
| 120 | 102 | 6000 | 5.1 | -15012.0322 | -11.06 | -2.44 | 44.3 |
| 140 | 119 | 7000 | 5.95 | -15015.2170 | -12.04 | -2.64 | 63.0 |
| 160 | 136 | 8000 | 6.8 | -15015.8747 | -12.20 | -2.59 | 124.1 |

The molecular pressure, which sets the density, has converged at E0 = 85 Ry: it lies 0.35 kbar above that at E0 = 136 Ry, and those at 102 and 119 Ry lie within 0.15 kbar of it.
Without the functional, the same configuration has a molecular pressure 17.4 kbar below the converged one at 100 Ry and 2.9 kbar below it at 120 Ry; that is the Pulay stress of a new setup at each cutoff, and the atomic pressures differ by about the same amounts.
The atomic pressure at a constant cutoff converges more slowly, 6.2 kbar above the converged one at E0 = 85 Ry, because it holds the virial of the O-H bonds, whose force at a fixed length changes with the basis.
In the dynamics the bonds relax to the length of each basis within a vibration, and the time average of the virial of the forces within the molecules cancels the kinetic energy of the motion within them, so the mean atomic and molecular pressures, each with its kinetic term, are equal and the density follows the molecular one.

# Density
`table` discards the start of each run that Chodera's method detects (reference 4), at least 0.05 ps of a run that starts from a state, and gives the Flyvbjerg-Petersen standard error of the mean (reference 5) at the coarsest blocking level with at least 8 blocks:

| Run | Length, ps | Discarded, ps | Frames used | Volume, nm^3 | Density, kg/m^3 | Pressure, bar | Temperature, K | Wall, s |
|-----+------------+---------------+-------------+--------------+-----------------+---------------+----------------+---------|
| cc100 | 0.7 | 0.05 | 651 | 1.1598 +- 0.00801 | 826.1 +- 5.67 | -23 +- 244.5 | 352 +- 6.1 | 8398 |

Only `cc100` is long enough for a mean, and its standard error is a lower bound: the error of the density still grows from 3.65 kg/m^3 at blocks of 0.016 ps to 5.67 kg/m^3 at 0.064 ps, the coarsest level with 10 blocks.
The density swings with a period of about 0.1 ps, so the 0.65 ps averaged hold six or seven swings, and the last took it from 824 kg/m^3 at 0.65 ps to 755 kg/m^3 at 0.69 ps.
The volume fluctuations over those 0.65 ps give a compressibility var(V)/(kT mean(V)) of 2.3e-5 /bar, uncertain by tens of percent with so few swings.
The mean temperature, 352 +- 6 K, agrees with the 350 K of the thermostat.

The runs that are too short for a mean:

| Run | No mean | Density at the start, kg/m^3 | Density at the end, kg/m^3 | Mean pressure, bar |
|-----+---------+------------------------------+----------------------------+--------------------|
| relax100 | 0.47 ps, less than 0.5 ps to discard and 0.1 ps to average | 1000.0 | 766.0 | 766 |
| cc100b | 0.05 ps, less than 0.05 ps to discard and 0.1 ps to average | 763.9 | 817.8 | 1463 |
| off100 | 0.05 ps, less than 0.05 ps to discard and 0.1 ps to average | 763.9 | 1049.5 | 5016 |
| off120 | 0.05 ps, less than 0.05 ps to discard and 0.1 ps to average | 763.9 | 859.0 | 1769 |
| cc120 | 0.1 ps, less than 0.05 ps to discard and 0.1 ps to average | 763.9 | 737.0 | 371 |

From the last state of `cc100`, with the same noise:

| After the start, ps | cc100b, kg/m^3 | off100, kg/m^3 | off120, kg/m^3 | cc120, kg/m^3 |
|--+--+--+--+--|
| 0 | 763.9 | 763.9 | 763.9 | 763.9 |
| 0.01 | 784.0 | 823.7 | 791.6 | 785.2 |
| 0.02 | 802.7 | 946.5 | 826.9 | 805.4 |
| 0.03 | 820.4 | 1074.4 | 859.5 | 820.8 |
| 0.04 | 828.2 | 1117.4 | 873.8 | 823.4 |
| 0.05 | 817.8 | 1049.5 | 859.0 | 807.9 |
| 0.06 |  |  |  | 780.5 |
| 0.07 |  |  |  | 762.0 |
| 0.08 |  |  |  | 745.9 |
| 0.09 |  |  |  | 735.2 |
| 0.1 |  |  |  | 737.0 |

With the kinetic term, the state has a pressure of -2.5 kbar at E0 = 85 Ry, -7.6 kbar at E0 = 102 Ry, -25.7 kbar at a fixed 100 Ry, and -11.5 kbar at a fixed 120 Ry.
At the same deck cutoff, the barostat of the run without the functional pulls the cell in by the Pulay stress, on top of the swing that all four runs share: at 40 fs, near the top of that swing, off100 stands 289 kg/m^3 (35%) above cc100b at 1117 kg/m^3, and the compression has heated it to 507 K by 50 fs, while off120 stands 50 kg/m^3 (6%) above cc120.
The static compressibility of `cc100` turns the 2.9 kbar Pulay stress of 120 Ry into a density 7% higher; 50 fs show the start of that shift, not where a run settles.

Between the two constant cutoffs, the change of basis at the start rings the O-D bonds, whose virial swings the pressure of cc120 against cc100b by up to 5 kbar at the 13 fs period of the stretch.
That difference averages +1.0, -0.2, and +0.5 kbar over steps 1 to 10, 11 to 30, and 31 to 50, and the first push leaves cc120 10 kg/m^3 (1.2%) below cc100b at 50 fs.
The molecular pressures of the single points, 0.2 kbar apart, put the equilibrium density at E0 = 102 Ry about 4 kg/m^3 above that at E0 = 85 Ry.

.. figure:: /_static/constant-cutoff-npt.svg
   :alt: Density of 32 PBE waters against time, with and without the constant cutoff

   Left, the density over windows of 0.02 ps from the start of relax100; the
   band is the mean of cc100 with one standard error over the frames it
   averages. Right, every step of the runs from the last state of cc100,
   1.17 ps after the start of relax100; a dashed line is a run without the
   constant cutoff. The dotted line is the PBE density of Miceli et al.
   (2015).

`docs/render_constant_cutoff_npt.py` draws the figure from `bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.json` when the docs build.

# Against a published PBE density
Miceli, de Gironcoli, and Pasquarello (reference 6) ran isobaric dynamics of 64 waters with PBE in Quantum ESPRESSO: Troullier-Martins pseudopotentials, Parrinello-Rahman cell dynamics at zero pressure, 0.48 fs steps, and velocities rescaled only when the mean temperature left 350 +- 20 K.
They kept the number of plane waves constant, at a cutoff of 85 Ry in a cell of 1 g/cm^3, which converges the stress within 1 kbar, and averaged runs of 25 to 35 ps after 5 ps of equilibration.
At a mean temperature of 349 K, PBE gave them 0.87 g/cm^3, 13% below experiment, which is 870 kg/m^3; they quote no error bar.

`cc100` gives 826 +- 6 kg/m^3 at 352 K, 44 kg/m^3 or 5% below their density, and its standard error is a lower bound.
Its basis explains little of the gap: with the compressibility of `cc100`, the 0.35 kbar between the molecular pressures at E0 = 85 and 136 Ry puts the density of the converged basis about 7 kg/m^3 higher, and the 1 kbar within which Miceli et al. converge their stress is worth about 20 kg/m^3.
The rest lies within what differs between the runs: 0.65 ps of 32 waters against 25 to 35 ps of 64, Troullier-Martins pseudopotentials on both sides but not necessarily the same ones, and a Langevin thermostat against occasional rescaling.
The deuterium masses do not enter, since the density of classical nuclei does not depend on their masses.
A fixed cutoff, by contrast, sets the density by its Pulay stress: 100 Ry passes 1100 kg/m^3 within 40 fs, and the 7% that 120 Ry adds would put it near 880 kg/m^3, close to the published density by accident.

# Cost
The records time every step and count its SCF iterations and new setups:

| Run | Ranks | Wall per step, s | SCF iterations per step | New setups | Wall, h |
|-----+-------+------------------+-------------------------+------------+---------|
| relax100 | 8 | 15.3 | 8.9 | 9 | 2.00 |
| cc100 | 7 | 11.9 | 8.9 | 16 | 2.33 |
| cc100b | 8 | 13.0 | 9.3 | 2 | 0.19 |
| off100 | 8 | 19.2 | 17.6 | 50 | 0.27 |
| off120 | 8 | 32.5 | 17.0 | 50 | 0.46 |
| cc120 | 8 | 16.5 | 9.4 | 5 | 0.47 |

At a constant cutoff a step takes 8.9 to 9.4 SCF iterations, and the in-place moves hold the new setups to 16 in the 700 steps of `cc100`.
Without the functional every step is a new setup and takes 17 to 18 iterations: on the same 8 ranks, off100 costs 1.5 times the wall time per step of cc100b, and off120 twice that of cc120.
The six single points took 6 minutes, and the runs 5.7 hours on the 8 cores of one VM.

# Tests that keep the stress
- `test_the_constant_cutoff_stress_is_the_volume_derivative_of_the_energy` in `tests/python/test_ase_calculator.py` integrates the pressure of the one-water deck at E0 = 30 Ry over a 2% stretch and requires it to equal the energy change; the fixed-basis stress of that deck misses the slope by 1.6e-2 eV/Angstrom^3, about 1 eV over the stretch.
- `test_a_constant_cutoff_cell_moves_in_place_within_the_strain_limit` requires the in-place moves to start from the stored orbitals and to give the energy, forces, and stress of a new setup.
- `test_constant_cutoff_virial_matches_ase` in `tests/python/test_lammps.py` and `test_opencpmd_constant_cutoff_stress_matches_ase` in `tests/python/test_gromacs_opencpmd.py` require the virial that LAMMPS integrates and the stress that GROMACS couples to, from `system.constantCutoff` in the message, to equal the stress of `CPMDCCalculator` for the same configuration, and to lie far from the fixed-basis stress.
- The `constant-cutoff-npt-plot` Meson test draws the figure from `bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.json` and requires a curve per run, a band per mean, the reference line, and the panel of the runs from a shared state.
- `tests/python/test_constant_cutoff_npt_table.py` checks how `table` finds the run that wrote each state, and requires this page to carry the tables of `bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.org` and `constant_cutoff_pressure.org` that it quotes.

# Run it
With an OpenCPMD build of `libcpmdc` in `build-cpmd`, `capnp` on `PATH`, and the pseudopotentials of the CPMD regression tests:

export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=$CPMD_ROOT/../Regtests/tests/PP_LIBRARY CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE=0.01
python bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py start --out box32.xyz
npt() {
  mpirun -np 7 -x CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1 -x CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR -x CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE \
    python bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py "$@" --library build-cpmd/libcpmdc.so
}
npt run --start box32.xyz --cutoff 100 --e0 85 --width 4.25 --conv 1e-5 --p-tau 500 \
  --steps 470 --out runs/relax100.json
npt run --start runs/relax100.state.npz --cutoff 100 --e0 85 --width 4.25 --conv 1e-5 \
  --steps 700 --out runs/cc100.json
cp runs/cc100.state.npz runs/cc100.final.state.npz
npt pressure --start runs/cc100.final.state.npz --output runs/pressure.org \
  100 100/85/4.25 120 120/102/5.1 140/119/5.95 160/136/6.8
from=runs/cc100.final.state.npz
npt run --start $from --cutoff 100 --e0 85 --width 4.25 --conv 1e-5 --steps 50 --out runs/cc100b.json
npt run --start $from --cutoff 100 --conv 1e-5 --steps 50 --out runs/off100.json
npt run --start $from --cutoff 120 --conv 1e-5 --steps 50 --out runs/off120.json
npt run --start $from --cutoff 120 --e0 102 --width 5.1 --conv 1e-5 --steps 100 --out runs/cc120.json

Each run checkpoints every 10 steps and continues with `run --library build-cpmd/libcpmdc.so --out RUN.json --resume`.
The records and state files stay out of the repository; the tables and the figure come from them:

python bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py table runs/relax100.json runs/cc100.json \
  runs/cc100b.json runs/off100.json runs/off120.json runs/cc120.json \
  --json bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.json --output bench/results/constant_cutoff_npt.org
python docs/render_constant_cutoff_npt.py --out constant-cutoff-npt.svg

## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/isolated-cells.org

An isolated deck (`SYMMETRY 0`, a Poisson solver, `CLUSTER`, `SURFACE` or
`POLYMER`) holds the density on a box of fixed size with its origin at a corner,
so a host whose atoms drift towards a face, or leave the box, puts density
across that face.
The energy then depends on where the molecule sits in the box, not only on its
shape, and an MD host sees a force that pushes the molecule about.

# What recentring computes
With `CPMDC_RECENTER` at `mass` or `geometry` the energy is that of the atoms
moved to the middle of the box, a function of their relative positions only, and
the forces are its gradient with respect to the caller's coordinates: the net
force the grid leaves is projected out, the fraction of it each atom carries
given by its weight in the centre.
Energy, forces and `sum_i x_i (x) f_i` then do not change when the caller
translates every atom.

# What drift costs without it
On one BLYP water in the 10 Angstrom Hockney box with `off`, a hydrogen 0.5
Angstrom from a face raises the energy by 5.0e-4 Hartree, a hydrogen 0.5
Angstrom past it lowers it by 8.4e-3 Hartree with a net force of 0.17
Hartree/Bohr, and the water about the corner lowers it by 7.9e-2 Hartree; with `mass` all of these give the energy of the centred molecule to 1.1e-14 Hartree (`bench/results/cluster_drift_scan.org`).
cpmdc inside MD engines (file:md-engines.org) shows the same effect in
GROMACS runs before and after recentring.

The environment reference (file:../reference/environment.org) lists the
values of `CPMDC_RECENTER` and `CPMDC_RECENTER_MARGIN` and the rules they
follow.


## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/md-engines.org

This page explains why GROMACS reaches cpmdc through its CP2K
QM/MM interface, reports runs of that route on OpenCPMD, and compares the cost per step of the LAMMPS and GROMACS routes. The steps are in Run GROMACS on cpmdc forces (file:../howto/gromacs.org) and Run LAMMPS on cpmdc forces (file:../howto/lammps.org); the conventions are in the GROMACS (file:../reference/gromacs.org) and LAMMPS (file:../reference/lammps.org)
interface references.

# Why the GROMACS CP2K interface
GROMACS offers four ways to bring outside forces into `mdrun`.
The choice was made from the GROMACS 2024 to 2026 sources and manuals and the
MiMiC papers:

| Route | Coupling | What rules it in or out |
|-------+----------+--------------------------|
| CP2K QM/MM interface (`GMX_CP2K`) | in process, one C call per step | GROMACS integrates; energy enters `Quantum En.` (`F_EQM`) and so the potential and the conserved energy; positions, box, and forces in double precision in a double build. Chosen |
| MiMiC (`GMX_MIMIC`, `integrator = mimic`) | two MPI programs over the MiMiC communication library | built for CPMD, but CPMD is the server that integrates and GROMACS a client that returns MM forces (`src/gromacs/mimic/communicator.cpp`); electrostatic embedding is computed against CPMD's density on its grid. A MiMiC client of cpmdc would need CPMD's integrator and MiMiC's embedding inside a session, which the C ABI does not expose, and GROMACS' `mimic` integrator reports no kinetic or total energy |
| neural-network potential (`GMX_NNPOT`, 2025 and later) | in process, a TorchScript model | `src/gromacs/applied_forces/nnpot/torchmodel.cpp` casts positions and box to `float32`, so no model can match a double reference to 1e-10; it adds no virial |
| PLUMED (native in 2025) | in process | the bias forces and virial reach GROMACS, but `plumedforceprovider.cpp` never adds the bias energy to GROMACS' energy terms, so the potential and NVE checks would miss it |
| i-PI | socket | GROMACS has no i-PI client |

MiMiC couples CPMD to GROMACS with electrostatic embedding and scales to
thousands of cores [1, 2], through the MiMiC communication library [3]; it is
the route for an MPI-launched CPMD that integrates.
For GROMACS integrating on cpmdc forces, the CP2K interface is the one
in-process route that carries the energy, the forces, and the box at full
precision, and it is the one built and tested here.

# OpenCPMD in GROMACS
`bench/gromacs_opencpmd.py` runs GROMACS on the OpenCPMD backend: one BLYP water (the deck of `tests/water_blyp_params.capnp.txt`,
50 Ry, Hockney, orbital convergence 1e-7) at the centre of the deck's 1 nm cell,
among 26 flexible TIP3P waters in a 1.8 nm box, with `CELL NONE`, mechanical
embedding with the TIP3P charges on the QM atoms, PME for MM-MM, and NVE at 0.25
fs from 300 K velocities.
It runs the same system with every water classical as a control, and fails
unless `md_cp2k.out` reports the `opencpmd` backend.

meson setup build-cpmd -Dwith_cpmd=true -Dcpmd_root=$CPMD_ROOT
meson compile -C build-cpmd
scripts/ci/build_gromacs_cpmdc.sh 2025.5 $GMX_PREFIX build-cpmd/tools/gromacs mpi
python bench/gromacs_opencpmd.py --gmx $GMX_PREFIX/bin/gmx_mpi_d --mpiexec mpiexec \
  --pseudo-dir $CPMD_ROOT/../Regtests/tests/PP_LIBRARY --ranks 4,1 --steps 200

One run on an 8-core Xeon virtual machine, GROMACS 2025.5 (double, Open MPI
5.0.10, OpenBLAS), OpenCPMD with Open MPI, `QM_RANKS ALL`, 200 steps (50 fs);
the 4-rank run shared the machine with other jobs:

| Run | Drift, kJ/mol/ps | Per atom | Largest excursion, kJ/mol | Kinetic energy std, kJ/mol | Wall, s |
|-----+------------------+----------+---------------------------+----------------------------+---------|
| OpenCPMD QM water, 4 ranks | 0.768 | 0.00948 | 1.274 | 28.81 | 1079.5 |
| OpenCPMD QM water, 1 rank | 0.768 | 0.00948 | 1.274 | 28.81 | 2194.0 |
| all classical, 1 rank | 0.697 | 0.00861 | 1.292 | 28.94 | |

The step-0 QM energy is -17.055716980795 Hartree; `CPMDCCalculator` gives
-17.05571697 for the same water.
The total energy oscillates by about 1.3 kJ/mol as 105 kJ/mol of kinetic energy
goes into the flexible O-H bonds; the classical control shows the same, and
halving the time step divides it by four, so it is leap-frog's error, not the QM
forces'.
Over 50 fs the QM water adds 0.07 kJ/mol/ps to the drift of the control.

Between rank counts the QM energy at step 0 agrees to 1.3e-9
kJ/mol and the total energy over the run to 2.4e-5 kJ/mol, but the QM atom
forces differ by 1e-5 kJ/mol/nm at step 0 and 2e-3 at step 200, about 2e-6 of
the largest force: OpenCPMD distributes its plane waves over the ranks, its sums
run in a different order, and its SCF stops at a slightly different point.
A tighter orbital convergence does not shrink that difference: at 1e-9 the
step-0 oxygen forces of 1 and 2 ranks differ by 5e-4 kJ/mol/nm.
With `QM_RANKS 1` the QM calculation runs on rank 0 alone, and 4 ranks match 1
rank to 3e-13 kJ/mol/nm in the forces and 7e-12 kJ/mol in the total energy over
10 steps, at the cost of the SCF time of one rank.
For 1e-10 agreement with a one-rank run, use `QM_RANKS 1`.

## Stress
`tests/python/test_gromacs_opencpmd.py` compares
`cp2k_get_stress_tensor()` with ASE's central difference of the library's own energy under strains of the cell, at orbital convergence 1e-8, when `CPMDC_GROMACS_LIB` is an OpenCPMD build and `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR`
is set.
With `CELL PERIODIC` (`tests/water_blyp_periodic_params.capnp.txt`) the strain
is 1e-6: each strained cell is a new setup at the deck's cutoff, and in the
triclinic cell a strain of 1e-4 already takes plane waves across the cutoff.
With `CELL NONE` and the mechanical embedding the strain is 1e-5.
One run, 1 rank, in eV/Angstrom^3:

| Case | Largest stress element | Largest difference | Ratio |
|------+------------------------+--------------------+-------|
| `CELL PERIODIC`, 1 nm cube | 1.889e-2 | 9.703e-9 | 5.1e-7 |
| `CELL PERIODIC`, triclinic | 1.927e-2 | 7.553e-9 | 3.9e-7 |
| `CELL NONE` in TIP3P, cube | 2.545e-4 | 5.875e-10 | 2.3e-6 |
| `CELL NONE` in TIP3P, triclinic | 2.545e-4 | 3.096e-9 | 1.2e-5 |

The test allows 1e-6 of the largest element with `CELL PERIODIC`, where the
stress also matches `CPMDCCalculator` to 1e-7, and 3e-5 with `CELL NONE`, where
the difference shrinks as the strain squared.

## NPT
`bench/gromacs_opencpmd_npt.py` runs NPT on the system above, v-rescale at 300 K
and isotropic C-rescale (or `--pcoupl Parrinello-Rahman`) at 1 bar with `tau-p`
0.5 ps, compressibility 4.5e-5
/bar, and 0.5 fs steps, once with the QM water and once all classical. The deck predicts the orbitals with ASPC of order 4 at orbital convergence 1e-6. `--lattice 4 --spacing 0.31 --minimize` replaces the 27 waters at 0.14 g/cm^3
by 64 at 1.00 g/cm^3 in a 1.24 nm box, relaxed classically first:

python bench/gromacs_opencpmd_npt.py --gmx $GMX_PREFIX/bin/gmx_mpi_d --mpiexec mpiexec \
  --ranks 8 --pseudo-dir $CPMD_ROOT/../Regtests/tests/PP_LIBRARY --steps 30000 \
  --lattice 4 --spacing 0.31 --minimize --workdir npt --json npt.json
python bench/gromacs_opencpmd_npt.py --gmx $GMX_PREFIX/bin/gmx_mpi_d --mpiexec mpiexec \
  --classical-only --steps 2000000 --lattice 4 --spacing 0.31 --minimize \
  --workdir npt-long --json npt-long.json
python bench/npt_block_average.py npt.json --reference npt-long.json \
  --output bench/results/gromacs_npt_crescale_64w.org

The first command writes the energy frames of both runs, every 10 steps, to
`npt.json`; the second runs the classical control alone for 1 ns, which takes
minutes; the third discards each run's equilibration, block-averages the rest,
and writes the tables below.
The JSON files and the run directories stay out of the repository; for the run
below, `bench/results/gromacs_npt_crescale_64w_blocks.csv` and
`_windows.csv` hold the block averages and window means at full precision, and `_runs.json`
the per-run summaries and arguments of both JSON files without their frames or
paths.

### 64 waters over 15 ps
One run on the 8-core Xeon virtual machine, GROMACS 2025.5 (double, Open MPI
5.0.10, OpenBLAS) with the virial patch, OpenCPMD with Open MPI, the QM water on
8 ranks with `QM_RANKS ALL` and nothing else on the machine beyond seconds of
analysis; the classical controls run on 1 rank.
The library recentres the QM water in its cluster cell on every call
(`CPMDC_RECENTER` in
environment variables (file:../reference/environment.org)).
The QM run took 19875 s of wall time by `md.log`, 0.66 s per step.
It reported the `opencpmd` backend and the stress on the first request, and
`md.log` has no missing-stress line.

`bench/npt_block_average.py` discards, for each run, the latest start in its
first half that maximises the number of uncorrelated frames after it (Chodera,
J. Chem. Theory Comput. 12, 1799 (2016)) over volume, density and pressure, and
at least four `tau-p`, 2 ps.
The error is the Flyvbjerg-Petersen standard error of the mean at the coarsest
blocking level with at least 8 blocks.

The classical box has settled: over 1 ns its pressure, -13 +- 26 bar, matches
the 1 bar of the barostat, and its density, 918.5 +- 3.4
kg/m^3, is that of this flexible TIP3P with 0.55 nm cut-offs in a 64-water box. Its blocking error still grows from 20 to 82 ps blocks, so that error is a lower bound too; it puts the statistical inefficiency of the volume at 7.2 ps, and the volume of 64 waters fluctuates by 0.09 nm^3, so a 15 ps run holds few independent samples. The 15 ps control, 906.3 +- 7.7 kg/m^3,
is 1.5 errors from it; its 1 ps window means of the volume span 0.20 nm^3 from 2
ps on.

The QM run, 931.4 +- 7.3 kg/m^3, is 1.6 combined errors above the 1 ns control.
From 2 ps on its 1 ps window means of the volume span 0.17 nm^3, 1.99 to 2.16
nm^3, without a trend: the last window, 2.078 nm^3, lies inside the range of the
first ones, and the box ends at 2.044 nm^3.
Its blocking error, like that of the 15 ps control, still grows at the largest
block, so it is a lower bound, and the mean pressure, 310 +- 128 bar, is 2.4 of
those errors from 1 bar.
The barostat follows the pressure GROMACS reports: the least-squares slope of
the change of ln V from one frame to the next against the pressure is 1.049
times compressibility x 5 fs / `tau-p` with the QM water and 1.005 times in the
control.
From 1 ps on, the 1 ps window means of `Quantum En.` lie within 15.5
kJ/mol of each other, without a step. GROMACS' conserved energy drifts by 191.5 kJ/mol/ps
with the QM water and 181.5 in the control, so the drift is not from the QM
water.
The final `md.gro` puts the QM oxygen at (0.511, 0.455, 0.892) nm, 0.44 nm from
where it started after the minimisation, with its nearest oxygens 0.269, 0.281
and 0.299 nm away, against 0.274, 0.283 and 0.304 nm for the same water in the
control.

#### Before recentring
The first run of these commands, on a library that kept the QM region's absolute
position in its cell, gave the QM water 844.6 +- 14.3
kg/m^3 (2.2761 +- 0.0390 nm^3, -337 +- 171 bar, 5.7 ps discarded): its box held 1.98 to 2.08 nm^3 for 6 ps, then grew to 2.5 nm^3 by 13 ps while the pressure turned more negative, and its final QM oxygen sat 0.2 nm from a face of the 1 nm cluster cell. A water diffuses half a nanometre or more in 15 ps, as the one above did. `bench/cluster_drift_scan.py`
moves a BLYP water towards a face of the deck's 10 Angstrom Hockney cell;
`bench/results/cluster_drift_scan.org` has the tables. On that library the
energy moves by -3.9e-5 Hartree with the outer hydrogen 3 Angstrom from the
face, -2.8e-4 at 1 Angstrom, +5.0e-4 at 0.5 Angstrom and -8.4e-3 at 0.5 Angstrom
past it, where the net force is 0.17 Hartree/Bohr.
The trace of `sum x (x) f` goes from +0.049 Hartree at the centre to +0.093 at 1
Angstrom and -0.099 at 0.5 Angstrom; the 0.19 Hartree between those two is 1300
bar on a 2.1 nm^3 box, against the -13 +- 26 bar of the control, and past the
face it is +3.2 Hartree.
The barostat scales coordinates about the origin, so a growing box also moves a
QM water that is off the origin towards a face.
With recentring every one of those positions gives the energy of the centred
water to 1.1e-14 Hartree and its forces to 3.4e-14 Hartree/Bohr, the forces sum
to zero, and the trace is 0.062214 Hartree at all of them.

### 2 ps runs
One run of each system, C-rescale, 4000 steps (2 ps), the QM water on 4 ranks
with `QM_RANKS ALL`, both systems at once; the classical control runs on 1 rank.
Means and standard deviations of the energy frames, every 10 steps, over the
second picosecond:

| System | Run | Volume, nm^3 | Density, kg/m^3 | Pressure, bar | Temperature, K | Volume at 0 and 2 ps, nm^3 |
|--------+-----+--------------+-----------------+---------------+----------------+----------------------------|
| 27 waters | QM water | 5.946 (0.054) | 135.8 (1.2) | 45 (664) | 311.5 (24.7) | 5.832, 5.853 |
| 27 waters | classical | 6.022 (0.063) | 134.2 (1.4) | 170 (805) | 329.1 (32.5) | 5.832, 6.261 |

Both QM runs reported the `opencpmd` backend and the stress on the first
request, and `md.log` has no missing-stress line.
GROMACS' conserved energy, which includes the thermostat and barostat work,
drifts by 13.9 kJ/mol/ps with the QM water and 11.1 without in the 27-water
system.
The 64-water runs of this length, which the 15 ps runs above replace, had not
settled.
Each QM run took 6907 s, 1.73 s per step.

With `--pcoupl Parrinello-Rahman --tau-p 2.0 --steps 2000` on the 64 waters,
beside a one-rank job for part of the time, the QM run took 2891 s.
Over the second half picosecond:

| Run | Volume, nm^3 | Density, kg/m^3 | Pressure, bar | Temperature, K | Volume at 0 and 1 ps, nm^3 |
|-----+--------------+-----------------+---------------+----------------+----------------------------|
| QM water | 1.967 (0.006) | 973.4 (2.9) | -21 (2957) | 273.3 (14.2) | 1.907, 1.978 |
| classical | 2.015 (0.043) | 950.5 (20.0) | 323 (3048) | 294.6 (12.6) | 1.907, 2.099 |

Both runs start near 205 K, as the 300 K velocities flow into the minimised
structure; in 1 ps the thermostat has brought the classical run near 300 K but
not yet the QM run, which the 15 ps C-rescale run above reaches within its
second picosecond.

# Overhead per step
## LAMMPS routes
`bench/lammps_routes.py` integrates two water molecules in a 9 Angstrom cubic
box (`metal`, NVE) through each route and reports the median wall time per step
over fresh repeats, with the raw values.
With the reference evaluator this is coupling overhead: an OpenCPMD step adds
the same SCF time to every route.

python bench/lammps_routes.py --build build --steps 2000 --repeats 7

One run on an 8-core Xeon virtual machine with LAMMPS 22 Jul 2025 from the pip
wheel and i-PI 3.3.1:

| Route | Median, microseconds per step |
|-------+-------------------------------|
| `Session.calculate_au` in a Python loop, no integrator | 7.4 |
| LAMMPS with `pair_style zero`, no cpmdc | 0.65 |
| `pair_style cpmdc` | 7.1 |
| `FixExternal` | 87 |
| `FixExternal` through ASE's `SocketServer` and `cpmdc-ipi-c` | 253 |
| i-PI with `cpmdc-ipi-c` | 231 |
| i-PI with `cpmdc-ipi-c` and LAMMPS `fix ipi` | 318 |

The in-process routes time `run` inside one process; the i-PI routes use i-PI's
own per-step timing, so no route counts process startup.
The GROMACS table below times GROMACS on the same system beside
`pair_style cpmdc`.

## GROMACS routes
`bench/gromacs_routes.py` integrates the system of `bench/lammps_routes.py`, two
water molecules in a 0.9 nm cube on the reference evaluator with the periodic
deck, NVE at 0.25 fs, through GROMACS and through LAMMPS.
GROMACS runs twice, for 1000 and 1000 + `STEPS` steps, and the per-step time is
the difference of md.log's wall times over `STEPS`, so startup and the first
evaluation cancel.

CPMDC_GMX=gmx_d python bench/gromacs_routes.py --build build --steps 20000 --repeats 7

One run on an 8-core Xeon virtual machine, GROMACS 2025.5 (double, thread-MPI,
one rank, one OpenMP thread) and LAMMPS 22 Jul 2025 from the pip wheel, 20000
steps, 7 repeats:

| Route | Median, microseconds per step | Raw |
|-------+-------------------------------+-----|
| `Session.calculate_au` in a Python loop, no integrator | 5.95 | 6.00 5.91 5.92 5.91 6.05 6.02 5.95 |
| LAMMPS with `pair_style zero`, no cpmdc | 0.48 | 0.48 0.49 0.49 0.48 0.50 0.48 0.48 |
| LAMMPS with `pair_style cpmdc` | 10.43 | 10.46 10.45 10.43 10.41 10.46 10.42 10.40 |
| GROMACS, QM/MM off, no interactions | 1.55 | 1.50 1.60 1.55 1.55 1.50 1.50 1.65 |
| GROMACS with `libcpmdc_gromacs`, both waters QM | 4.50 | 4.50 4.55 4.50 4.65 4.50 4.60 4.50 |

Over the engine alone, cpmdc adds 2.95 microseconds per step to GROMACS and 9.95
to LAMMPS; both include the reference evaluation itself. md.log prints wall
times to 1 ms, which resolves 0.05 microseconds per step over 20000 steps.
An OpenCPMD step adds the same SCF time to every route.

## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/mpi-model.org

CPMD is an MPI program: one SCF is spread over the ranks of a communicator, and
one of those ranks, the parent, owns input and output.
Embedding it in a host that is itself started under `mpirun` raises three
questions: which ranks form one CPMD calculation, which rank's result counts,
and who ends MPI.
This page explains the answers `cpmdc` gives and why.

# Every rank is a copy of the host
Under `mpirun`, each rank runs the whole host program, and each rank's copy of
`libcpmdc` calls into its own copy of CPMD.
CPMD's collective operations tie those copies together: an SCF can only advance
when every rank of its communicator takes part.
So every rank must make the same `cpmdc` calls, with the same messages, in the
same order.
A rank that skips a call, or evaluates a different geometry, leaves the others
waiting inside CPMD.

# The communicator CPMD uses
An OpenCPMD build (`-Dwith_cpmd=true`) takes MPI from the CPMD archive it is
linked into, and always needs it.
The `with_mpi` option only decides whether the default library, the reference
evaluator, links MPI.

OpenCPMD keeps its world communicator in `mp_comm_world`.
`mp_start` assigns that variable only when CPMD itself calls `MPI_Init`.
When MPI is already running, `mp_start` leaves `mp_comm_world` as the host set
it.

`cpmdc_bind_calculator(ranks_per_calc)` initialises MPI when it is not running,
then splits `MPI_COMM_WORLD` with `MPI_Comm_split`, colour
`world_rank / ranks_per_calc` and key `world_rank mod ranks_per_calc`, and
installs the new communicator as `mp_comm_world` before `mp_start`.
Each colour is one calculator: its own CPMD setup, its own SCF, its own stored
orbitals, all driven by the same deck.
The split happens at most once per process.
`embed_calculator_bound`, a module variable in `cpmd_embed_c_api`, records it,
and a second bind does not split again.
It returns `world_rank / ranks_per_calc` for its own value, or -1 when that
value does not divide the world size or is above it, and the communicator
already stored stays as it was.
A host that already holds the calculator communicator calls
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm` instead.
That call reads rank and size from the adopted communicator, copies it into
`mp_comm_world` on an OpenCPMD build, and does not call
`MPI_Init` or `MPI_Comm_split`.
`cpmdc_adopted_comm` copies the stored handle back out.
A null communicator, a size that is not `ranks_per_calc` when that argument is
positive, MPI that has not been initialised, or a build without MPI returns -1.
The text is `cpmdc_last_error()`.
A later adopt replaces the communicator when no live `CPMDCSession` has started
an evaluation.
A session that was created but has not evaluated holds no CPMD state, so it does
not block the adopt.
If any rank of the group has a live session that has evaluated, every rank
returns -1 and leaves the handle alone.

| World size | `ranks_per_calc` | Calculators | Parent ranks |
|------------+------------------+-------------+--------------|
| 16 | 16, 0, or no call | 1 | 0 |
| 16 | 4 | 4 | 0, 4, 8, 12 |
| 16 | 5 | refused, returns -1 | |

# The adopted index
The calculator index is the lowest `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rank of the group divided by
the adopted size.
The group must be one aligned block of that many consecutive world ranks,
starting at a multiple of the size.
Any other layout returns -1 on every rank of the group.
Indices are unique when every group has the same size.
Passing the same `ranks_per_calc > 0` on every rank enforces that size.
A striped split of 4 ranks into groups {0, 2} and {1, 3} is refused: both have
size 2 and lowest ranks 0 and 1, so both would have been index 0.
Reversing the key order inside an aligned block does not change the index.
One group of 4, two groups of 2, and four groups of 1 are the same rule.
The mpirun how-to (file:../howto/mpi.org) shows the call.
rgpot (https://rgpot.rgoswami.me) is the host that loads this library and may
already have split the ranks; its group contract is the
rgpot MPI reference (https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/mpi.html).

Open MPI's Fortran handle for `MPI_COMM_WORLD` is 0, and `MPI_COMM_NULL` is a
different value.
The stored handle uses that numbering, so 0 means the world communicator.
The index is the lowest world rank of an aligned block divided by that size.
cpmdc does not make the SCF energy or the forces bitwise identical across rank
counts.
Those reductions run inside OpenCPMD (`mp_sum` is `MPI_Allreduce`, the FFT plane
split follows the rank count, and OpenMP `REDUCTION` clauses run inside the
archive).
A single point at one rank and at two ranks can be compared by the maximum
absolute deviation of the energy and of the forces.
That comparison is a report, not a bitwise claim.

| Adopted size | `ranks_per_calc` | Result |
|--------------+------------------+--------|
| 2 | 2 | index = lowest world rank / 2, the same on both ranks |
| 2 | 4 | -1, `cpmdc_last_error()` names 2 and 4 |
| 4 | 0 or less | index = lowest world rank / 4 |
| 1 | 1 | index = that rank's world rank |
| 2, striped {0, 2} | 2 | -1, not an aligned block |

# Why the parent rank's result counts
CPMD computes the energy and ionic forces for the calculation as a whole, and
its parent rank, rank 0 of `mp_comm_world`, is the one CPMD itself treats as
holding them.
`cpmd.x` writes the output, the restart file, and `GEOMETRY` from that rank.
A library force call writes none of those files.
The other ranks return from the same call with values of their own.
They agreed with the parent in a 4-rank water single point.
Over the many steps of a search they need not: in a 4-rank dimer search where
every rank also ran the host's optimiser, the ranks' paths diverged, and only
rank 0's results matched the file route.
The robust rule is that the host takes the parent's result and broadcasts it, so
every rank's optimiser steps from the same numbers.
The MPI standard gives the same advice: an application that needs a reproducible
result computes it at one process and broadcasts it
(MPI 4.1, section 6.9.1 (https://www.mpi-forum.org/docs/mpi-4.1/mpi41-report/node130.htm)).
`cpmdc` does not broadcast by default.
`CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` makes it broadcast inside each calculator: after each
evaluation, rank 0 of the calculator communicator sends its energy, gradient,
and result snapshots to the other ranks of that communicator.
`cpmdc_last_rank_spread()` reports how far the other ranks were from those
values, which is the size of the disagreement the broadcast removed.
A host that needs every calculator's result on every world rank still broadcasts
across calculators, because only the host knows which of its communicators
should receive them.

# One session per calculator
CPMD's module state and the stored orbitals live in the process, one set per
rank.
A calculator therefore evaluates one `CPMDCSession`.
A second session in the same process keeps the stored orbitals when the
functional, deck, cutoff, cell, charge, multiplicity, and elemental composition
match.
Switching to a different method or composition drops them on the next
evaluation.
Independent calculations belong on separate calculators: one per image of a
nudged elastic band, one per end of a dimer.

# Who ends MPI
CPMD calls
`MPI_Init` in its setup when MPI is not running yet, and `cpmdc_bind_calculator`
does the same.
Neither `cpmdc` nor the patched CPMD calls `MPI_Finalize`: in a host, the host
decides when MPI ends, and a library that finalized MPI would break a host that
still needs it.
The host has to finalize on every rank before exit.
Open MPI 5 counts a rank that exits without it as an abnormal termination and
kills the others, which in a 4-rank single point killed rank 0 before it had
written its result.
`cpmdc_finalize()` marks the library finalized and leaves MPI alone for the same
reason.

# Threads inside ranks
An OpenCPMD build with OpenMP adds threads inside each rank.
Ranks, threads, and calculators multiply: 16 cores can hold one calculator of 16
single-threaded ranks, four calculators of four ranks, or other combinations,
set with `mpirun -np`, `cpmdc_bind_calculator`, and `OMP_NUM_THREADS`.
The mpirun how-to (file:../howto/mpi.org) shows the calls.


## File: docs/orgmode/explanation/opencpmd-patches.org

A stock OpenCPMD runs one job per process and ends it with `STOP`.
`libcpmdc` runs many evaluations in one host process, keeps the orbitals between
them, and must survive a CPMD error.
The patches in
`tools/` add the hooks for that; the [[file:../howto/opencpmd-archive.org][archive
how-to]] lists them and the order to apply them.

# What the patches change
The rwfopt patch publishes `embed_set_warm_orbitals`, `embed_set_need_forces`,
`embed_reset_warm_orbitals`, and `embed_set_write_files`.
Its geometry-aware selector is `embed_choose_warm_start_metric_v2`.
The bridge requires that exact versioned procedure in both the Fortran module
interface and the archive object.
An unversioned selector has a different calling convention and cannot be
substituted, even if a newer module file is supplied beside it.
A missing versioned symbol requires rebuilding the patched archive; copying
module files alone is insufficient.
The geometry patch adds `embed_ctrl`, which holds `embed_write_files` (default
true).
Setting it false skips `geofile` in `initrun` and the `zhwwf` and `geofile`
writes in `rwfopt`.
`wrgeof` still prints coordinates.
`embed_set_warm_orbitals(.FALSE.)` frees the saved orbitals.
`embed_warm_orbitals` and `embed_need_forces` default to false, which is the
`cpmd.x` behaviour.
`rwfopt` leaves `fion` allocated only when `embed_need_forces` is true, and
frees a surviving `fion` before its own `ALLOCATE`.
It saves `c0` only when `embed_warm_orbitals` is true and the SCF converged.
An unconverged pass leaves the previous copy and marks it stale, so a
later copy from that key is refused.
When a converged copy was already stored, that pass also empties the
extrapolation ring. The rwfopt hunk records the stale donor, and
`opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch` breaks the history on the same branch.
A failed store allocation calls `stopgm`.
On the next call it copies that `c0` in before `initrun`.
`rinitwf` then returns after the phase factors when `embed_have_orbitals` is
true, so the guess does not run.
A restart read inside `initrun` can replace `c0`, so the same copy is applied
again after `initrun` when the shape still matches, and a different shape calls
`stopgm`.
`rwfopt` sets `tfor` when `embed_need_forces` is true.
The stop patch publishes `cpmd_stopgm_hook`, a C function pointer.
`stopgm` calls it with the stop code passed by value, after writing
`LocalError-*.log`.
A nonzero return makes `stopgm` return to its caller, and a null pointer makes
`stopgm` call `my_stopall`.
The caller then continues past the failed check.
The wavefunction, `fion`, and module state of that call are undefined, so
`cpmdc` discards the result and sets CPMD up again before the next call.
`stopgm` runs only on the ranks that hit the error.
A host with more than one rank aborts the others, because a rank that returns
while the rest wait in an MPI call leaves them waiting.
A standalone `cpmd.x` leaves the pointer null and links without `libcpmdc`.
While an evaluation is armed, `libcpmdc` stores a catch in the pointer.
The catch records the code and returns 1, and `cpmdc` reports the stop as a
failed call (see troubleshooting (file:../howto/troubleshooting.org)).
The catch and the code it records live in `src/cpmd_stop_intercept.c`, inside
`libcpmdc`, and resolve when `libcpmd.a` links into it; they are internal and
not exported.
A serial build, including the default wheel, does not reference
`cpmd_stopgm_hook`.
The reference is compiled only with `CPMDC_HAS_CPMD`, and on that build it
stays a weak reference, so an archive without the hook leaves the catch unset.
An undefined weak reference links on ELF.
ld64 rejects it, which is why the serial object omits the symbol instead of
marking the declaration weak or `weak_import`.
The calculator split does not need a patch:
`mp_start` assigns `mp_comm_world` only when CPMD itself calls `MPI_Init`, and
`cpmdc_bind_calculator()` initialises MPI and stores its communicator before
that.
A module flag, `embed_calculator_bound`, stops a second bind from splitting
again: it returns `world_rank / ranks_per_calc` for its own value, or -1 when
that value does not divide the world size or is above it, and keeps the
communicator it has.
The timer patch changes `tistopgm`.
`trace_depth` stays `HUGE(0)` until `tistart`, and without the guard the call-stack walk indexes `trace_names`
from that value, so a `stopgm` before `tistart` faults instead of writing
`LocalError`.
The walk runs only when the depth is inside `SIZE(tname%trace_names)`.

The teardown patch adds the module
`embed_teardown` and its routine `embed_teardown_state`, which `libcpmdc` calls
before a second setup.
It frees the saved orbitals, the communicators `set_cp_grp` built, and every
`ALLOCATABLE` module variable and module-variable component that a `USE`
reaches, outside the timer, stop, and CUDA device modules.
It then adds one to `embed_teardowns` in `embed_ctrl`.
39 routines in those 34 modules keep work on the setup and wavefunction
optimisation path for their first call behind a `SAVE` flag: `phfac`,
`setbasis`, `hf_init`, `addfftnset`, `stress`, the density mixers, the symmetry
setup, the Vanderbilt and core-charge splines, `localize2`, and others.
The SCF of a `DIPOLE DYNAMICS` deck calls `localize2`, which keeps its orbital
maps and dipole matrices in `SAVE` arrays sized by the first basis.
A second evaluation at another cutoff overran them in `opeigr`.
Each of these routines compares the count it last saw with `embed_teardowns`, and on a change
frees its own `SAVE` arrays and runs as the first call again.
The next setup then gives the energies of a fresh process.
`tistart` keeps its state: it executes `STOP` on a second call, so the embed
calls it once per process.
`cpmd.x` never tears down, and `embed_teardowns` stays 0 there.

The extrapolation patch keeps the `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` request that `control_test`
turns off for every job other than Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics.
`control_test` copies `cntl%textrap` into `embed_extrap_wfn` in `embed_ctrl`
before it does so.
Only the
I/O rank runs `control_test`, so `rwfopt` broadcasts the flag before it reads it; otherwise the other ranks of a multi-rank run skip `extrapwf` and the ranks wait on different collectives. When that flag is true and a call starts from stored orbitals, `rwfopt` passes them to the `extrapwf` that the molecular dynamics driver calls between steps. That routine adds them to a ring of earlier converged orbitals and returns the always stable predictor-corrector or polynomial prediction, orthonormalised, which starts the self-consistent field iteration. `embed_extrapolation_used` returns how many sets the last prediction combined. The ring keeps the orbitals of one trajectory: a call that does not converge, another orbital key, a store beyond the distance limit, or a reset empties it. `cpmd.x` never sets `embed_warm_orbitals` and never takes this path. Its molecular dynamics runs are unchanged. The [[file:../howto/extrapolate-orbitals.org][extrapolation
how-to]] shows the message and the check.

The constant-cutoff patch is optional and changes no physics.
With `CONSTANT CUTOFF` in `&SYSTEM`, `kin_energy`, `vpsi`, and the kinetic
stress replace G^2 by G^2 + A [1 + erf((G^2 - E0) / sigma)], but `hesele` still
builds the ODIIS preconditioner from G^2 alone.
That diagonal underestimates the curvature of the plane waves above E0 by up to
2A, so ODIIS overshoots on them and stops at its step limit, and `cpmdc` falls
back to PCG.
The patch adds the same term to the diagonal.
On the 60 Ry water deck with A = 100, sigma = 4, and E0 = 40 Ry, ODIIS then
converges in 16 steps, a stress call takes 7.1 s instead of 42.5 s, and the
