   A missing or zero box is `SYMMETRY 0` with `POISSON SOLVER HOCKNEY`.
2. If the deck has no `CELL` keyword, a `CELL` line from `ForceInput.box` is
   inserted after `ANGSTROM` in `&SYSTEM`, or a 12 Angstrom cube when the step
   has no box.
   A tilted box is written as `CELL VECTORS`.
3. If the deck names no `SYMMETRY`, no `POISSON SOLVER`, no `CLUSTER`, and no
   isolated-molecule keyword, the same symmetry choice is written into
   `&SYSTEM`.
   An explicit symmetry line, Hockney solver, `CLUSTER`, or isolated-molecule
   keyword is left as written.
   `CELL VECTORS` is not given a `SYMMETRY` line.
4. If the deck has no `MAXITER` keyword, `MAXITER 40` is inserted after
   `&CPMD`.

The method text is kept in full, including a block longer than a few thousand
characters. A preview buffer shorter than the composed deck returns an error
and does not keep a shortened copy.

So read `method.inp` with those edits in mind.
The `&ATOMS` block in the file lists the pseudopotential lines with a
placeholder atom count of 0; the coordinates come from each step.

# Checks worth making on the file

| Look for | Why |
|----------+-----|
| `SYMMETRY` and `POISSON SOLVER` in `&SYSTEM` | `SYMMETRY 0` with `POISSON SOLVER HOCKNEY` is an isolated system: a zero box, or a deck that asked for isolation. A positive-volume box with no such keyword is symmetry 1, symmetry 8, or `CELL VECTORS` with no symmetry line |
| `CELL` | present means the message fixes the cell; absent means each step's box supplies it |
| `KLEINMAN-BYLANDER` on the `*file` line | on the `LMAX` line CPMD ignores it and integrates the projectors by Gauss-Hermite |
| `MAXITER` | absent means the OpenCPMD path caps the SCF at 40 steps |
| the optimiser keyword (`ODIIS`, `PCG`, `PCG MINIMIZE`) | decides the cost per SCF step; see choosing the optimiser (file:wavefunction-optimiser.org) |
| `FUNCTIONAL` in `&DFT` | the functional CPMD uses; the `dft` section wins over the top-level `functional` |

# Compare with a deck that works
When a hand-written CPMD deck gives the expected energy under `cpmd.x` and the
library does not, compare the two after the edits above:

diff -u reference.inp method.inp

Differences in `&ATOMS` are expected: coordinates, atom counts, and the
species order come from the step.
Every other difference is a field that the message sets differently or leaves
to a default.


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/embedding.org

# Goal
Call `libcpmdc` from a host program: pick an entry point, send the method
message and one geometry message per step, step a session, read the result,
and keep orbitals, RESTART files, and MPI ranks consistent between steps.
This page names the call for each task.
The C ABI reference (file:../reference/c-abi.org) states what each call
promises (arguments, return codes, size rules, units), and
API contracts (file:../reference/contracts.org) adds ownership, thread and
MPI behaviour, errors, and defaults.

# Pick the entry point

| Need | Entry point | Input | Output |
|------+-------------+-------+--------|
| Repeated RPC or optimizer steps | `cpmdc_session_calculate_result` | one `CPMDParams` session, one `ForceInput` per step | serialized `PotentialResult` |
| Repeated native C forces | `cpmdc_session_energy_forces` | one `CPMDParams` session, C coordinate arrays | Hartree plus Hartree/Bohr forces |
| Repeated periodic steps without Cap'n Proto | `cpmdc_session_calculate_au` | one `CPMDParams` session, Bohr positions and an optional cell | Hartree, Hartree/Bohr forces, Hartree virial |
| Single serialized calculation | `cpmdc_calculate_result` | `CPMDParams` and `ForceInput` bytes | serialized `PotentialResult` |
| Scalar compatibility call | `cpmdc_energy_forces` | C coordinate arrays plus `CPMDParams` bytes | Hartree plus Hartree/Bohr forces |
| Capability discovery | `cpmdc_feature_find` | stable feature ID | `CPMDCFeatureEntry` or `NULL` |

Use the session result path for new drivers.
It keeps method setup and topology state in one object while preserving the same
`PotentialResult` carrier used by RPC frontends, cross-language bindings, and
drivers that already use the shared OmniPotentRPC schema.
The compatibility array calls suit a host that already owns native C arrays and
only needs Hartree and Hartree/Bohr values.

Molecular dynamics engines with their own integrator and units usually want
`cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`: one copy of the positions in, the forces and the
virial out.
`tools/lammps/pair_cpmdc.cpp`, the LAMMPS `pair_style cpmdc`, is a complete host
on it, with unit conversion, the triclinic cell, and the MPI gather to one rank;
Run LAMMPS on cpmdc forces (file:lammps.org) documents it beside the Python
`fix external` route.
`tools/gromacs/cpmdc_gromacs.c` is a host on the same call behind another
program's C API, libcp2k, with mechanical QM-MM embedding; see
Run GROMACS on cpmdc forces (file:gromacs.org).

Arguments, units, and return conventions of each row are in
the C ABI conventions (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Conventions) and the
section for its call family
(global array calls (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Global array calls),
sessions (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Sessions),
one-shot calls (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*One-shot message calls),
discovery (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Discovery)).

# Check what the build supports
`cpmdc.h` also exposes a small feature table.
Inspect it before building inputs, hiding unsupported controls, or deciding
whether a stub build is sufficient for a workflow.

size_t feature_count = cpmdc_feature_count();
const CPMDCFeatureEntry *features = cpmdc_feature_table();
const CPMDCFeatureEntry *pimd =
    cpmdc_feature_find("catalog.section.PIMD");
const CPMDCFeatureEntry *result_call =
    cpmdc_feature_find("abi.cpmdc_session_calculate_result");

if (pimd != NULL && pimd->embed_applicable) {
  /* The embedded OpenCPMD build can render a &PIMD section. */
}

The entry layout (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*`CPMDCFeatureEntry` and `CPMDCFeatureKind`)
says which builds expose a feature.
The CPMD option mapping (file:../reference/cpmd-options.org) lists the ID
namespaces (`catalog.section.*`, `catalog.cpmd.*`, `catalog.dft.*`, `params.*`,
`abi.*`) and the `params.inputSections.<section>.<field>` field IDs;
the feature inventory (file:../reference/feature-inventory.org) describes the
table.

The public C entry points are feature rows too.
Use those rows when a host needs to negotiate the serialized result path before
allocating Cap'n Proto buffers:

| Host action | ABI feature ID | Carrier |
|-------------+----------------+---------|
| Accept a process-wide method buffer | `abi.cpmdc_set_params` | `CPMDParams` bytes |
| Create a reusable method session | `abi.cpmdc_session_create` | `CPMDParams` bytes |
| Replace method setup before topology is accepted | `abi.cpmdc_session_set_params` | `CPMDParams` bytes |
| Evaluate one session step into a result message | `abi.cpmdc_session_calculate_result` | `ForceInput` to `PotentialResult` |
| Evaluate one one-shot serialized calculation | `abi.cpmdc_calculate_result` | `CPMDParams` plus `ForceInput` to `PotentialResult` |

# Send the message
There are two wire messages in a normal embedded driver:

| Message | Lifetime | Contents |
|---------+----------+----------|
| `CPMDParams` | Session setup | method, structured CPMD sections, pseudopotentials, engine hints |
| `ForceInput` | One calculation step | positions, atomic numbers, optional cell, requested output units |

Wire structs are generated from `schema/Potentials.capnp`; the header does not
redefine `CPMDParams` fields as a second C struct language.
`CPMDParams` owns method and backend setup.
`ForceInput` owns coordinates, atomic numbers, unit strings, and the optional 3
by 3 cell for a single evaluation.
The runtime renders a CPMD `INPUT` deck from `CPMDParams` and merges the step
geometry into it on each cold evaluation.

Build `CPMDParams` once and serialize it as an unpacked flat Cap'n Proto
message; Writing a CPMDParams message (file:write-cpmdparams.org) shows how to
write one by hand.
Build one `ForceInput` per geometry step.
The `PotentialResult` path converts the output to `ForceInput.energyUnit` and
`ForceInput.energyUnit / ForceInput.lengthUnit`.
The C ABI conventions (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Conventions) state the
buffer format, the `ForceInput` unit strings, and the box rules.

When the host owns arrays in Angstrom and wants Hartree or Hartree/Bohr output
directly, the scalar calls take the arrays and the `CPMDParams` bytes:

#include <cpmdc.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int rc = cpmdc_set_params(params_bytes, params_size);
CPMDCResult result = cpmdc_energy_gradient(
    n_atoms, positions_ang, atomic_numbers, params_bytes, params_size,
    gradient_h_bohr);
CPMDCResult forces = cpmdc_energy_forces(
    n_atoms, positions_ang, atomic_numbers, params_bytes, params_size,
    forces_h_bohr);

The reference covers these under
global array calls (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Global array calls) and
session array steps (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Session array steps).

# Step a session
Callers that drive multiple geometry steps keep method state in a session and
pass a serialized `ForceInput` for each step.
The result-carrier entry point writes an unpacked flat `PotentialResult` for
RPC-style or in-process loops.

CPMDCSession *session = cpmdc_session_create(params_bytes, params_size);

if (session != NULL) {
  size_t forces_len = n_atoms * 3;
  double *forces_h_bohr = calloc(forces_len, sizeof(*forces_h_bohr));
  size_t potential_result_capacity =
      cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input(
          force_input_bytes, force_input_size);
  unsigned char *potential_result_bytes =
      malloc(potential_result_capacity);
  size_t potential_result_size = 0;

  CPMDCResult step = cpmdc_session_calculate_forces(
      session, force_input_bytes, force_input_size, forces_h_bohr,
      forces_len);

  CPMDCResult rpc_step = cpmdc_session_calculate_result(
      session, force_input_bytes, force_input_size,
      potential_result_bytes, potential_result_capacity,
      &potential_result_size);

  free(forces_h_bohr);
  free(potential_result_bytes);
  cpmdc_session_destroy(session);
}

Use the session path for optimizers, molecular dynamics drivers, and RPC
frontends.
It avoids reparsing method setup on every step and gives the runtime one place
to enforce topology consistency.

Three habits keep a host loop correct:

- Size the `PotentialResult` buffer with
  `cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input()` before each serialized call,
  as above; session message steps (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Session message steps)
  say what a zero size and a short buffer mean.
- Free the `CPMDParams` bytes after creating the session; the session keeps its
  own copy (the session type (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*`CPMDCSession`)).
- Create a new `CPMDCSession` to change the atom count, the elemental
  composition, or the method once an evaluation has been accepted
  (sessions (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Sessions) say when the topology is
  fixed).

Read the energy terms of the last evaluation in Hartree with
`cpmdc_last_energy_components()` instead of parsing CLI `ENERGY` files; see
results of the last evaluation (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Results of the last evaluation).

For a complete host-side skeleton, see `examples/host_step.c`.
The checked `example-host-step` Meson test runs that program with generated
fixture bytes and expects output shaped like:

energy_h=...
potential_result_size_bytes=...
message=...

# Handle status and errors
Check every call before using its outputs.
A call that returns `CPMDCResult` reports success in `ok` and carries the
status or error text in `message`.
A session helper that returns `int`, such as `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`,
`cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()`, or `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals()`, returns 0
or -1 and puts the reason in `cpmdc_last_error()` instead of filling
`CPMDCResult`.
The C ABI conventions (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Conventions) list the
return convention of each call, and
library status (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Library status) lists which
calls write `cpmdc_last_error()` and how it behaves.

To find the cause of a failure, read `message` or `cpmdc_last_error()`, then
look the text up in Troubleshooting (file:troubleshooting.org), which lists
common `message` values.
From Python the same failures arrive as `CPMDCError`,
`cpmdc.ipi.ProtocolError` on the i-PI driver, and ASE's `CalculationFailed`; see
the Python reference (file:../reference/python.org).

# Keep orbitals between steps
OpenCPMD keeps one set of converged orbitals for the whole process, not inside a
`CPMDCSession`, and starts the next step from it when the functional, deck,
cutoff, cell, charge, multiplicity, atom count, and elemental composition match.
A change to any of these is a cold start, and so is the first step of the
process.
A session refuses a new atom count or composition, so those change only with a
new session, and a new session whose values match starts warm.
A constant-cutoff deck under `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` may also move the cell
without a cold start.
Wavefunction state between calls (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org)
explains warm starts, extrapolation, and when a step restarts from atomic
orbitals.

To run several trajectories on one session, name an orbital store with
`cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()` and duplicate one with
`cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals()`; see
extrapolate the orbitals (file:extrapolate-orbitals.org) for the workflow and
the session section of the reference (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*Sessions)
for the calls.
`CPMDC_ORBITAL_SLOT_LIMIT` caps how many of those copies stay parked, and a
new park past the cap fails without discarding the ones already stored; see
environment variables (file:../reference/environment.org).

# Choose a CPMDParams carrier
Structured `inputSections` should be preferred over raw blocks when a typed arm
exists:

- `system` for cells, cutoff/grid/mesh controls, state occupation, external
  fields, CDFT (constrained DFT) Gaussian controls, pressure and stress
  controls, Poisson settings, isolated-shape controls, charge, and spin
  multiplicity
- `cpmd` for wavefunction optimization, MD, convergence, restart, and trajectory
  controls
- `dft` for functional and spin-polarized DFT controls
- `atoms` for pseudopotential grouping and fixed non-coordinate `&ATOMS`
  directives
- named OpenCPMD section arms such as `pimd`, `vdw`, `linres`, and `tddft` for
  keyword/value lines and nested subsection blocks

Use `generic` for non-catalog aliases, `set` for merge-only keywords inside a
named section, and `raw` or `inputBlocks` for text-preserving deck fragments.
Choose the least lossy structured carrier:

| Need | Carrier | Feature ID to discover |
|------+---------+------------------------|
| A field exists in `CPMDCpmdSection` | typed `cpmd` arm | `params.inputSections.cpmd.maxIter` |
| A field exists in `CPMDSystemSection` | typed `system` arm | `params.inputSections.system.cell` |
| A field exists in `CPMDDftSection` | typed `dft` arm | `params.inputSections.dft.hfxScreening` |
| Pseudopotentials and fixed non-coordinate `&ATOMS` controls | typed `atoms` arm | `params.inputSections.atoms.pseudopotentials` |
| A catalog section contains keyword/value lines | matching typed long-tail arm | `catalog.section.PIMD` plus `params.inputSections.pimd.directives` |
| A catalog section contains nested blocks | matching typed long-tail arm | `catalog.section.VDW` plus `params.inputSections.vdw.subsections` |
| One merge-only keyword belongs inside a typed section | `set` with `SECTION.KEYWORD` | `params.inputSections.set.key` |
| A non-catalog alias can be expressed as keyword/argument lines | `generic` | `params.inputSections.generic.directives` |
| A complete section fragment must be preserved as text | `raw` | `params.inputSections.raw` |
| A complete deck fragment must be prepended before structured sections | top-level `inputBlocks` | `params.inputBlocks` |

On a geometry render that is not the OpenCPMD merge, typed `atoms` sections
must cover every element present in the step, and a missing `atoms` section
covers H and O only
(CPMD option mapping (file:../reference/cpmd-options.org)).
On the OpenCPMD path the `&ATOMS` block is rebuilt from each step: elements in
`atoms.pseudopotentials` supply the file, `LMAX`, `LOC`, and
`KLEINMAN-BYLANDER`, elements the message omits use the built-in table for H, C,
N, O, Si, and Ge, and an element in neither is an error
(writing a CPMDParams message (file:write-cpmdparams.org)).

# Keep the wavefunction from a RESTART file
The binary `RESTART` file is a separate object from the deck keyword.
Read and rewrite it with `cpmdc-restart` or
`cpmdc_restart.h` (`libcpmdc_restart`).
To keep orbitals while the host owns the next geometry:

1. Read the file with `cpmdc_restart_read_path()` or
   `cpmdc_restart_read_mem()`.
2. Replace the positions with `cpmdc_restart_set_coordinates()`.
3. Write the file back with `cpmdc_restart_write_path()` or
   `cpmdc_restart_write_mem()`.

Coordinates in that file are Bohr in species order.
A coordinate patch copies the wavefunction records unchanged, which is how a
host keeps orbitals while it owns the next geometry.
The RESTART file library (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*RESTART file library)
section of the reference gives every call's contract.

Put `RESTART WAVEFUNCTION` in the deck to start a cold SCF from
the patched file; the OpenCPMD path ignores restarted coordinates, velocities,
and geometry, because each step supplies them.

# Adopt an MPI communicator
When a host already split `MPI_COMM_WORLD` into calculator groups, call
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm()` before the first session evaluates, instead of
`cpmdc_bind_calculator()`.
The call borrows the communicator: keep it alive until the last session is
destroyed or a later adopt replaces it.
The rules and a sketch are in Run under mpirun (file:mpi.org), and the
contracts of both calls are under
MPI in the C ABI reference (file:../reference/c-abi.org::*MPI).

The optional plane-wave scaffold in `include/cpmdc_pwscale.h` times FFT and
MPI paths separately from production `libcpmdc`; see
Plane-wave scaffold reference (file:../reference/pwscale.org) and
Time plane-wave scaling across ranks (file:pwscale-ranks.org).
`cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda()` runs the CUDA kernel when the build uses
`-Dwith_pwscale_cuda=true`.

# Set the OpenCPMD runtime inputs
Archive builds require `-Dwith_cpmd=true` and `-Dcpmd_root=/path/to/OpenCPMD`.
That tree must contain `lib/libcpmd.a` and the OpenCPMD object/include files
from a completed executable build with the patches in `tools/`; see
building the archive (file:opencpmd-archive.org).

Set `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` to the directory holding the pseudopotential files.
A cold evaluation changes into that directory while CPMD reads
them (`ratom` and `recpnew`), then returns to the host's directory.
`CPMD_PP_LIBRARY_PATH` is the fallback when `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` is unset; with
neither set, a cold evaluation fails.
Environment variables (file:../reference/environment.org) name
`CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` and the embed flags `CPMDC_STRESS`, `CPMDC_WARM_RMSD`, and
the rest.

`CPMDC_DECK_OUT` names a file that receives the method deck cpmdc renders from
`CPMDParams`; see debugging a deck (file:debug-deck.org) for what the
OpenCPMD path adds before CPMD parses it.

On a cold OpenCPMD evaluation the Fortran bridge in
`src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90` composes the full deck, and `src/cpmdc_memfd.c` puts
it in an anonymous Linux `memfd_create` file that CPMD reads as
`/proc/self/fd/N`, so no `INPUT` file reaches the disk.
`src/cpmdc_embed_host.c` resolves the pseudopotential directory and maps
species-block gradients back to atom order.
Architecture (file:../explanation/architecture.org) walks the layer list.

# Drive cpmdc through rgpot or a socket
rgpot (https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgpot) loads `libcpmdc.so` in
`CPMDPot`, maps host coordinates into `ForceInput`, and reads a serialized
`PotentialResult` from `cpmdc_session_calculate_result()`.
`CPMDC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, and `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE` name the
library path; see environment variables (file:../reference/environment.org)
and eOn through rgpot (file:../tutorials/eon-rgpot.org) for a full
minimisation.

Drive cpmdc over the i-PI socket protocol (file:socket-drivers.org) documents
`cpmdc-ipi`, which holds one Python `Session`, and `cpmdc-ipi-c`, which holds
one `CPMDCSession *` and calls `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` with Bohr arrays
and the virial output.
Each evaluates when the server's `POSDATA` message arrives and sends the
stored result when `GETFORCE` asks for it.
The page also names the C ABI call that `cpmdc-ipi` makes for each step.

# Check forces from a live link
Nuclear forces from repeated SCF calls (file:../explanation/opencpmd-patches.org::*Nuclear forces from repeated SCF calls)
explains how a live OpenCPMD link exports forces and what makes a call warm.
Check forces and stress by finite differences (file:check-forces.org)
compares the forces of a session with central differences of its energy.

Prefer an off-equilibrium water or similar system when checking forces.
Some tightly packed cluster geometries can report a zero nuclear gradient even
under native `cpmd.x`; an energy that changes between calls does not show that
the forces are right.

Example environment for a live driver:

export CPMDC_LIBRARY=/path/to/libcpmdc.so
export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=/path/to/pseudopotentials
# one session, many ForceInput steps via cpmdc_session_calculate_forces


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/extrapolate-orbitals.org

# Goal
Start each self-consistent field (SCF) of a host-driven trajectory from a prediction over the orbitals of the previous steps.
Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (CPMD) does this in its own Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (BO-MD) with `EXTRAPOLATE WFN`.
Use it when the host takes equal time steps, as a molecular dynamics (MD) integrator does.
An optimiser, a saddle search, or a nudged elastic band moves by unequal steps, and the plain warm start of wavefunction state between calls (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org) suits them.

# Apply the patch
`tools/opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch` goes onto the OpenCPMD tree after `opencpmd_embed_teardown.patch`, as the archive how-to (file:opencpmd-archive.org) lists.
Without it, OpenCPMD prints `WARNING! WAVEFUNCTION EXTRAPOLATION ONLY SUPPORTED FOR BO-MD. DISABLING...`.
Every warm call then starts from the unchanged stored orbitals.
A `libcpmdc` built from this tree needs the patch: it links `embed_extrapolation_used` from the archive.

# Ask for it in the message
( cpmd = ( optimizeWavefunction = true,
           convergenceOrbitals = 1.0e-6,
           maxIter = 200,
           extrapolateWfnOptions = "ASPC",
           extrapolateWfnOrder = 4 ) )

The message renders `EXTRAPOLATE WFN ASPC` with `4` on the next line.
`ASPC` selects the always stable predictor-corrector (ASPC) coefficients of Kolafa (J. Comput. Chem. 25, 335 (2004), doi:10.1002/jcc.10385).
`POLY` selects the polynomial ones.
OpenCPMD starts from the ASPC coefficients and switches only for `POLY` on the `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` line.
An `extrapolateWfnOrder` with an empty `extrapolateWfnOptions` renders `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` alone, and that deck uses ASPC.
The order is the number of earlier converged orbital sets that the prediction combines.
OpenCPMD still prints its warning, because `control_test` keeps `cntl%textrap` off for a wavefunction optimisation; the patch reads the request from `embed_extrap_wfn` instead.

# Check that it runs
Run the host with `CPMDC_SCF_STEPS=1`.
A call that starts from a prediction writes `cpmdc_wfn_extrapolated K` before its `cpmdc_scf_steps N` line, with `K` the number of orbital sets combined.
`tests/test_extrapolate_wfn.c` captures these first lines from the error stream while it steps through the water trajectory of `tests/golden/water_aspc_bomd.txt`:

cpmdc_warm_start -2 periodic=F
cpmdc_scf_steps 18
cpmdc_warm_start 0  4.3467596441160280E-004 donor_key=0 periodic=F
cpmdc_scf_steps 8
cpmdc_warm_start 0  1.2970053609380071E-003 donor_key=0 periodic=F
cpmdc_wfn_extrapolated 2
cpmdc_scf_steps 9
cpmdc_warm_start 0  2.1382110087115411E-003 donor_key=0 periodic=F
cpmdc_wfn_extrapolated 3
cpmdc_scf_steps 8

The first call is cold.
The second starts from the first call's orbitals.
From the third call on, `K` grows to the order.

# Know when the history restarts
The prediction is valid only when the stored orbitals come from the previous calls of one trajectory.
Each of these events empties the history:

- a call whose SCF does not converge, including one that already held a converged copy, or an orbital direct inversion in the iterative subspace (ODIIS) pass that ends in the preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) `MINIMIZE` continuation. `tools/opencpmd_embed_rwfopt.patch` marks that donor stale, and `tools/opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch` empties the ring on the same branch
- `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()` with another key
- stored orbitals farther than `CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` from the new geometry
- anything that clears the stored orbitals, such as a cell, cutoff, or composition change; a constant-cutoff cell that moves in place under `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` keeps the history

The next calls then build the history again from the stored orbitals.
`STORE` and `CSTEPS` have no effect on this route.
A library call writes no `RESTART` file, and every call converges its SCF to `CONVERGENCE ORBITALS`.
The energy and forces are those of a converged SCF, so only the number of iterations changes.


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/gromacs.org

GROMACS can integrate on cpmdc energies and forces in process, for a QM group
that is part of the system or all of it.
`libcpmdc_gromacs` implements the libcp2k C API that GROMACS' CP2K QM/MM interface calls, and answers each call with one `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`
of the C ABI (file:../reference/c-abi.org). GROMACS links it in place of
CP2K, so `mdrun` needs no extra process and no socket. Energies and forces need
no change to GROMACS' source; the QM virial, and so the pressure and NPT, needs
a short patch to GROMACS' QM/MM module (see Pressure and NPT (*Pressure and NPT)).

| Route | GROMACS side | Needs |
|-------+--------------+-------|
| `libcpmdc_gromacs` | the CP2K QM/MM interface, `qmmm-cp2k-*` mdp options | GROMACS 2024 or later built with `-DGMX_DOUBLE=ON -DGMX_CP2K=ON` against cpmdc's `libcp2k.pc` |

The GROMACS interface reference (file:../reference/gromacs.org) lists the
input keys, units, cell, embedding, and virial conventions, and cpmdc inside MD engines (file:../explanation/md-engines.org)
explains why this route and reports runs on OpenCPMD.

The interface was checked with GROMACS 2024.6, 2025.5, and 2026.4; the three
call the same libcp2k functions, and 2026 adds `cp2k_get_positions` and
`cp2k_get_version`, which the library provides.
The MPI build, the installed library, the OpenCPMD backend, and the virial patch
were checked with 2025.5; the 2024.6 and 2026.4 patches apply and their QM/MM
sources compile.

# Build
Meson builds `libcpmdc_gromacs.so` with `libcpmdc` (`-Dwith_gromacs_shim=auto`,
the default; it is off for the Python wheel build) and writes
`build/tools/gromacs/pkgconfig/libcp2k.pc`, which points GROMACS at the library
and at `tools/gromacs/libcp2k.h`.
`meson install` puts the library in `LIBDIR`, the header in
`include/cpmdc/gromacs`, and the `.pc` file in `LIBDIR/cpmdc/gromacs/pkgconfig`,
apart from cpmdc's own `cpmdc.pc`, so that `libcp2k` is found only where asked
for.

GROMACS'
`cmake/gmxManageCP2K.cmake` requires `CP2K_DIR`, prepends `CP2K_DIR/pkgconfig`
to `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, and reads `libcp2k.pc` there, so pass the directory above
`pkgconfig`.
The `patch` line adds the QM virial; `qmmm-virial-2024.patch` is for 2024.6 and
2025.5, `qmmm-virial-2026.patch` for 2026.4.
Without it GROMACS builds and runs NVE and NVT as before:

meson setup build && meson compile -C build
patch -p1 -d gromacs-2025.5 < tools/gromacs/patches/qmmm-virial-2024.patch
cmake -S gromacs-2025.5 -B build-gmx -G Ninja -DGMX_DOUBLE=ON -DGMX_MPI=OFF \
  -DGMX_CP2K=ON -DCP2K_DIR=$PWD/build/tools/gromacs
cmake --build build-gmx --target install

From an installed cpmdc:

meson setup build --prefix=$PWD/build/prefix && meson compile -C build
meson install -C build
cp2k_dir=$(dirname "$(dirname "$(find build/prefix -path '*/cpmdc/gromacs/pkgconfig/libcp2k.pc')")")
patch -p1 -d gromacs-2025.5 < tools/gromacs/patches/qmmm-virial-2024.patch
cmake -S gromacs-2025.5 -B build-gmx -G Ninja -DGMX_DOUBLE=ON -DGMX_MPI=OFF \
  -DGMX_CP2K=ON -DCP2K_DIR=$cp2k_dir

The installed `libcp2k.pc` gives `-L`, `-Wl,-rpath` and the two libraries in
`Libs`, and `-I` for `include/cpmdc/gromacs` in `Cflags`, so any pkg-config
consumer compiles, links and runs against it with no further flags.
`libcpmdc_gromacs` records `$ORIGIN` on Linux and `@loader_path` on macOS, so
it opens `libcpmdc` from its own directory after the prefix is moved. The
installed library does not keep the build tree or the original prefix in
`RPATH` or `RUNPATH`.
GROMACS takes only the library names, directories, and include directories from
it, not the `-Wl,-rpath`; it finds the library at run time because it records
the directories it linked from as its run path
(`CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH`).
Either way `libgromacs` names the build tree or the prefix it was built against,
and a GROMACS built against one does not follow the library to the other.

`scripts/ci/build_gromacs_cpmdc.sh VERSION PREFIX CP2K_DIR [thread-mpi|mpi]` downloads a pinned GROMACS release, checks its SHA-256, applies the virial patch for that release, builds it this way (`mpi`: `-DGMX_MPI=ON`
with `mpicc`, `mpicxx` and `mpifort` from `PATH`), and checks that `libgromacs`
resolves `libcpmdc_gromacs` to the `libdir` of that `libcp2k.pc`.

With OpenCPMD linked, GROMACS must use the BLAS and LAPACK `libcpmdc` links:
GROMACS' bundled ones (`-DGMX_EXTERNAL_BLAS=OFF`) export `dgemm_` and the rest
from `libgromacs`, OpenCPMD's calls bind to them, and its nonlocal
pseudopotential forces come out wrong (see Troubleshooting (file:troubleshooting.org)).
The script passes `-DGMX_EXTERNAL_BLAS=ON -DGMX_EXTERNAL_LAPACK=ON` and the BLAS
of `libcpmdc` when `libcpmdc` links one, and
`libcpmdc_gromacs` stops `mdrun` when it finds `dgemm_` in `libgromacs` with
OpenCPMD linked.

Build GROMACS in double precision.
Its QM/MM module stores cpmdc's forces as `real`, which is `float` in a
mixed-precision build, and the 1e-10 agreement below holds only for `gmx_d`.

# Set up a run
The QM group is an index group.
For GROMACS to generate its normal CP2K input, select the same functional,
charge, and multiplicity as the `CPMDParams` message:

qmmm-cp2k-active      = true
qmmm-cp2k-qmgroup     = QM
qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod    = BLYP
qmmm-cp2k-qmcharge    = 0
qmmm-cp2k-qmmultiplicity = 1

Build the `.tpr` from the `.mdp`, then name the message when running it:

gmx_d grompp -f md.mdp -c conf.gro -p topol.top -n index.ndx -o md.tpr
CPMDC_GROMACS_PARAMS=water.params.bin \
  gmx_d mdrun -deffnm md -ntmpi 1

`PBE` works in place of `BLYP` when the deck's effective functional is
`PBE`.
The library refuses a disagreement in the functional, charge, or
multiplicity instead of replacing the deck value.

GROMACS writes zero, not the original topology charge, for every QM atom in
its generated PDB.
A generated run with charged MM atoms therefore cannot obtain the
`QM_CHARGES` needed for mechanical embedding and is refused.
Use the explicit route below for that case.

The explicit route sets `qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod = INPUT` and makes grompp take
the cpmdc settings from the file of `-qmi`:

qmmm-cp2k-active      = true
qmmm-cp2k-qmgroup     = QM
qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod    = INPUT
qmmm-cp2k-qmcharge    = 0
qmmm-cp2k-qmmultiplicity = 1

`cpmdc.gromacs.write_qmi()` writes that file; `qmi_input()` returns its text:

from cpmdc.gromacs import write_qmi

write_qmi("cpmdc.inp", "water.params.bin", embedding="MECHANICAL",
          qm_charges=[-0.834, 0.417, 0.417])

gmx_d grompp -f md.mdp -c conf.gro -p topol.top -n index.ndx -qmi cpmdc.inp -o md.tpr
gmx_d mdrun -deffnm md -ntmpi 1

The `CHARGE` and `MULTIPLICITY` of its `&DFT` section, which GROMACS reads for the
QM charge, must equal the charge and multiplicity of the `CPMDParams` message:
pass `charge=` and `multiplicity=` to `write_qmi()` for a deck that is not
neutral and singlet, and `mdrun` stops with both values when they differ.
The file of `-qmi` holds a `&CPMDC` section inside
`&FORCE_EVAL`: `PARAMS` names the `CPMDParams` message, `CELL` and `EMBEDDING` choose the cell and the QM-MM Coulomb term, `QM_CHARGES`
gives the QM atoms' classical charges, `EPSILON_R` scales the mechanical-embedding
QM-MM Coulomb term when `.mdp` sets `epsilon-r` other than 1 (because GROMACS'
CP2K module does not forward `epsilon-r` to `libcp2k`), and `QM_RANKS` sets the
ranks of an MPI GROMACS.
The reference (file:../reference/gromacs.org) lists every key and what the
library writes to `md_cp2k.out`.
An explicit `&CPMDC` section takes precedence over
`CPMDC_GROMACS_PARAMS`.

# Cap a bond across the QM boundary
A QM group that cuts a covalent bond needs no extra step with the generated
input: grompp finds each bond between a QM atom and an MM atom and writes a
`&LINK` section for it, and the library caps the bond with a hydrogen in the
QM calculation.
The `CPMDParams` message describes the QM atoms only; the hydrogens are added
to them for you, so their number does not appear in the deck.
The `CHARGE` and `MULTIPLICITY` of `&DFT` stay the charge and multiplicity of
that message when a bond is capped. The hydrogen is not counted into either
value.
`md_cp2k.out` reports `links N` on its line of atom counts.

With `qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod = INPUT` name each bond beside `&CPMDC`, by the
1-based atom numbers of the GROMACS system, QM atom first:

from cpmdc.gromacs import write_qmi

# atom 1 (QM) is bonded to atom 4 (MM)
write_qmi("cpmdc.inp", "water.params.bin", embedding="NONE", links=[(1, 4)])

`link_alpha` sets `ALPHA_IMOMM`; the library default is CP2K's 1.38.
Choose it as the ratio of the equilibrium QM-MM bond length to the QM-H bond
length of the method.

The MM atom gets its share of the force on the hydrogen, so GROMACS integrates
it as it does any other atom.
With `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` the charge of the MM atom of each cut bond leaves
the QM-MM Coulomb sum; see the reference (file:../reference/gromacs.org) for
the hydrogen position, the force shares, the virial, and what is not
implemented.

# Pressure and NPT
NPT works with a GROMACS patched as in Build (*Build).
The QM virial is the full tensor, in a cubic or triclinic box, so C-rescale,
Parrinello-Rahman, and the other barostats see the QM part of the pressure
whatever coupling type they use; the runs in the OpenCPMD runs (file:../explanation/md-engines.org)
use isotropic C-rescale and Parrinello-Rahman.

An unpatched GROMACS reports a pressure without the QM and QM-MM terms.
The reference (file:../reference/gromacs.org) gives the virial the library
returns in each cell mode, and when it reports none.

An NPT mdp adds the barostat to the QM/MM settings above, for example:

integrator       = md
tcoupl           = v-rescale
tc-grps          = System
tau-t            = 0.1
ref-t            = 300
pcoupl           = C-rescale
pcoupltype       = isotropic
tau-p            = 0.5
ref-p            = 1.0
compressibility  = 4.5e-5

Two cautions:

- with `CELL PERIODIC`, each new box is a new setup of the deck at its cutoff,
  so the plane-wave basis changes with the box.
  OpenCPMD's stress is the derivative at a fixed basis and carries the Pulay
  stress of that cutoff, so set `constantCutoff = [A, sigma, E0]` in the
  `system` section of the message for a periodic NPT run, as relax a cell at a constant cutoff (file:constant-cutoff.org)
  shows;
- with `CELL NONE` the deck's cell has to hold the QM region and its density,
  not the region's path: cpmdc centres the region in it on each step.

# Several ranks
A thread-MPI GROMACS runs
QM/MM on one rank: pass `-ntmpi 1`, because GROMACS refuses more thread-MPI ranks with QM/MM.

For more ranks, build GROMACS with
`-DGMX_MPI=ON` against the MPI that `libcpmdc_gromacs` links
(`scripts/ci/build_gromacs_cpmdc.sh` with `mpi`), and do not ask for separate
PME ranks, which GROMACS refuses with QM/MM.
Then choose `QM_RANKS` in `&CPMDC`:

- `QM_RANKS ALL`, the default, runs one cpmdc calculator on every rank of
  `mdrun`; with OpenCPMD the forces differ from a one-rank run by the order of
  its parallel sums;
- `QM_RANKS 1` runs the QM calculation on rank 0 alone and matches a one-rank
  run to 1e-10, at the SCF time of one rank.

A `libcpmdc_gromacs` built without MPI stops `mdrun` on an MPI GROMACS with the
reason.
The reference (file:../reference/gromacs.org) describes how the library
shares each step across the ranks.


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/install.org

# What gets built
A `cpmdc` build produces one shared library, `libcpmdc.so`, and a few helpers
around it.
The build has two modes, selected by the Meson option `with_cpmd`:

| Mode | Option | Evaluator behind the C ABI | `cpmdc_available()` |
|------+--------+----------------------------+---------------------|
| Default | `-Dwith_cpmd=false` | deterministic reference evaluator, no OpenCPMD | 0 |
| OpenCPMD | `-Dwith_cpmd=true -Dcpmd_root=DIR` | OpenCPMD linked from `DIR/lib/libcpmd.a` | 1 |

Both modes export the same symbols.
A third target,
`libcpmdc_stub.a`, is a link-only placeholder: every call fails and `cpmdc_available()`
returns 0.
The tests use it to check the ABI without a working evaluator.

| Artifact | Installed as | Purpose |
|----------+--------------+---------|
| `libcpmdc.so` | `lib/libcpmdc.so.MAJOR`, or an unversioned `lib/libcpmdc.so` when `with_python` is on | the C ABI from `include/cpmdc.h` |
| public headers | `include/cpmdc/cpmdc.h`, `cpmdc_features.h`, `cpmdc_export.h`, `cpmdc_restart.h` | declarations for hosts |
| `libcpmdc_restart.a` | `lib/libcpmdc_restart.a` | reader and writer for CPMD `RESTART` files |
| `cpmdc-restart` | `bin/cpmdc-restart` | command-line front end to `libcpmdc_restart` |
| pkg-config files | `cpmdc.pc`, `cpmdc-restart.pc` | compiler and linker flags |
| CMake package | `lib/cmake/cpmdc/cpmdcConfig.cmake`, `cpmdcConfigVersion.cmake` | imported target `cpmdc::cpmdc`; the version file accepts any release with the same major version |

The optional tools (`cpmdc-ipi-c`, the LAMMPS plugin, and `libcpmdc_gromacs`)
are listed with the options that build them in the
build reference (file:../reference/build-options.org).

`MAJOR` is the soversion, the first field of `version.txt`. A `with_python` build
sets no soversion, because a wheel stores no symlinks.

# Requirements
The checked-in Pixi manifest pins every build dependency.
Without Pixi, install the same set from your package manager:

| Dependency | Version in `pixi.toml` | Needed for |
|------------+------------------------+------------|
| Meson, Ninja | Meson 1.5.2 or newer, below 2; Ninja 1.11 or newer, below 2 | every build |
| Cap'n Proto (`capnp` compiler) | 1.0.2 or newer, below 2 | generating the schema readers, encoding messages |
| C and Fortran compilers | any recent GCC and gfortran | every build |
| C++ compiler and Rust (`cargo`) | Rust 1.70 or newer, below 2 | the `minimage` subproject |
| pkg-config | 2.5.1 or newer, below 3 | dependency lookup |
| CMake | 3.24 or newer | configuring: Meson reads the CMake template for `cpmdcConfigVersion.cmake` and stops when `cmake` is missing; also the `packaging` consumer build, whose CMake leg is skipped when `cmake` is not installed |
| Python 3 | 3.10 or newer, below 4 | build helpers and tests |
| ASE, pytest, i-PI | ASE 3.23 or newer, below 4; pytest 7 or newer; i-PI 3.3 or newer, below 4 | the `python-api` and `python-pytest` tests |
| cmocka | 1.1.7 or newer, below 3 | `-Dwith_tests=true` |
| MPI with Fortran bindings, BLAS and LAPACK | OpenMPI 4.1 or newer, below 6; OpenBLAS 0.3.34 or newer, below 0.4 | `-Dwith_cpmd=true` |
| FFTW3 | 3.3.11 or newer, below 4; optional | linked when OpenCPMD was configured with FFTW3 |

CI runs those two tests on ASE 3.23.0 and on the newest ASE 3 release.
`bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py run` needs ASE 3.27 for `LangevinBAOAB`.
Its `start` command draws Maxwell-Boltzmann momenta with `thermalize_momenta`
on ASE 3.29 and with `MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution` on earlier releases.

The C Cap'n Proto runtime (`c-capnproto`) is vendored in `subprojects/`.
Meson fetches three subprojects on the first `meson setup`: the shared schema
(`potentials-schema`, pinned in `subprojects/potentials-schema.wrap`),
`capnp-fortran`, and `minimage`; `-Dwith_readcon=true` adds `readcon-core`.
On a machine without network access, download them first where the network is
available:

meson subprojects download

# Build the default library
Clone the repository and run the default suite:

git clone https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/cpmdc.git
cd cpmdc
pixi run test-stub

`test-stub` configures `build/` with tests on, compiles, and runs the Meson
suite.
A healthy run reports no failures.
The same steps without Pixi:

meson setup build -Dwith_tests=true
meson compile -C build
meson test -C build --print-errorlogs

The build reference (file:../reference/build-options.org) lists every Meson
option, installed artifact, and Pixi task.

# Build against OpenCPMD
The OpenCPMD archive needs the patches in `tools/` and position-independent
code; the archive how-to (file:opencpmd-archive.org) covers that build.
With the archive in place:

export CPMD_ROOT=/path/to/opencpmd-build
meson setup build-cpmd \
  -Dwith_cpmd=true \
  -Dcpmd_root="$CPMD_ROOT" \
  -Dwith_tests=true
meson compile -C build-cpmd
export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=/path/to/PP_LIBRARY
meson test -C build-cpmd --print-errorlogs

Configuration stops when
`$CPMD_ROOT/lib/libcpmd.a` or `$CPMD_ROOT/obj/timetag.o` is missing.
The live tests run OpenCPMD, which reads the pseudopotentials from
`CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` (see the
environment reference (file:../reference/environment.org)).

The link uses the MPI Fortran dependency, OpenBLAS (or LAPACK and BLAS when
OpenBLAS is absent), FFTW3 when found, `libgfortran`, and `libquadmath`.
When OpenCPMD was built with MPI compiler wrappers, configure with the same
wrappers so both sides agree on one MPI:

CC=mpicc FC=mpif90 meson setup build-cpmd \
  -Dwith_cpmd=true -Dcpmd_root="$CPMD_ROOT"

# Install
meson setup build-install --prefix "$HOME/.local" -Dwith_tests=false
meson install -C build-install
pkg-config --modversion cpmdc

The last command prints the project version, which Meson reads from
`version.txt`.
Hosts that load the library at run time, such as `rgpot`, look for it through
`CPMDC_LIBRARY`; see the
environment reference (file:../reference/environment.org).

Installed shared libraries and plugins that need another library from the
prefix record a run path relative to their own file: `$ORIGIN` on Linux and
`@loader_path` on macOS. `libcpmdc` sets an empty install run path, because
it does not load another library from the prefix; toolchain directories
Meson already recorded, such as the one for `libgfortran`, stay.
`libcpmdc_gromacs` records `$ORIGIN` (its own directory). The LAMMPS plugin
is installed one directory deeper, in `lib/cpmdc`, and records `$ORIGIN/..`.
`cpmdc-ipi-c` records the normalised relative path from the resolved
`bindir` to the resolved `libdir`. `-Dbindir=.`, absolute `bindir` and
`libdir` under the prefix, a nested `libdir`, and a path that contains
`..` or a trailing slash still open `libcpmdc`. A layout whose relative
path cannot be stored as one run path entry fails at configure time.
Meson keeps a build-tree run path only on uninstalled binaries. After
`meson install`, an installed `.so` or `.dylib` does not point at the build
tree or at the prefix path used for that install, so the tree can be moved
and `libcpmdc_gromacs` still opens `libcpmdc`.

The installed `cpmdc.pc`, `cpmdc-restart.pc`, and `libcp2k.pc` files derive
`prefix` and `includedir` from `${pcfiledir}`, using the relative path from
the pkg-config directory to those locations. `-Dlibdir=.`, a nested
`libdir`, a `libdir` that contains `..`, and an absolute `includedir` under
the prefix stay inside the prefix. A directory that cannot be expressed as
one relative path fails at configure time.

# Install the Python package
Release tags publish wheels for Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (manylinux_2_28) and
macOS arm64 (macOS 15 or newer).
One wheel per platform serves CPython 3.10 and newer; CI tests 3.10 to 3.13.
The `ase` extra installs ASE for `cpmdc.ase`:

pip install "cpmdc[ase]"
python -c "import cpmdc; print(cpmdc.find_library())"

The second command prints the `libcpmdc` inside the installed package.
That library is the default build: the reference evaluator, without OpenCPMD and
without MPI, so `Session.available()` is false.
The wheel carries `libgfortran` and `schema/Potentials.capnp`.
A periodic cell needs no other tool: the package encodes each step as
`ForceInput` itself.
The `capnp` command is needed only to encode a `CPMDParams` text file, and
`cpmdc.find_schema()` returns the schema to encode it against.
The `test` extra adds pytest for `tests/python`.
To evaluate with OpenCPMD, build `libcpmdc` with
`-Dwith_cpmd=true` and set `CPMDC_LIBRARY` to it; the variable takes precedence
over the copy in the wheel.

On other platforms pip builds the sdist.
That needs the C, C++, and Fortran compilers, Rust (`cargo`, for the `minimage`
subproject), the `capnp` command, and network access for the Meson subprojects.
The same build from a checkout:

pip install ".[ase]"

# Build the docs
pixi run -e docs docbld

The build reference (file:../reference/build-options.org) lists the other
Pixi tasks.
The published site is cpmdc.rgoswami.me (https://cpmdc.rgoswami.me).


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/lammps.org

LAMMPS can take its energy, forces, and virial from cpmdc in process, so its
integrators, thermostats, barostats, minimizers, and output run on a cpmdc
potential energy surface.
Two routes call `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` of the C ABI (file:../reference/c-abi.org)
once per force evaluation; both pass the same numbers to LAMMPS.

| Route | LAMMPS side | Needs |
|-------+-------------+-------|
| `cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal` | rgpot's generic `fix external pf/callback` frontend | `rgpot`, the `lammps` Python module (`pip install lammps` works), `mpi4py` for more than one rank |
| `pair_style cpmdc` | a LAMMPS plugin, `cpmdcplugin.so`, loaded with `plugin load` | LAMMPS with the `PLUGIN` package and the headers it was built from; no Python |
| i-PI sockets | `fix ipi`, a client of an i-PI server | i-PI and `cpmdc-ipi`; see the socket drivers (file:socket-drivers.org) |

The plugin suits LAMMPS input scripts run by `lmp` and has the least overhead
per step (see cpmdc inside MD engines (file:../explanation/md-engines.org)).
`FixExternal` suits Python workflows and needs no compiler.  The cpmdc class is
a compatibility wrapper: it presents a `cpmdc.Session` as a Python rgpot
potential and delegates the LAMMPS protocol, unit conversion, cell, virial,
MPI gather and callback errors to `rgpot.lammps.FixExternal`.  Install rgpot
alongside cpmdc to use this route.  `rgpot.lammps` is not in a released rgpot
wheel yet; the Python tests skip, with that reason, when the import fails.
The socket route keeps cpmdc in a separate process and lets i-PI integrate;
LAMMPS then contributes forces of its own.

The LAMMPS interface reference (file:../reference/lammps.org) gives the unit
styles, the cell, and the virial both routes use.

# From Python with fix external
Define the box, the atoms, and the masses as usual, without a pair style for the
atoms cpmdc covers, then hand the `lammps` object to `FixExternal` with one
element per atom type, in type order:

from lammps import lammps

from cpmdc.lammps import FixExternal

lmp = lammps()
lmp.file("in.setup")  # units metal, box, atoms, masses
with FixExternal(lmp, "water.params.bin", "O H") as cpmdc:
    lmp.commands_string("""
        velocity all create 300 4928
        fix nve all nve
        timestep 0.00025
        thermo 10
    """)
    cpmdc.run(1000)
    print(lmp.get_thermo("pe"), cpmdc.evaluations)

`FixExternal` issues `fix cpmdc all external pf/callback 1 1` and
`fix_modify cpmdc energy yes virial yes`, so `pe` holds the cpmdc energy and
`press` includes its virial.
On a periodic OpenCPMD deck that virial carries the Pulay stress of the cutoff.
Before `fix npt` or `fix box/relax`, set `constantCutoff = [A, sigma, E0]` in
the `system` section of the message, as relax a cell at a constant cutoff (file:constant-cutoff.org)
shows; the `pair_style cpmdc` route reads the same message.
With `create=False` it attaches to a `fix external` the input already defines
under `fix_id`; that fix needs the same two `fix_modify` settings.
`close()`, or leaving the `with` block, removes the fixes it added and closes
the session.

A failed evaluation cannot raise through LAMMPS' C callback.
`FixExternal` keeps the error in `error`, returns zero forces for that step, and
a `fix halt` it adds stops LAMMPS at the end of the step.
`FixExternal.run()` then raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError` with the library's message; a
bare `lmp.command("run ...")` raises LAMMPS' halt error instead.

Any `run` or `minimize` works: `minimize` uses the cpmdc energy through
`fix_modify energy yes`.

# From an input script with pair_style cpmdc
Meson builds `cpmdcplugin.so` when a C++ compiler, MPI for C++, and the LAMMPS
headers are found.
The headers come from `-Dlammps_include=DIR`, or from the `include/lammps`
directory of an importable `lammps` Python package, which the pip wheel ships:

meson setup build -Dwith_lammps_plugin=enabled
# or, with the headers of a LAMMPS source tree:
meson setup build -Dwith_lammps_plugin=enabled -Dlammps_include="$LAMMPS_SRC/src"
meson compile -C build

`meson install` puts the plugin in `lib/cpmdc` under the prefix, with a run path
to `libcpmdc`.
Load it and select the pair style:

plugin load      /path/to/lib/cpmdc/cpmdcplugin.so
units            metal
read_data        water.data
pair_style       cpmdc water.params.bin
pair_coeff       * * O H
fix              nve all nve
timestep         0.00025
run              1000

LAMMPS also loads every `*plugin.so` in the directories of `LAMMPS_PLUGIN_PATH`
at startup.
`pair_coeff * *` takes one element symbol or atomic number per atom type.
The pair style needs no cutoff and requests no neighbor list.
A failed evaluation stops LAMMPS with `pair_style cpmdc:` and the library's
message.
A compute that asks for a per-atom energy or virial (`pe/atom`, `stress/atom`,
`centroid/stress/atom`) is refused when the run starts, because cpmdc returns
totals, see the LAMMPS interface reference (file:../reference/lammps.org).

The plugin is a C++ shared object compiled against one LAMMPS: build it with the
headers of the LAMMPS that loads it.
LAMMPS' integer sizes must match, so pass `-Dcpp_args=-DLAMMPS_BIGBIG` for a
LAMMPS built with `LAMMPS_BIGBIG`.
The plugin and LAMMPS must also share one MPI library; the pip wheel links an
MPICH-compatible `libmpi.so.12`.
The plugin links only `libcpmdc`'s public C ABI.
LAMMPS is GPL-2.0; check its terms before you distribute a plugin binary built
against its headers.

# Several MPI ranks
Under `mpirun` LAMMPS spreads the atoms over its ranks, and cpmdc still
evaluates the whole system once per step:

- World rank 0 owns the one `CPMDCSession`.
  Before it opens the session it adopts `MPI_COMM_SELF` as the calculator
  communicator, so an OpenCPMD build runs on rank 0 alone and never waits in a
  collective for ranks that do not call it.
- Each step gathers every rank's positions and atom types, by atom ID, onto rank
  0; rank 0 evaluates; the energy, the virial, and all forces go back to every
  rank, which keeps the forces of the atoms it owns.
- The other ranks wait during the evaluation, so extra ranks speed up only
  LAMMPS' own work.
  The traffic per step is `O(N)` doubles.
- Both routes order a step by increasing atom ID. Positive, unique IDs may
  have gaps, so `delete_atoms ... compress no` and `fix evaporate` work
  without a `reset_atoms id` pass.
- A step with a new elemental composition opens a new session.

`FixExternal` needs `mpi4py` for this, and `comm=` when the `lammps` object was
created on a communicator other than `MPI.COMM_WORLD`.
The plugin uses LAMMPS' own `world` communicator.
Running one cpmdc evaluation on several ranks under the same LAMMPS is not part
of either route.

# The harness on the reference well and on OpenCPMD
`tests/python/test_lammps.py` is the harness for both routes.
It compares each LAMMPS step with `CPMDCCalculator` and runs short NVE and NPT
trajectories, plus an `mpiexec -n 1` launch and an `mpiexec -n 2` launch of the
same step.
Which tests it collects depends on the library `CPMDC_LIBRARY` names.
The `opencpmd` fixture reads `cpmdc_available()`, which is 1 only when that
library is linked to OpenCPMD.
A test that holds for one library is marked `cpmd_backend` with the reason.
Collection keeps that test only when the bit matches, and the `cpmd_backend`
fixture then supplies the name, so the other library does not collect it and a
run reports no skips from it.

Both libraries collect every comparison of one message between LAMMPS and ASE
and the two-rank check on the two waters.

The reference well is a quadratic energy anchored at the origin.
It collects four tests that use that shape:

- An unwrapped path held to the tolerances of the single steps (forces to
  rtol 1e-10), since the well's forces are linear in the coordinates.
- An NVE run of 800 steps of 0.25 fs through the box corner, with etotal
  within 2e-3 of the swing of pe, the fall into the well.
- An NPT run toward -20000 bar, near the well's own stress, with econserve
  within 5e-3 of that swing.
- A central difference of the energy over strains of 1e-5 on the triclinic
  cell, within 1e-6 of the largest virial component.

OpenCPMD collects the constant-cutoff step and a plane-wave counterpart of each.
The finite differences and trajectories run the periodic water deck at an
orbital threshold of 1e-7 instead of its 1e-5, on the `FixExternal` route only;
the single steps show that both routes pass the same numbers.

| Test | What it measures | Measured | Bound |
|------+------------------+----------+-------|
| `test_positions_are_unwrapped_on_plane_waves` | forces after the wrap and unwrap against ASE | 1.3e-11 eV/Angstrom | 1e-9 eV/Angstrom |
| `test_forces_are_the_energy_gradient` | central difference of the energy, 1e-3 Angstrom steps, against the forces | 2.6e-5 eV/Angstrom | 1e-4 eV/Angstrom |
| `test_virial_is_the_strain_derivative_of_one_basis` | strains of 1e-5 of the plain deck against its virial, over the largest component | 2.5e-7 | 1e-6 |
| `test_virial_is_the_strain_derivative_in_place` | Richardson extrapolation of strains of 2.5e-3 and 5e-3 on one held basis | 4.8e-6 | 5e-5 |
| `test_constant_cutoff_virial_is_the_strain_derivative` | new constant-cutoff setups at strains of 1e-4, and of 5e-3 | 6.9e-7, 2.0e-2 | 1e-5, 4e-2 |
| `test_nve_energy_error_falls_with_the_timestep_squared` | etotal drift over 50 fs; RMS at 0.5 fs over RMS at 0.25 fs | 8.5e-5 eV; 4.0 | 5e-4 eV; 3 to 5 |
| `test_npt_conserves_the_extended_energy_at_a_constant_cutoff` | iso NPT toward 0 bar over 50 fs: range of the volume; departure of econserve over the swing of pe | 3.7%; 6.2e-3 | above 1%; 1e-2 |

The plain-deck virial is the derivative of the energy at a fixed set of plane
waves.
Each strained cell is a new setup at the deck's 40 Ry, so a central difference
holds the basis only while no plane wave crosses that sphere: on the triclinic
cell a strain of 1e-5 keeps all of them, and at 3e-5 the difference misses by
1.8 times the largest component.
At the deck's own orbital threshold the 1e-5 difference misses by 1.1e-3, the
SCF error over the step; at 1e-7 it meets the virial to 2.5e-7.
With `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE=0.01` a constant-cutoff deck keeps the plane waves of
its setup cell through the strain, and the misses at 5e-3 and 2.5e-3, 1.3e-3
and 3.2e-4, fall as the square of the step.

At 0.25 fs the Verlet fluctuation of etotal on the two waters is 8.6e-4 eV RMS,
above the 8e-4 eV that 2e-3 of their 0.4 eV swing of pe allows, so the
reference NVE bound belongs to the well.
At the deck's threshold of 1e-5, etotal also falls at 2.9e-2 eV/ps, 17 times
the 1.7e-3 eV/ps at 1e-7; over 800 steps, 200 fs, that adds 5.7e-3 eV.

The NPT run uses the constant-cutoff deck with `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE=0.05`,
since a plain deck sets up a new basis whenever the cell moves.
Its target, 0 bar, lies near the -135 bar the two waters average over the run.
The pressure at the first step, +18 kbar, is the virial of the stretched O-H
bonds, which swings by about 15 kbar each vibration; as the target it
compressed the cube from 729 to 202 Angstrom^3 in 50 fs.
NVE on the same deck leaves its start by 5.9e-3 of the swing of pe, so the
barostat adds no visible error to econserve.

`test_reference_cell_holds_the_basis` is the plain deck with `REFERENCE CELL`
and `MESH` at the triclinic cell, which keeps its 10347 plane waves and its
72 72 80 mesh through the strain.
It is marked `xfail(strict=True)`: the strain difference is +3.28 eV where the
virial is -32.42 eV (xx), at strains of 1e-5 and 5e-3 alike.
A cold setup with `REFERENCE CELL` builds the G vectors from the reference
lattice rather than the strained cell, which looks like a library bug.

Build LAMMPS `stable_22Jul2025` as a shared library with MPI, exceptions,
`PKG_PYTHON`, and `PKG_PLUGIN`, against the same Open MPI that cpmdc uses.
The installed include directory is missing headers the plugin includes
(`json_fwd.h`, `version.h`, `lammpsplugin.h`), so point `-Dlammps_include` at
that LAMMPS source `src` directory.
Build the OpenCPMD archive with `scripts/ci/build_opencpmd.sh`, which applies
the patches the harness needs, including the optional constant-cutoff and PCG
patches.
`tools/rebuild_opencpmd_embed.sh`, `tools/rebuild_opencpmd_omp_info.sh`,
`tools/rebuild_opencpmd_pcg_step.sh`, and
`tools/rebuild_opencpmd_constant_cutoff.sh` rebuild those members when the
tree was already compiled.
Then point meson at that archive and at the LAMMPS headers, and run the
harness with the pseudopotentials the deck names:

# OpenCPMD library, plugin, and the LAMMPS harness.
meson setup build-cpmd -Dwith_cpmd=true -Dcpmd_root="$CPMD_ROOT" \
  -Dwith_lammps_plugin=enabled -Dlammps_include="$LAMMPS_SRC/src"
meson compile -C build-cpmd
CPMDC_LIBRARY=build-cpmd/libcpmdc.so \
  CPMDC_LAMMPS_PLUGIN=build-cpmd/cpmdcplugin.so \
  CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR="$CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR" \
  python3 -m pytest tests/python/test_lammps.py

The `lammps` Python module has to be the one built from that same LAMMPS, on
`PYTHONPATH`.
Unset `CPMDC_LIBRARY` (the tests then load `build/libcpmdc.so`) to run the
reference well instead.
With the plugin present, the pseudopotentials present for OpenCPMD, and
`mpiexec` able to start two ranks, each run collects only its own tests and
reports zero skips.


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/mpi.org

# Goal
Run a host that embeds `cpmdc` on several MPI (Message Passing Interface) ranks,
so that CPMD parallelises each self-consistent field (SCF) calculation over the
ranks, and keep every rank's view of the result consistent.
This page needs an OpenCPMD build of `cpmdc`; the default build runs the
reference evaluator on each rank independently.

# The rules
1. Start every rank of the host under `mpirun`.
   CPMD initialises MPI on the first evaluation when the host has not.
2. Every rank makes the same `cpmdc` calls with the same messages in the same
   order.
   An evaluation is collective over the ranks of its calculator.
3. Take the energy and forces from the first rank of each calculator, CPMD's
   parent rank, and broadcast them to the other ranks.
   The other ranks return from the call with values of their own, unless
   `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` is set, as the section on sharing the parent's
   result describes.
   In a 4-rank water single point all four printed the parent's energy and
   forces, but in a 4-rank dimer search, where every rank also ran the host's
   optimizer, rank 1 took 3 steps on different curvatures while rank 0 took 5,
   and only rank 0's results matched an independent `cpmd.x` run.
4. Keep one `CPMDCSession` per calculator.
5. Call `MPI_Finalize` on every rank before the host exits.
   `cpmdc_finalize()` does not finalize MPI.

# One calculator over all ranks
Without further setup, CPMD uses `MPI_COMM_WORLD`, so all ranks form one
calculator:

export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=/path/to/pseudopotentials
mpirun -np 16 ./host params.bin step.bin

Rank 0 of `MPI_COMM_WORLD` is then CPMD's parent rank.

# Several calculators in one job
`cpmdc_bind_calculator(ranks_per_calc)` splits `MPI_COMM_WORLD` into groups of
`ranks_per_calc` consecutive ranks.
Each group becomes one CPMD calculator with its own communicator and its own
wavefunction, running the same deck.
Call it on every rank, before the first evaluation:

#include <cpmdc.h>
#include <mpi.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
  int group = cpmdc_bind_calculator(4); /* 16 ranks -> 4 calculators */
  if (group < 0) {
    /* world size not a multiple of 4, or no CPMD backend */
    MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);
  }
  int world_rank = 0;
  MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &world_rank);
  int is_parent = (world_rank % 4) == 0;

  /* group 0 evaluates image 0, group 1 image 1, ... */
  /* ... create one session, evaluate, share the parent's result ... */

  cpmdc_finalize();
  MPI_Finalize();
  return 0;
}

## How the ranks are divided
`ranks_per_calc` is the number of ranks in each group.
The world size must be a multiple of it.
`cpmdc` makes no group of a different size: there is no remainder group and no
smaller last group.
A world size that is not a multiple, such as 6 ranks with `ranks_per_calc` 4, or
a `ranks_per_calc` above the world size, is refused on every rank and nothing is
split.

The groups are consecutive blocks of world ranks.
Group `g` holds world ranks `g * ranks_per_calc` to
`(g + 1) * ranks_per_calc - 1`, and there are `world_size / ranks_per_calc`
groups.
With 16 ranks and `ranks_per_calc` 4, group 0 is ranks 0 to 3, group 1 is ranks
4 to 7, and so on.
A rank's group index is `world_rank / ranks_per_calc`, with integer division,
and its rank inside the group is `world_rank % ranks_per_calc`.
The group's first rank, world rank `group * ranks_per_calc`, is its parent rank.

| Argument or result | Meaning |
|--------------------+---------|
| `ranks_per_calc > 0` | ranks per calculator; the world size must be a multiple of it |
| `ranks_per_calc <= 0` | the world size is used: one calculator over every rank |
| return value `>= 0` | index of this rank's calculator: `world_rank / ranks_per_calc`, or 0 when `ranks_per_calc <= 0` |
| return value `-1` | the world size is not a multiple of `ranks_per_calc`, `MPI_Comm_split` returned an error, or the library has no CPMD backend (the default build and the stub) |

A call that returns -1 for the world size splits nothing, and a later call with
a valid value can still split.
`cpmdc_last_error()` gives the reason.

## Calls after the first
The first call that is not refused splits `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
A later call does not split again, also when the communicator in use came from
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm` instead of an earlier bind.
It still checks its own `ranks_per_calc` as above, and it returns
`world_rank / ranks_per_calc` for that value.
That is the index of the group in use only when the value is the same as the
one that made the split.
A value that does not divide the world size, or is above it, returns -1 on
every rank, as it does on the first call, and the split already in use stays as
it was.

## MPI start
On an OpenCPMD build, `cpmdc_bind_calculator` calls `MPI_Init` when MPI is not
running, before it looks at `ranks_per_calc`, so the call starts MPI even when
it then refuses the value.
`cpmdc` starts MPI only in OpenCPMD builds.
The default build, which runs the reference evaluator, and the link stub never
call `MPI_Init`.
In those builds `cpmdc_bind_calculator` returns -1 without calling MPI, and
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm` returns -1 while MPI is not running, so the host
has to start MPI itself.
`cpmdc` remembers the split in `embed_calculator_bound`.
`mp_start` assigns `mp_comm_world` only when CPMD itself calls `MPI_Init`, and
`cpmdc_bind_calculator` has already initialised MPI and stored the calculator
communicator by the time setup reaches `mp_start`.

# A communicator the host already split
A host that has already split its ranks passes that communicator to
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm(comm, nbytes, ranks_per_calc)`.
rgpot (https://rgpot.rgoswami.me) does this when it binds calculator groups.
Its MPI contract is the
rgpot MPI reference (https://rgpot.rgoswami.me/reference/mpi.html), and the
messages those hosts share are the ones in the
cpmdc overview (file:../index.org).
`nbytes` is `sizeof(MPI_Comm)`.
The call is collective on `comm`.
It reads rank and size from `comm`.
It does not call `MPI_Init` or `MPI_Comm_split`.
The size check uses `comm`.

When `ranks_per_calc` is greater than zero, the adopted size must equal it.
A different size returns -1, and `cpmdc_last_error()` names both numbers.
Zero or less skips that check.
The same positive `ranks_per_calc` on every rank gives every group the same
size, and the calculator indices are then unique.
The group must be one aligned block of `size` consecutive world ranks, starting
at a multiple of `size`.
The calculator index is the lowest world rank in that block, divided by `size`.
Any other layout returns -1 on every rank of the group, and `cpmdc_last_error()`
says the communicator is not an aligned block.
Reversing the key order inside an aligned block does not change the index.
A striped split is refused: world ranks 0 and 2 in one group of size 2, and
ranks 1 and 3 in the other, would otherwise both receive index 0.

The handle is borrowed.
The call does not use `MPI_Comm_dup`.
It stores the caller's communicator, and an OpenCPMD build also stores it in
`mp_comm_world`.
The caller keeps ownership and must not free the communicator until the last
session is destroyed or a later adopt replaces it.
An adopt after `cpmdc_bind_calculator` replaces the communicator that call
split, and the caller of bind cannot free that one.

`cpmdc_adopted_comm` copies the stored handle back to the caller.
`cpmdc_bind_calculator` remains the split for a host that has not split.
That split still runs once per process.

A later adopt replaces the communicator when no live `CPMDCSession` has started
an evaluation.
A session that was created but has not evaluated does not block it. rgpot
creates its session before it binds calculator groups, and relies on this.
To replace the communicator after an evaluation, destroy every session first.
If any rank of the group has a live session that has evaluated, every rank
returns -1, `cpmdc_last_error()` says a session has evaluated, and the stored
communicator stays as it was.
That refusal is the same collective as the index, so one rank does not return
while another waits.
The index is the same rule for 1 group of 4 ranks, 2 groups of 2, and 4 groups
of 1.

# Share the parent's result
The host owns the broadcast.
With one calculator over the whole world, broadcast from world rank 0:

double buf[1 + 3 * N_ATOMS];
if (world_rank == 0) {
  buf[0] = result.energy_h;
  memcpy(buf + 1, forces, sizeof(double) * 3 * N_ATOMS);
}
MPI_Bcast(buf, 1 + 3 * N_ATOMS, MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);

With several calculators, each group's parent broadcasts inside its group, and a
host that needs every group's result on every rank broadcasts once per group
over `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.
An optimizer that runs on every rank must step from the broadcast values; ranks
that step from their own copies drift apart after the first step.

Inside one calculator, `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` does this broadcast in the
library, so every rank of the calculator returns the parent's energy and forces:

mpirun -np 16 -x CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1 ./host params.bin step.bin

`-x` is the Open MPI flag that exports a variable to every rank.
After an evaluation, `cpmdc_last_rank_spread()` reports the largest energy and
gradient difference from the parent before the broadcast, and the rank count:

CPMDCRankSpread spread;
if (cpmdc_last_rank_spread(&spread) == 0 && world_rank == 0)
  printf("%d ranks, dE %.3g Ha, dG %.3g Ha/Bohr\n", spread.ranks,
         spread.energy_h, spread.gradient_h_bohr);

Both differences are 0 when the ranks agreed bit for bit.

# One session per calculator
The OpenCPMD module state and the stored orbitals belong to the process, not to
a `CPMDCSession`.
A second session keeps those orbitals when its functional, deck, cutoff, cell,
charge, multiplicity, and elemental composition match.
A different method or composition drops them on the next evaluation.
Run independent calculations, such as the images of a nudged elastic band, on
separate calculators, one session each.

# Finalize MPI
CPMD calls
`MPI_Init` during its setup, and nothing in `cpmdc` calls `MPI_Finalize`.
Open MPI 5 treats a rank that exits without `MPI_Finalize` as an abnormal
termination and kills the ranks still running; `mpirun` then reports a rank
"exiting improperly" and lists a missing finalize among the reasons.
Call `MPI_Finalize` on every rank, after `cpmdc_finalize()`, as the example
above does.
When the host cannot restructure its exit path, register a handler with `atexit`
that calls `MPI_Finalize` when `MPI_Initialized` reports true and
`MPI_Finalized` reports false.

# Threads
CPMD also runs OpenMP threads inside each rank when OpenCPMD was built with
`-omp`.
Set `OMP_NUM_THREADS` per rank so that ranks times threads matches the cores the
job holds.


## File: docs/orgmode/howto/opencpmd-archive.org

# Goal
Produce an OpenCPMD build tree whose `lib/libcpmd.a` can be linked into the
shared `libcpmdc.so` and evaluated repeatedly from one host process.
A stock OpenCPMD archive does not work inside a host: `libcpmdc` imports
routines that only the patches add, the shared link stops on code built without
`-fPIC`, and the unpatched SCF driver drops the forces and the orbitals that
`cpmdc` reads after each call.
The patches in `tools/` and one compiler flag fix those.
`opencpmd_c_mem_addrs.patch` makes `cGetMemAddrs` return the address as `size_t`.
GCC 14 rejects the stock return of a pointer from that function.
`cuda_get_address` stores the `size_t` that function returns.

# Patches

| Patch | File patched | Without it |
|-------+--------------+------------|
| `opencpmd_embed_rinitwf.patch` | `src/rinitwf_driver.mod.F90` | a warm call still builds the wavefunction guess and then discards it |
| `opencpmd_embed_geometry.patch` | `src/embed_ctrl.mod.F90`, `src/initrun_driver.mod.F90`, `src/SOURCES` | `initrun` still writes `GEOMETRY` after `embed_set_write_files(.FALSE.)`, and `rwfopt` has no `embed_ctrl` to read |
| `opencpmd_embed_rwfopt.patch` | `src/rwfopt_utils.mod.F90` | `rwfopt` deallocates `fion` on return and starts every SCF from a fresh guess, and `cpmd_embed_c_api.F90` does not compile |
| `opencpmd_converged_state.patch` | `src/updwf_utils.mod.F90` | the optimiser applies one more update after convergence, so the saved orbitals no longer match the reported energy and forces; steepest descent with `iproj <= 1` also needs its `gemax` reset before the convergence check |
| `opencpmd_kpoints_inputfile.patch` | `src/rkpnt_utils.mod.F90` | the k-point report reads the host's `argv[1]` as the input file name and stops with `STOP 12345` when it is missing or longer than 80 characters |
| `opencpmd_stopgm_return.patch` | `src/error_handling.mod.F90` | a CPMD stop inside an evaluation takes the `my_stopall` path, which OpenCPMD writes to end the run |
| `opencpmd_tistopgm.patch` | `src/timer.mod.F90` | `tistopgm` indexes `trace_depth` before `tistart`, while the depth is still `HUGE(0)`, and the process faults before `LocalError` |
| `opencpmd_c_mem_addrs.patch` | `src/c_mem_utils.c` | `cGetMemAddrs` returns a `size_t` pointer, and GCC 14 stops on that conversion |
| `opencpmd_embed_teardown.patch` | `src/embed_teardown.mod.F90`, `src/embed_ctrl.mod.F90`, `src/SOURCES`, and 34 modules with first-call state | a second setup in one process, after a basis change or a `stopgm`, stops in `ratom` with `allocation problem` or faults, because the arrays of the first setup are still allocated |
| `opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch` | `src/embed_ctrl.mod.F90`, `src/control_test_utils.mod.F90`, `src/rwfopt_utils.mod.F90` | `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` in the deck is dropped with a warning, and `libcpmdc` does not link, because it reads `embed_extrapolation_used` |
| `opencpmd_embed_dipole.patch` | `src/wfopts_utils.mod.F90`, `src/ddipo_utils.mod.F90` | the in-process wavefunction optimisation never calls `ddipo`, so `ddip%pdipole` is stale and no dipole belongs to the current geometry; `ddipo_embed` is the new entry point, and `ddipo` keeps its argument list |
| `opencpmd_omp_info.patch` | `src/rggen_utils.mod.F90` | a calculator that spans nodes with unequal numbers of ranks calls `MPI_Allreduce` with different counts in the report and can stop before the first electronic iteration |
| `opencpmd_pcg_step.patch` (optional) | `src/pcgrad_driver.mod.F90` | the PCG line minimisation can suppress its interpolated step for strict orbital targets; see the optimiser how-to (file:wavefunction-optimiser.org) |
| `opencpmd_constant_cutoff_precon.patch` (optional) | `src/hesele_utils.mod.F90` | with `CONSTANT CUTOFF` the ODIIS preconditioner misses the penalty on plane waves above E0, ODIIS stops at its step limit, and `cpmdc` falls back to PCG: a water stress call at 60 Ry took 42.5 s instead of 7.1 s; see relaxing a cell at a constant cutoff (file:constant-cutoff.org) |
| `opencpmd_atomwf_kpts_ortho.patch` | `src/atomwf_utils.mod.F90`, `src/gsortho_utils.mod.F90` | k-point atomic wavefunction initialization with randomized extra states overflows `zmatat` because `gs_ortho_c` passes `2*np*n0` to `mp_sum` on a `COMPLEX(real_8)` array and `atomwf` passes `zmatat(atwp%nattot, atwp%nattot)` instead of sizing the orthogonalization scratch to `(nleft, MAX(atwp%nattot, nleft))` |

The loops below apply every patch but the optional
`pcg_step` and `constant_cutoff_precon`; `scripts/ci/build_opencpmd.sh` applies
them too.
After that patch, rebuild `hesele` and its member of `lib/libcpmd.a`.
`tools/rebuild_opencpmd_constant_cutoff.sh` does both.
Its one argument is the root of the OpenCPMD tree.

How the OpenCPMD patches work (file:../explanation/opencpmd-patches.org)
explains what each patch changes inside CPMD and why `libcpmdc` needs it.

`tests/test_opencpmd_patch_integrity.py` checks that the patches are portable
unified diffs against the files named above.
Apply `opencpmd_embed_rinitwf.patch` before the rwfopt patch.
`rwfopt` reads `embed_have_orbitals` from `rinitwf_driver`.
Apply `opencpmd_embed_geometry.patch` before that rwfopt patch as well: `rwfopt`
reads `embed_ctrl`.
The rwfopt, converged-state, k-point, stop, and timer patches are the commits on OpenCPMD pull request 9 (https://github.com/OpenCPMD/CPMD/pull/9)
(branch `embedding-hooks`, `43cf4e7`) and apply in sequence to OpenCPMD commit
`062582b`.
Apply `opencpmd_c_mem_addrs.patch` with them.
Apply `opencpmd_embed_teardown.patch` after those: it adds to the
`embed_ctrl` of the geometry patch and calls `embed_reset_warm_orbitals` from
the rwfopt patch.
Apply `opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch` after the teardown patch, whose lines
in `embed_ctrl` it follows.
Apply `opencpmd_embed_dipole.patch` after it.

# Build a patched tree
Start from an OpenCPMD source checkout and apply the patches before the first
build:

git clone https://github.com/OpenCPMD/CPMD.git opencpmd
cd opencpmd
git checkout 062582b7cfd832d36f88f504cd08e4ead42eb404
for p in embed_rinitwf embed_geometry embed_rwfopt converged_state \
         kpoints_inputfile stopgm_return tistopgm c_mem_addrs \
         embed_teardown embed_extrapolate embed_dipole omp_info \
         atomwf_kpts_ortho; do
  patch -p1 < /path/to/cpmdc/tools/opencpmd_$p.patch
done

The OpenCPMD sample `LINUX-X86_64-GFORTRAN-MPI` sets `LIBS` to one person's
library path.
Copying that file and adding `-fPIC` leaves the path in the build.
`cpmdc` ships `tools/LINUX-X86_64-GFORTRAN-MPI-PIC` for the command below.
It calls `mpif90` and `gcc` from `PATH`, adds `-fPIC` and `-ffp-contract=off` to
`FFLAGS` and `CFLAGS`, and sets `LIBS` to `-lopenblas`.
The aarch64 file is `tools/LINUX-AARCH64-GFORTRAN-MPI-PIC`.
The section Building OpenCPMD for mixed clusters below says when to use each
file.
When `mpif90` accepts it, `FFLAGS` also gains `-fallow-argument-mismatch`.
`mp_bcast_byte` broadcasts the bytes of its first argument, and one procedure
calls it with several derived types. gfortran 10 and later stop on those calls
without the flag.
That OpenBLAS build has to export the LAPACK symbols.
`libcpmdc` is a shared library; a member of `libcpmd.a` compiled without `-fPIC`
fails the link with a `R_X86_64_PC32` relocation error.
Copy the shipped file into the clone, then configure and build:

cp /path/to/cpmdc/tools/LINUX-X86_64-GFORTRAN-MPI-PIC configure/
./configure.sh -DEST=/path/to/opencpmd-build LINUX-X86_64-GFORTRAN-MPI-PIC
make -C /path/to/opencpmd-build -j 8
ls /path/to/opencpmd-build/lib/libcpmd.a /path/to/opencpmd-build/obj/timetag.o

`/path/to/opencpmd-build` is the `cpmd_root` passed to Meson.
The `cpmdc` build reads `lib/libcpmd.a`, the module files in `obj/`, and the
headers in `src/`.

# Patch a tree that is already built
When the tree was built before the patches were applied, patch the source and
rebuild only the affected members:

cd /path/to/opencpmd-source
for p in embed_rinitwf embed_geometry embed_rwfopt converged_state \
         kpoints_inputfile stopgm_return tistopgm c_mem_addrs \
         embed_teardown embed_extrapolate embed_dipole omp_info \
         atomwf_kpts_ortho; do
  patch -p1 < /path/to/cpmdc/tools/opencpmd_$p.patch
done
/path/to/cpmdc/tools/rebuild_opencpmd_embed.sh /path/to/opencpmd-build
/path/to/cpmdc/tools/rebuild_opencpmd_omp_info.sh /path/to/opencpmd-build

`rebuild_opencpmd_embed.sh` recompiles the object of the embedding patch,
`error_handling.mod.o`, `embed_ctrl.mod.o`, `control_test_utils.mod.o`,
`rinitwf_driver.mod.o`, `initrun_driver.mod.o`,
`rwfopt_utils.mod.o`, `ddipo_utils.mod.o`, `wfopts_utils.mod.o`,
`updwf_utils.mod.o`,
`rkpnt_utils.mod.o`, `timer.mod.o`, `c_mem_utils.o`,
`gsortho_utils.mod.o`, `atomwf_utils.mod.o`,
the 34 modules of the teardown patch, and `embed_teardown.mod.o`
after them, and `scex_utils.mod.o` for the module order, with one Make job, then
replaces those members with `ar r` and runs `ranlib`.
`tests/test_opencpmd_embed_objects.py` fails when a source file in
`tools/opencpmd_*.patch` has no object in that list or in the dedicated
rebuild scripts.
It runs one job because gfortran stores a copy of
`Scex_t` inside `rwfopt_utils.mod`: a parallel rebuild can leave the two module
files naming different components.
It calls `ar` directly because the generated Makefile sets `AR` without an
operation letter, so its archive rule does not replace members.
`MAKE` and `AR` in the environment override the programs it runs.
