| `release-assert`, `version-sync`, `towncrier-draft`, `release-cog-dry` | default | release metadata checks, and `version.txt` copies |
| `mkrst` | `docs` | export `docs/orgmode` to `docs/source` RST |
| `doxybuild` | `docs` | Doxygen XML and Doxyrest pages for the public headers |
| `sphinxbld`, `docbld` | `docs` | `mkrst`, `doxybuild`, then the Sphinx HTML site in `docs/build` |

Run a docs task with `pixi run -e docs docbld`.

One sanitizer CI failure was traced to libfabric's memhooks monitor replacing
AddressSanitizer's `mprotect` interceptor during `MPI_Init`.  In a separate
Open MPI 5 reproduction, `FI_MR_CACHE_MONITOR=disabled` alone still ended in
SIGILL, while `--mca memory ^patcher` prevented it.  Selecting a non-UCX
transport also prevented that reproduction.  The sanitize job disables the
observed libfabric path, and `tests/run_mpi_test.py` passes the Open MPI memory
and transport exclusions in both the environment and launcher arguments.

# Meson test parallelism and BLAS threads
The default test setup (`blasthreads`) sets `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, and `MKL_NUM_THREADS` to `1` so parallel `meson test`
workers do not each spawn a full OpenBLAS pool. Meson applies those values to
every test child; exports of the same names in the shell that runs `meson test`
are not passed through. To force different caps, set them on the `env:` keyword
of the individual test or run the executable outside Meson.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/c-abi.org

The public C ABI (application binary interface) of `libcpmdc` is declared in
`include/cpmdc.h` and `include/cpmdc_features.h`, with the export mark in `include/cpmdc_export.h`.
`include/cpmdc_restart.h` declares the separate `libcpmdc_restart` (see RESTART file library (*RESTART file library)).
`include/cpmdc_pwscale.h` declares the opt-in plane-wave scaffold, which is not part of this ABI; its contract is in the plane-wave scaffold reference (file:pwscale.org).
Installed headers live under `include/cpmdc/`; include them as
`#include <cpmdc.h>` with the flags of `pkg-config --cflags cpmdc`.
Every function has C linkage, and the header compiles as C and as C++.
`libcpmdc` exports those 52 functions and no other symbol; the exported symbols
section below gives the mechanism.
`schema/inventory/surface_map_abi.txt` records them; it is generated from the
built library, and the `c-abi-inventory` test fails when the headers, the
library, and the file disagree (see the surface map (file:surface-map.org)).
The header records the ABI generation once, as `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION`; no function
carries its own `@since` generation.
The header comments, which the documentation site renders as the generated API
pages, carry the declarations; this page adds the units, the return conventions,
and the behaviour that the implementation in `src/cpmdc.c` gives each call.
The API contracts (file:contracts.org) page lists every function, type, and constant with its units, layout, ownership, thread and MPI behaviour, errors, and defaults; the `reference-audit` test keeps it in step with the headers.

# Exported symbols
Every function of `cpmdc.h` and `cpmdc_features.h` is declared with `CPMDC_API`
from
`include/cpmdc_export.h`, and `libcpmdc` is compiled with hidden visibility (Meson `gnu_symbol_visibility: 'hidden'`).
A function without the mark stays inside the library.

| Compiler and macro | `CPMDC_API` |
|--------------------+-------------|
| GCC or Clang | `__attribute__((visibility("default")))` |
| Windows, `CPMDC_BUILDING_LIBRARY` defined | `__declspec(dllexport)` |
| Windows, `CPMDC_STATIC` defined | empty |
| Windows, neither | `__declspec(dllimport)` |

The library build defines `CPMDC_BUILDING_LIBRARY`.
A host that links the shared library defines neither macro.
Code that compiles the cpmdc sources or links a static archive defines
`CPMDC_STATIC`, as every in-tree test does.

gfortran does not apply `-fvisibility` to Fortran procedures, so the `BIND(C)`
glue in `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90` and `src/cpmdc_embed_apply_params.f90` would
still be exported, as would the symbols of the static archives linked into the
library (`c-capnproto`, `capnp-fortran`, `minimage`, and `libcpmd.a`).
The build therefore also links with an export list that
`scripts/abi_inventory.py` writes from the same `CPMDC_API` declarations: a
version script with `local: *` for an ELF linker (`ld.bfd`, `gold`, `lld`,
`mold`), and `-exported_symbols_list` for `ld64` on macOS.
The list adds no symbol the attribute does not mark: a hidden symbol stays
hidden whatever the list says.
The version script names no version node, so the exported names carry no symbol
version.

An ELF version script and an ld64 export list do not treat a missing literal
name the same way.
A `global:` pattern exports a symbol when the link defines it, and does not
require the symbol to exist.
`-exported_symbols_list` requires every literal name to be defined, reporting
an absent literal as an undefined symbol, while a wildcard entry matches only
symbols the link defines.
Every MPI Fortran sentinel is therefore written as a wildcard pattern so neither
Open MPI nor MPICH leaves required undefined names for the other implementation.
The version script always names them; the macOS list adds them when OpenCPMD is
linked, and the serial macOS library lists the literal public `cpmdc_`
functions alone.

Releases up to and including 0.4.0 also export 56 internal functions with the
`cpmdc_` prefix: the glue between `src/cpmdc.c`, the parameter renderer, and the
Fortran embed.
No installed header declared them, so they were never part of the ABI, and
hiding them changes no public function, `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION`, or the soversion.
The tests that call them link a static archive of the library sources or the
sources directly; the Python package loads only public functions.

# Conventions

| Item | Convention |
|------+------------|
| Parameter buffers | unpacked flat Cap'n Proto messages: `CPMDParams`, `PotentialConfig`, or `ForceInput` from `schema/Potentials.capnp`; the header does not redefine their fields as a C struct |
| Positions in array calls | Angstrom, `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major (`x0 y0 z0 x1 ...`) |
| Energy in `CPMDCResult` | Hartree |
| Gradient and force arrays | Hartree/Bohr; forces are the negative gradient |
| `PotentialResult` values | energy in `ForceInput.energyUnit`, forces in `energyUnit` per `lengthUnit`, stress in `energyUnit` per `lengthUnit` cubed |
| `int` calls | 0 on success, -1 on failure; `cpmdc_bind_calculator` returns the calculator index (0 or more) instead of 0 |
| `CPMDCResult` calls | `ok` non-zero on success; `message` holds `"ok"` or the reason |
| pointer returns | `NULL` on failure (`cpmdc_session_create`, `cpmdc_session_create_from_config`) or when not found (`cpmdc_feature_find`) |
| `size_t` returns | 0 on failure (`cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input`) |
| failure text | `cpmdc_last_error()`, per thread, for the calls listed under Library status (*Library status); snapshot getters do not write it |
| names | functions `cpmdc_` and snake case, types `CPMDC` and CamelCase, macros and enum constants `CPMDC_` and upper case |
| argument order | session, atom count, positions, atomic numbers, cell, then the outputs; a size follows the buffer it measures |
| unit suffixes | `_ang` Angstrom, `_bohr` Bohr, `_h` Hartree, `_h_bohr` Hartree/Bohr, `_bytes` bytes |
| Ownership | the caller owns every buffer it passes; the library copies what it keeps |
| Threads | one process-wide CPMD state; serialize calls into one library instance |

The bytes can come from pycapnp, a memory-mapped file, rgpot, or any other
Cap'n Proto binding that writes the standard flat stream format.
`ForceInput` unit strings are matched without regard to case.
Length: `angstrom`, `angstroms`, `a`, `aa`, `bohr`, `au`, `a.u.`, `atomic`,
`nm`, `nanometer`.
Energy: `hartree`, `ha`, `au`, `a.u.`, `ev`, `electronvolt`, `ry`, `rydberg`,
`kj/mol`, `kjmol`, `kcal/mol`, `kcalmol`.
The schema defaults are `angstrom` and `eV`; a unit set to the empty string
reads as `angstrom` or `hartree`.
`ForceInput.box` is empty or nine values, a row-major 3 by 3 cell in
`lengthUnit`, one lattice vector per row.
The caller's box is the cell.
A non-zero `ForceInput.box` replaces every `CELL` line of `&SYSTEM` and its
`SYMMETRY`: a cubic deck and a cubic box keep `SYMMETRY 1`, another orthorhombic
box gets `SYMMETRY 8` and `CELL a b/a c/a`, and a box with off-diagonal
components gets `CELL VECTORS` without `SYMMETRY`, which CPMD refuses beside it.
An isolated deck (`SYMMETRY 0`, the default deck) keeps `SYMMETRY 0` and takes
only an orthorhombic box with positive diagonal entries; a box with
off-diagonal entries fails with
`an isolated deck (SYMMETRY 0) needs an orthorhombic box`,
and one with a non-positive diagonal fails with
`the ForceInput box has a non-positive diagonal`.
Before fixing the session topology, a non-zero box converted to Angstrom
is checked by one-sided Jacobi singular values and scaled LU with partial
pivoting on a power-of-two scaled copy: a non-finite component fails with
`cell contains a non-finite component`, a cell whose singular values do not
all exceed the largest singular value times 3 times `DBL_EPSILON` (or whose
scaled LU determinant is zero) fails with
`cell does not have three independent vectors`, and a full-rank cell
whose Angstrom volume falls below the normal binary64 range fails with
`cell volume is too small for binary64`.
Deck rendering also rejects a non-zero cell without a representable rank-3
volume (`the periodic cell does not have a representable rank-3 volume` or
`the cell does not have a representable rank-3 volume`).
Without `ANGSTROM` the box goes in as Bohr.
An all-zero box is a system without a cell: the deck's `CELL` stays, or a 12
Angstrom cube when the deck has none.
The `hasCharge`, `charge`, `hasMultiplicity`, and `multiplicity` fields of
`ForceInput` are not read by `cpmdc`.

# Macros
| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|-------+-------+---------|
| `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION` | the first field of `version.txt` | the ABI generation the consumer compiled with; `cpmdc_abi_version()` returns the generation of the library |
| `CPMDC_API` | the mark of the exported symbols (*Exported symbols) table | placed before each function declaration of `cpmdc.h` and `cpmdc_features.h` |

# Types

## ~CPMDCResult~

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------+------+---------|
| `ok` | `int` | non-zero when the calculation succeeded |
| `energy_h` | `double` | total energy in Hartree, 0 on failure |
| `message` | `char[512]` | null-terminated status or error text |

## ~CPMDCSession~
An opaque handle.
A session holds a copy of the `CPMDParams` bytes, the rendered deck, the
topology, scratch arrays for step geometry, and the results of its last
evaluation.
`session_accept_topology` fixes the topology only after an evaluation call
passes its argument checks and collective orbital preflight. A rejected
preflight leaves the topology configurable.

## Result snapshots
Each snapshot struct starts with `int valid`, set by a successful evaluation.

| Struct | Contents | Units |
|--------+----------+-------|
| `CPMDCEnergyComponents` | the 24 scalars of OpenCPMD's `ener_com`, `etot` to `eefield` | Hartree |
| `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` | `csumg`, `csumr`, `csums`, `csumsabs` from `chrg` | electrons |
| `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies` | `count` doubles in `values[64]` from `ener_c` and `ener_d` | Hartree |
| `CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow` | `count` doubles in `values[32]`: `etot ekin epseu enl eht exc ehep ehee ehii esr eself EKINC` | Hartree |
| `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | deprecated nuclear-gradient name `hessian[4096]`, optional molecular dipole in `dipole[3]`, polarizability in `polarizability[9]`, each with a count | atomic units (Hartree/Bohr for the gradient) |
| `CPMDCDipole` | `valid` and the molecular dipole in `values[3]` | electron Bohr |
| `CPMDCStressTensor` | row-major `values[9]`, `paiu/omega` | Hartree/Bohr^3 |
| `CPMDCRankSpread` | `ranks`, `energy_h`, `gradient_h_bohr` (see Results of the last evaluation (*Results of the last evaluation)) | Hartree, Hartree/Bohr |
| `CPMDCMethodInfo` | effective `functional[64]`, `charge`, and `multiplicity` decoded from `CPMDParams` | text and integers |

Fields of `CPMDCMethodInfo`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------+------+---------|
| `functional[64]` | `char` | null-terminated effective DFT functional |
| `charge` | `int` | effective total system charge |
| `multiplicity` | `int` | effective spin multiplicity, `2S + 1` |

With OpenCPMD linked, `CPMDCEnergyComponents` fills `etot`, `ekin`, `epseu`,
`enl`, `eht`, and `exc`; the other fields stay zero.
The reference evaluator fills `etot` only.
`EKINC`, the fictitious electronic kinetic energy, is zero for a wavefunction
optimisation.
`CPMDCPropertySnapshot.hessian` and `hessian_count` are deprecated because the
values are the nuclear gradient, not a Hessian.
Use `cpmdc_last_gradient()` or `cpmdc_session_last_gradient()`.
The legacy array fixes the current maximum at 4096 gradient components, or
1365 atoms. An evaluation with more atoms fails before it runs, with
`property gradient snapshot supports at most 1365 atoms`; it is not truncated.
On a session the check is part of the evaluation preflight, after the topology
check and before the topology is fixed. A first call that is too large leaves
the session without a topology. A session that already holds another system
reports `topology change requires a new session` instead of the atom limit.

Fields of `CPMDCEnergyComponents`; `valid` is an `int`, non-zero when the
snapshot was written by a successful evaluation, and every other field is a
`double`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------+------+---------|
| `valid` | `int` | non-zero after a successful evaluation |
| `etot` | `double` | the `etot` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ekin` | `double` | the `ekin` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `epseu` | `double` | the `epseu` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `enl` | `double` | the `enl` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eht` | `double` | the `eht` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ehep` | `double` | the `ehep` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ehee` | `double` | the `ehee` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ehii` | `double` | the `ehii` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `exc` | `double` | the `exc` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `vxc` | `double` | the `vxc` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `egc` | `double` | the `egc` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `esr` | `double` | the `esr` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eeig` | `double` | the `eeig` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eband` | `double` | the `eband` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `entropy` | `double` | the `entropy` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eself` | `double` | the `eself` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ecnstr` | `double` | the `ecnstr` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `amu` | `double` | the `amu` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ebogo` | `double` | the `ebogo` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eext` | `double` | the `eext` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `etddft` | `double` | the `etddft` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `ehsic` | `double` | the `ehsic` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `erestr` | `double` | the `erestr` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |
| `eefield` | `double` | the `eefield` term of `ener_com`, Hartree |

Fields of the other snapshot structs; each also starts with `int valid`.
Arrays have the fixed capacity shown, and a `size_t` count says how many
entries a call filled.

| Field | Struct | Meaning |
|-------+--------+---------|
| `valid` | `CPMDCChargeIntegrals`, `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies`, `CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow`, `CPMDCPropertySnapshot`, `CPMDCDipole`, `CPMDCStressTensor`, `CPMDCRankSpread` | `int`, non-zero when the snapshot was written |
| `csumg` | `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` | `csumg` of OpenCPMD `chrg`, electrons |
| `csumr` | `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` | `csumr` of OpenCPMD `chrg`, electrons |
| `csums` | `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` | `csums` of OpenCPMD `chrg`, electrons |
| `csumsabs` | `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` | `csumsabs` of OpenCPMD `chrg`, electrons |
| `count` | `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies`, `CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow` | `size_t`, the number of doubles copied into `values` |
| `values[64]` | `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies` | `ener_c` and `ener_d` values, Hartree |
| `values[32]` | `CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow` | trajectory terms in the order of the table above, Hartree |
| `hessian_count` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | `size_t`, the number of doubles copied into `hessian` |
| `hessian[4096]` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | deprecated nuclear gradient dE/dR in Hartree/Bohr packed as `n_atoms * 3`; use the gradient accessors. Evaluations above its 4096-component capacity fail instead of truncating |
| `dipole_count` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | `size_t`, the number of doubles copied into `dipole` |
| `dipole[3]` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | molecular dipole in electron Bohr when OpenCPMD recomputed it for the current geometry; unavailable otherwise |
| `polarizability_count` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | `size_t`, the number of doubles copied into `polarizability` |
| `polarizability[9]` | `CPMDCPropertySnapshot` | always zeros, in atomic units (Bohr^3), with `polarizability_count` 9: no build computes it |
| `values[3]` | `CPMDCDipole` | Cartesian molecular dipole, electron Bohr; see the periodic-cell caveat on the struct in `cpmdc.h` |
| `values[9]` | `CPMDCStressTensor` | row-major `[xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz]`, Hartree/Bohr^3 |
| `ranks` | `CPMDCRankSpread` | `int`, ranks in the calculator communicator |
| `energy_h` | `CPMDCRankSpread` | largest absolute energy difference from rank 0 over the ranks, Hartree |
| `gradient_h_bohr` | `CPMDCRankSpread` | largest nuclear-gradient component difference from rank 0, Hartree/Bohr |

## ~CPMDCFeatureEntry~ and ~CPMDCFeatureKind~

| Field | Meaning |
|-------+---------|
| `feature_id` | stable ID such as `abi.cpmdc_session_calculate_result` |
| `kind` | a `CPMDCFeatureKind`, listed below |
| `stub_applicable` | non-zero when the stub build exposes the feature |
| `embed_applicable` | non-zero when an OpenCPMD build exposes the feature |

| `CPMDCFeatureKind` constant | Value | Namespace |
|-----------------------------+-------+-----------|
| `CPMDC_FEATURE_SECTION` | 1 | CPMD input section support, such as `catalog.section.PIMD` |
| `CPMDC_FEATURE_PARAMS` | 2 | `CPMDParams` field support |
| `CPMDC_FEATURE_ABI` | 3 | exported C ABI symbol support |
| `CPMDC_FEATURE_KEYWORD` | 4 | CPMD keyword support inside a catalog section |

# Library status

| Function | Returns |
|----------+---------|
| `const char *cpmdc_version(void)` | `"cpmdc/"` followed by the project version, or `"cpmdc-stub/"` followed by the project version in the link stub |
| `int cpmdc_abi_version(void)` | the ABI generation, equal to `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION` and the shared-library soversion, which are the first field of `version.txt` |
| `int cpmdc_available(void)` | 1 when OpenCPMD is linked, ready, and not finalized; 0 on the reference build; 0 after finalize and from the link stub |
| `void cpmdc_finalize(void)` | reference and OpenCPMD builds: marks the runtime finalized; later calls that need it fail with `CPMD embed not available`, but a session evaluation that repeats the step the session stored last still returns 0 from the session's cache; the link stub does nothing and its evaluations always fail with `OpenCPMD embed not available in cpmdc stub` followed by the called function's name in parentheses; no build calls `MPI_Finalize` |
| `const char *cpmdc_last_error(void)` | per-thread text of the last failing public call, empty after a success |
| `CPMDCErrorCode cpmdc_last_error_code(void)` | machine-readable code for that failure; periodic electrostatic embedding is `CPMDC_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PERIODIC_EMBEDDING`, and a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` combined with session charges is `CPMDC_ERROR_DECK_EXTERNAL_POTENTIAL` |

| `CPMDCErrorCode` constant | Value | Meaning |
|---------------------------+-------+---------|
| `CPMDC_ERROR_NONE` | 0 | no failure recorded on the calling thread |
| `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` | 1 | a null handle, a bad buffer, or a value the call refuses, such as a Gaussian width below 1e-12 Angstrom |
| `CPMDC_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE` | 2 | the backend is not linked, not ready, or this build is the link stub |
| `CPMDC_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PERIODIC_EMBEDDING` | 3 | session charges with a periodic cell or a periodic deck |
| `CPMDC_ERROR_EVALUATION_FAILED` | 4 | the evaluation ran and produced no result |
| `CPMDC_ERROR_DECK_EXTERNAL_POTENTIAL` | 5 | session charges with a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` or `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL ADD` |

`cpmdc_last_error()` is written by `cpmdc_params_method()`,
`cpmdc_set_params()`,
`cpmdc_configure()`, `cpmdc_bind_calculator()`, `cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm()`,
`cpmdc_session_create()`,
`cpmdc_session_set_params()`, `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()`,
`cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals()`,
`cpmdc_session_create_from_config()`, `cpmdc_session_configure()`,
`cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input()`, and every evaluation entry
point, `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` among them.
`cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff()` writes it too.
When the call returns `CPMDCResult`, the text matches `message`, including a
missing pseudopotential directory.
Snapshot readers (`cpmdc_last_stress()` and the other
`cpmdc_last_*` / `cpmdc_session_last_*` getters) do not write it, except
`cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces()`, which writes the code and the
text on every failure and clears both on success. For the other readers, -1
means the snapshot is absent or the output pointer is null.
`cpmdc_adopted_comm()` and `cpmdc_capabilities_result()` do not write it either.
A capabilities return of -1 is the size query.

# MPI

| Function | Behaviour |
|----------+-----------|
| `int cpmdc_bind_calculator(int ranks_per_calc)` | collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`; splits the world into calculators of `ranks_per_calc` consecutive ranks, group `g` holding world ranks `g * ranks_per_calc` to `(g + 1) * ranks_per_calc - 1`; the world size must be a multiple of `ranks_per_calc`, with no remainder group, and any other world size or a value above it returns -1 on every rank and splits nothing; `ranks_per_calc <= 0` means the world size, one calculator; returns this rank's calculator index `world_rank / ranks_per_calc`, or -1 when the world size is not a multiple, `MPI_Comm_split` returns an error, or the library has no CPMD backend; on an OpenCPMD build it calls `MPI_Init` when MPI is not running, and the reference build and the link stub return -1 without calling MPI; a later call does not split again and returns the index its own `ranks_per_calc` gives, or -1 on every rank when that value does not divide the world size or is above it, and the existing split stays |
| `int cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm(const void *comm, size_t nbytes, int ranks_per_calc)` | collective on the caller's communicator; reads rank and size from that communicator; does not call `MPI_Init` or `MPI_Comm_split`; when `ranks_per_calc > 0` the adopted size must equal it, and a mismatch returns -1 with both numbers in `cpmdc_last_error()`; the group must be one aligned block of world ranks, and any other layout returns -1 on every rank; the calculator index is the lowest world rank of that block divided by the adopted size; indices are unique when every group has the same size, which the same `ranks_per_calc > 0` on every rank enforces; the handle is borrowed, so the caller keeps ownership and does not free the communicator until the last session is destroyed or a later adopt replaces it; an OpenCPMD build stores the communicator as `mp_comm_world`; a later call replaces it when no live `CPMDCSession` has started an evaluation, and if any rank has a live session that has evaluated every rank returns -1; a session that has not evaluated does not block it; also returns -1 when the pointer is null, MPI is not initialized, or the build has no MPI |
| `int cpmdc_adopted_comm(void *out, size_t nbytes)` | copies the stored calculator communicator into `out` (on an OpenCPMD build, `mp_comm_world`); returns 0, or -1 when no communicator is stored; does not write `cpmdc_last_error()` |

`cpmdc_bind_calculator()` splits at most once per process, so call it before the first evaluation.
A later call does not split again.
`cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm()` may run again after every session has been
destroyed.
See running under mpirun (file:../howto/mpi.org).

# Configuration without a session
These calls configure the process-wide state that the global array calls use.

| Function | Behaviour |
|----------+-----------|
| `int cpmdc_params_method(const void *params, size_t size, CPMDCMethodInfo *out)` | decode the effective functional, charge, and multiplicity without applying the deck; 0 or -1 |
| `int cpmdc_set_params(const void *params, size_t size)` | decode `CPMDParams`, render the deck, apply it; 0 or -1 |
| `int cpmdc_configure(const void *config, size_t size)` | resolve a `PotentialConfig` and apply the result like `cpmdc_set_params()`; 0 or -1 |

`cpmdc_configure()` takes the `cpmd` arm when it is set.
With the arm unset, a `common` overlay (`CommonMethodSpec`) lowers into
synthesized `CPMDParams`.
The fields it lowers are the ones `cpmdc_capabilities_result()` lists:
`xcFunctionals`, `basisSet`, `planewaveCutoffEv`, `charge`, `hasCharge`,
`spinMultiplicity`, `scfEnergyToleranceEv`, `scfMaxIterations`, `kMesh`,
`smearing`, `vanDerWaalsMethod`, and `vanDerWaalsS6`.
`scfEnergyToleranceEv` fills both values of `CONVERGENCE ORBITALS`: the orbital
threshold and the total-energy change between steps, which ends a smeared
(free-energy) SCF once the energy settles.
A set `cpmd` arm and a set `common` overlay are merged.
The arm bytes stay.
Both deck renderers and the configuration the embed records apply the same
precedence to the functional, cutoff, charge, and multiplicity lines cpmdc
writes.
A value a typed field sets beats the overlay, and the overlay beats a schema
default.
A typed `dft` or `system` section beats the top-level field of the same name.
A field that is omitted or holds its schema default (functional `BLYP`, cutoff
70 Ry, charge 0 with `hasCharge` `false`, multiplicity 1) is unset and does not
replace the top-level arm or overlay value.
So `xcFunctionals` fills a `BLYP` functional, `planewaveCutoffEv` fills a
70 Ry cutoff, `charge` fills a charge of 0 with `hasCharge` `false`, and
`spinMultiplicity` fills a multiplicity of 1.
A typed `system` charge of 0 with `hasCharge` `false` is unset; a non-zero
system charge, and zero `system.charge` with `system.hasCharge` `true`, is
explicit.
`planewaveCutoffEv` is in eV and the deck cutoff is in Ry, so the merge
divides by the Rydberg energy in eV (13.605693 eV).
`spinMultiplicity` 0 is unset, and any other value, an explicit singlet
included, is merged and checked like the other overlay scalars.
An `xcFunctionals` list is mapped before that precedence, and an unmapped
token is rejected for every arm functional.
An opaque carrier is rendered as given and is not read back into the
recorded functional, cutoff, charge, or multiplicity.
So the carrier check runs for every set overlay field, whether or not a
typed field also sets it, including zero `charge` with `hasCharge` `true` and
an explicit singlet `spinMultiplicity` of 1.
The overlay field is rejected when `inputBlocks`, a raw section, or a generic
section opens the owning section (`&DFT` for `xcFunctionals`, `&SYSTEM` for
the cutoff, charge, and multiplicity), when a set directive names
`DFT.FUNCTIONAL`, `SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or
`SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY`, or when the `directives` list of the typed `dft`
section holds `FUNCTIONAL` or that of the typed `system` section holds
`CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY`.
Without an overlay, a `FUNCTIONAL` directive in the typed `dft` section or a
`DFT.FUNCTIONAL` set directive is rejected when the deck is rendered, because
the rendered `&DFT` section already carries the functional.
The same render rejects a `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY` directive in
the typed `system` section, and a `SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or
`SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY` set directive.
`CUTOFF` is written on every deck, including the default 70 Ry.
`CHARGE` is written only when it is not 0 and `MULTIPLICITY` only when it is
greater than 1; an omitted line is the schema default the recorded
configuration carries.
Those directives are rejected for a default value and for any other value
alike.
A default leaves the directive as a value the recorded configuration does not
carry, and any other value leaves two lines.
The render does not keep one and drop the other.
Fermi `smearing` is copied as `FREE-ENERGY` and `TEMPERATURE ELECTRON` when
`&CPMD` sets no free-energy or electron-temperature control (including split
`TEMPERATURE` and `ELECTRON` arguments in `cpmd.directives` or
`CPMD.TEMPERATURE` set directives) and the arm has no raw or generic `&CPMD`
block.
`vanDerWaalsS6` is copied into a `vdwParams` section whose `s6` is unset.
`basisSet` must be unset or `"planewave"`.
Next to the arm the call rejects `kMesh`, `scfMaxIterations`,
`scfEnergyToleranceEv`, `vanDerWaalsMethod`, and `relativityMethod`, and also
already-set smearing or `s6`, `vanDerWaalsS6` without `vdwParams`, a
non-plane-wave `basisSet`, and a negative or non-finite overlay scalar.
With the arm unset, an overlay field without a CPMD lowering is rejected,
including `relativityMethod` and a `basisSet` other than `planewave`.
That overlay-only lowering also rejects `vanDerWaalsS6` without
`vanDerWaalsMethod` and a non-zero `smearing.widthEv` with `kind = none`.
Every rejection leaves a `cpmdc_last_error()` that names its cause.
An arm `inputBlocks`, `inputSections`, or `directives` list the merge cannot
read is reported with the overlay field that needed it, as in
`charge cannot merge: the cpmd arm has an invalid inputBlocks list`.
A message with neither the arm nor an overlay applies nothing and returns 0.

# Global array calls
Each call applies the message it is given like `cpmdc_set_params()` and then
evaluates.
`cpmdc_set_params()` detaches the process image without clearing the stored
orbitals: a call whose functional, deck, cutoff, charge, multiplicity, atom
count, and elemental composition match the latched basis, and whose step
without a cell matches a latched state that also has no cell
(`CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` does not apply without a cell, because
`embed_cell_moves_in_place` returns false when `has_cell` is 0), skips full
CPMD setup.
It starts the SCF from the stored orbitals when the geometry is within
`CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` (default 0.15 Angstrom) of a stored geometry, and from the
deck's guess without full setup beyond that limit.
Any other call runs full CPMD setup and starts from a cold SCF.

| Function | Output |
|----------+--------|
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params, size_t size)` | energy |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy_gradient(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params, size_t size, double *grad_h_bohr)` | energy and gradient |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_energy_forces(int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, const void *params, size_t size, double *forces_h_bohr)` | energy and forces |

The output array holds `3 * n_atoms` doubles.

# Sessions

| Function | Behaviour |
|----------+-----------|
| `CPMDCSession *cpmdc_session_create(const void *params, size_t size)` | copy and render `CPMDParams`; `NULL` on a decode or render failure |
| `CPMDCSession *cpmdc_session_create_from_config(const void *config, size_t size)` | resolve a `PotentialConfig` like `cpmdc_configure()`, then create a session |
| `int cpmdc_session_set_params(CPMDCSession *s, const void *params, size_t size)` | replace the parameters and drop any `common` overlay; -1 once the session has accepted a topology; a failed call leaves the session unchanged |
| `int cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff(CPMDCSession *session, double cutoff_ry, double height_ry, double width_ry)` | add `CONSTANT CUTOFF` to the rendered `&SYSTEM`; `cutoff_ry <= 0` removes it; same topology rule |
| `int cpmdc_session_set_external_charges(CPMDCSession *s, size_t n, const double *positions_ang, const double *charges_e, const double *widths_ang)` | copy `n` Gaussian MM charges for subsequent calls; widths may be `NULL` for the 0.30 Angstrom default and must be at least 1e-12 Angstrom; `n == 0` clears them |
| `int cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces(const CPMDCSession *s, double *forces_h_bohr, size_t forces_len)` | copy the `3 * n` MM forces from the last successful evaluation and clear `cpmdc_last_error()`; -1 writes `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a null session, a missing result, the wrong length, or a null buffer |
| `int cpmdc_session_configure(CPMDCSession *s, const void *config, size_t size)` | replace the configuration from a `PotentialConfig`; same rule, and a failed call keeps the previous parameters and overlay |
| `void cpmdc_session_destroy(CPMDCSession *s)` | free the session; `NULL` is accepted |
| `int cpmdc_session_select_orbitals(CPMDCSession *s, long long key)` | record `key`; the next evaluations start from the orbitals stored under `key`; a key named and replaced before an evaluation parks nothing; every calculator rank names the same key; an evaluation that would park another copy past `CPMDC_ORBITAL_SLOT_LIMIT` fails, `cpmdc_last_error()` and the result message name that variable, and the parked copies already stored are left unchanged; -1 for a `NULL` session |
| `int cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals(CPMDCSession *s, long long from_key, long long to_key)` | duplicate the converged orbitals of `from_key`, and the geometry they converged at, into `to_key`, replacing any previous copy; the selected key is unchanged; when `to_key` is selected its live store is replaced immediately, otherwise the live store is unchanged; selecting `to_key` afterwards starts from that copy; a donor whose last pass did not converge is refused, including a parked copy and a copy onto the same key; a copy that would park a new key past `CPMDC_ORBITAL_SLOT_LIMIT` returns -1, `cpmdc_last_error()` names that variable, and the copies already stored stay; every calculator rank names the same keys, the same rule `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()` has; the reference build returns 0 because it has no orbital store, unless the limit is set to a value that is not a positive integer, which fails the call; the link stub returns -1, including a same key copy; -1 for a `NULL` session, before any evaluation, when `from_key` has no converged orbitals, or on backend copy failure |

`cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff()` sets the constant-cutoff kinetic
functional of Bernasconi et al. (1995), which CPMD applies as G^2 + A [1 +
erf((G^2 - E0) / sigma)], with `cutoff_ry` as E0, `height_ry` as A, and
`width_ry` as sigma, all in Ry.
A height or width of 0 selects 50 times the deck cutoff, or E0 / 10.
The stress then carries no Pulay stress; see relaxing a cell at a constant cutoff (file:../howto/constant-cutoff.org).
The call returns -1 and writes `cpmdc_last_error()` when a value is not finite,
when E0 + 2 sigma exceeds the deck cutoff, when the message gives `&SYSTEM` as
raw text, or when it already sets `system.constantCutoff`; the session keeps its
previous setting.
It survives a later `cpmdc_session_set_params()`.
The link stub returns -1.

`session_accept_topology` fixes the topology only after an evaluation call
passes its argument checks and collective orbital preflight. A rejected
preflight leaves the topology configurable.
A later step with a different count or composition fails with
`topology change requires a new session` before CPMD runs.
A reordering of the same elements stays on the session.
Coordinates, the cell, and units may change between steps.
External charges contribute
\(-q\,\mathrm{erf}(r/(\sqrt{2}\sigma))/r\) to the electronic potential.
For \(r/\sigma > 1/8\) the closed form is used. At or below that ratio the
potential and the force coefficient are evaluated from their Taylor series in
\((r/\sigma)^2\) through \((r/\sigma)^{14}\), because the closed force
coefficient subtracts two terms of size \(O(1/r^2)\) and loses digits to that
cancellation as \(r\) shrinks.
The series is continuous with the closed form at the switch, finite at
\(r = 0\), and keeps the force on a charge that sits on an ion.
No term is dropped and nothing is clamped to the origin.
Every charge and position must be finite, and every width must be finite and at
least 1e-12 Angstrom, from the argument or from `CPMDC_EXTERNAL_CHARGE_WIDTH_ANG`.
A narrower width fails `cpmdc_session_set_external_charges()` with
`CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and keeps the previous charge set, because the
\(1/\sigma^4\) force terms overflow to NaN for much narrower Gaussians.
The total energy includes electron--MM and ion--MM coupling; QM and MM force
arrays are both `-dE/dR`. External charges are supported on an isolated system
only, because periodic images are not implemented. A step with a cell, and a
step on a deck that is not an isolated system (a `SYMMETRY` above 0, or a
`SURFACE` or `POLYMER` deck), fails with
`CPMDC_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PERIODIC_EMBEDDING` on every evaluation path,
including `cpmdc_session_energy_gradient()`.
Session charges and a deck-defined `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` or
`EXTERNAL POTENTIAL ADD` are mutually exclusive.
An evaluation that requests both fails with
`CPMDC_ERROR_DECK_EXTERNAL_POTENTIAL` instead of replacing the deck potential.
On an isolated OpenCPMD deck the atoms are moved to the middle of the deck's
cell before each evaluation and the net force is removed, so a rigid translation
of every atom changes neither the energy nor the forces (see `CPMDC_RECENTER` in environment variables (file:environment.org)).
An evaluation with the same positions returns the stored energy and forces.
A session evaluated after another session in the same process reuses the stored
orbitals when the functional, deck, cutoff, cell, charge, multiplicity, and
elemental composition match.
A different method or composition runs setup on the next evaluation (see wavefunction state (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org)).

## Session array steps

| Function | Output |
|----------+--------|
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy(CPMDCSession *s, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers)` | energy |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy_gradient(CPMDCSession *s, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, double *grad_h_bohr)` | energy and gradient |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_energy_forces(CPMDCSession *s, int n_atoms, const double *positions_ang, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr)` | energy and forces |

These calls pass no cell: the deck's `CELL` applies, or a 12 Angstrom cube when
the deck has none.

## Session message steps

| Function | Output |
|----------+--------|
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_calculate_forces(CPMDCSession *s, const void *force_input, size_t size, double *forces_h_bohr, size_t forces_len)` | energy in Hartree and forces in Hartree/Bohr; `forces_len >= 3 * n_atoms` |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_session_calculate_result(CPMDCSession *s, const void *force_input, size_t size, void *out, size_t capacity, size_t *out_size)` | a serialized `PotentialResult` in `out`, its byte count in `*out_size` |

`cpmdc_session_calculate_forces()` and `cpmdc_session_calculate_result()`
enforce the `ForceInput.box` rules above before fixing the session topology:
a `box` length other than 0 or 9 fails with `invalid ForceInput geometry`,
and a non-zero box fails with `cell contains a non-finite component`,
`cell does not have three independent vectors`, or
`cell volume is too small for binary64` on the Angstrom cell, or fails
in the reference evaluator when a non-zero periodic cell cannot represent
a finite positive stress volume (`cell volume is too large for binary64`
or `cell volume is not representable for stress`).
`cpmdc_session_calculate_result()` writes the required byte count to `*out_size`
before it checks `capacity`.
When `capacity` is too small, or `out` is `NULL`, it returns `ok == 0` with
`PotentialResult buffer too small` and does not evaluate; this is the contract
of the session result call of the NWChem library `nwchemc` as well.
`out_size` is required: a `NULL` there fails with `ok == 0`, and it is set to 0
when the `ForceInput` does not parse or its geometry is invalid.
A `forces_len` below `3 * n_atoms` fails `cpmdc_session_calculate_forces()`
with `ok == 0`.
The written `PotentialResult` carries `energy` and `forces` in the requested
units, `stress`, `gradient`, `dipole`, `polarizability`, and the `cpmdc`
extension fields `energyComponents`, `chargeIntegrals`, `multiStateEnergies`,
and `mdTrajectoryRow` with their `...Valid` flags.

## Session steps in atomic units

| Function | Output |
|----------+--------|
| `int cpmdc_session_calculate_au(CPMDCSession *s, int n_atoms, const double *positions_bohr, const int *atomic_numbers, const double *cell_bohr, double *energy_h, double *forces_h_bohr, double *virial_h)` | energy in Hartree, forces in Hartree/Bohr, the virial in Hartree; 0 or -1 |

This call takes a periodic cell without a Cap'n Proto message.
Its arguments come in the order of `cpmdc_session_energy_forces()`: the atom
count, the positions, then the atomic numbers.
Every quantity is in atomic units.

| Argument | Layout |
|----------+--------|
| `positions_bohr` | `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major (`x0 y0 z0 x1 ...`), Bohr |
| `atomic_numbers` | `n_atoms` values in 1..118 |
| `cell_bohr` | `NULL`, or nine doubles: row-major 3 by 3, one lattice vector per row (`a_x a_y a_z b_x ...`), Bohr |
| `energy_h` | one double, Hartree |
| `forces_h_bohr` | `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, Hartree/Bohr, `-dE/dR` |
| `virial_h` | `NULL`, or nine doubles, row-major, Hartree |

`cell_bohr` follows the `ForceInput.box` rules above for the deck: `NULL` and an
all-zero cell leave the deck's `CELL` in place, and a cell with a non-zero entry
replaces the deck's `CELL` lines and `SYMMETRY`.
The session still keeps an all-zero cell as a step with a cell.
A repeat of a step with a `NULL` cell does not match a stored step with an
all-zero cell, and the other way round.
With OpenCPMD linked, stored orbitals follow the same rule: an all-zero cell
starts from them only when the latched step had a cell equal to it, and `NULL`
only when the latched step had none.
The virial is `W = -dE/d(strain)`, the strain derivative of the energy taken
with the opposite sign, so a compressed cell whose energy falls on expansion has
a positive diagonal.
It equals `|det(cell)|` times the stress of `cpmdc_session_last_stress()` and of
`PotentialResult.stress`, which is `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)` in Hartree/Bohr^3.
`virial_h` holds zeros when the cell is `NULL` and when the evaluation produced
no stress, for example for an isolated deck or a cell of zeros.
ASE's stress is `-W/V` and i-PI's virial is `W`.

Energy, forces, and stress are bit-for-bit those of
`cpmdc_session_calculate_result()` for a `ForceInput` with `lengthUnit` `bohr`, `energyUnit` `hartree`, the same positions, and `box` equal to `cell_bohr`:
both paths scale Bohr to Angstrom with the same factor and share the evaluation
and the session's cache.
The topology and repeat-step rules of the session apply.

It returns -1 and sets `cpmdc_last_error()` for a `NULL` session
(`null session`), `n_atoms` outside 1 to `INT_MAX / 3` or a `NULL` required
pointer (`invalid arguments`), a topology change, and a failed evaluation.
For a non-zero `cell_bohr`, it fails before fixing the session topology with
`cell contains a non-finite component`,
`cell does not have three independent vectors`, or
`cell volume is too small for binary64` judged on the converted
Angstrom cell; when `virial_h` is not `NULL` and `cell_bohr` is finite, a
Bohr volume above `DBL_MAX` fails before evaluation with
`cell volume is too large for binary64`, and any non-finite component of
`volume * stress` after evaluation fails with `virial is not finite`.
When `virial_h` is `NULL`, the reference evaluator still fails a non-zero
periodic cell whose Bohr volume cannot be represented for stress
(`cell volume is too large for binary64` or
`cell volume is not representable for stress`).
On failure the output arrays are left unspecified.
The stub archive `libcpmdc_stub.a` returns -1 with the stub message.
`tools/cpmdc_ipi.c` is an i-PI client on this call (see [[file:../howto/socket-drivers.org][the
socket drivers]]).
`tools/lammps/pair_cpmdc.cpp`, the LAMMPS `pair_style cpmdc`, and `cpmdc.lammps`
call it once per force evaluation (see LAMMPS (file:../howto/lammps.org)).
`tools/gromacs/cpmdc_gromacs.c`, `libcpmdc_gromacs`, calls it once per MD step
behind the libcp2k API of GROMACS'
QM/MM interface (see GROMACS (file:../howto/gromacs.org)).

# One-shot message calls

| Function | Behaviour |
|----------+-----------|
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_calculate_result(const void *params, size_t params_size, const void *force_input, size_t force_size, void *out, size_t capacity, size_t *out_size)` | create a session, evaluate one step, destroy the session |
| `CPMDCResult cpmdc_calculate_result_from_config(const void *config, size_t config_size, ...)` | the same with a `PotentialConfig` |
| `size_t cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input(const void *force_input, size_t size)` | bytes needed for one `PotentialResult`; parses geometry only; 0 when the message is invalid or too large |

A one-shot call reuses the stored orbitals when its basis matches the previous
call in the process.
The first call of the process is cold.
Use a session for more than one step.

# Results of the last evaluation
Each getter copies a snapshot into `*out` and returns 0 when `out->valid` is
set, -1 otherwise.
A host reads the energy terms in Hartree through
`cpmdc_last_energy_components()` without parsing CLI `ENERGY` files or opening a
network socket.
The plain form reads the calculator that ran last: the active session, or the
global state after a global call.
The `session` form reads that session's own last result, also after another
session has run.

| Plain | Per session |
|-------+-------------|
| `int cpmdc_last_energy_components(CPMDCEnergyComponents *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_energy_components(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCEnergyComponents *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_charge_integrals(CPMDCChargeIntegrals *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_charge_integrals(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCChargeIntegrals *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_multi_state_energies(CPMDCMultiStateEnergies *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_multi_state_energies(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCMultiStateEnergies *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_md_trajectory_row(CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_md_trajectory_row(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_property_snapshot(CPMDCPropertySnapshot *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_property_snapshot(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCPropertySnapshot *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_dipole(CPMDCDipole *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_dipole(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCDipole *out)` |
| `int cpmdc_last_stress(CPMDCStressTensor *out)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_stress(const CPMDCSession *s, CPMDCStressTensor *out)` |

The gradient accessors take a caller buffer:

| Plain | Per session |
|-------+-------------|
| `int cpmdc_last_gradient(double *out, size_t capacity, size_t *count)` | `int cpmdc_session_last_gradient(const CPMDCSession *s, double *out, size_t capacity, size_t *count)` |

`count` receives the required number of doubles.
The call returns -1 when there is no gradient, an argument is null, or
`capacity` is too small.

The dipole getter returns 0 only when the linked OpenCPMD recomputed
`dipomod%moment%dmom` from the converged wavefunction of this evaluation.
The supported route is a periodic Gamma-point, non-broken-symmetry deck with
`DIPOLE DYNAMICS` or `PROP / DIPOLE MOMENT BERRY`.
An isolated deck, a k-point calculation, the reference evaluator, and a deck
without either request leave the dipole invalid.
A deck that sets `DIPOLE DYNAMICS` in `&CPMD` and `KPOINTS` in `&SYSTEM` is
rejected before any evaluation, by `cpmdc_session_create()`,
`cpmdc_session_set_params()`, and the calls that take parameters, because
OpenCPMD stops in `localize2` on it; `cpmdc_last_error()` names both keywords.
OpenCPMD's `ddip%pdipole` is not this molecular dipole: `ddipo` adds the ionic
term to make `pdipolt`, then multiplies by the cell volume to set
`moment%dmom`. Reading `pdipole` after `wfopts` without calling `ddipo` would
return stale module state.

The stress snapshot is valid only when the tensor was computed for a periodic
cell: OpenCPMD ran `totstr` (`cntl%tpres`, which requires a periodic cell and
`CPMDC_STRESS` other than `0`), or the reference evaluator filled the toy tensor
for a periodic deck using scaled LU with partial pivoting on the cell in Bohr.
Accepted near-singular periodic cells receive a valid stress tensor, while a
non-zero periodic cell whose stress volume overflows or is not positive fails
the evaluation instead of leaving `valid` unset.
An isolated cell (symmetry 0, `CLUSTER`, or an isolated-molecule keyword,
including Hockney) leaves `valid` unset even when the box volume is positive.
`CPMDC_STRESS=0` leaves it unset on a periodic cell as well.

| Function | Behaviour |
|----------+-----------|
| `int cpmdc_last_rank_spread(CPMDCRankSpread *out)` | copies the rank spread of the last evaluation in the process; 0 when it ran with `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` under a running MPI, -1 otherwise; does not write `cpmdc_last_error()` |

`CPMDCRankSpread` holds `ranks`, the size of the calculator communicator,
`energy_h`, the largest `|E_r - E_0|` over its ranks in Hartree, and `gradient_h_bohr`,
the largest nuclear-gradient component difference from rank 0 in Hartree/Bohr.
Both are taken before every rank receives rank 0's values, and a NaN difference
is reported as infinity.
A repeat of the stored positions keeps the spread of the evaluation that stored
them.
The spread belongs to the process, not to a session, so it has no
`cpmdc_session_` form.
See environment variables (file:environment.org).

# Discovery

| Function | Returns |
|----------+---------|
| `size_t cpmdc_feature_count(void)` | number of rows in the feature table |
| `const CPMDCFeatureEntry *cpmdc_feature_table(void)` | the contiguous table, owned by the library |
| `const CPMDCFeatureEntry *cpmdc_feature_find(const char *feature_id)` | the matching row or `NULL` |
| `int cpmdc_capabilities_result(void *out, size_t capacity, size_t *out_size)` | a serialized `Capabilities` message; 0, or -1 with the required size in `*out_size` |

Call `cpmdc_capabilities_result(NULL, 0, &size)` to query the size.
The message names the backend, its version, the ABI generation, availability,
the operations `energy`, `forces`, `gradient`, and `stress`, the
`CommonMethodSpec` fields the overlay lowers, and the `cpmd` `PotentialConfig`
arm.
The feature inventory (file:feature-inventory.org) describes the table.

# RESTART file library
`include/cpmdc_restart.h` declares a separate static library, `libcpmdc_restart`,
that reads and writes CPMD `RESTART.n` files without OpenCPMD.
Its functions are not marked
`CPMDC_API` and are not part of `libcpmdc`; link `libcpmdc_restart`
(`pkg-config cpmdc-restart`) to use them.

| Item | Convention |
|------+------------|
| `CPMDCRestart` | opaque image of one file, from a reader, released with `cpmdc_restart_free` |
| `cpmdc_restart` | deprecated name of `CPMDCRestart`, the same type; kept for 0.4.0 callers |
| `CPMDC_RESTART_ANGSTROM_PER_BOHR` | 0.529177210859, Angstrom per Bohr; multiply a Bohr value by it, divide an Angstrom value by it |
| `int` returns | 0 on success, -1 on failure, except `cpmdc_restart_is_stream` and `cpmdc_restart_ncoords` |
| errors | no error state in the library; readers and writers write the reason into the caller's `err` buffer of `err_cap` bytes, which may be `NULL` |
| units | coordinates and the initial geometry in Bohr, velocities in Bohr per atomic unit of time, in CPMD species order |

| Function | Contract |
|----------+----------|
| `CPMDCRestart *cpmdc_restart_read_mem(const void *bytes, size_t nbytes, char *err, size_t err_cap)` | parse an image from memory; the image owns a copy; `NULL` with the reason in `err` |
| `CPMDCRestart *cpmdc_restart_read_path(const char *path, char *err, size_t err_cap)` | read and parse a file; `NULL` with the reason in `err` |
| `void cpmdc_restart_free(CPMDCRestart *file)` | release an image; `NULL` is accepted |
| `int cpmdc_restart_is_stream(const CPMDCRestart *file)` | 1 when the file uses continuing (negative-marker) records, 0 otherwise or for `NULL` |
| `const char *cpmdc_restart_header(const CPMDCRestart *file)` | the section 1 header text, owned by the image; `NULL` when absent |
| `int cpmdc_restart_section(const CPMDCRestart *file, int section, int *count)` | the record count of section 1..99 in `*count` (1 for section 1, 0 for an empty one); -1 when the section is absent |
| `int cpmdc_restart_cell(const CPMDCRestart *file, int *ibrav, int *indpg, double celldm[6])` | `ibrav`, `indpg` (each may be `NULL`) and the six `celldm` values; -1 without a cell section |
| `int cpmdc_restart_species(const CPMDCRestart *file, int *nsp, const int **na_per_species)` | the species count and a pointer to the image's atom count per species, valid until the image is freed; -1 without a species section |
| `int cpmdc_restart_expand_species_symbols(const CPMDCRestart *file, const char *const *species_symbols, int nspecies, const char **atom_symbols, int n_atoms)` | one symbol pointer per coordinate, aliasing `species_symbols`; -1 when `nspecies` or `n_atoms` disagrees with the image or a symbol is empty |
| `int cpmdc_restart_ncoords(const CPMDCRestart *file)` | the number of coordinate triples in section 4; 0 when empty or for `NULL` |
| `int cpmdc_restart_coordinates(const CPMDCRestart *file, double *xyz, int n3)` | copy the coordinates, Bohr; `n3` must be `3 * ncoords` |
| `int cpmdc_restart_velocities(const CPMDCRestart *file, double *xyz, int n3)` | copy the velocities, Bohr per atomic unit of time; same size rule |
| `int cpmdc_restart_initial_coordinates(const CPMDCRestart *file, double *xyz, int n3)` | copy the initial geometry of section 6, Bohr; same size rule |
| `int cpmdc_restart_set_coordinates(CPMDCRestart *file, const double *xyz, int n3)` | replace the coordinate records, Bohr; another `n3` returns -1 and leaves the image unchanged |
| `int cpmdc_restart_set_velocities(CPMDCRestart *file, const double *xyz, int n3)` | replace the velocity records, Bohr per atomic unit of time; same rule |
| `int cpmdc_restart_set_cell(CPMDCRestart *file, const double celldm[6])` | replace the six lattice parameters; -1 without a cell section |
| `int cpmdc_restart_cutoff(const CPMDCRestart *file, double *ecut, double *cdual, int *dual_flag, int *nel, int *nr1s, int *nr2s, int *nr3s)` | the section 7 cutoff, real dual factor `cdual`, logical `dual_flag` (0 or 1), `nel`, and grid sizes; each output may be `NULL`; -1 without the section |
| `int cpmdc_restart_states(const CPMDCRestart *file, int *n, int *nkpts, int *ngw, int *ngwl, int *nhg, int *nhgl)` | the state, k-point and plane-wave counts; each output may be `NULL`; -1 without the section |
| `int cpmdc_restart_write_mem(const CPMDCRestart *file, void **bytes, size_t *nbytes, char *err, size_t err_cap)` | serialize the image into a `malloc` buffer the caller releases with `free` |
| `int cpmdc_restart_write_path(const CPMDCRestart *file, const char *path, char *err, size_t err_cap)` | write the image to `path` |

Editing coordinates or velocities rewrites only those 24-byte records and copies
every other record, the wavefunction among them, byte for byte.
The host endianness must match the file (little endian for gfortran on x86_64
and aarch64).
The `cpmdc-restart` command exposes `info`, `positions`, `velocities`,
`patch-positions`, and `patch-velocities`, with `--angstrom` for Angstrom input
and output (Angstrom per atomic unit of time for velocities), and, in a
`-Dwith_readcon=true` build, `export-con` and `import-con`.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/contracts.org

Every public name of cpmdc has one entry on this page: the exported C functions, the C types and constants, the Python names that each module lists in `__all__` with the public members of its classes, and the properties and parameters of the ASE calculator. Each entry states the units, the array layout or shape, who owns every pointer or object, what threads and MPI ranks may do, every return or error code with the Python exception it becomes, and the defaults.

The `reference-audit` test keeps the page and the code together. It reads the C names from the headers that `meson install` places, and the Python names from the imported package. It fails when a public name has no entry, when an entry names a symbol that does not exist, when a Python signature row differs from the one `inspect` reports, and when a row that must say something is empty. The other reference pages explain the behaviour at more length: the C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org), the Python reference (file:python.org), the GROMACS page (file:gromacs.org) and the LAMMPS page (file:lammps.org).

# Conventions

Units are stated in every entry. The array calls of the C library take positions in Angstrom and give Hartree and Hartree/Bohr. `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` takes Bohr and gives Hartree, Hartree/Bohr and a virial `-dE/d(strain)` in Hartree. The stress of the C library has the OpenCPMD sign `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)` in Hartree/Bohr^3, which is the opposite of ASE's. The Python `Potential` and the ASE calculator return eV, eV/Angstrom and eV/Angstrom^3 with the ASE sign. `Session` returns the atomic units of the C ABI.

Arrays are C order and atom-major: `x0 y0 z0 x1 ...`. A matrix is row-major with one lattice vector per row, except in the i-PI wire, where the cell holds the lattice vectors as columns. Atomic numbers are `int` values in 1..118.

Threads: the C library keeps the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state in process globals, so evaluation, configuration and session calls are used by one thread at a time. The error text of `cpmdc_last_error()` is per thread. The snapshot readers share the globals of the evaluation. The static restart library has no global state.

MPI: a build compiled without MPI never calls it. A reference build compiled
with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache
path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized, so every rank
agrees before a stored result is returned. The same setting runs the
collectives in `rank_consensus` on an evaluation. An OpenCPMD build also runs
the evaluation as a collective on the calculator communicator, so every rank
of a calculator makes the same call in the same order. The Python package
never calls MPI itself; `cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal` gathers on rank 0 with
`mpi4py`.

Errors: a C call reports failure in the return value and writes the reason to `cpmdc_last_error()` of the calling thread. The Python package turns every such failure into `cpmdc.CPMDCError`, and it raises `ValueError` or `TypeError` for an argument that it can reject before the call.

# C functions

## Library status

Calls that report the build and the failure text. None of them evaluates.

### ~cpmdc_version~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | Returns a pointer to a static NUL-terminated string, `cpmdc/` followed by the project version; the caller never frees it and it lives as long as the library. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: read-only data. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail. `cpmdc_last_error()` is not written. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.version`, which returns the same text; no exception. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_abi_version~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | none |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: read-only data. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail; returns the ABI generation, equal to `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION` of the header the library was built from. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.abi_version`; no exception. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_available~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | none |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe on the first call, which initialises the embed once; call it from one thread before others start. MPI: local, the call does not communicate. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail; 1 when OpenCPMD is linked, ready and not finalized, 0 on the reference build, after `cpmdc_finalize()` and from the link stub. `cpmdc_last_error()` is not written. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.available`; no exception. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_finalize~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | none: live `CPMDCSession` objects stay valid and the caller still destroys them. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: call once, from the thread that ran the evaluations, after the last evaluation. MPI: does not call `MPI_Finalize` and does not communicate; call it on every rank. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail. In the reference and OpenCPMD builds, later calls that need the runtime fail with `CPMD embed not available`: the no-session evaluations, `cpmdc_set_params()`, `cpmdc_configure()`, and a session evaluation of any step but the one that session stored last. A session evaluation that repeats its stored step still returns 0 from the session's cache, and `cpmdc_last_error()` stays empty. The link stub does nothing and its evaluations always fail with `OpenCPMD embed not available in cpmdc stub` followed by the called function's name in parentheses. |
| Python | not wrapped; `cpmdc.Session` never finalizes the runtime. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_error~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | Returns a pointer to the calling thread's own NUL-terminated buffer of 512 bytes; the caller never frees it, and the text lasts until the next `cpmdc_` call that writes it on that thread. Copy it to keep it. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: each thread reads its own buffer, so a failure on one thread never shows on another. MPI: local to each rank. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail; the text is empty after a successful call of a function that writes it. See the table of writers in the C ABI reference. |
| Python | the text of `cpmdc.CPMDCError`; the package reads it after each failing call. |
| Defaults | empty string before any call |

### ~cpmdc_last_error_code~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | none: the code is returned by value, so there is nothing to free. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: each thread reads its own code, written together with its `cpmdc_last_error()` text. MPI: local to each rank; the gate messages of a collective evaluation map to the same code on every rank. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail. The code is `CPMDC_ERROR_NONE` when the text is empty and otherwise names the failure: a bad argument, an unavailable backend, periodic embedding, an evaluation that produced no result, or a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` combined with session charges. A later failure replaces an earlier code. |
| Python | the `code` attribute of `cpmdc.CPMDCError` and of its subclasses; a library without the symbol gives code 0. |
| Defaults | `CPMDC_ERROR_NONE` before any call |

## MPI calculator binding

Calls that choose the communicator of one calculator. See the MPI how-to for the sequence.

### ~cpmdc_bind_calculator~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: `ranks_per_calc` is a rank count; the world is split into consecutive blocks of that size, group `g` holding world ranks `g * ranks_per_calc` to `(g + 1) * ranks_per_calc - 1`. |
| Ownership | none: the library keeps the new communicator and the caller cannot free it. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: call from one thread, before the first evaluation. MPI: collective on `MPI_COMM_WORLD`; on an OpenCPMD build it initialises MPI when it is not running, and the reference build and the link stub never call MPI; it splits the world with `MPI_Comm_split`; every rank passes the same value. |
| Returns and errors | Returns this rank's calculator index `world_rank / ranks_per_calc`, 0 or more; -1 when the world size is not a multiple of `ranks_per_calc` (no remainder group is made, nothing is split, and every rank gets -1), `MPI_Comm_split` returns an error, or the library has no CPMD backend (the reference build and the link stub always return -1); the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. A second call does not split again; it checks its own `ranks_per_calc` as the first call does, returns the index that value gives, or returns -1 on every rank when the value does not divide the world size or is above it, and the existing split stays. |
| Python | not wrapped; use `cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal` or the host's own communicator. |
| Defaults | `ranks_per_calc` zero or less takes the whole world as one calculator |

### ~cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `comm` points at one `MPI_Comm` of exactly `comm_bytes` bytes (the size of `MPI_Comm` in the host's MPI); `ranks_per_calc` is a rank count. |
| Ownership | `comm` is borrowed: the library copies the handle, does not call `MPI_Comm_dup`, and the caller keeps the communicator alive until the last session is destroyed or a later adopt replaces it. The caller owns `comm` and the library never frees it. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: call, `cpmdc_session_create()` and `cpmdc_session_destroy()` from one thread. MPI: collective on `comm`; does not call `MPI_Init` or `MPI_Comm_split`; the group must be one aligned block of world ranks, and every rank of it passes the same `ranks_per_calc`. |
| Returns and errors | Returns the calculator index (0 or more); -1 when `comm` is NULL, `comm_bytes` is not the size of `MPI_Comm`, MPI is not initialized, the build has no MPI, the size differs from a positive `ranks_per_calc`, the group is not an aligned block, or a rank of the group has a live session that has evaluated; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. On -1 the stored communicator is unchanged. |
| Python | `cpmdc.CPMDCError` in `cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal`, which adopts `MPI_COMM_SELF` on rank 0. |
| Defaults | `ranks_per_calc` zero or less skips the size check |

### ~cpmdc_adopted_comm~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `out` receives one `MPI_Comm` of exactly `nbytes` bytes. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the copied handle is borrowed from the adopted communicator and is valid while that communicator is. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a concurrent adopt. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when a calculator communicator is stored; -1 when `out` is NULL, `nbytes` is not the size of `MPI_Comm`, or none has been adopted. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

## Configuration and one-shot arrays without a session

These calls use the process-wide state.
An evaluation is cold when the process has no stored basis or the basis
differs, and warm when the basis matches.

### ~cpmdc_params_method~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `functional` is a method token, `charge` is an integer elementary-charge count, and `multiplicity` is dimensionless. |
| Layout | `params_capnp` points at `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message; `out` points at one `CPMDCMethodInfo`. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `params_capnp` and `out` and may free them on return; the library keeps nothing. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe except for the thread-local error text. MPI: local, no communication and no OpenCPMD initialization. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 after filling `out`; -1 for a NULL output, a NULL or empty message, a parse failure, or unreadable effective settings. Failure text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | `cpmdc.params_method` returns the corresponding frozen `cpmdc.MethodInfo`. |
| Defaults | Top-level functional `BLYP`, charge 0 and multiplicity 1; a structured DFT or SYSTEM typed field takes precedence when it is explicit, and a typed SYSTEM charge of 0 is explicit only with `hasCharge` `true`. |

### ~cpmdc_set_params~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the message carries its own units (the schema names them per field). |
| Layout | `params_capnp` points at `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `params_capnp` and may free it on return; the library copies what it keeps. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; the reference build does no MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 on a NULL or empty buffer, a parse failure or a configuration failure; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped; `cpmdc.Session` takes the bytes instead. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_configure~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the overlay fields carry their own units (`planewaveCutoffEv` eV, `scfEnergyToleranceEv` eV). |
| Layout | `config_capnp` points at `config_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `PotentialConfig` message. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `config_capnp` and may free it on return. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; the reference build does no MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 on a NULL or empty buffer, a parse or lowering failure, a `cpmd` arm together with overlay `kMesh`, `scfMaxIterations`, `scfEnergyToleranceEv`, `vanDerWaalsMethod`, or `relativityMethod`, an unmapped `xcFunctionals` token for any arm functional, a set overlay scalar, an explicit `spinMultiplicity` of 1 and zero `charge` with `hasCharge` `true` included and whether or not a typed field also sets it, while `inputBlocks`, a raw section, or a generic section opens the owning `&DFT` or `&SYSTEM` section, a set directive names `DFT.FUNCTIONAL`, `SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or `SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY`, or the typed `dft` section holds a `FUNCTIONAL` directive or the typed `system` section holds a `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY` directive, Fermi `smearing` next to `FREE-ENERGY` or `TEMPERATURE ELECTRON` controls (including split `TEMPERATURE` and `ELECTRON` arguments in `cpmd.directives` or `CPMD.TEMPERATURE` set directives), a `FUNCTIONAL` directive in the typed `dft` section or a `DFT.FUNCTIONAL` set directive next to the functional the deck renders, a `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY` directive in the typed `system` section or a `SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or `SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY` set directive, rejected for a default value and for any other value alike, an arm `inputBlocks`, `inputSections`, or `directives` list the merge cannot read, or an overlay field without a CPMD lowering when the arm is unset; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and names the cause. A typed field that is omitted or holds its schema default is unset, including a typed `system` charge of 0 with `hasCharge` `false`, while `hasCharge` `true` marks zero charge explicit. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_energy_gradient~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; `grad_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr; `energy_h` of the result in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major (`x0 y0 z0 x1 ...`), C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `params_capnp` is `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes; `grad_h_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles laid out as the positions. |
| Ownership | The caller owns every buffer and may reuse or free all of them on return; the library keeps nothing. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls the collectives in `rank_consensus` when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is non-zero on success. Otherwise `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` (a failed message parse, a missing pseudopotential directory, a failed SCF). An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none: the gradient is `dE/dR`, the negative of the force |

### ~cpmdc_energy~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; the returned energy in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `params_capnp` is `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes. |
| Ownership | The caller owns every buffer; the library keeps nothing. It evaluates the gradient into a temporary array that it frees before returning. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls the collectives in `rank_consensus` when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_energy_forces~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; `forces_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr; the returned energy in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `params_capnp` is `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes; `forces_h_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles laid out as the positions. |
| Ownership | The caller owns every buffer and may free all of them on return. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls the collectives in `rank_consensus` when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none: forces are the negative nuclear gradient |

## Session lifetime and configuration

A session is created by one of two functions and released by `cpmdc_session_destroy()`.

### ~cpmdc_session_create~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the message carries its own units. |
| Layout | `params_capnp` points at `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message. |
| Ownership | Returns a new `CPMDCSession` that the caller owns and releases with `cpmdc_session_destroy()`; the session copies `params_capnp`, so the caller may free it on return. A session holds no MPI object. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: create, use and destroy sessions from one thread. MPI: not collective; every rank of a calculator creates its own session from the same message. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL on a NULL or empty buffer, a parse failure or a render failure; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session` constructor raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError` with that text. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_create_from_config~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the overlay fields carry their own units. |
| Layout | `config_capnp` points at `config_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `PotentialConfig` message. |
| Ownership | Returns a new `CPMDCSession` that the caller owns and releases with `cpmdc_session_destroy()`; `config_capnp` may be freed on return. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time. MPI: not collective; every rank creates its own session. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL on any failure `cpmdc_configure()` reports; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_set_params~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the message carries its own units. |
| Layout | `params_capnp` points at `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `CPMDParams` message. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; `params_capnp` may be freed on return, since the session copies it. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL session, a NULL or empty buffer, a parse failure, or a session that has accepted a topology (`session topology is already fixed`). A successful call also drops any common overlay a `cpmdc_session_configure()` call installed. A failed call leaves the session exactly as it was (parameters, deck, effective settings, overlay, and embed state) and only the text of `cpmdc_last_error()` changes. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_configure~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: the overlay fields carry their own units. |
| Layout | `config_capnp` points at `config_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `PotentialConfig` message. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; `config_capnp` may be freed on return. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
