| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL session, a session that has evaluated, or any failure `cpmdc_configure()` reports; a failed call keeps the previous parameters and overlay, and the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `cutoff_ry`, `height_ry` and `width_ry` in Rydberg. |
| Layout | none: `cutoff_ry`, `height_ry` and `width_ry` are three scalar doubles. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL session, a value that is not finite, a session that has accepted a topology, E0 + 2 sigma above the deck cutoff, a message that sets `system.constantCutoff`, or a raw `&SYSTEM` block; the session keeps its previous setting and the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. The link stub returns -1. |
| Python | `cpmdc.CPMDCError` from the `cpmdc.Session` constructor when `constant_cutoff=` is given. |
| Defaults | `cutoff_ry` zero or less turns the functional off; `height_ry` zero or less selects 50 times the deck cutoff; `width_ry` zero or less selects `cutoff_ry / 10` |

### ~cpmdc_session_set_external_charges~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` and `widths_ang` in Angstrom; `charges_e` in units of the elementary charge. |
| Layout | none: `positions_ang` holds `3 * n` doubles in C order, `charges_e` `n` doubles, and `widths_ang` `n` doubles or NULL for the default width of 0.30 Angstrom (or `CPMDC_EXTERNAL_CHARGE_WIDTH_ANG` when set). |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the library copies `positions_ang`, `charges_e` and `widths_ang`, so the caller keeps and may free them on return. `n` of 0 clears the set. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 with `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a NULL session, NULL arrays with `n` above 0, a value that is not finite, or a width below 1e-12 Angstrom; the previous set is kept. The link stub returns -1 with `CPMDC_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE`. A periodic or deck-potential clash is reported by the next evaluation, not by this call. A successful call clears `cpmdc_last_error()`, and every failure writes it. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.set_external_charges` raises `cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument`. |
| Defaults | no external charges |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | Hartree/Bohr. |
| Layout | none: `forces_h_bohr` holds `3 * n` doubles in C order for the `n` charges of the last successful evaluation, in the order they were set. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns the output buffer `forces_h_bohr`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe only with the session: one thread at a time. MPI: local to the rank, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 and clears `cpmdc_last_error()`, or -1 with `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a NULL session or buffer, a length that is not `3 * n`, or no successful evaluation with charges. The link stub returns -1 with `CPMDC_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE`. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.external_charge_forces_au` raises `cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_destroy~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: the only argument is the handle. |
| Ownership | Frees `session` and everything it owns; the handle is invalid afterwards and must not be used or destroyed again. NULL is accepted and does nothing. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time. MPI: not collective and does not communicate; every rank destroys its own session. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail, and `cpmdc_last_error()` is not written. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.close` (also on leaving a `with` block and when the object is collected). |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_select_orbitals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: `key` is one `long long` chosen by the host; any value is valid. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the library keeps the converged orbitals of each key inside the process until a basis change clears them. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 and clears `cpmdc_last_error()`, or -1 for a NULL session (`null session`). The call only records the key; the next evaluation applies it. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.select_orbitals` raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`. |
| Defaults | a session that never names a key keeps one stored copy |

### ~cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: `from_key` and `to_key` are `long long` keys chosen by the host. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the copy lives in the process store until a basis change clears it. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, and never during an evaluation. MPI: local to the rank, no communication; every rank of a calculator makes the same call before the same evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL session, before any evaluation, when `from_key` has no converged orbitals, or when the backend copy fails; the text is `cpmdc_last_error()`. The reference build has no orbital store: it returns 0 after any evaluation and copies nothing. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.copy_orbitals` raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`, also for a library that lacks the symbol. |
| Defaults | none |

## Session evaluation

`session_accept_topology` fixes the topology only after an evaluation call
passes its argument checks and collective orbital preflight. A rejected
preflight leaves the topology configurable; see the C ABI reference.
More than 1365 atoms fails that preflight with
`property gradient snapshot supports at most 1365 atoms`, before the topology
is fixed. A session that already holds another system reports the topology
change instead of the atom limit.

### ~cpmdc_session_energy_gradient~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; `grad_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr; the returned energy in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `grad_h_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles laid out as the positions. No cell is passed: the deck's `CELL` applies, or a 12 Angstrom cube. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `positions_ang`, `atomic_numbers` and `grad_h_bohr`, and the library copies the geometry into the session. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | not wrapped; `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` calls `cpmdc_session_energy_forces()` and raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_energy~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; the returned energy in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118. No cell is passed. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `positions_ang` and `atomic_numbers`. A temporary gradient array is allocated and freed inside the call. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_energy_forces~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_ang` in Angstrom; `forces_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr; the returned energy in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_ang` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major, C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `forces_h_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles laid out as the positions. No cell is passed. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `positions_ang`, `atomic_numbers` and `forces_h_bohr`. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, before a session fixes its topology. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` without a cell raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`; the sizes, the range of the atomic numbers and the finiteness are checked first and raise `ValueError`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_calculate_forces~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `force_input_capnp` carries its own `lengthUnit` and `energyUnit`; `forces_h_bohr` is always Hartree/Bohr and the returned energy Hartree, whatever the message says. |
| Layout | `force_input_capnp` is `force_input_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `ForceInput`; `forces_h_bohr` holds `forces_len` doubles, and `forces_len` must be at least `3 * n_atoms`, atom-major, C order. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `force_input_capnp` and the output array `forces_h_bohr`. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0, `energy_h` is 0 and `message` names the reason; the same text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output array is unspecified. `ok` is non-zero on success and `cpmdc_last_error()` is empty. An atomic number outside 1..118 fails with `atomic numbers must be in 1..118`, and a `box` whose length is neither 0 nor 9 fails with `invalid ForceInput geometry`. A non-zero `box` in Angstrom fails before a session fixes its topology for a non-finite component (`cell contains a non-finite component`), rank below 3 under the `numpy.linalg.matrix_rank` cutoff (`sigma_max * 3 * DBL_EPSILON`) or a zero scaled LU determinant (`cell does not have three independent vectors`), or a normal-range Angstrom volume underflow (`cell volume is too small for binary64`); an isolated deck also refuses an off-diagonal or non-positive-diagonal box, and the reference evaluator fails a non-zero periodic cell whose Bohr stress volume overflows or is not positive (`cell volume is too large for binary64` or `cell volume is not representable for stress`). |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` with a cell encodes a `ForceInput` in process and raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`. |
| Defaults | `ForceInput` unit strings left empty read as `angstrom` and `hartree` |

### ~cpmdc_session_calculate_result~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `force_input_capnp` carries its own `lengthUnit` and `energyUnit`; the `PotentialResult` energy is in `energyUnit`, forces in `energyUnit` per `lengthUnit`, stress in `energyUnit` per `lengthUnit` cubed; the returned `energy_h` is Hartree. |
| Layout | `force_input_capnp` is `force_input_capnp_size_bytes` bytes; `potential_result_capnp` has room for `potential_result_capnp_capacity_bytes` bytes and receives one unpacked flat `PotentialResult`; `potential_result_capnp_size_bytes` is one `size_t` that receives the byte count. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `force_input_capnp`, `potential_result_capnp` and `potential_result_capnp_size_bytes`; the written message does not alias the session. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0 with `message` and `cpmdc_last_error()` naming the reason for a NULL session or buffer, an invalid message (including a `box` length other than 0 or 9 with `invalid ForceInput geometry`), an atomic number outside 1..118, a non-zero `box` failing finiteness (`cell contains a non-finite component`), rank 3 under `sigma_max * 3 * DBL_EPSILON` (`cell does not have three independent vectors`), or Angstrom volume underflow (`cell volume is too small for binary64`) before topology is fixed, an isolated deck given an off-diagonal or non-positive-diagonal box, a topology change, or a failed evaluation (including `cell volume is too large for binary64` or `cell volume is not representable for stress` in the reference evaluator). `*potential_result_capnp_size_bytes` is written before the capacity is checked: a capacity that is too small gives `ok` 0 with `PotentialResult buffer too small` and no evaluation. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_calculate_au~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `positions_bohr` and `cell_bohr` in Bohr; `energy_h` in Hartree; `forces_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr; `virial_h` in Hartree. |
| Layout | `positions_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles, atom-major (`x0 y0 z0 x1 ...`), C order; `atomic_numbers` is `n_atoms` ints in 1..118; `cell_bohr` is NULL or 9 doubles, row-major, one lattice vector per row; `energy_h` is one double; `forces_h_bohr` is `3 * n_atoms` doubles laid out as the positions; `virial_h` is NULL or 9 doubles, row-major. |
| Ownership | `session` stays owned by the caller; the caller owns every array, none is kept after the call, and the outputs are written only on success. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL session (`null session`), `n_atoms` outside 1 to `INT_MAX / 3` or a NULL required pointer (`invalid arguments`), an atomic number outside 1..118 (`atomic numbers must be in 1..118`), a non-zero `cell_bohr` whose converted Angstrom cell has a non-finite component (`cell contains a non-finite component`), rank below 3 under `sigma_max * 3 * DBL_EPSILON` (`cell does not have three independent vectors`), or a normal-range volume underflow (`cell volume is too small for binary64`) before topology is fixed, a topology change, a failed evaluation (including `cell volume is too large for binary64` or `cell volume is not representable for stress` in the reference evaluator), a finite cell whose Bohr volume is above `DBL_MAX` when `virial_h` is not NULL (`cell volume is too large for binary64`, before the evaluation), or a virial component that is not finite (`virial is not finite`); the text is `cpmdc_last_error()` and the output arrays are unspecified. The volume is `abs(det cell_bohr)` by LU with partial pivoting on the cell scaled by a power of two, so it neither cancels to zero for an accepted near-singular cell nor overflows before the final scaling. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.calculate_au` raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError`; wrong sizes, non-finite values and atomic numbers outside 1..118 raise `ValueError` before the call, and a wrong type raises `TypeError`. |
| Defaults | `cell_bohr` NULL is a system without a cell; `virial_h` NULL skips the virial |

## One-shot message calls

Each call creates a session, evaluates one step and destroys the session.

### ~cpmdc_calculate_result~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | units of `force_input_capnp` and of the `PotentialResult` as for `cpmdc_session_calculate_result()`; the returned `energy_h` is Hartree. |
| Layout | `params_capnp` is `params_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of `CPMDParams`; `force_input_capnp` is `force_input_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of `ForceInput`; `potential_result_capnp` has room for `potential_result_capnp_capacity_bytes` bytes; `potential_result_capnp_size_bytes` is one `size_t`. |
| Ownership | The caller owns every buffer; the session the call creates is destroyed before it returns. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | `ok` is 0 with `message` and `cpmdc_last_error()` naming the reason for a NULL or empty input, an invalid message, a buffer that is too small (`PotentialResult buffer too small`, with the required size in `*potential_result_capnp_size_bytes`) or a failed step. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_calculate_result_from_config~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | As for `cpmdc_calculate_result()`: `force_input_capnp` carries its own `lengthUnit` and `energyUnit`, the `PotentialResult` energy is in `energyUnit`, and the returned `energy_h` is Hartree. |
| Layout | `config_capnp` is `config_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one `PotentialConfig`; `force_input_capnp` is `force_input_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one `ForceInput`; `potential_result_capnp` has room for `potential_result_capnp_capacity_bytes` bytes; `potential_result_capnp_size_bytes` is one `size_t`. |
| Ownership | The caller owns every buffer; the session is destroyed before the call returns. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: the active calculator, its stored orbitals and the OpenCPMD state are process globals, so one thread at a time. MPI: collective on the calculator communicator when OpenCPMD is linked, so every rank passes the same arguments in the same order; a reference build compiled with MPI calls `MPI_Allreduce` from `rank_consensus_all` on the session cache path when `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` is `1` and MPI is initialized. |
| Returns and errors | As for `cpmdc_calculate_result()`: `ok` is 0 with `message` and `cpmdc_last_error()` naming the reason, with the failures of `cpmdc_configure()` added; `ok` is non-zero on success. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_potential_result_size_for_force_input~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: a byte count. |
| Layout | `force_input_capnp` is `force_input_capnp_size_bytes` bytes of one unpacked flat `ForceInput`. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `force_input_capnp`; nothing is kept. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe for distinct inputs apart from `cpmdc_last_error()`, which is per thread. MPI: local, no communication, no evaluation. |
| Returns and errors | Returns the byte count; 0 when the message is invalid or too large for the C ABI, with the reason in `cpmdc_last_error()`. A success clears it. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

## Discovery

Read-only tables and the capabilities message.

### ~cpmdc_capabilities_result~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: names fields; `planewaveCutoffEv` and `scfEnergyToleranceEv` are listed as eV fields. |
| Layout | `capabilities_capnp` is NULL for the size query or a buffer of `capabilities_capnp_capacity_bytes` bytes that receives one unpacked flat `Capabilities` message; `capabilities_capnp_size_bytes` is one `size_t` and required. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `capabilities_capnp` and `capabilities_capnp_size_bytes`; the library keeps nothing. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe once `cpmdc_available()` has run on one thread. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success; -1 with the required size in `*capabilities_capnp_size_bytes` when the buffer is too small (the pure size query is NULL and 0), and -1 for a NULL size pointer. The -1 does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_feature_count~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none |
| Ownership | none |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: read-only data. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail; returns the row count of the table. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_feature_table~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: the table is `cpmdc_feature_count()` contiguous `CPMDCFeatureEntry` rows. |
| Ownership | Returns a pointer to the library's static table; the caller never frees or modifies it, and it lives as long as the library. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: read-only data. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail; never NULL. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_feature_find~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `feature_id` is one NUL-terminated string. |
| Ownership | Returns a pointer into the static table, owned by the library; `feature_id` stays owned by the caller. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe: read-only data. MPI: local, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL when `feature_id` is NULL or names no row; `cpmdc_last_error()` is not written. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

## Result snapshots

Each getter copies one snapshot struct and returns 0 when it is valid.

### ~cpmdc_last_energy_components~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCEnergyComponents` in Hartree. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCEnergyComponents` that the call overwrites whole; its `valid` field says whether the snapshot was written. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the library keeps nothing and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 when the snapshot is absent or `out` is NULL. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads the calculator that ran last: the active session, or the global state after a global call. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_energy_components~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCEnergyComponents` in Hartree. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCEnergyComponents` that the call overwrites whole. |
| Ownership | `session` is borrowed and stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `out` and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 for a NULL session, a NULL `out`, or an absent snapshot. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads that session's own last result, also after another session has run. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_charge_integrals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` in electrons. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` that the call overwrites whole; its `valid` field says whether the snapshot was written. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the library keeps nothing and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 when the snapshot is absent or `out` is NULL. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads the calculator that ran last: the active session, or the global state after a global call. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_charge_integrals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` in electrons. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCChargeIntegrals` that the call overwrites whole. |
| Ownership | `session` is borrowed and stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `out` and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 for a NULL session, a NULL `out`, or an absent snapshot. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads that session's own last result, also after another session has run. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_multi_state_energies~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies` in Hartree. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCMultiStateEnergies` that the call overwrites whole; its `valid` field says whether the snapshot was written. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the library keeps nothing and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 when the snapshot is absent or `out` is NULL. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads the calculator that ran last: the active session, or the global state after a global call. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 for a NULL session, a NULL `out`, or an absent snapshot. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads that session's own last result, also after another session has run. |

### ~cpmdc_last_gradient~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `out` receives the nuclear gradient in Hartree/Bohr; `capacity` and `count` count doubles. |
| Layout | `out` points at `capacity` doubles; `count` points at one `size_t` that receives the required component count. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out` and `count`; the copied gradient does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 after copying the complete gradient; -1 for a NULL argument, no valid gradient, a zero-length gradient, or insufficient `capacity`. The legacy snapshot limits successful evaluations to 4096 components. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped; `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` returns the force, the negative of this gradient. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_gradient~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `out` receives the nuclear gradient in Hartree/Bohr; `capacity` and `count` count doubles. |
| Layout | `out` points at `capacity` doubles; `count` points at one `size_t` that receives the required component count. |
| Ownership | `session` is borrowed and stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `out` and `count`, and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation on that session: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 after copying the session's complete last gradient; -1 for a NULL argument, no valid gradient, a zero-length gradient, or insufficient `capacity`. The legacy snapshot limits successful evaluations to 4096 components. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped; `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` returns the force, the negative of this gradient. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_dipole~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCDipole` in electron Bohr. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCDipole` that the call clears before checking availability. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the copied dipole does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 only when OpenCPMD recomputed the dipole for the current geometry; -1 for NULL `out` or when the reference, isolated, k-point, or unrequested evaluation has no dipole. An unavailable call leaves `out->valid` zero and does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | not wrapped directly; `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` uses the session form. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_dipole~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCDipole` in electron Bohr. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCDipole` that the call clears before checking availability. |
| Ownership | `session` is borrowed and stays owned by the caller; the caller owns `out` and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation on that session: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 only when that session's last evaluation recomputed the dipole for its current geometry; -1 for a NULL argument or when the reference, isolated, k-point, or unrequested evaluation has no dipole. An unavailable call leaves `out->valid` zero and does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` reads this value; -1 gives `Evaluation.dipole_e_bohr` of `None`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_stress~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCStressTensor` in Hartree/Bohr^3. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCStressTensor` that the call overwrites whole; its `valid` field says whether the snapshot was written. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the library keeps nothing and the copy does not alias library memory. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation: read from the thread that evaluates. MPI: local to each rank, no communication; a rank holds its own snapshot. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set; -1 when the snapshot is absent or `out` is NULL. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. It reads the calculator that ran last: the active session, or the global state after a global call. The sign is OpenCPMD's, `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)`; ASE's stress is its negative. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session.energy_forces` reads the stress through the session form; -1 gives `Evaluation.stress_h_bohr3` of `None`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_session_last_stress~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | the fields of `CPMDCStressTensor` in Hartree/Bohr^3. |

| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_last_rank_spread~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `energy_h` in Hartree and `gradient_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr, as `CPMDCRankSpread` gives them. |
| Layout | `out` points at one `CPMDCRankSpread` that the call overwrites whole. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `out`; the library keeps nothing. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe against a running evaluation. MPI: local to each rank; the spread was measured with a collective during the evaluation under `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1`, and this call itself does not communicate. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when `out->valid` is set, that is the last evaluation ran with `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` under a running MPI; -1 otherwise or for a NULL `out`. Does not write `cpmdc_last_error()`. The spread belongs to the process, so there is no session form. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

## RESTART file library

These functions live in `libcpmdc_restart`, not in `libcpmdc`, and keep no error state.

### ~cpmdc_restart_read_mem~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: no argument is a quantity; `bytes` holds a RESTART image whose coordinates are Bohr and whose velocities are Bohr per atomic unit of time. |
| Layout | `bytes` is `nbytes` bytes of one gfortran sequential unformatted RESTART image; `err` is a buffer of `err_cap` bytes or NULL. |
| Ownership | Returns an image that the caller owns and releases with `cpmdc_restart_free()`; the image copies `bytes`, so the caller may free them on return; `err` is a caller-owned buffer that the library only writes. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL on a NULL or malformed buffer. Writes the reason into `err` (of `err_cap` bytes, NUL included, or NULL to skip it); the library keeps no error state. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_read_path~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: no argument is a quantity; the image's coordinates are Bohr, as for `cpmdc_restart_read_mem()`. |
| Layout | `path` is one NUL-terminated filesystem path; `err` is a buffer of `err_cap` bytes or NULL. |
| Ownership | Returns an image that the caller owns and releases with `cpmdc_restart_free()`; `path` stays owned by the caller; `err` is a caller-owned buffer that the library only writes. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL when the file cannot be read or parsed. Writes the reason into `err` (of `err_cap` bytes, NUL included, or NULL to skip it); the library keeps no error state. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_free~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: the only argument is the image. |
| Ownership | Frees `file` and every pointer taken from it (`cpmdc_restart_header()`, the array of `cpmdc_restart_species()`). NULL is accepted. The image must not be used afterwards. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | none: cannot fail. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_is_stream~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: the only argument is the image. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed and unchanged. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 1 for the continuing-record layout and 0 otherwise or for a NULL image; there is no -1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_header~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | none: the result is one NUL-terminated string. |
| Ownership | Returns a pointer into `file`, owned by the image and valid until `cpmdc_restart_free()`; the caller never frees it. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns NULL when the image has no header or is NULL. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_section~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `section` is a 1-based index in 1..99; `count` is one int or NULL. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `count`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when the section is present and -1 otherwise (a NULL image, a section outside 1..99, an absent section); `*count` is 1 for section 1 and 0 for an empty one. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | `count` NULL skips the count |

### ~cpmdc_restart_cell~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `celldm` holds the six CPMD lattice parameters of the file (`celldm[0]` in Bohr, the others ratios and cosines, as CPMD stores them). |
| Layout | `celldm` is 6 doubles and required; `ibrav` and `indpg` are one int each or NULL. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `celldm`, `ibrav` and `indpg`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when the cell section is present and -1 for a NULL image, a NULL `celldm` or no cell section. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | `ibrav` and `indpg` NULL skip them |

### ~cpmdc_restart_species~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: counts of atoms. |
| Layout | `nsp` is one int or NULL; `na_per_species` is one pointer to an int array of `*nsp` entries, or NULL. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed. `nsp` is a caller-owned int that the call only writes. `*na_per_species` points at the image's own array: the caller never frees it, and it is valid until the image is freed or rewritten. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when the species section is present and -1 otherwise. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | `nsp` and `na_per_species` NULL skip them |

### ~cpmdc_restart_expand_species_symbols~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `species_symbols` is `nspecies` NUL-terminated strings; `atom_symbols` receives `n_atoms` pointers and is required; `nspecies` and `n_atoms` must match the image. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed. `atom_symbols[i]` aliases `species_symbols[s]` and no string is copied: the caller keeps `species_symbols` alive as long as it uses `atom_symbols`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument, a species count other than `nspecies`, an empty symbol, or an atom count other than `n_atoms`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_ncoords~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: a count of coordinate triples. |
| Layout | none: the only argument is the image. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed and unchanged. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns the triple count of section 4, or 0 when that section is empty or the image is NULL; there is no -1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_coordinates~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `xyz` receives the coordinates in Bohr. |
| Layout | `xyz` is `n3` doubles, `ncoords * 3`, in CPMD species order and then atom order, x y z each; `n3` must equal `ncoords * 3`. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `xyz`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument, another `n3` or a malformed record; `xyz` is unspecified on -1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_velocities~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `xyz` receives the velocities in Bohr per atomic unit of time. |
| Layout | `xyz` is `n3` doubles, `ncoords * 3`, in CPMD species order and then atom order, x y z each; `n3` must equal `ncoords * 3`. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `xyz`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument, another `n3` or a malformed record; `xyz` is unspecified on -1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_initial_coordinates~

| Layout | `xyz` is `n3` doubles, `ncoords * 3`, in CPMD species order and then atom order, x y z each; `n3` must equal `ncoords * 3`. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `xyz`. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument, another `n3` or a malformed record; `xyz` is unspecified on -1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |

### ~cpmdc_restart_set_coordinates~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `xyz` holds the new coordinate records in Bohr. |
| Layout | `xyz` is `n3` doubles, `ncoords * 3`, in CPMD species order and then atom order; `n3` must equal `ncoords * 3`. |
| Ownership | `file` is modified in place; the caller owns `xyz`, which the image copies. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument or another `n3`; the image is unchanged on -1. Every other record, the wavefunction included, is kept byte for byte. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_set_velocities~

| Layout | `xyz` is `n3` doubles, `ncoords * 3`, in CPMD species order and then atom order; `n3` must equal `ncoords * 3`. |
| Ownership | `file` is modified in place; the caller owns `xyz`, which the image copies. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |

### ~cpmdc_restart_set_cell~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `celldm` holds the six CPMD lattice parameters, as `cpmdc_restart_cell()` returns them: the first is a length in Bohr, the rest are dimensionless ratios and angle cosines. |

| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 for a NULL argument or an image without a cell section. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_cutoff~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `ecut` in Rydberg as CPMD stores it; `cdual` is a dimensionless ratio; `nel` and the grid sizes are counts. |
| Layout | `ecut` and `cdual` are each one double, and `dual_flag`, `nel`, `nr1s`, `nr2s` and `nr3s` are each one int; every output may be NULL. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `ecut`, `cdual`, `dual_flag`, `nel`, `nr1s`, `nr2s` and `nr3s`, which the call only writes. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when section 7 is present and -1 otherwise. `dual_flag` is the logical `dual` of the file (0 or 1), not the factor `cdual`. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | an output NULL skips that value |

### ~cpmdc_restart_states~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: counts of states, k-points and plane waves. |
| Layout | `n`, `nkpts`, `ngw`, `ngwl`, `nhg` and `nhgl` are each one int; every output may be NULL. |
| Ownership | `file` is borrowed; the caller owns `n`, `nkpts`, `ngw`, `ngwl`, `nhg` and `nhgl`, which the call only writes. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 when the section is present and -1 otherwise. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | an output NULL skips that value |

### ~cpmdc_restart_write_mem~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: bytes are copied as stored, in Bohr. |
| Layout | `bytes` is one `void *` that receives the buffer; `nbytes` is one `size_t` that receives its length; `err` is a buffer of `err_cap` bytes or NULL. |
| Ownership | The buffer `*bytes` comes from `malloc` and the caller releases it with `free`; `nbytes` and `err` are caller-owned and only written; `file` is borrowed. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. Writes the reason into `err` (of `err_cap` bytes, NUL included, or NULL to skip it); the library keeps no error state. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc_restart_write_path~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none: bytes are copied as stored, in Bohr. |
| Layout | `path` is one NUL-terminated filesystem path; `err` is a buffer of `err_cap` bytes or NULL. |
| Ownership | `file`, `path` and `err` stay owned by the caller; `err` is only written. The file is written to a temporary file in the same directory, synced, and renamed over `path`, so a reader sees the old or the finished file. |
| Threads and MPI | Thread-safe on distinct images; one image must not be used by two threads at once when either writes. MPI: none, the library never calls MPI. |
| Returns and errors | Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure, with the reason in `err`; a failure before the rename leaves `path` untouched, and a failure to sync the directory returns -1 with `path` already holding the new image. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

## libcp2k shim for GROMACS

Declared in the installed `gromacs/libcp2k.h` with CP2K's signatures and served by `libcpmdc_gromacs`.

### ~cp2k_get_version~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | none |
| Layout | `version_str` is a buffer of `str_length` chars that receives one NUL-terminated string. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `version_str`. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: GROMACS calls from its main thread. MPI: under an MPI GROMACS every rank of the simulation communicator makes each call; the shim duplicates the communicator and uses collectives on it. |
| Returns and errors | none returned: the libcp2k API has no error channel. A failure prints `cpmdc-gromacs:` and the reason to stderr and to the CP2K output file, and stops the process with status 1. |
| Python | not wrapped. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cp2k_set_cell~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Units | `new_cell` in Bohr. |
| Layout | `new_cell` is 9 doubles, one lattice vector after the other (`a_x a_y a_z b_x ...`) as GROMACS 2026 sends it, or the transpose as GROMACS 2024 and 2025 send it; the library tells them apart by the zeros of GROMACS' lower triangular box. |
| Ownership | The caller owns `new_cell`; the library copies it. |
| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: GROMACS calls from its main thread. MPI: under an MPI GROMACS every rank of the simulation communicator makes each call; the shim duplicates the communicator and uses collectives on it. |

| Python | not wrapped. |

### ~cp2k_get_stress_tensor~

| Item | Description |

| Threads and MPI | Not thread-safe: GROMACS calls from its main thread. MPI: under an MPI GROMACS every rank of the simulation communicator makes each call; the shim duplicates the communicator and uses collectives on it. |
| Returns and errors | none returned: the libcp2k API has no error channel. A failure prints `cpmdc-gromacs:` and the reason to stderr and to the CP2K output file, and stops the process with status 1. Without a box, or on an isolated deck, `*available` is 0. |
| Python | not wrapped. |

# C types

Each type of the installed headers, with the rows Layout, Units, Ownership and Python.

## ~CPMDCResult~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int ok`, then a `double energy_h`, then `char message[512]`, a NUL-terminated text. |
| Units | `energy_h` in Hartree. |
| Ownership | Returned by value; the caller owns the copy. `message` is inside the struct, so there is nothing to free. |
| Python | Not wrapped as a type; the Python `Session` reads `ok`, `energy_h` and `message` and raises `cpmdc.CPMDCError` with the message when `ok` is 0. |

## ~CPMDCErrorCode~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `enum` of `int` values 0 to 5: `CPMDC_ERROR_NONE`, `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `CPMDC_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE`, `CPMDC_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PERIODIC_EMBEDDING`, `CPMDC_ERROR_EVALUATION_FAILED`, `CPMDC_ERROR_DECK_EXTERNAL_POTENTIAL`. |
| Units | none |
| Ownership | Returned by value from `cpmdc_last_error_code()`. |
| Python | Not wrapped as a type; the integer is `cpmdc.CPMDCError.code` and selects the subclass that the package raises. |

## ~CPMDCEnergyComponents~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, then 24 contiguous `double` values starting at `etot` (OpenCPMD `ener_com`). |
| Units | Hartree for every double; `entropy` and `amu` keep the unit of the OpenCPMD field. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_energy_components()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCChargeIntegrals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, then four `double` values `csumg`, `csumr`, `csums`, `csumsabs`. |
| Units | Electrons. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_charge_integrals()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCMultiStateEnergies~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, a `size_t count`, then `double values[64]` of which the first `count` are set. |
| Units | Hartree. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_multi_state_energies()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCMDTrajectoryRow~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, a `size_t count`, then `double values[32]` of which the first `count` are set. |
| Units | Hartree. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_md_trajectory_row()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCPropertySnapshot~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, then `size_t hessian_count` and `double hessian[4096]`, `size_t dipole_count` and `double dipole[3]`, `size_t polarizability_count` and `double polarizability[9]`. |
| Units | Atomic units: `hessian` holds the nuclear gradient in Hartree/Bohr, `dipole` is the molecular dipole in electron Bohr, and `polarizability` is always zeros. Evaluations above the 4096-component gradient capacity fail instead of truncating. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_property_snapshot()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCDipole~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, followed by `double values[3]` in Cartesian x, y, z order. |
| Units | Electron Bohr. The periodic Berry-phase dipole is defined for a neutral cell modulo a lattice quantum. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_dipole()` or `cpmdc_session_last_dipole()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Evaluation.dipole_e_bohr` holds the three values, or `None` when `valid` is 0. |

## ~CPMDCStressTensor~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, then `double values[9]`, row-major `xx xy xz yx yy yz zx zy zz`. |
| Units | Hartree/Bohr^3, OpenCPMD sign `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)`. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_stress()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Evaluation.stress_h_bohr3` holds the nine values, or `None` when `valid` is 0. |

## ~CPMDCRankSpread~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An `int valid`, an `int ranks`, then `double energy_h` and `double gradient_h_bohr`. |
| Units | `energy_h` in Hartree, `gradient_h_bohr` in Hartree/Bohr, `ranks` is a count. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_last_rank_spread()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCMethodInfo~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | `char functional[64]`, then `int charge` and `int multiplicity`. The functional is NUL-terminated. |
| Units | none: one method token and two integer quantum numbers. |
| Ownership | Filled by `cpmdc_params_method()` into a caller-owned struct; no pointers. |
| Python | Wrapped as the frozen `cpmdc.MethodInfo` dataclass. |

## ~CPMDCSession~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | Opaque: only a pointer is public and the struct is defined inside the library. |
| Units | none: a handle has no unit. |
| Ownership | Created by `cpmdc_session_create()` or `cpmdc_session_create_from_config()`, owned by the caller, and freed only by `cpmdc_session_destroy()`; a NULL handle is accepted by destroy. A session is used by one thread at a time. |
| Python | `cpmdc.Session` owns one handle and closes it. |

## ~CPMDCFeatureEntry~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | A `const char *feature_id`, a `CPMDCFeatureKind kind` and two `int` flags `stub_applicable` and `embed_applicable`, in that order. |
| Units | none: an identifier and two flags. |
| Ownership | `feature_id` points at static storage of the library; the table is contiguous, read-only and never freed. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCFeatureKind~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | An enum with the four values listed in the constants table. |
| Units | none: a tag. |
| Ownership | A value type with no ownership. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~CPMDCRestart~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | Opaque: only a pointer is public; the struct is defined inside `libcpmdc_restart`. |
| Units | `libcpmdc_restart` holds Bohr, Hartree and atomic mass units as the RESTART file does; see the restart functions. |
| Ownership | Created by the `cpmdc_restart_read_*` functions, owned by the caller, freed only by `cpmdc_restart_free()`. One image is not used by two threads at once when either writes. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~cpmdc_restart~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | The deprecated name of `CPMDCRestart`, the same type. |
| Units | As for `CPMDCRestart`. |
| Ownership | As for `CPMDCRestart`. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

## ~force_env_t~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Layout | A `typedef int`: the handle of one GROMACS force environment, an index into the table of the `libcpmdc_gromacs` shim. |
| Units | none: a handle has no unit. |
| Ownership | `cp2k_create_force_env()` writes it into a caller-owned `int`; `cp2k_destroy_force_env()` ends it. The shim keeps its own state in process globals, so one thread at a time. |
| Python | Not wrapped. |

# C constants

Every macro and enum constant of the installed headers.

| Name | Value | Meaning | Python |
|--------+--------+--------+--------|
| CPMDC_ABI_VERSION | 0 for every 0.x release | The ABI generation: the major number of `version.txt`, written into the header by cog. Compare it with `cpmdc_abi_version()`. | `cpmdc.Session.abi_version` returns the compiled value. |
| CPMDC_API | the platform export attribute | Marks an exported function: default visibility on GCC and Clang, `__declspec(dllexport)` or `dllimport` on Windows, empty for a static build. | none |
| CPMDC_ERROR_NONE | 0 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: no failure recorded. | `cpmdc.CPMDCError.code` is 0 for a failure that did not come from the library. |
| CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT | 1 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: a null handle, a bad buffer, or a refused value. | `cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument` |
| CPMDC_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE | 2 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: the backend is not linked or this build is the link stub. | `cpmdc.CPMDCUnavailable` |
| CPMDC_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PERIODIC_EMBEDDING | 3 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: session charges with a periodic cell or deck. | `cpmdc.CPMDCUnsupportedPeriodicEmbedding` |
| CPMDC_ERROR_EVALUATION_FAILED | 4 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: the evaluation ran and produced no result. | `cpmdc.CPMDCEvaluationFailed` |
| CPMDC_ERROR_DECK_EXTERNAL_POTENTIAL | 5 | `CPMDCErrorCode`: session charges with a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL`. | `cpmdc.CPMDCDeckExternalPotential` |
| CPMDC_FEATURE_SECTION | 1 | `CPMDCFeatureKind`: a CPMD input section, such as `catalog.section.PIMD`. | none |
| CPMDC_FEATURE_PARAMS | 2 | `CPMDCFeatureKind`: a `CPMDParams` field. | none |
| CPMDC_FEATURE_ABI | 3 | `CPMDCFeatureKind`: an exported C function. | none |
| CPMDC_FEATURE_KEYWORD | 4 | `CPMDCFeatureKind`: a CPMD keyword inside a catalog section. | none |
| CPMDC_RESTART_ANGSTROM_PER_BOHR | 0.529177210859 | Angstrom per Bohr as `libcpmdc_restart` uses it. The parameter lowering uses 0.529177210903, which `cpmdc.BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` repeats. | none |

# Python names

The Signature row is what `inspect.signature` reports for the object, without `self`; the audit compares the two. A name that is a context manager says so in its Ownership and threads row.

## ~cpmdc~

The package: sessions, the rgpot-shaped provider and the unit helpers.

### ~cpmdc.ATOMIC_NUMBER_MAX~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `ATOMIC_NUMBER_MAX = 118` |
| Units | none: an atomic number, dimensionless. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 118, the largest atomic number any call accepts. |

### ~cpmdc.ATOMIC_NUMBER_MIN~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `ATOMIC_NUMBER_MIN = 1` |
| Units | none: an atomic number, dimensionless. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 1, the smallest atomic number any call accepts. |

### ~cpmdc.BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM = 0.529177210903` |
| Units | Angstrom per Bohr. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `float`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 0.529177210903, the constant of the parameter lowering (`CPMDC_BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` in `src/cpmdc_params.h`). The restart library uses 0.529177210859 (see the restart section of the C ABI reference). |

### ~cpmdc.HARTREE_TO_EV~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `HARTREE_TO_EV = 27.211386245988` |
| Units | eV per Hartree. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `float`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 27.211386245988, the constant of `src/cpmdc.c` (`CPMDC_HARTREE_EV`). |

### ~cpmdc.HARTREE_TO_KCAL_PER_MOL~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `HARTREE_TO_KCAL_PER_MOL = 627.5094740630558` |
| Units | kcal/mol per Hartree: the energy unit of LAMMPS `real` units, thermochemical kilocalories of 4184 J. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `float`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | CODATA 2018 Hartree energy times the Avogadro constant over 4184 J, 627.5094740630558. |

### ~cpmdc.CPMDCError~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `CPMDCError(RuntimeError)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | An exception carrying one message string, the text of `cpmdc_last_error()` or the loader's reason. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless: raised and caught on the calling thread, safe to pass between threads. It never holds a session. |
| Raises | none: this is the exception. It subclasses `RuntimeError`. The C status codes map to it as listed in the C contracts, and `cpmdc.ase.CalculationFailed` and `cpmdc.ipi.ProtocolError` subclass it. |
| Defaults | none: the message is whatever the library or the loader reported. |

### ~cpmdc.CPMDCError.code~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `code (attribute)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`: the `CPMDCErrorCode` of the library failure, or 0 when Python rejected the call or the library lacks `cpmdc_last_error_code()`. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the exception instance; read it on the thread that caught the exception. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 0 on `CPMDCError`; each subclass has its own class value, and the constructor takes `code=None` to keep it. |

### ~cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `CPMDCInvalidArgument(cpmdc.CPMDCError)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | An exception carrying one message string and `code` 1. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless: raised and caught on the calling thread. It never holds a session. |
| Raises | none: this is the exception. Raised for a null handle, a bad buffer, or a value the library refuses, such as a Gaussian width below 1e-12 Angstrom. |
| Defaults | none: the message is what the library reported. |

### ~cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument.code~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `code (attribute)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`, 1. |
| Ownership and threads | Class attribute; immutable by convention and readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 1, equal to `CPMDC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. |

### ~cpmdc.CPMDCUnavailable~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `CPMDCUnavailable(cpmdc.CPMDCError)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | An exception carrying one message string and `code` 2. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless: raised and caught on the calling thread. It never holds a session. |
| Raises | none: this is the exception. Raised when the backend is not linked or the library is the link stub. |
| Defaults | none: the message is what the library reported. |

### ~cpmdc.ConstantCutoff~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `ConstantCutoff(cutoff_ry, height_ry=None, width_ry=None)` |
| Units | Rydberg for every field. |
| Shape and dtype | A frozen dataclass of three scalars; `height_ry` and `width_ry` are `float` or `None`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable value, thread-safe; it is copied into the session by `Session`. |
| Raises | `TypeError` when a field is not a real number (a `bool` is refused); `ValueError` when a field is not finite and positive. |
| Defaults | `height_ry` and `width_ry` are `None`: the library then uses 50 times the cutoff of the message and `cutoff_ry / 10`. `cutoff_ry` has no default. |

### ~cpmdc.ConstantCutoff.coerce~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `coerce(value)` |
| Units | Rydberg: a bare number is `E0`. |
| Shape and dtype | Takes `None`, a `ConstantCutoff`, a mapping with the field names as keys, or one real number; returns `ConstantCutoff` or `None`. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns the same object for a `ConstantCutoff` and a new one otherwise; classmethod, thread-safe. |
| Raises | `TypeError` for an unsupported type or a mapping with an unknown key; `ValueError` for a non-finite or non-positive value. |
| Defaults | none: `None` in gives `None` out. |

### ~cpmdc.ConstantCutoff.cutoff_ry~

| Shape and dtype | scalar `float`, finite and positive. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the object; it follows the thread rule of the class. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | No default: it is the one required field. |

| Raises | none |
| Defaults | `None`: 50 times the cutoff of the `CPMDParams` message. |

### ~cpmdc.Evaluation~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `Evaluation(energy_h, forces_h_bohr, stress_h_bohr3, dipole_e_bohr=None)` |
| Units | Hartree, Hartree/Bohr, Hartree/Bohr^3 and electron Bohr (atomic units, not eV). |
| Shape and dtype | A dataclass of four fields, compared and hashed by identity: `energy_h` a `float`, `forces_h_bohr` an N by 3 `list[list[float]]`, `stress_h_bohr3` nine floats or `None`, and `dipole_e_bohr` three floats or `None`. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain data the caller owns; it holds no handle. Not thread-safe to mutate; reading it from several threads is safe. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | `dipole_e_bohr=None`; the first three fields are required, in this order or by keyword. |

| Raises | none |

### ~cpmdc.Evaluation.stress_h_bohr3~

| Shape and dtype | Nine `float` values, a row-major 3 by 3 Cartesian tensor, or `None` when the step had no periodic cell or the library computed no stress. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the object; it follows the thread rule of the class. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | No default. |
