### ~cpmdc.Potential~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `Potential(params, *, library=None, schema=None, constant_cutoff=None)` |
| Units | Angstrom in; eV, eV/Angstrom and eV/Angstrom^3 out; `constant_cutoff` in Rydberg. |
| Shape and dtype | See `Potential.evaluate`. `params` is `bytes` or a path of a serialized `CPMDParams` message. |
| Ownership and threads | Owns one `Session`, which it creates and closes; it is a context manager (`with` closes it) and `close()` is idempotent. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `CPMDCError` when the library cannot be found or loaded, the message is empty or rejected, or the library lacks constant-cutoff support; `OSError` when a path cannot be read; `TypeError` or `ValueError` for a bad `constant_cutoff`. |
| Defaults | `library` is `None` (the search of `find_library`), `schema` is `None` and ignored (a `DeprecationWarning` when given), `constant_cutoff` is `None` (the message as it is). |

### ~cpmdc.Potential.caps~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `caps()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a new `dict[str, bool]` with the keys `stress`, `dipole`, and `energies`. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns a new dict. Reads the owned session, including whether its library exports `cpmdc_session_last_dipole` and whether the last evaluation produced a dipole, so it is not thread-safe against evaluation or close on that session. MPI: local. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | `stress` is true and `energies` is false. `dipole` is `Session.dipole_possible()`. A dipole result on `Potential.evaluate` is three e*Angstrom components, present only when that evaluation recomputed one. |

### ~cpmdc.Potential.close~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `close()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Closes the owned session. A second call does nothing. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.Potential.evaluate~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `evaluate(positions, numbers, box=None)` |
| Units | `positions` and `box` in Angstrom; the result has `energy` in eV, `forces` in eV/Angstrom and `stress` in eV/Angstrom^3 with the ASE sign `(1/V) dE/d(strain)`. |
| Shape and dtype | `positions` N by 3 floats; `numbers` N integers in 1..118; `box` a 3 by 3 matrix or nine floats in row-major order, one lattice vector per row. Returns a new `dict`: `energy` a float, `forces` an N by 3 list, `stress` nine floats only when the library computed one, and `dipole` three e*Angstrom components only when the evaluation recomputed one. |
| Ownership and threads | The caller keeps every argument; nothing is retained. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for empty or ragged positions, a non-finite value, a wrong number of atomic numbers or one outside 1..118, a malformed box, and `TypeError` for a non-integer atomic number; `CPMDCError` for a closed session, a change of composition, a non-zero box rejected by the C ABI (rank below 3, volume underflow, volume overflow, or isolated-deck mismatch), or a failed step. |
| Defaults | `box` is `None`: an isolated system, which the deck's boundary conditions then define. |

### ~cpmdc.Session~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `Session(params, *, library=None, schema=None, constant_cutoff=None)` |
| Units | `energy_forces` takes Angstrom and returns Hartree and Hartree/Bohr; `calculate_au` takes Bohr and returns Hartree and Hartree/Bohr; `constant_cutoff` is in Rydberg. |
| Shape and dtype | `params` is `bytes` or a path of one serialized flat `CPMDParams` message; the methods take the shapes listed with each. |
| Ownership and threads | Owns one `CPMDCSession` handle, created in the constructor and destroyed by `close()`, by leaving a `with` block (it is a context manager) or by garbage collection; the bytes of `params` are copied. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `CPMDCError` when the library cannot be found or loaded, the message is empty or rejected, or the library lacks `cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff`; `OSError` when a path cannot be read; `TypeError` or `ValueError` for a bad `constant_cutoff`. |
| Defaults | `library` is `None` (see `find_library`), `schema` is `None` and ignored (a `DeprecationWarning` when given), `constant_cutoff` is `None` (the message as it is). |

### ~cpmdc.Session.abi_version~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `abi_version()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a scalar `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | Reads a constant of the loaded library; thread-safe. |
| Raises | none: cannot fail, even on a closed session. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.Session.available~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `available()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a `bool`. |
| Ownership and threads | Calls `cpmdc_available()`, which initialises the embed on the first call, so call it from one thread first; otherwise thread-safe. MPI: local. |
| Raises | none: cannot fail, even on a closed session. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.Session.dipole_possible~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `dipole_possible()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a `bool`. False when the library has no `cpmdc_session_last_dipole`, when the session is closed, or for the reference evaluator. Before the first step a linked library that has the symbol answers true. After a step the answer is whether that step produced a dipole. |
| Ownership and threads | Reads the session handle and its last dipole state. Not thread-safe against evaluation or close on the same session. MPI: local. |
| Raises | none: a closed session, the reference evaluator, and a library without `cpmdc_session_last_dipole` return `False`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.Session.calculate_au~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `calculate_au(positions_bohr, atomic_numbers, cell_bohr=None, *, forces=None, virial=None)` |
| Units | `positions_bohr` and `cell_bohr` in Bohr; returns the energy in Hartree, forces in Hartree/Bohr (`-dE/dR`) and the virial `-dE/d(strain)` in Hartree (zero without a cell or a stress tensor). |
| Shape and dtype | `positions_bohr`: `3 * N` finite floats, flat or N rows; `atomic_numbers`: N integers in 1..118 (a C-contiguous `int32` buffer is used without a copy); `cell_bohr`: nine finite floats or three rows, one lattice vector per row, or `None`; `forces` and `virial`: writable C-contiguous `float64` buffers of `3 * N` and nine values, or `None`. Returns ; a buffer is the one passed in or a new `array('d')`. |
| Ownership and threads | The caller keeps the inputs. Output buffers passed in are filled in place and returned. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for no atoms, a wrong number of values, a non-finite coordinate or cell value, an atomic number outside 1..118, or an output buffer that is not writable and C-contiguous with the right size; `TypeError` for a value that is not a real number or an atomic number that is not an integer; `CPMDCError` for a closed session, a change of composition, a non-zero cell rejected by the C ABI (rank below 3, Angstrom volume underflow, Bohr volume overflow, or isolated-deck mismatch), a non-finite virial, or a failed step. |
| Defaults | `cell_bohr` is `None`: no cell is passed; `forces` and `virial` are `None`: new buffers are returned. |

### ~cpmdc.Session.close~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `close()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Destroys the handle; a second call does nothing and the session cannot be reused. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.Session.copy_orbitals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `copy_orbitals(from_key, to_key)` |
| Units | none: `from_key` and `to_key` are dimensionless orbital keys. |
| Shape and dtype | Two scalar `int` keys that fit a signed 64-bit integer. |
| Ownership and threads | Copies stored wavefunctions inside the session; the caller owns nothing. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `TypeError` for a key that is not an integer (a `bool` is refused); `ValueError` for a non-whole float or a key outside the signed 64-bit range; `CPMDCError` for a closed session, a library without `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals`, or the library's refusal: before the first evaluation there are no stored orbitals, and an OpenCPMD build refuses a `from_key` that never converged. The reference build has no orbital store, so after one evaluation the call succeeds and copies nothing. |
| Defaults | none: both keys are required. |

### ~cpmdc.Session.energy_forces~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `energy_forces(positions, atomic_numbers, cell=None)` |
| Units | `positions` and `cell` in Angstrom; returns Hartree, Hartree/Bohr and Hartree/Bohr^3 (atomic units, the stress with the OpenCPMD sign `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)`). |
| Shape and dtype | `positions`: N rows of three finite floats; `atomic_numbers`: N integers in 1..118; `cell`: a 3 by 3 matrix or nine finite floats in row-major order, one lattice vector per row, or `None`. Returns an `Evaluation`. |
| Ownership and threads | The caller keeps every argument; the result is new data. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for empty or ragged positions, a non-finite value, a wrong number of atomic numbers or one outside 1..118, or a malformed cell; `TypeError` for an atomic number that is not an integer (a whole float such as `8.0` is accepted); `CPMDCError` for a closed session, a change of atom count or composition, a non-zero cell rejected by the C ABI (rank below 3, volume underflow, volume overflow, or isolated-deck mismatch), or a failed step. |
| Defaults | `cell` is `None`: an isolated system, evaluated with `cpmdc_session_energy_forces()`; a cell goes through `cpmdc_session_calculate_forces()`. |

### ~cpmdc.Session.set_external_charges~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `set_external_charges(positions_angstrom, charges_e, widths_angstrom=None)` |
| Units | `positions_angstrom` and `widths_angstrom` in Angstrom; `charges_e` in units of the elementary charge. |
| Shape and dtype | `positions_angstrom` holds `3 * M` finite floats, flat or `M` rows; `charges_e` and `widths_angstrom` hold `M` finite floats; `M` of 0 clears the charges. |
| Ownership and threads | The library copies the arrays; the caller keeps them. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; every rank of a calculator makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for a non-finite value or a wrong length; `cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument` for a width below 1e-12 Angstrom, with the previous charges kept; `CPMDCError` for a closed session, or for a library without `cpmdc_session_set_external_charges`. |
| Defaults | `widths_angstrom` is `None`: the library default of 0.30 Angstrom. A new session has no charges. |

### ~cpmdc.Session.external_charge_forces_au~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `external_charge_forces_au(n_charges)` |
| Units | Hartree/Bohr. |
| Shape and dtype | `n_charges` a non-negative `int`; returns `3 * n_charges` floats in an `array('d')`, in the order the charges were set. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns a new buffer. Not thread-safe: one session is used by one thread at a time. MPI: local to the rank. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for a negative count; `cpmdc.CPMDCInvalidArgument` before a successful evaluation or for a count that differs from the charges set; `CPMDCError` for a closed session or for a library without `cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces`. |
| Defaults | none: the count is required. |

### ~cpmdc.Session.select_orbitals~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `select_orbitals(key)` |
| Units | none: `key` is a dimensionless orbital key. |
| Shape and dtype | One scalar `int` that fits a signed 64-bit integer. |
| Ownership and threads | The session keeps the key; the caller owns nothing. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `TypeError` for a key that is not an integer (a `bool` is refused); `ValueError` for a non-whole float or a key outside the signed 64-bit range; `CPMDCError` for a closed session or the library's refusal. |
| Defaults | none: the key is required. A new session has no key selected. |

### ~cpmdc.find_library~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `find_library(path=None)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Takes a path or `None`; returns a `pathlib.Path`. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns a new `Path`; stateless apart from reading the environment, so thread-safe. |
| Raises | `CPMDCError` when no library is found; the message lists the places searched. |
| Defaults | `path` is `None`: `CPMDC_LIBRARY`, then `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, then `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE`, then the library beside the package that a wheel installs, then the dynamic linker, then `build/libcpmdc.so` in the working directory. |

### ~cpmdc.find_schema~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `find_schema(path=None)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Takes a path or `None`; returns a `pathlib.Path`. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns a new `Path`; stateless apart from reading the environment, so thread-safe. |
| Raises | `CPMDCError` when no schema file is found. |
| Defaults | `path` is `None`: `CPMDC_SCHEMA`, then the copy a wheel installs inside the package, then `schema/Potentials.capnp` in the working directory. |

### ~cpmdc.params_method~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `params_method(params, *, library=None)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | `params` is serialized `CPMDParams` bytes or a path; returns a frozen `MethodInfo`. |
| Ownership and threads | Reads and copies the bytes, loads the library for the call, and returns new immutable data. Thread-safe except for dynamic-loader and environment behavior. |
| Raises | `FileNotFoundError` for an unreadable path; `CPMDCError` for an empty or invalid message, a missing library, a library without `cpmdc_params_method`, or a library failure. |
| Defaults | `library` is `None`, using `find_library`. |

### ~cpmdc.forces_to_ev_per_angstrom~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `forces_to_ev_per_angstrom(forces_h_bohr)` |
| Units | Hartree/Bohr in, eV/Angstrom out. |
| Shape and dtype | N rows of three floats in; a new N by 3 `list[list[float]]` out. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless pure function: thread-safe, keeps nothing, returns new objects. |
| Raises | none: a row that is not a sequence of numbers raises the ordinary `TypeError` of the multiplication. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.dipole_to_e_angstrom~

## ~cpmdc.ase~

The ASE calculator. Importing it imports ASE.

### ~cpmdc.ase.CalculationFailed~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `CalculationFailed(cpmdc.CPMDCError, ase.calculators.calculator.CalculationFailed)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | An exception with a message that names the working directory of the step and the library's reason. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless: raised and caught on the calling thread. |
| Raises | none: this is the exception. It subclasses both `cpmdc.CPMDCError` and ASE's `CalculationFailed`, so either `except` clause catches it. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `CPMDCCalculator(params=None, *, library=None, constant_cutoff=None, **kwargs)` |
| Units | ASE units: eV, eV/Angstrom, eV/Angstrom^3 (Voigt); `constant_cutoff` in Rydberg. |
| Shape and dtype | `params` is `bytes` or a path of a `CPMDParams` message; the properties are listed in the ASE tables. |
| Ownership and threads | Owns one `cpmdc.Potential`, opened on first use and closed by `close()` or by leaving a `with` block (it is a context manager); it can be copied and pickled, and a copy opens its own session. Not thread-safe: one thread at a time, as ASE requires. MPI: the package never calls MPI. |
| Raises | `TypeError` when `params` is missing or a keyword is unknown; the errors of `Calculator.__init__` and of `set`. |
| Defaults | `params`, `library` and `constant_cutoff` are `None`; `params` is then required. `directory` is `'.'` and `label` is ASE's default. |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.calculate~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `calculate(atoms=None, properties=None, system_changes=['positions', 'numbers', 'cell', 'pbc', 'initial_charges', 'initial_magmoms'])` |
| Units | ASE units: energy in eV, forces in eV/Angstrom, stress in eV/Angstrom^3 in Voigt order. |
| Shape and dtype | `atoms` an `ase.Atoms`; fills `results` with `energy` and `free_energy` floats, `forces` an N by 3 `float64` array, and `stress` a six-component `float64` array when the cell is fully periodic. |
| Ownership and threads | The calculator keeps the results; `atoms` is copied by ASE. Not thread-safe. The step runs with `directory` as the working directory, which is a process-wide change. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for no atoms, an `initial_charges` or `initial_magmoms` total that is not an integer (it must lie within `n * eps * sum(abs(x))` of one, the float64 rounding bound of `n` terms, `eps` the float64 unit roundoff), non-collinear `initial_magmoms`, a nonzero total charge or total moment that differs from the charge or multiplicity `params` sets, where charge 0 is set when `hasCharge` is true and unset when `hasCharge` is false (the message names both values and both sources, and the set charge is kept) or that a typed section of `params` fixes, a partly periodic cell, a cell of rank below 3 (singular values count only above sigma_max times 3 times the float64 unit roundoff, the numpy.linalg.matrix_rank cutoff), a cell volume below the normal float64 range, `pbc` of the wrong length, and invalid coordinates or atomic numbers; `PropertyNotImplementedError` when stress is asked for a cluster or for a step the library gave no stress for; `CalculationFailed` when the library rejects the step or returns a non-finite value; `CPMDCError` when an `Atoms` total needs `cpmdc_params_method()` and the library has none or refuses the message as ambiguous. |
| Defaults | `atoms` is `None`: the atoms already attached; `properties` is `None`: `['energy']`, but all four properties are always filled; `system_changes` is ASE's `all_changes`. |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.close~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `close()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Closes the session; the next step opens a new one. Not thread-safe. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.default_parameters~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `default_parameters (attribute)` |
| Units | none: the parameters are listed in the ASE parameters table. |
| Shape and dtype | A `dict` with the keys `params`, `library` and `constant_cutoff`. |
| Ownership and threads | Class attribute shared by every instance; do not mutate it. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | Every value is `None`. |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.discard_results_on_any_change~

| Ownership and threads | Class attribute read by ASE. |

| Raises | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.potential~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|

| Shape and dtype | Returns the `cpmdc.Potential` the calculator owns. |
| Ownership and threads | Opened on first use after `close()`, a copy or an unpickle; the calculator owns it, so do not close it yourself. Not thread-safe. |

| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.reset~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `reset()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Clears the stored results; the session stays open. Not thread-safe. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.read~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `read(label)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | Returns nothing; it never returns normally. |
| Ownership and threads | Changes no state: the label, the directory, the atoms and the results stay as they were. Not thread-safe. |
| Raises | `ase.calculators.calculator.ReadError`, with the refused `label` in the message, because a step writes no file that holds results. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.set~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `set(**kwargs)` |
| Units | `constant_cutoff` in Rydberg. |
| Shape and dtype | Keyword arguments `params`, `library`, `constant_cutoff` and `parameters` (a file written by `Parameters.write`); returns the `dict` of changed parameters. A relative `params` or `library` path is resolved against the working directory of the process and stored absolute. |
| Ownership and threads | A change opens a new session before it closes the old one, so a failed change keeps the old session. Not thread-safe. |
| Raises | `TypeError` for an unknown key or a `params` of `None`; `CPMDCError`, `OSError` or `ValueError` when the new session cannot be opened. |
| Defaults | No keyword is required; `schema` is deprecated and ignored. |

### ~cpmdc.ase.CPMDCCalculator.todict~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `todict(skip_default=True)` |
| Units | `constant_cutoff` in Rydberg. |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a new `dict` of the parameters. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns a new dict; a `params` buffer given as `bytes` is left out, and a `params` or `library` path is kept absolute. Not thread-safe against `set`. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | `skip_default` is `True`: parameters equal to their default are left out. |

## ~cpmdc.gromacs~

Input files and unit constants for GROMACS.

| Units | kJ/mol per Hartree: the GROMACS energy unit. |

| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |

### ~cpmdc.gromacs.qmi_input~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `qmi_input(params, *, cell=None, embedding=None, qm_charges=None, ewald_rcut=None, ewald_precision=None, epsilon_r=None, qm_ranks=None, links=None, link_alpha=None, charge=0, multiplicity=1)` |
| Units | `ewald_rcut` in nm; `ewald_precision`, `epsilon_r`, `link_alpha` and `multiplicity` are dimensionless; `qm_charges` in units of the elementary charge; `charge` in elementary charges. |
| Shape and dtype | `params` a path; `qm_charges` a sequence of floats, one per QM atom; `links` a sequence of  pairs of 1-based GROMACS atom numbers, one `&LINK` section each in `&QMMM`; the others are scalars or strings. Returns the `qmi` file as one `str` that ends in a newline. |
| Ownership and threads | Builds a new string and touches no file; stateless, so thread-safe. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for an unknown `cell` or `embedding` keyword, `qm_ranks` other than `ALL` or `1`, `qm_charges` or `epsilon_r` without `MECHANICAL` embedding or `MECHANICAL` embedding without `qm_charges`, a non-finite value, a non-positive `ewald_rcut`, `ewald_precision`, or `epsilon_r`, a `multiplicity` below 1, a `charge`, `multiplicity`, or link atom number that is not a whole number, a link that is not a pair, has an atom number below 1, or joins an atom to itself, a `link_alpha` of 1 or less, or `link_alpha` without `links`; `TypeError` for a value that is not a real number or not an integer. |
| Defaults | `cell`, `embedding`, `qm_charges`, `ewald_rcut`, `ewald_precision`, `epsilon_r` and `qm_ranks` are `None` and not written, so the library defaults apply (`PERIODIC` when every atom is QM and `NONE` otherwise; no embedding; the smaller of 1 nm and half the shortest box height; Ewald precision 10^-8 as assigned in tools/gromacs/cpmdc_gromacs.c; `EPSILON_R` 1; `ALL`); `links` and `link_alpha` are `None`, so no bond is capped, and `ALPHA_IMOMM` is not written, so the library takes 1.38; `charge` is 0 and `multiplicity` is 1. |

### ~cpmdc.gromacs.write_qmi~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `write_qmi(path, params, *, cell=None, embedding=None, qm_charges=None, ewald_rcut=None, ewald_precision=None, epsilon_r=None, qm_ranks=None, links=None, link_alpha=None, charge=0, multiplicity=1)` |
| Units | As for `qmi_input`: `ewald_rcut` in nm, `qm_charges` and `charge` in elementary charges, `epsilon_r` and `link_alpha` dimensionless. |
| Shape and dtype | `path` is the file to write, `params` a path; the options are those of `qmi_input`. Returns the `pathlib.Path` written. |
| Ownership and threads | Writes one file in UTF-8, replacing it; thread-safe for distinct paths. |
| Raises | `ValueError` as for `qmi_input`; `OSError` when the file cannot be written. |
| Defaults | As for `qmi_input`. |

## ~cpmdc.ipi~

The i-PI protocol driver.

| Signature | `DEFAULT_SOCKET_PREFIX (str)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `str`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | The `ipi_` prefix in the temporary directory that i-PI and ASE use. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.HEADER_BYTES~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `HEADER_BYTES = 12` |
| Units | bytes. |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | Immutable module constant, readable from any thread. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 12, the width of an i-PI message header. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.ProtocolError~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `ProtocolError(cpmdc.CPMDCError)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | An exception with a message naming the offending message. |
| Ownership and threads | Stateless: raised and caught on the calling thread. |
| Raises | none: this is the exception. It subclasses `cpmdc.CPMDCError`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `Driver(params, atomic_numbers, *, library=None, cluster=False, log=None)` |
| Units | Bohr, Hartree and Hartree/Bohr on the wire (i-PI uses atomic units). |
| Shape and dtype | `atomic_numbers` N integers in server order; the wire carries 3N-float positions, a nine-float cell and returns 3N forces and a nine-float virial. |
| Ownership and threads | Owns one `cpmdc.Session`, closed by `close()` or by leaving a `with` block (it is a context manager). `log` is borrowed. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for no atoms or an atomic number outside 1..118; `CPMDCError` when the session cannot be opened. |
| Defaults | `library` is `None` (see `find_library`), `cluster` is `False`, `log` is `None` (no log). |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.atomic_numbers~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `atomic_numbers (attribute)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | A `list[int]` of N atomic numbers in server order. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the object; it follows the thread rule of the class. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | No default: it is set by the constructor. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.close~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `close()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Closes the session. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.cluster~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `cluster (attribute)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `bool`. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the object; it follows the thread rule of the class. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | `False` unless the constructor was given `cluster=True`. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.compute~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `compute(positions, cell)` |
| Units | `positions` and `cell` in Bohr; returns the energy in Hartree, forces in Hartree/Bohr and the virial `-dE/d(strain)` in Hartree. |
| Shape and dtype | `positions` 3N floats; `cell` nine floats, the lattice vectors as columns in row-major order (the i-PI wire layout), all zero for a cluster. Returns  of 1, 3N and 9 values. |
| Ownership and threads | Returns new lists; counts the step in `steps`. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ProtocolError` for a position count that is not a multiple of three, an atom count that differs from the driver's, a cell of rank below 3 (the numpy.linalg.matrix_rank cutoff, sigma_max times 3 times the float64 unit roundoff), or a cell volume below the normal float64 range, both judged on the Bohr values of `cell`; `CPMDCError` for a cell volume above the largest float64, before the session is called, or a virial component that is not finite; `ValueError` for a position that is not finite (`positions must be finite`) or, when the cell is used, a cell value that is not finite (`cell must be finite`), checked after the rank and before the volume; `CPMDCError` and `ValueError` from the session. |
| Defaults | none: both arguments are required. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.serve~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `serve(sock)` |
| Units | Atomic units on the wire, as for `compute`. |
| Shape and dtype | `sock` a connected stream socket; returns the number of steps served as an `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | The caller owns the socket and closes it. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ProtocolError` for a connection closed in the middle of a message, a message out of order, an unknown header, an `INIT` that is not UTF-8 or whose `batch_size` appears more than once or is not the integer 1, or a negative announced size; `OSError` for a socket failure; `CPMDCError` from the session. A close between messages ends the run like `EXIT`. |
| Defaults | none |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.Driver.steps~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `steps (attribute)` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | scalar `int`. |
| Ownership and threads | Plain attribute of the object; it follows the thread rule of the class. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | 0 until the first step. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.connect~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `connect(*, unix=None, host='localhost', port=None, prefix=None, wait=0.0)` |
| Units | `wait` in seconds. |
| Shape and dtype | Returns a connected `socket.socket`; give exactly one of `unix` (a name or a path) and `port`. |
| Ownership and threads | The caller owns the returned socket and must close it. Thread-safe: it uses no shared state. |
| Raises | `ValueError` unless exactly one of `unix` and `port` is given, or, before a socket is opened, when `wait` is negative, NaN or infinite; `CPMDCError` when the server is not listening after `wait` seconds; `OSError` for any other socket failure. |
| Defaults | `host` is `'localhost'`, `prefix` is `None` (`DEFAULT_SOCKET_PREFIX`), `wait` is 0.0: one attempt. |

### ~cpmdc.ipi.main~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `main(argv=None)` |
| Units | As for `cpmdc-ipi --help`; `--wait` in seconds. |
| Shape and dtype | `argv` a sequence of strings; returns the exit status as an `int`: 0, or 1 after printing the error. |
| Ownership and threads | Opens and closes its own session and socket; one thread at a time. Not thread-safe: the C library keeps the active calculator in process globals, so one session is used by one thread at a time and two sessions are not evaluated at the same time. MPI: the package never calls MPI; an OpenCPMD build runs the collectives of the C call on the calculator communicator, so every rank makes the same call. |
| Raises | `ValueError`, `OSError` and `CPMDCError` are caught and turn into status 1; `SystemExit` comes from the argument parser for a bad command line. |
| Defaults | `argv` is `None`: `sys.argv[1:]`. |

## ~cpmdc.lammps~

The `fix external` driver for LAMMPS.

### ~cpmdc.lammps.UNIT_STYLES~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `UNIT_STYLES (dict)` |
| Units | Per style, a pair: length unit per Bohr (Angstrom per Bohr, or 1.0 for `electron`) and energy unit per Hartree (eV, kcal/mol or 1.0). |
| Shape and dtype | A `dict` from style name to a pair of floats. |
| Ownership and threads | Module-level dict; do not mutate it. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | The keys `metal`, `real` and `electron`. |

### ~cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `FixExternal(lmp, params, elements, *, fix_id='cpmdc', create=True, library=None, comm=None, qm_types=None, mm_width_angstrom=0.3)` |
| Units | The LAMMPS unit style of the run: `metal` (Angstrom, eV), `real` (Angstrom, kcal/mol) or `electron` (Bohr, Hartree); `mm_width_angstrom` in Angstrom; the charges of the MM atoms are the LAMMPS `q` in units of the elementary charge. |
| Shape and dtype | `lmp` a `lammps.lammps` object with box, atoms and masses; `elements` one symbol or atomic number per atom type; atom IDs must be positive and unique but may have gaps; `qm_types` a sequence of atom type numbers, whose complement is MM; `mm_width_angstrom` a scalar. With MM atoms the virial is zero and the charge set is cleared on the first step that has none. |
| Ownership and threads | Owns the session on world rank 0 and the fixes it creates, removed by `close()` or by leaving a `with` block (it is a context manager). `lmp` and `comm` are borrowed. Not thread-safe: LAMMPS calls back from one thread. MPI: with more than one rank every rank constructs the object and calls `run`; rank 0 adopts `MPI_COMM_SELF` and evaluates, and `mpi4py` is needed. |
| Raises | `ValueError` for an unsupported unit style, a wrong number of elements, an unknown element, a partly periodic box, empty `qm_types`, or an `mm_width_angstrom` that is not finite or is below 1e-12; `CPMDCError` in a step for MM atoms on a periodic box, for a LAMMPS atom style without charges, or for no QM atom; `CPMDCError` when the session cannot be opened, `mpi4py` is missing on several ranks, or `comm` has the wrong size. |
| Defaults | `fix_id` is `'cpmdc'`, `create` is `True`, `library` is `None`, `comm` is `None` (`MPI.COMM_WORLD`), `qm_types` is `None` (every atom is QM), `mm_width_angstrom` is 0.3. |

### ~cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal.close~

| Item | Description |
|--------+--------|
| Signature | `close()` |
| Units | none |
| Shape and dtype | none |
| Ownership and threads | Closes the session and removes the fixes this object added; safe to call twice. Not thread-safe: call it from the thread that runs LAMMPS, on every rank. |
| Raises | none |
| Defaults | none |

# ASE properties

The properties `CPMDCCalculator` implements, in ASE units.

| Property | Units | Shape and dtype | Sign and convention | Raises |
|--------+--------+--------+--------+--------|
| energy | eV | scalar `float` | The potential energy of the step; the library separates no electronic entropy. | `CalculationFailed` when the library rejects the step or returns a non-finite value; `ValueError` for invalid atoms. |
| free_energy | eV | scalar `float` | Equal to `energy`. | As for `energy`. |
| forces | eV/Angstrom | (N, 3) `float64` array | The negative nuclear gradient `-dE/dR`. | As for `energy`. |
| stress | eV/Angstrom^3 | (6,) `float64` array in Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy | ASE sign, `(1/V) dE/d(strain)`, the opposite of the OpenCPMD sign; shear parts are averaged. | `PropertyNotImplementedError` for a cluster (every `pbc` flag false) or for a step the library gave no stress for; `ValueError` for a partly periodic cell. |
| dipole | e*Angstrom | (3,) `float64` Cartesian array | Molecular dipole from the current geometry only when OpenCPMD recomputed it; the periodic Berry-phase value is defined modulo a lattice quantum. | `PropertyNotImplementedError` when the library has no `cpmdc_session_last_dipole`, or when the reference, isolated, k-point or unrequested evaluation produced no dipole. `CalculationFailed` when the dipole is not finite. |

# ASE parameters

The parameters of `CPMDCCalculator`; `set` and the constructor take them as keywords.

| Parameter | Units | Type | Default | Meaning |
|--------+--------+--------+--------+--------|
| params | none: the message carries its own units. | `bytes`, `bytearray`, `memoryview`, or a path of a serialized `CPMDParams` message | None | The method: functional, cutoff, charge, multiplicity and the boundary conditions of a cluster. Required: the constructor raises `TypeError` without it. The bytes are read once, when the parameter is set. |
| library | none | `str` or path of `libcpmdc` | None | The shared library. `None` uses the search of `cpmdc.find_library`. |
| constant_cutoff | Rydberg | a number `E0`, a mapping of the `ConstantCutoff` fields, or a `ConstantCutoff` | None | The constant-cutoff kinetic functional, whose stress carries no Pulay stress. `None` evaluates the message as it is. |

# Deprecated aliases

Names kept for existing callers. A Python name warns with `DeprecationWarning` and will be removed in a later release.

| Old name | New name | Behaviour |
|--------+--------+--------|
| cpmdc.CpmdcError | cpmdc.CPMDCError | The same class under its old spelling; reading the name emits a `DeprecationWarning`. |
| cpmdc_restart | CPMDCRestart | The same C type under its name of 0.4.0; the compiler does not warn. |
| schema keyword | none | `Session`, `Potential` and `CPMDCCalculator` ignore `schema` and emit a `DeprecationWarning` when it is not `None`: a cell is encoded in process, so no schema file is read. |
| restart keyword | none | `CPMDCCalculator` ignores `restart` and emits a `DeprecationWarning` when it is not `None`. |


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/cpmd-options.org

# Contract
All method knobs for the OpenCPMD backend are fields of `CPMDParams` in
`schema/Potentials.capnp`.
Geometry is never part of `CPMDParams`; it is always a `ForceInput` step message
(or the raw C array entry points that take positions and atomic numbers).

# Top-level ~CPMDParams~ fields

| Feature ID | Field | Role |
|------------+-------+------|
| `params.functional` | `functional` | Default DFT functional (also used when no `dft` section is present) |
| `params.cutOffRy` | `cutOffRy` | Plane-wave cutoff in Rydberg |
| `params.charge` | `charge` | System charge |
| `params.hasCharge` | `hasCharge` | Mark `CPMDParams.charge` as explicit, including zero |
| `params.multiplicity` | `multiplicity` | 2S+1; values `> 1` imply LSD defaults |
| `params.task` | `task` | Frontend hint: `energy`, `gradient`, `md`, `optimize` |
| `params.title` | `title` | Optional comment header in rendered decks |
| `params.memoryMb` | `memoryMb` | Frontend memory hint |
| `params.scratchDir` | `scratchDir` | `&CPMD FILEPATH` and the working directory for CPMD output when `permanentDir` is empty |
| `params.permanentDir` | `permanentDir` | `&CPMD FILEPATH` and the working directory for CPMD output; wins over `scratchDir` |
| `params.cpmdRoot` | `cpmdRoot` | OpenCPMD source/build tree |
| `params.enginePath` | `enginePath` | Frontend engine selection hint |
| `params.inputBlocks` | `inputBlocks` | Raw `&SECTION` text blocks prepended to the deck |
| `params.inputSections` | `inputSections` | Structured `CPMDInputSection` list |

The feature-discovery table exposes these as `params.<field>` IDs.
Structured fields use `params.inputSections.<section>.<field>`, for example
`params.inputSections.cpmd.maxIter`, `params.inputSections.dft.hfxScreening`,
`params.inputSections.system.cell`, and `params.inputSections.pimd.directives`.

# Feature ID namespaces
Feature IDs separate writable schema fields from parser/catalog capability rows.

| Namespace | Meaning |
|-----------+---------|
| `abi.*` | Exported C ABI symbols |
| `params.*` | Top-level `CPMDParams` fields |
| `params.inputSections.*` | Typed fields and directive carriers inside `CPMDInputSection` |
| `params.inputSections.system.*` | Structured `&SYSTEM` controls such as cell, cutoff, Poisson, KPOINTS, CDFT, pressure, and stress fields |
| `catalog.cpmd.*` | Named `&CPMD` keyword capability rows |
| `catalog.dft.*` | Named `&DFT` keyword capability rows |
| `catalog.section.*` | OpenCPMD section names discovered from parser `inscan('&SECTION')` calls |

`catalog.section.SYSTEM` means the `&SYSTEM` deck section is recognized as a
section kind.
Individual `&SYSTEM` controls stay under
`params.inputSections.system.*` rather than a separate `catalog.system.*`
namespace.

Manual keyword names do not always map to a `catalog.cpmd.*` feature ID.
Use the field namespace when the renderer owns a typed section field:

| Manual name | Feature or field ID | Rendered deck form |
|-------------+---------------------+--------------------|
| `BOX WALLS` | `params.inputSections.system.boxWalls` | `&SYSTEM` / `BOX WALLS` |
| `MODIFIED GOEDECKER` | `params.inputSections.system.modifiedGoedecker` | `&SYSTEM` / `MODIFIED GOEDECKER` |
| `MODIFIED GOEDECKER PARAMETERS` | `params.inputSections.system.modifiedGoedeckerParameters` | `&SYSTEM` / `MODIFIED GOEDECKER PARAMETERS` |
| `SOC` | `catalog.cpmd.SOC` and `params.inputSections.cpmd.spinOrbitCouplingStates` | `&CPMD` / `SPIN-ORBIT COUPLING` |

`FFTW WISDOM` is not a typed feature row because the OpenCPMD manual source
comments out that keyword and the parser tree used for inventory probing has no
matching branch.
Use `inputSections.raw` or `inputBlocks` only for a downstream tree that still
accepts it.

# Mapping a CPMD manual line
Use this order when turning a CPMD manual line into an ABI input:

1. Search this page for the literal keyword spelling.
2. Prefer a `params.inputSections.<section>.<field>` row when one exists; that
   is the writable schema field.
3. Use a `catalog.cpmd.*` row for recognized `&CPMD` keyword and inline option
   spellings.
   These rows are capability/discovery IDs; many render through an existing text
   field such as `roksOptions`, `langevinOptions`, or `interfaceOptions`.
4. Use a `catalog.section.*` row only to detect support for a whole OpenCPMD
   section such as `&PIMD` or `&VDW`.
5. Use `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or top-level `inputBlocks` when no structured
   field or catalog row represents the required deck text.

Examples:

| Manual line | Writable carrier | Discovery row |
|-------------+------------------+---------------|
| `ROKS TRIPLET LOCALIZED EXPERT` | `roksOptions` plus `roksExpertPayload` | `catalog.cpmd.ROKS`, `catalog.cpmd.ROKS_LOCALIZED`, `catalog.cpmd.ROKS_EXPERT` |
| `LANGEVIN SMART MOVECM CENTROIDOFF` | `langevinOptions` plus `langevinParameter` | `catalog.cpmd.LANGEVIN_SMART`, `catalog.cpmd.LANGEVIN_MOVECM`, `catalog.cpmd.LANGEVIN_CENTROIDOFF` |
| `INTERFACE GMX ESP PCGFIRST` | `interfaceOptions` | `catalog.cpmd.INTERFACE_GMX`, `catalog.cpmd.INTERFACE_ESP`, `catalog.cpmd.INTERFACE_PCGFIRST` |
| `CENTER MOLECULE ON` | `centerMoleculeOn` | `catalog.cpmd.CENTER_MOLECULE_ON` |
| `BOX WALLS` in `&SYSTEM` | `system.boxWalls` | `params.inputSections.system.boxWalls` |
| `OPTIMIZE GEOMETRY CLASSICAL XYZ SAMPLE` | `optimizeGeometryOptions` plus `optimizeGeometrySample` | `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_CLASSICAL`, `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_XYZ`, `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_SAMPLE_OPTION` |
| `NOSE IONS ULTRA MASSIVE T0` | `noseIonsOptions` | `catalog.cpmd.NOSE_IONS_ULTRA`, `catalog.cpmd.NOSE_IONS_MASSIVE`, `catalog.cpmd.NOSE_IONS_T0` |
| `&VDW` with nested `EMPIRICAL CORRECTION` | `vdw.directives` and `vdw.subsections` | `catalog.section.VDW` |

# Inventory guardrails
The inventory files are part of the public compatibility contract, not only
generated lookup data.
`schema/inventory/cpmd_cp_keywords.txt` lists base `&CPMD` controls that must
exist as normalized `catalog.cpmd.*` feature rows.
Punctuation and spaces normalize to underscores, so `FREE-ENERGY` maps to
`catalog.cpmd.FREE_ENERGY`.
The JSON inventory carries both `opencpmd_inscan_sections` and `cpmd_sections`;
they must describe the same OpenCPMD parser section set.
`catalog.section.*`
feature rows must be owned by that set and by the checked-in
`schema/inventory/opencpmd_sections.txt` allowlist.

Run the focused inventory guards with:

meson test -C build \
  feature-inventory cpmd-base-keyword-inventory \
  cpmd-params-field-inventory cpmd-public-abi-inventory \
  stub-abi-symbol-coverage \
  shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage \
  cpmd-schema-render-coverage cpmd-option-token-coverage \
  cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage \
  cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage \
  --print-errorlogs

`feature-inventory` cross-checks the JSON inventory against the schema, public C
feature table, the C ABI reference, and this reference page.
When `CPMD_ROOT` points at an OpenCPMD tree, it also compares parser
`inscan('&SECTION')` calls with the checked-in section inventory.
`cpmd-base-keyword-inventory` proves the base keyword list cannot drop a
`catalog.cpmd.*` row silently.
`cpmd-params-field-inventory` requires every top-level `CPMDParams` schema field
to keep a `params.*` feature row.
It rejects duplicate inventory IDs/lists and C feature table duplicates before
set comparisons can hide them.
`cpmd-public-abi-inventory` requires every public
`cpmdc_*` header function to resolve through `abi_symbols` and the feature
table, then verifies the native
`src/cpmdc.c`, stub `src/cpmdc_stub.c`, or shared `src/cpmdc_features.c`
implementation that exports it.
`stub-abi-symbol-coverage` requires the standalone stub test to assert every
`abi_symbols` feature row is present and stub-applicable.
`shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage` requires the shared-library `dlopen` test to
load every `abi_symbols` entry from `libcpmdc.so`.
`cpmd-schema-render-coverage` requires typed `CPMDCpmdSection` fields to appear
in the catalog render fixtures, and `cpmd-option-token-coverage` requires inline
option spellings in Cap'n Proto fixtures to have render coverage.
`cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage` requires typed `cpmd`, `system`, `dft`, and
`atoms` fields to appear in render fixtures or render assertions.
`cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage` requires every `CPMDDirectiveSection` union
arm to appear in the long-tail fixture, render assertions, and this reference
page.
`cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage` requires `inputBlocks`, `generic`, `set`, and `raw`
carriers to stay covered by schema, fixtures, render tests, and this reference
page.

# ~CPMDInputSection~ kinds

| Kind | Cap'n Proto type | Deck effect |
|------+------------------+-------------|
| `atom` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&ATOM` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `cpmd` | `CPMDCpmdSection` | `&CPMD` (wavefunction/geometry optimization, MD, isolated/centered molecule controls, convergence, iteration limits, timestep, electron mass, …) |
| `system` | `CPMDSystemSection` | `&SYSTEM` (symmetry, cell/reference/classical cell, cutoff/grid/mesh controls, state occupation, external fields, CDFT Gaussian controls, pressure/stress controls, Poisson solver, surface/polymer/cluster, charge, …) |
| `dft` | `CPMDDftSection` | `&DFT` (functional, LSD, GC cutoff, XC driver, hybrid/Hubbard scalars, extra directives) |
| `atoms` | `CPMDAtomsSection` | `&ATOMS` (pseudopotential lines; coordinates come from `ForceInput`) |
| `basis` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&BASIS` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `clas` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&CLAS` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `eam` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&EAM` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `exte` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&EXTE` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `hardness` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&HARDNESS` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `info` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&INFO` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `linres` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&LINRES` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `molstates` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&MOLSTATES` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `mts` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&MTS` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `nlcc` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&NLCC` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `path` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&PATH` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `pimd` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&PIMD` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `potential` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&POTENTIAL` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `prop` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&PROP` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `ptddft` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&PTDDFT` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `resp` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&RESP` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `tddft` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&TDDFT` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `vdw` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&VDW` keyword/value lines and nested subsections such as `EMPIRICAL CORRECTION` |
| `vectors` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&VECTORS` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `wavefunction` | `CPMDDirectiveSection` | `&WAVEFUNCTION` keyword/value lines and nested subsections |
| `generic` | `CPMDGenericSection` | Arbitrary `&NAME` … `&END` |
| `set` | `CPMDSetDirective` | Embed-path logical `SECTION.KEYWORD` merged into the section |
| `raw` | `Text` | Full section text inserted as-is |

Missing core sections receive minimal defaults from the renderer so a sparse
`CPMDParams` still produces a valid-looking deck for debugging.
When structured `dft` or `system` sections provide scalar method values
(functional, cutoff, charge, multiplicity, or zero `system.charge` with
`system.hasCharge` `true`), those section values are also the
effective embed configuration passed through the C ABI.
The functional, cutoff, charge, and multiplicity lines the renderer writes
and that configuration follow the same precedence.
`raw`, `generic`, and `set` sections, `inputBlocks`, and section `directives`
are rendered as given and are not read back into that configuration, so the
carrier check runs for every set overlay field of a `common` overlay,
whether or not a typed field also sets it, including zero `charge` with
`hasCharge` `true`, and a carrier of the same setting
rejects that field.
A `FUNCTIONAL` directive in a typed `dft` section or a `DFT.FUNCTIONAL` set
directive is rejected when the deck is rendered, because the rendered `&DFT`
section already carries the functional.
The same render rejects a `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY` directive in
the typed `system` section, and a `SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or
`SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY` set directive.
`CUTOFF` is written on every deck, including the default 70 Ry.
`CHARGE` is written only when it is not 0 and `MULTIPLICITY` only when it is
greater than 1; an omitted line is the schema default the recorded
configuration carries.
Those directives are rejected for a default value and for any other value
alike.
A default leaves the directive as a value the recorded configuration does not
carry, and any other value leaves two lines.
The render does not keep one and drop the other.
A section value that differs from the schema default (functional `BLYP`,
cutoff 70 Ry, charge 0 with `hasCharge` `false`, multiplicity 1) beats the
top-level field.
A method field in a typed `dft` or `system` section that is omitted or holds
its schema default is unset and does not replace the top-level arm or overlay
value, so a typed `system` charge of 0 with `hasCharge` `false` is also unset,
while zero `system.charge` with `system.hasCharge` `true` is explicit.
For geometry deck rendering, `atoms.pseudopotentials` groups `ForceInput`
coordinates by element symbol.
Explicit pseudopotential entries accept standard element symbols and must cover
every atomic number present in the step geometry; otherwise rendering fails.
When no `atoms` section is supplied, the renderer only provides built-in BLYP
pseudopotential defaults for H and O. An explicit `atoms` section may rely on
those H/O defaults while still carrying `CPMDDirective` entries for additional
`&ATOMS` keywords.

# Escape hatches
Long-tail CPMD keywords go in `CPMDDirective` lists or `subsections` inside the
matching typed section, `CPMDSetDirective` dotted keys, `CPMDInputSection.raw`,
or `inputBlocks`.
`&VDW` uses `subsections` for nested blocks such as `EMPIRICAL CORRECTION`.
`set.key` uses `SECTION.KEYWORD` form, for example `CPMD.PRINT FORCES ON` or
`SYSTEM.POISSON SOLVER HOCKNEY`; non-empty `set.value` is emitted on the
following indented line.
Prefer new structured fields in the schema over inventing a second config file
format.

# Choosing an input carrier
Use the most structured carrier that represents the deck intent.
The usual path is:

1. Put functional, cutoff, charge, multiplicity, task, and embed hints in the
   top-level `CPMDParams` fields.
2. Put named OpenCPMD section controls in typed `inputSections` arms such as
   `system`, `cpmd`, `dft`, and `atoms`.
3. Put extra section keywords in that section's `directives` list when they
   naturally belong to a typed section.
4. Use `set` for one merge-only keyword, `generic` for a non-catalog section
   alias, and `raw` or `inputBlocks` for text that must remain literal.

| Requirement | Carrier | Reason |
|-------------+---------+--------|
| Supported OpenCPMD `inscan('&SECTION')` block | typed section field | Schema readers, tests, and feature discovery can name the field directly |
| Catalog section without typed fields, such as `&PIMD`, `&VDW`, `&LINRES`, or `&TDDFT` | the matching section arm with `directives` and `subsections` | The section kind stays typed while its keywords stay lines |
| One extra keyword inside a generated section | `set` | The renderer merges it into the matching section without duplicating defaults |
| Non-catalog section alias with ordinary keyword/argument lines | `generic` | The section remains structured even when it is not an inventory ID |
| Existing deck text that must survive byte-for-byte apart from surrounding output | `raw` or `inputBlocks` | The renderer does not reinterpret the fragment |

For example, a compact typed setup with one extra `&SYSTEM` keyword looks like:

(
  functional = "PBE0",
  cutOffRy = 85.0,
  multiplicity = 2,
  task = "gradient",
  inputSections = [
    ( system = (
        symmetry = 0,
        angstrom = true,
        cutOffRy = 85.0,
        cell = [12.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
      ) ),
    ( cpmd = (
        optimizeWavefunction = true,
        convergenceOrbitals = 1.0e-6,
        maxStep = 50,
        electronMass = 450.0
      ) ),
    ( dft = (
        functional = "PBE0",
        lsd = true,
        hfx = true,
        hfxScreening = "0.2"
      ) ),
    ( atoms = ( pseudopotentials = [
        ( element = "O", path = "O_MT_BLYP.psp", lmax = 1 ),
        ( element = "H", path = "H_CVB_BLYP.psp", lmax = 0 )
      ] ) ),
    ( set = ( key = "SYSTEM.POISSON SOLVER", value = "HOCKNEY" ) )
  ]
)

# Catalog section exposure
The public feature table advertises every OpenCPMD `inscan('&SECTION')` name as
a `catalog.section.<NAME>` feature ID.
Typed sections have dedicated schema arms; every section can still be rendered
through `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` when a dedicated field is
unnecessary.

| Feature ID | Deck section | ABI carrier |
|------------+--------------+-------------|
| `catalog.section.ATOM` | `&ATOM` | typed `atom`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.ATOMS` | `&ATOMS` | typed `atoms`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.BASIS` | `&BASIS` | typed `basis`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.CLAS` | `&CLAS` | typed `clas`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.CPMD` | `&CPMD` | typed `cpmd`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.DFT` | `&DFT` | typed `dft`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.EAM` | `&EAM` | typed `eam`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.EXTE` | `&EXTE` | typed `exte`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.HARDNESS` | `&HARDNESS` | typed `hardness`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.INFO` | `&INFO` | typed `info`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.LINRES` | `&LINRES` | typed `linres`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.MOLSTATES` | `&MOLSTATES` | typed `molstates`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.MTS` | `&MTS` | typed `mts`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.NLCC` | `&NLCC` | typed `nlcc`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.PATH` | `&PATH` | typed `path`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.PIMD` | `&PIMD` | typed `pimd`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.POTENTIAL` | `&POTENTIAL` | typed `potential`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.PROP` | `&PROP` | typed `prop`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.PTDDFT` | `&PTDDFT` | typed `ptddft`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.RESP` | `&RESP` | typed `resp`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.SYSTEM` | `&SYSTEM` | typed `system`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.TDDFT` | `&TDDFT` | typed `tddft`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.VDW` | `&VDW` | typed `vdw`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.VECTORS` | `&VECTORS` | typed `vectors`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |
| `catalog.section.WAVEFUNCTION` | `&WAVEFUNCTION` | typed `wavefunction`, `set`, `generic`, `raw`, or `inputBlocks` |

# Other structured parameter features
These `params.inputSections.*`
IDs cover carriers and fields that are not single CPMD/DFT catalog keyword rows
in the typed tables below.

A `system.cellVectors` cell contains nine numbers grouped by lattice vector.
Typed parameter rendering preserves them on one data line; geometry overrides
use three vector rows.
OpenCPMD accepts either layout in one list-directed read.
`CELL VECTORS` specifies implicit triclinic symmetry, so its deck omits the
`SYMMETRY` line and the default isolated Poisson solver.
Combining `SYMMETRY` with `CELL VECTORS` is rejected by the native parser.
The vector qualifier also requires nine values and excludes `ABSOLUTE` and
`DEGREE`.

| Parameter feature ID | Field | Deck effect |
|----------------------+-------+-------------|
| `params.inputSections.generic.name` | `generic.name` | Section name for an arbitrary `&NAME` block |
| `params.inputSections.generic.directives` | `generic.directives` | Keyword/value lines inside the generic section |
| `params.inputSections.atom.directives` | `atom.directives` | Keyword/value lines inside `&ATOM` |
| `params.inputSections.atom.subsections` | `atom.subsections` | Nested blocks inside `&ATOM` |
| `params.inputSections.system.symmetry` | `system.symmetry` | `&SYSTEM SYMMETRY` |
| `params.inputSections.system.angstrom` | `system.angstrom` | `&SYSTEM ANGSTROM` |
| `params.inputSections.system.cell` | `system.cell` | `&SYSTEM CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.cellAbsolute` | `system.cellAbsolute` | Add `ABSOLUTE` to `&SYSTEM CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.cellDegree` | `system.cellDegree` | Add `DEGREE` to `&SYSTEM CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.cellVectors` | `system.cellVectors` | Add `VECTORS` to `&SYSTEM CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.referenceCell` | `system.referenceCell` | `&SYSTEM REFERENCE CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.referenceCellAbsolute` | `system.referenceCellAbsolute` | Add `ABSOLUTE` to `REFERENCE CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.referenceCellDegree` | `system.referenceCellDegree` | Add `DEGREE` to `REFERENCE CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.referenceCellVectors` | `system.referenceCellVectors` | Add `VECTORS` to `REFERENCE CELL` |
| `params.inputSections.system.classicalCell` | `system.classicalCell` | `&SYSTEM CLASSICAL CELL` |

| `params.inputSections.raw` | `raw` | Full section text inserted as-is |

# Typed ~&CPMD~ controls
`CPMDCpmdSection` exposes these driver controls directly; parser-accepted
escape-hatch rows use `directives`.
The feature IDs are the stable discovery keys returned by
`cpmdc_feature_table()`.

| Catalog feature ID | Parameter feature ID | Field | Deck keyword |
|--------------------+----------------------+-------+--------------|
| `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_WAVEFUNCTION` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.optimizeWavefunction` | `optimizeWavefunction` | `OPTIMIZE WAVEFUNCTION` |
| `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.optimizeGeometry` | `optimizeGeometry` | `OPTIMIZE GEOMETRY` |
| `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_OPTIONS` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.optimizeGeometryOptions` | `optimizeGeometryOptions` | `OPTIMIZE GEOMETRY` |
| `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_CLASSICAL` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.optimizeGeometryOptions` | `optimizeGeometryOptions` | `OPTIMIZE GEOMETRY CLASSICAL` |
| `catalog.cpmd.OPTIMIZE_GEOMETRY_XYZ` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.optimizeGeometryOptions` | `optimizeGeometryOptions` | `OPTIMIZE GEOMETRY XYZ` |

`EXTRAPOLATE WFN` renders into every deck that sets `extrapolateWfnOptions` or
`extrapolateWfnOrder`.
`cpmd.x` applies it in Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics only.
On the in-process route it applies to every call that starts from stored
orbitals, when the archive carries `tools/opencpmd_embed_extrapolate.patch`.
The extrapolation how-to (file:../howto/extrapolate-orbitals.org) shows a
message and the check.

| Part | In-process route |
|------+------------------|
| `ASPC`, or no option | always stable predictor-corrector (ASPC) coefficients, OpenCPMD's default |
| `POLY` | polynomial coefficients |
| order | number of earlier calls in the prediction |
| `STORE` | no effect, with no `RESTART` file from a library call |
| `CSTEPS` | no effect, with converged orbitals on every call |

# ~PotentialConfig~
For rgpot / multi-backend configure RPCs, `PotentialConfig` is a tagged union
with `cpmd @2 :CPMDParams` (ordinal aligned with the shared schema; `nwchem @1`
is reserved void in this package).


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/cpmdparams-schema.org

The schema is `schema/Potentials.capnp`, a vendored copy of the shared
`potentials-schema` release pinned in `subprojects/potentials-schema.wrap`.
This page lists the fields that decide what CPMD computes.
The option mapping (file:cpmd-options.org) lists every typed field with its feature ID
and deck spelling.

# ~CPMDParams~

| Field | Type, default | Role |
|-------+---------------+------|
| `functional` | `Text`, `"BLYP"` | functional when no `dft` section sets one |
| `cutOffRy` | `Float64`, 70.0 | plane-wave cutoff in Rydberg when no `system` section sets one |
| `charge` | `Int32`, 0 | system charge when the `system` section does not set one |
| `hasCharge` | `Bool`, `false` | mark `charge` as explicit, including zero |
| `multiplicity` | `Int32`, 1 | 2S+1; above 1 selects spin-polarized defaults |
| `task` | `Text`, `"gradient"` | host hint: `energy`, `gradient`, `md`, `optimize` |
| `title` | `Text` | comment header of the rendered deck |
| `memoryMb` | `UInt32`, 0 | host memory hint |
| `scratchDir`, `permanentDir` | `Text` | `FILEPATH` in `&CPMD`. `cpmd.x` writes `RESTART.1`, `LATEST`, `GEOMETRY`, and `GEOMETRY.xyz` there. A library force call writes none of them. `permanentDir` wins |
| `cpmdRoot` | `Text` | OpenCPMD tree hint for hosts |
| `enginePath` | `Text` | library path hint for hosts such as `rgpot` |
| `inputBlocks` | `List(Text)` | literal `&SECTION ... &END` blocks placed before the rendered sections |
| `inputSections` | `List(CPMDInputSection)` | structured sections, rendered in list order |

A section missing from `inputSections` gets a default: `&CPMD` with
`OPTIMIZE WAVEFUNCTION` and `CONVERGENCE ORBITALS` 1e-6, `&SYSTEM` with
`ANGSTROM` and the top-level cutoff, charge, and multiplicity, and `&DFT`
with the top-level functional.
That deck has no `SYMMETRY` line.
A force call with a positive volume writes symmetry 1 for a cube, symmetry 8
for unequal orthogonal edges, or `CELL VECTORS` with no symmetry line when
the box is tilted.
A zero box stays `SYMMETRY 0` and adds `POISSON SOLVER HOCKNEY`.

# ~CPMDInputSection~
A union; each list entry sets exactly one arm.

| Arm | Payload | Renders |
|-----+---------+---------|
| `cpmd` | `CPMDCpmdSection` | `&CPMD` |
| `system` | `CPMDSystemSection` | `&SYSTEM` |
| `dft` | `CPMDDftSection` | `&DFT` |
| `atoms` | `CPMDAtomsSection` | `&ATOMS` without coordinates |
| `vdwParams`, `propParams`, `linresParams`, `pimdParams`, `pathParams`, `tddftParams`, `respParams`, `exteParams`, `vectorsParams` | typed long-tail sections | the matching section |
| `atom`, `basis`, `clas`, `eam`, `exte`, `hardness`, `info`, `linres`, `molstates`, `mts`, `nlcc`, `path`, `pimd`, `potential`, `prop`, `ptddft`, `resp`, `tddft`, `vdw`, `vectors`, `wavefunction` | `CPMDDirectiveSection`: `directives` and nested `subsections` | the matching section, one line per directive |
| `set` | `CPMDSetDirective`: `key = "SECTION.KEYWORD"`, `value` | one keyword merged into a named section |
| `generic` | `CPMDGenericSection`: `name`, `directives` | a section by name |
| `raw` | `Text` | a full `&SECTION ... &END` block, verbatim |

# ~CPMDDirective~

| Field | Meaning |
|-------+---------|
| `keyword` | the line, for example `"PCG MINIMIZE"` |
| `args` | `List(Text)`; each entry becomes one indented line below the keyword |

Every typed section has a `directives` list for keywords without a typed
field.

# ~CPMDCpmdSection~, the fields a force call uses

| Field | Default | Deck |
|-------+---------+------|
| `optimizeWavefunction` | `true` | `OPTIMIZE WAVEFUNCTION` |
| `convergenceOrbitals` | 1e-6 | `CONVERGENCE ORBITALS` |
| `maxIter` | 0, omitted | `MAXITER`; the OpenCPMD path inserts 40 when absent |
| `maxStep` | 0, omitted | `MAXSTEP`, the geometry step limit of CPMD's own drivers |
| `odiis`, `odiisVectors`, `odiisOptions` | off | `ODIIS` and its vector count |
| `pcg` | off | `PCG`; `PCG MINIMIZE` goes in `directives` |
| `diis` | off | `DIIS` |
| `centerMoleculeOff`, `centerMoleculeOn` | off | `CENTER MOLECULE OFF` / `ON` |
| `restartWavefunction` | off | `RESTART WAVEFUNCTION`; read on a cold evaluation only |
| `isolatedMolecule` | off | `ISOLATED MOLECULE` |

The OpenCPMD path ignores restarted coordinates, velocities, and geometry:
the host owns them.

# ~CPMDSystemSection~, the fields that set the cell

| Field | Default | Deck |
|-------+---------+------|
| `symmetry` | 0 | `SYMMETRY`; 0 is isolated |
| `angstrom` | `true` | `ANGSTROM`, the unit of `CELL` and `&ATOMS` |
| `cell` | empty | `CELL`: six values `a, b/a, c/a, cos(alpha), cos(beta), cos(gamma)`, or nine with `cellVectors` |
| `cellAbsolute`, `cellDegree`, `cellVectors` | off | `CELL ABSOLUTE`, `DEGREE`, `VECTORS` |
| `cutOffRy` | 70.0 | `CUTOFF` |
| `poissonSolver`, `poissonParameter` | empty | `POISSON SOLVER`; `SYMMETRY 0` without one adds `HOCKNEY`, or `TUCKERMAN` for a hybrid functional |
| `charge`, `hasCharge`, `multiplicity` | 0, `false`, 1 | `CHARGE`, `MULTIPLICITY`; `hasCharge` marks zero `charge` explicit |
| `kpointsMonkhorstPack` | empty | `KPOINTS MONKHORST-PACK` |

# ~CPMDDftSection~

| Field | Default | Deck |
|-------+---------+------|
| `functional` | `"BLYP"` | `FUNCTIONAL` |
| `lsd` | `false` | `LSD` |
| `gcCutoff` | 0, omitted | `GC-CUTOFF` |
| `oldCode`, `newCode` | off | `OLDCODE` / `NEWCODE` |
| `hfx`, `hfxScreening` | off | hybrid exchange controls |

# ~CPMDAtomsSection~ and ~CPMDAtomsPseudopotential~

| Field | Default | Deck |
|-------+---------+------|
| `element` | | element symbol, such as `"Si"` |
| `path` | | the `*file` line, a library name or a path |
| `lmax`, `loc`, `skip` | -1, omitted | `LMAX=`, `LOC=`, `SKIP=`; 0 is `S`, 1 `P`, 2 `D`, 3 `F` |
| `kleinmanBylander` | `false` | `KLEINMAN-BYLANDER` on the `*file` line |
| `raggio` | 0, omitted | `RAGGIO=` |
| `nonlinearCore` | `false` | `NLCC` |

The `atoms` section also carries `constraints`, `isotopes`, `velocities`,
`dummyAtoms`, `changeBonds`, `generate`, and `directives`.
Coordinates never go here.
On the OpenCPMD path, the `&ATOMS` block CPMD reads is rebuilt from each
step's geometry.
Entries in `pseudopotentials` supply the file, `LMAX`, `LOC`, and
`KLEINMAN-BYLANDER` for the elements they name.
Elements left out of that list use a built-in table for H, C, N, O, Si, and
Ge; see writing a CPMDParams message (file:../howto/write-cpmdparams.org).

# ~ForceInput~

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|-------+---------+---------|
| `pos` | | `3 * natoms` coordinates in `lengthUnit` |
| `atmnrs` | | atomic numbers |
| `box` | empty | nine values, row-major cell vectors in `lengthUnit` |
| `lengthUnit` | `"angstrom"` | unit of `pos` and `box` |
| `energyUnit` | `"eV"` | unit of the `PotentialResult` energy |

# ~PotentialConfig~
A union of backend arms plus a `common` overlay (`CommonMethodSpec`).
`cpmdc` accepts the `cpmd` arm, which holds a `CPMDParams`, the overlay alone,
or both together.
When both are set, a value the arm sets beats the overlay, and the overlay
fills only what the arm leaves at the schema defaults and beats a schema
default.
The overlay fills `xcFunctionals`, `planewaveCutoffEv`, `charge`,
`spinMultiplicity`, Fermi `smearing` (when `&CPMD` sets none), and
`vanDerWaalsS6` (into a `vdwParams` section with `s6` unset).
An arm field sets a value when it differs from the schema default (functional
`BLYP`, cutoff 70 Ry, charge 0 with `hasCharge` `false`, multiplicity 1), and
a typed `dft` or `system` section beats the top-level field.
A method field in a typed section that is omitted or holds its schema default
is unset and does not replace the top-level arm or overlay value; a typed
`system` charge of 0 with `hasCharge` `false` is unset, and a non-zero charge
or zero `system.charge` with `system.hasCharge` `true` is explicit.
`planewaveCutoffEv` is in eV and is converted to the Ry the deck carries.
`spinMultiplicity` 0 is unset, so an explicit singlet of 1 is merged and
checked like the other overlay scalars.
The functional, cutoff, charge, and multiplicity lines the deck renderers
write and the recorded settings follow this precedence.
An unmapped `xcFunctionals` token is rejected for every arm functional,
before that precedence.
Opaque carriers are rendered as given and are not folded into the recorded
settings, so the carrier check runs for every set overlay field, whether or
not a typed field also sets it, including zero `charge` with `hasCharge`
`true` and an explicit singlet `spinMultiplicity` of 1.
The overlay field is rejected when `inputBlocks`, a raw section, or a generic
section opens `&DFT` (`xcFunctionals`) or `&SYSTEM` (cutoff, charge,
multiplicity), when a set directive names `DFT.FUNCTIONAL`,
`SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or `SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY`, or when the
`directives` list of the typed `dft` section holds `FUNCTIONAL` or that of
the typed `system` section holds `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or `MULTIPLICITY`.
Without an overlay, the deck render rejects a `CUTOFF`, `CHARGE`, or
`MULTIPLICITY` directive in the typed `system` section, and a
`SYSTEM.CUTOFF`, `SYSTEM.CHARGE`, or `SYSTEM.MULTIPLICITY` set directive.
`CUTOFF` is written on every deck, including the default 70 Ry.
`CHARGE` is written only when it is not 0 and `MULTIPLICITY` only when it is
greater than 1; an omitted line is the schema default the recorded
configuration carries.
Those directives are rejected for a default value and for any other value
alike.
A default leaves the directive as a value the recorded configuration does not
carry, and any other value leaves two lines.
The render does not keep one and drop the other.
Fermi `smearing` also rejects split `TEMPERATURE` and `ELECTRON` arguments
in `cpmd.directives` and `CPMD.TEMPERATURE` set directives.
The merge requires `basisSet` to be unset or `"planewave"`, and rejects
negative or non-finite scalars and conflicting or unmergeable fields
(`kMesh`, SCF controls, `vanDerWaalsMethod`, `relativityMethod`, already-set
smearing or `s6`, or `vanDerWaalsS6` without `vdwParams`); see the
C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org) for the lowering rules.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/environment.org

# Read by libcpmdc at run time

| Variable | Read in | Effect |
|----------+---------+--------|
| `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` | `src/cpmdc_embed_host.c`, each cold OpenCPMD evaluation | directory holding the pseudopotential files named in the deck; `cpmdc` changes into it while CPMD reads them, then leaves it before CPMD writes output files |
| `CPMD_PP_LIBRARY_PATH` | same place, when `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` is unset | fallback for the same directory |
| `CPMDC_DECK_OUT` | `src/cpmdc.c`, each time a message is rendered | file that receives the rendered method deck; each write replaces the last |
| `CPMDC_STRESS` | `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90`, each evaluation, OpenCPMD or the reference evaluator | `0` skips the stress tensor on periodic cells; any other value, or unset, computes it |
| `CPMDC_SCF_STEPS` | `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90`, each OpenCPMD evaluation | `1` writes `cpmdc_warm_start`, `cpmdc_wfn_extrapolated K`, and `cpmdc_scf_steps N` to the error stream |
| `CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` | `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90`, each OpenCPMD evaluation | largest root-mean-square distance per atom, Angstrom, at which stored orbitals start the SCF on a matching basis; default 0.15, a negative value takes them at any distance, and beyond the limit the SCF starts from the deck's guess without full setup |
| `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` | `src/cpmdc_orbital_limit.c`, before each OpenCPMD evaluation or orbital copy | calculator rank 0's largest principal strain from the cell CPMD was set up at, as a fraction of a length, at which a constant-cutoff deck keeps its plane waves and stored orbitals; unset, 0, a negative value, or a value that does not parse sets CPMD up again for every new cell |
| `CPMDC_RECENTER` | `src/cpmd_embed_c_api.F90`, each OpenCPMD evaluation on an isolated deck | `mass` (default) or `geometry` moves the atoms rigidly so that that centre is the middle of the cell along every non-periodic lattice vector, and removes the net force; `off` or `0` keeps the caller's coordinates; `MASS`, `GEOMETRY` and `OFF` are accepted too; any other value fails the call |
| `CPMDC_RECENTER_MARGIN` | same place | least distance, Angstrom, between an atom and a face of the isolated cell after the move; a closer atom fails the call; default 0, a negative value turns the check off, a value that does not parse fails the call |
| `CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS` | `src/cpmdc.c`, each evaluation under a running MPI | `1` gives every rank of the calculator rank 0's energy, gradient, and result snapshots, and records the rank spread; any other value, or unset, leaves each rank's own result |
| `CPMDC_ORBITAL_SLOT_LIMIT` | `src/cpmdc.c` on each evaluation and orbital copy, and `tools/opencpmd_embed_rwfopt.patch` when the host has not already agreed a value | unset leaves parked orbital copies unbounded; a positive integer is the most parked copies, excluding the selected key; empty, zero, negative, and non-integer values fail the call |

A cold OpenCPMD evaluation fails when neither `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` nor
`CPMD_PP_LIBRARY_PATH` names an existing directory.
The result message and `cpmdc_last_error()` name that directory; the call does
not report an unconverged SCF.
While `cpmdc` is in the pseudopotential directory it also sets
`CPMD_PP_LIBRARY_PATH` and `PP_LIBRARY_PATH` to that directory with a trailing
slash, for OpenCPMD's own lookup.
