The change of directory is needed because OpenCPMD's `get_pplib` takes `argv[2]`
as the library path whenever the process has more than one argument, which most
hosts do.
Once the pseudopotential files are read, the working directory becomes
`permanentDir` if that field is set, otherwise `scratchDir`, otherwise the host
directory from before the call.
A library force call writes no `RESTART.1`, `LATEST`, `GEOMETRY`, or
`GEOMETRY.xyz` there.
`cpmd.x` writes those files in that directory.
The pseudopotential directory is left unchanged.

`CPMDC_STRESS=0` saves the stress calculation for callers that use only energy
and forces, and the stress snapshot stays invalid.
Isolated cells never compute stress, whatever the variable says, and the
snapshot stays invalid for them even when the box volume is positive.

`CPMDC_RECENTER` acts on an isolated deck (`SYMMETRY 0`, a Poisson solver,
`CLUSTER`, `SURFACE` or `POLYMER`); a periodic deck is not moved.
A slab (`SURFACE`) moves only along its normal and a wire (`POLYMER`) only
across its axis.
With `mass` or `geometry`, energy, forces and `sum_i x_i (x) f_i` do not change
when the caller translates every atom.
Warm-start distances and stored orbitals use the moved coordinates; the caller's
arrays are not changed.
The margin applies with `off` too, so by default an atom outside the cell fails
the call instead of running with density across a face;
`CPMDC_RECENTER_MARGIN=-1` lets it run, as releases before the recentring did.
`cpmd.x` keeps the deck's coordinates, so a comparison with it needs
`CPMDC_RECENTER=off`, and `CPMDC_RECENTER_MARGIN=-1` for atoms outside the cell;
the `water-capnp-cli-parity` and `extrapolate-wfn` tests set both.
Atoms in an isolated cell (file:../explanation/isolated-cells.org) explains
why the library moves the atoms and what drift costs without it.

`CPMDC_SCF_STEPS=1` writes one line, `cpmdc_scf_steps N`, for each SCF that
returns.
`N` is that SCF's iteration count.
Before each evaluation it also writes `cpmdc_warm_start S D`: where the SCF
starts (`S` 0 the selected key's stored orbitals, 1 another key's parked
orbitals, -1 the deck's guess because every stored geometry lies beyond
`CPMDC_WARM_RMSD`) and the nearest distance `D` in Angstrom, or
`cpmdc_warm_start -2` when nothing is stored.
Lines with a distance also include `donor_key=K`, the key whose converged
orbitals supply the selected history, and `periodic=T` or `periodic=F`, the
native boundary model used for the distance.
A rejected history's donor key describes the nearest stored candidate, not an
accepted warm start.
A call whose orbitals start from the `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` prediction writes
`cpmdc_wfn_extrapolated K` before its `cpmdc_scf_steps` line, with `K` the
number of earlier converged orbital sets that the prediction combined.
Each line is flushed as it is written, so a log file shows it while the host
runs.

`CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` is the distance limit of
the stored orbitals (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org) (section
Distance limit).
A value that does not parse as a number keeps the default.

`CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` acts only on a periodic deck with `CONSTANT CUTOFF`; any
other deck sets CPMD up again for every new cell, whatever the variable says.
A cell within the limit takes the plane waves of the setup cell, so the call
starts from the stored orbitals and keeps the `EXTRAPOLATE WFN` history.
Wavefunction state between calls (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org)
(section Cell changes at a constant cutoff) gives the conditions and what the
move changes in the energy and the stress.
Calculator rank 0 reads the value and broadcasts it; values on the other ranks
are ignored.

`CPMDC_ORBITAL_SLOT_LIMIT` is the most parked orbital copies a calculator keeps,
excluding the key that is selected.
Unset, the table grows with each new key.
A positive integer refuses a park that would pass that count: the evaluation
or the copy fails, `cpmdc_last_error()` names the variable, and the copies
already stored stay where they are.
Lowering the value does not discard copies already parked; the next new park
fails until the count is within the new limit.
An empty value, zero, a negative value, or any value that is not a positive
integer fails the call and does not leave the table unbounded.
Every calculator rank must use the same value.
A rank that disagrees, or an MPI collective that fails, fails the call on
every rank.
Each evaluation and each copy checks its own arguments and session first and
agrees the value only after that, so a call that is itself bad reports that
reason even when the value is unusable.
A rank that rejects its own call still joins the agreement, and every other
rank then fails the call too, with a message that another rank rejected it,
instead of waiting for it.
A session evaluation validates its topology without mutating the session and
commits it only after the collective preflight succeeds on every rank, so a
failed preflight leaves the session unchanged.
Every rank also agrees whether an orbital key is selected, whether stale
orbitals were cleared, and whether orbital preparation succeeded, failing
every rank with the same error when any rank diverges or fails.
`cpmd.x` and a warm-start call that does not go through the library read the
variable themselves.

`CPMDC_RANK_CONSENSUS=1` adds three collectives to each evaluation on the
calculator communicator: the one bound or adopted, or `MPI_COMM_WORLD` when
neither call was made.
Every rank fails when one rank failed, and every rank resets its CPMD state when
one rank stopped.
A repeat of the stored positions returns the stored result only when every rank
repeats.
`cpmdc_last_rank_spread()` then reports the largest energy and gradient
difference from rank 0 before the broadcast.
Set it to the same value on every rank.
A build without MPI ignores it.

# Test hooks in libcpmdc
These change results on purpose and must be unset in ordinary runs.

| Variable | Read in | Effect |
|----------+---------+--------|
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_MPI_FAULT` | `src/cpmdc_pwscale.c`, builds with `-Dwith_pwscale=true` and MPI (`pwscale-mpi-fault`) | `gather` drops rank 0's gather buffer when the bind is created; `team` fails the last rank's team; every rank still reports the failure |

# Read by the tests and tools

| Variable | Read by | Effect |
|----------+---------+--------|
| `CPMD_ROOT`, then `CPMDC_CPMD_ROOT` | `tools/check_feature_inventory.py` (`feature-inventory` test) | OpenCPMD source tree to probe for `inscan('&SECTION')` calls; without it the live completeness check is skipped with a warning |
| `CPMD_SRC`, then `OPENCPMD_SRC` | `tests/test_cpmd_inscan_token_fidelity.py` | OpenCPMD source tree for the parser token check |
| `CPMDC_CPMD_EXE`, then `CPMD_ROOT` | `tools/cpmd_root_probe.py` | the `cpmd.x` to check, or the tree whose `bin/cpmd.x` it checks |
| `MAKE`, `AR` | `tools/rebuild_opencpmd_embed.sh` | the Make and archiver programs; default `make` and `ar` |
| `CPMDC_TEST_PARAMS`, `CPMDC_TEST_PERIODIC_PARAMS` | `tests/python/conftest.py` (`python-pytest`) | encoded cluster and periodic water `CPMDParams`; without them the text messages in `tests/` are encoded with `capnp` |
| `CPMDC_TEST_INSTALLED` | `tests/python/conftest.py` | `1` tests the installed package instead of `python/` of the checkout |
| `CPMDC_IPI_C` | `tests/python/test_ipi_c_driver.py` | the `cpmdc-ipi-c` to test; default `build/cpmdc-ipi-c` |
| `CPMDC_LAMMPS_PLUGIN` | `tests/python/test_lammps.py` | the `cpmdcplugin.so` to load; default `build/cpmdcplugin.so` |
| `CPMDC_GROMACS_LIB` | `tests/python/test_gromacs.py`, `test_gromacs_opencpmd.py` | the `libcpmdc_gromacs.so` to load; default `build/libcpmdc_gromacs.so` |
| `CPMDC_GMX` | `tests/python/gromacs_case.py`, `bench/gromacs_routes.py` | the double-precision `gmx_d` built against `libcp2k.pc`; default `gmx_d` on `PATH` |
| `CPMDC_GMX_MPI`, `CPMDC_MPIEXEC` | `tests/python/gromacs_case.py` | an MPI `gmx_mpi_d` and its launcher; default `gmx_mpi_d` and `mpiexec` on `PATH` |
| `CPMDC_EXAMPLE_WORK` | `tests/test_docs_examples.py` | set by the test itself to its scratch directory |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_FFT_FAULT` | `bench/pwscale_fft.c` (`pwscale-fft-fail`) | names an FFT setup step that must fail, to check the cleanup path |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_POISON_RUN` | `bench/pwscale_harness.c` (`pwscale-logger`) | adds 1 Hartree to the energy of that run number, to check the logger rejects it |
| `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK`, `PMIX_RANK`, `PMI_RANK`; `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_SIZE`, `PMI_SIZE` | `bench/constant_cutoff_npt.py` | set by the MPI launcher; the first of each that is set gives the rank, and rank 0 writes the record, the state, and the tables, and the rank count that the record keeps; unset, one rank |
| `CPMDC_ORG_EXPORT` | `docs/export.el` | `pandoc` exports the Org pages with pandoc instead of ox-rst |

The live tests of an OpenCPMD build (`meson test -C build-cpmd`) run `libcpmdc`,
so they need `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` like any other host.

# Read by hosts that load libcpmdc
These belong to the host, not to `cpmdc`, and are listed here because they
decide which `libcpmdc` a host loads.

| Variable | Host | Effect |
|----------+------+--------|
| `CPMDC_GROMACS_PARAMS` | `libcpmdc_gromacs` | `CPMDParams` message used when GROMACS generated `md_cp2k.inp` from an `.mdp` and `.tpr` without an explicit `&CPMDC` section; its functional, charge, and multiplicity must match the generated input |
| `CPMDC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE` | `rgpot` `CPMDPot` and `python/cpmdc` | path of the `libcpmdc.so` to `dlopen`, tried in that order after an explicit engine path |
| `CPMDC_PARAMS` | `examples/python/ase_energy.py` | encoded `CPMDParams` the example reads; the ASE tutorial (file:../tutorials/ase-energy.org) sets it |
| `CPMDC_SCHEMA` | `python/cpmdc` `find_schema` | path of `schema/Potentials.capnp` for encoding `CPMDParams` text; a cell needs no schema, because the package encodes `ForceInput` itself |
| `RGPOT_PARAMS_PATH` | eOn `RgpotPot` builds that read `params_path` | overrides `[RgpotPot] params_path` |
| `OMP_NUM_THREADS` | OpenMP runtime | threads per rank inside CPMD when OpenCPMD was built with OpenMP |


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/feature-inventory.org

# Two copies of one list
`cpmdc` keeps its capability list twice.
`src/cpmdc_features.c` compiles it into the library, where `cpmdc_feature_count()`, `cpmdc_feature_table()`, and `cpmdc_feature_find()`
serve it at run time.
`schema/inventory/cpmd_features.json` holds the same rows with metadata for the
checks.
The Meson suite fails when the two copies, the schema, the headers, or the docs
drift apart.

# Feature IDs

The inventory describes the cpmdc engine boundary, not transport protocols.
i-PI is an optional rgpot frontend over =CPMDPot= and other potentials;
protocol frontends are not =cpmdc_feature_*= rows.  The audited rgpot
develop snapshot provides the audited generic
i-PI route (file:../howto/socket-drivers.org) through =CPMDPot=.
The cpmdc-specific i-PI drivers remain compatibility fallbacks, not engine
capabilities.

| Namespace | Kind | Example | Means |
|-----------+------+---------+-------|
| `abi.*` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_ABI` | `abi.cpmdc_session_calculate_result` | an exported C function |
| `params.*` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_PARAMS` | `params.cutOffRy` | a top-level `CPMDParams` field |
| `params.inputSections.<arm>.<field>` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_PARAMS` | `params.inputSections.cpmd.maxIter` | a typed field inside a section arm |
| `catalog.section.*` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_SECTION` | `catalog.section.PIMD` | a deck section OpenCPMD's parser reads with `inscan('&NAME')` |
| `catalog.cpmd.*` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_KEYWORD` | `catalog.cpmd.ODIIS` | a `&CPMD` keyword or inline option spelling |
| `catalog.dft.*` | `CPMDC_FEATURE_KEYWORD` | `catalog.dft.PCGC` | a `&DFT` keyword |
| `section.*` | inventory only | `section.generic` | a `CPMDInputSection` union arm |

A `params.*` row names a field you can write.
A `catalog.*` row says that the renderer can emit a keyword or section, often
through a text field of a typed section rather than a field of its own.
`stub_applicable` and `embed_applicable` say whether the stub build and the
OpenCPMD build expose the row.

# Query it from C
const CPMDCFeatureEntry *e = cpmdc_feature_find("params.inputSections.cpmd.odiisVectors");
if (e != NULL && e->embed_applicable) {
  /* this library renders ODIIS with a vector count */
}
for (size_t i = 0; i < cpmdc_feature_count(); ++i) {
  const CPMDCFeatureEntry *row = &cpmdc_feature_table()[i];
  /* row->feature_id, row->kind, row->stub_applicable, row->embed_applicable */
}

# The inventory file
Top-level keys of `schema/inventory/cpmd_features.json`:

| Key | Holds |
|-----+-------|
| `version` | inventory format version |
| `schema` | the schema file it describes |
| `opencpmd_reference` | the OpenCPMD source it was probed against, as a description, never a local path |
| `opencpmd_inscan_sections`, `cpmd_sections` | the 25 sections OpenCPMD parses with `inscan`; the two lists must be equal |
| `section_kinds` | the `CPMDSectionKind` enum values with their `section.*` IDs |
| `params_fields` | the top-level `CPMDParams` fields |
| `abi_symbols` | every public `cpmdc_*` function |
| `cpmd_keywords`, `dft_keywords`, `dft_functionals` | keyword and functional catalogs |
| `features` | one object per row: `feature_id`, `kind`, `name`, `stub_applicable`, `embed_applicable`, `role` |

Plain-text companions in `schema/inventory/`:
`opencpmd_sections.txt` (the section allowlist), `cpmd_cp_keywords.txt` (base `&CPMD` keywords), `dft_functionals.txt`,
and `surface_map_abi.txt` (the exported C ABI, generated by
`scripts/abi_inventory.py`; see the surface map (file:surface-map.org)).

# The checks
All run in the default Meson suite.
The `inventory` suite selects the first twelve and `inventory-docs`; the `docs`
suite selects the last five.

| Test | Fails when |
|------+------------|
| `feature-inventory` | the JSON inventory disagrees with `schema/Potentials.capnp`, the C table, or the public headers, when the C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org) does not name an `abi_symbols` function, or when the CPMD option mapping (file:cpmd-options.org) loses a feature ID namespace; with `CPMD_ROOT` set, also when the live `inscan` probe finds a section the inventory lacks |
| `cpmd-base-keyword-inventory` | a base `&CPMD` keyword in `cpmd_cp_keywords.txt` has no `catalog.cpmd.*` row |
| `cpmd-params-field-inventory` | a top-level `CPMDParams` field has no `params.*` row, or the inventory or the C table has a duplicate |
| `cpmd-public-abi-inventory` | a public `cpmdc_*` function is missing from `abi_symbols`, the table, or its implementation in `src/cpmdc.c`, `src/cpmdc_stub.c`, or `src/cpmdc_features.c` |
| `stub-abi-symbol-coverage` | the stub test does not assert every `abi_symbols` row |
| `shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage` | the `dlopen` test does not load every `abi_symbols` entry from `libcpmdc.so` |
| `c-abi-inventory` | `surface_map_abi.txt` differs from what the built `libcpmdc` and the public headers give, a public declaration lacks `CPMDC_API` or is not exported, or the library exports any other symbol |
| `cpmd-schema-render-coverage` | a typed `CPMDCpmdSection` field has no render mapping |
| `cpmd-option-token-coverage` | an inline option token in a fixture has no render coverage |
| `cpmd-typed-render-field-coverage` | a typed `cpmd`, `system`, `dft`, or `atoms` field is absent from the render fixtures and assertions |
| `cpmd-long-tail-section-coverage` | a `CPMDDirectiveSection` arm is missing from the long-tail fixture, the render assertions, or the option reference |
| `cpmd-escape-hatch-coverage` | `inputBlocks`, `generic`, `set`, or `raw` lose schema, fixture, render, or docs coverage |
| `cpmd-embedding-docs-coverage` | the embedding how-to does not name the public ABI feature IDs and the typed, long-tail, and escape-hatch `CPMDParams` carriers |
| `cpmd-public-header-docs-coverage` | the public header or the generated C API docs lose the tie to the serialized `CPMDParams` input |
| `examples-documented` | the public docs do not point to the runnable `examples/host_step.c` host program |
| `readme-navigation` | the README or the build-and-test how-to loses its entry paths, work-loop labels, or current wording, or the README Documentation section misses a page |
| `inventory-docs` | this table, the contributing guide, or the option mapping stops naming these tests |
| `llms-txt` | `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt` differ from `scripts/generate_llms_txt.py` output |
| `docs-coverage-inventory` | `scripts/docs_coverage_inventory.py` reports a missing C symbol, Python name, parameter feature, or embed term |

Run them together:

meson test -C build --suite inventory --print-errorlogs

To include the live probe, point `CPMD_ROOT` at an OpenCPMD source tree:

CPMD_ROOT=/path/to/opencpmd meson test -C build feature-inventory -v

A passing live probe prints `probed /path/to/opencpmd: 25 inscan sections`.
Without `CPMD_ROOT` the test prints a warning and skips that part.

# Add a row
Adding a typed keyword touches the schema, the renderer, the C table, the
inventory file, and the option docs in one change; the
contributing guide (file:../contributing/index.org) lists the files and the
focused test command.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/glossary.org

# A
- ABI :: Application binary interface: the functions, types, and calling
  conventions of `libcpmdc` as a compiled library.
  `CPMDC_ABI_VERSION` and `cpmdc_abi_version()` number its generations.
- BLYP :: Becke exchange with Lee, Yang, and Parr correlation, a generalized
  gradient density functional; the default `functional` of `CPMDParams`.

# C
- Calculator :: A group of MPI ranks that runs one CPMD calculation with its own
  communicator and orbitals.
  Created by `cpmdc_bind_calculator()`.
- Cap'n Proto :: The serialization format of every message `cpmdc` reads or
  writes.
  `capnp encode` turns a text message into the binary form.
- Cold call :: An evaluation that runs CPMD's full setup and starts the SCF
  without stored orbitals: the first call of the process, or a call that changes
  the functional, deck, cutoff, charge, multiplicity, atom count, or elemental
  composition, or the cell.
  A constant-cutoff cell within `CPMDC_CELL_IN_PLACE` stays warm, and a new
  session with the same setup is warm (see
  wavefunction state (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org)).
- CPMD :: Car-Parrinello Molecular Dynamics, the plane-wave density functional
  code; `cpmdc` embeds its OpenCPMD distribution.
- `CPMDParams` :: The message holding method setup: functional, cutoff, and the
  deck sections.
  One per session.
- `CPMDCSession` :: The C handle that owns one `CPMDParams`, a fixed topology,
  and the results of its last evaluation.

# D
- Deck :: A CPMD input file of `&SECTION ... &END` blocks.
  `cpmdc` renders one from `CPMDParams` and hands it to CPMD in memory.
- Default build :: `libcpmdc.so` built without OpenCPMD.
  It evaluates a deterministic reference function so the ABI can be tested
  anywhere.
- DFT :: Density functional theory.

# E
- `ener_com` :: The OpenCPMD module that holds the energy terms of the last SCF; `cpmdc_last_energy_components()`
  copies it.

# F
- Feature ID :: A stable string naming a capability, such as
  `abi.cpmdc_session_calculate_result` or `params.inputSections.cpmd.maxIter`.
  Looked up with `cpmdc_feature_find()`.
- File route :: Running `cpmd.x` once per force call and exchanging decks and
  output files through the file system; the alternative to embedding.
- `fion` :: OpenCPMD's array of ionic forces, `coor%fion`, read by `cpmdc` after
  each SCF.
- `ForceInput` :: The message holding one geometry: positions, atomic numbers,
  an optional cell, and output units.

# G
- Gauss-Hermite integration :: CPMD's default numerical treatment of the
  nonlocal pseudopotential projectors, used when `KLEINMAN-BYLANDER` is not on
  the pseudopotential file line.

# H
- Hockney solver :: `POISSON SOLVER HOCKNEY`, CPMD's Poisson solver for an
  isolated system in a box.
  Added by `cpmdc` when `SYMMETRY 0` has no solver.

# K
- Kleinman-Bylander form :: A separable form of the nonlocal pseudopotential,
  selected per species with `KLEINMAN-BYLANDER` on the `*file` line, or
  `kleinmanBylander = true` in `CPMDAtomsPseudopotential`.

# M
- `memfd` :: An anonymous in-memory file.
  `cpmdc` writes the composed deck to one and passes CPMD its `/proc/self/fd/N`
  path.
- MPI :: Message Passing Interface, the library CPMD uses to spread one SCF over
  several processes (ranks).

# N
- NEB :: Nudged elastic band, a method that relaxes a chain of images between
  two minima to find the minimum energy path.

# O
- ODIIS :: Orbital direct inversion in the iterative subspace, CPMD's
  preconditioned DIIS wavefunction optimiser and its default.
- OpenCPMD :: The open-source CPMD code base at `github.com/OpenCPMD/CPMD`.

# P
- Parent rank :: Rank 0 of CPMD's communicator; it writes CPMD's output and
  holds the result the host should use.
- PCG :: Preconditioned conjugate gradient wavefunction optimiser.
  `PCG MINIMIZE` adds a line minimisation along each search direction.
- `PotentialConfig` :: A message with one backend arm, such as `cpmd`, and an
  optional `CommonMethodSpec` overlay; read by `cpmdc_configure()`.
- `PotentialResult` :: The result message: energy, forces, and the extension
  fields, in the units `ForceInput` asked for.
- Pseudopotential :: A file, such as `O_MT_BLYP.psp`, replacing the core
  electrons of an element; found through `CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR`.

# R
- Reference evaluator :: The deterministic function the default build evaluates
  instead of CPMD.
- `RESTART.1` :: CPMD's binary restart file with orbitals, coordinates, and
  cell; read and patched by `cpmdc-restart`.
- rgpot :: The OmniPotentRPC library that loads potential backends, among them
  `libcpmdc` through its `CPMDPot` frontend.

# S
- SCF :: Self-consistent field: the iterative optimisation of the orbitals for
  fixed nuclei that each force call runs.
- Stub ::
  `libcpmdc_stub.a`, a link-only build whose calls all fail and whose `cpmdc_available()`
  is 0.

# T
- `tau0` :: OpenCPMD's array of ionic positions in Bohr, `coor%tau0`, written by
  `cpmdc` from each step's positions.
- Topology :: The atom count and elemental composition of a session.
  `session_accept_topology` fixes the topology only after an evaluation call
  passes its argument checks and collective orbital preflight. A rejected
  preflight leaves the topology configurable.
  A reordering of those elements stays on the session.

# W
- Warm call :: An evaluation that reuses CPMD's setup and starts the SCF from
  the orbitals of a previous successful call in the same process.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/gromacs.org

`libcpmdc_gromacs` answers the libcp2k C API of GROMACS' CP2K QM/MM interface with `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`
calls. Run GROMACS on cpmdc forces (file:../howto/gromacs.org) builds GROMACS
against it and sets up a run.

# Input file
The file is CP2K input in form, because grompp checks it for `CHARGE`,
`MULTIPLICITY`, `RUN_TYPE ENERGY_FORCE`, `COORD_FILE_FORMAT PDB`,
`CHARGE_EXTENDED TRUE`, and `COORD_FILE_NAME` and refuses `@INCLUDE`.
GROMACS stores it in the `.tpr`, writes it out at `mdrun` as `md_cp2k.inp` with
the name of the PDB file it generates, and passes both to the library.
The PDB file gives each atom's element, whether it is QM or MM, and each MM
atom's charge.

With `qmmm-cp2k-qmmethod = PBE` or `BLYP`, GROMACS 2024.6, 2025.5,
and 2026.4 generate this structure:

- `&DFT` contains `CHARGE`, `MULTIPLICITY`, and
  `&XC_FUNCTIONAL PBE` or `BLYP`;
- `&QMMM` contains a periodic QM cell, QM atom indices, `ECOUPL GAUSS`,
  and one `&LINK` with `QM_INDEX` and `MM_INDEX` for each bond between a QM
  atom and an MM atom;
- `&SUBSYS &CELL` contains the full GROMACS box;
- the generated PDB contains every atom, each MM topology charge, and zero
  instead of every QM topology charge.

When the input has no `&CPMDC` section,
`CPMDC_GROMACS_PARAMS` names the `CPMDParams` message.
The library compares its effective functional, charge, and multiplicity with
the generated values and refuses any disagreement.
The cell and embedding defaults are the same as below.

An explicit `&CPMDC` section inside `&FORCE_EVAL` takes precedence:

| Key | Meaning |
|-----+---------|
| `PARAMS path` | the `CPMDParams` message; a relative path is relative to `mdrun`'s directory. Required |
| `CELL PERIODIC` | send the GROMACS box as the cell; the default when every atom is QM |
| `CELL NONE` | send no cell, so the deck's cell holds the QM region; the default with MM atoms |
| `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` | add the QM-MM Coulomb energy and forces of `QM_CHARGES` and the MM charges |
| `EMBEDDING NONE` | add nothing; allowed only when no MM atom carries a charge |
| `QM_CHARGES q ...` | one classical charge per QM atom, in index-group order; required by `MECHANICAL` |
| `EWALD_RCUT r` | real-space cutoff of the QM-MM Ewald sum in nm; default the smaller of 1 nm and half the smallest box height |
| `EWALD_PRECISION p` | `erfc(alpha rcut) = p`, and the reciprocal cutoff `2 alpha sqrt(-ln p)`; default 10^-8 as assigned in `tools/gromacs/cpmdc_gromacs.c` |
| `EPSILON_R r` | relative dielectric constant dividing the mechanical-embedding QM-MM Coulomb energy, forces, and virial (positive, finite); default 1; requires `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` |
| `QM_RANKS ALL` | under an MPI GROMACS, every rank of `mdrun` takes part in one cpmdc calculator; the default |
| `QM_RANKS 1` | rank 0 alone runs the QM calculation, the other ranks wait for its result |

On the explicit path the method is the `CPMDParams` deck, not CP2K's `&DFT`, and
the library refuses a file whose `&DFT` `CHARGE` or `MULTIPLICITY` differs from
the effective charge or multiplicity of that deck, as it does for the generated
input.
GROMACS takes the QM charge from those two keys, so a value that the deck does
not share would run another system than the one GROMACS set up.
The message names both values, for example
`&DFT CHARGE 1 disagrees with &CPMDC PARAMS charge 0`, and a value that is not
an integer is refused.
A `CHARGE` or `MULTIPLICITY` outside `&DFT` is not read.
The `&XC_FUNCTIONAL` of the file is not compared, because CP2K writes a
functional as nested sections as well as a name; the deck holds the functional.
A link hydrogen is not part of that comparison. The values are the effective
charge and multiplicity of the deck, which describes the QM atoms, and not a
recount of the capped region.
Everything else outside `&CPMDC` is checked for structure and otherwise
ignored, apart from the `&LINK` sections of Link atoms (*Link atoms).
With neither `&CPMDC` nor `CPMDC_GROMACS_PARAMS`, the input is refused.

The library writes one log, the CP2K output file GROMACS names (`md_cp2k.out`):
the cpmdc version, the atom counts, the cell and embedding modes, the Ewald
precision, `epsilon_r`, the number of ranks, QM ranks, and link atoms, the
Ewald parameters in Bohr, and, for the first step,
the backend (`opencpmd`, or `reference` for the evaluator of a build without
OpenCPMD) and the QM and QM-MM energies.
A refused input or a failed step prints `cpmdc-gromacs:` and the reason to
stderr and to that log and stops `mdrun` with status 1, because the libcp2k API
returns no errors.

# Units
cpmdc works in Bohr and Hartree; GROMACS in nm, kJ/mol, and ps. GROMACS' QM/MM
module converts with its own constants from
`src/gromacs/math/units.h` (CODATA 2018), so the library receives Bohr and returns Hartree and Hartree/Bohr.
`cpmdc.gromacs` reproduces the factors bit for bit:

| Quantity | GROMACS | cpmdc | Factor |
|----------+---------+-------+--------|
| length | nm | Bohr | `BOHR_TO_NM` = 0.0529177210903 |
| energy | kJ/mol | Hartree | `HARTREE_TO_KJ_PER_MOL` = 2625.4996394798673 |
| force | kJ/(mol nm) | Hartree/Bohr | `HARTREE_PER_BOHR_TO_KJ_PER_MOL_NM` = 49614.752589206466 |
| virial | kJ/mol, `-0.5 sum r (x) f` | Hartree, stress times volume | -0.5 `HARTREE_TO_KJ_PER_MOL` |
| QM-MM Coulomb | `ONE_4PI_EPS0` kJ nm/(mol e^2) | e^2/Bohr = 1 | the charges are used as they are |

# Cell and positions
GROMACS sends every atom, QM and MM, each step, after putting each into the box.
GROMACS 2024 and 2025 send the box as
`box_d[3 i + j] = box[j][i]`, and GROMACS 2026 as `box_d[3 i + j] = box[i][j]`,
one lattice vector after the other, which is CP2K's layout.
GROMACS' box is lower triangular, so the two differ only in where the zeros are,
and the library reads either back as one lattice vector per row, the layout of
`cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`; any triclinic shape GROMACS accepts passes
through.

A wrapped atom jumps by a lattice vector.
The library unwraps the QM atoms against their positions of the previous step,
nearest image, so each follows a continuous path and wavefunction extrapolation
sees smooth steps.
With `CELL NONE` the first step also puts every QM atom at the nearest image of
the first one, so the QM region starts whole.
With `CELL NONE` cpmdc moves the QM region to the middle of the deck's cell on
every step, by its centre of mass, and removes the net force the cell would
leave (`CPMDC_RECENTER` in
environment variables (file:../reference/environment.org)), so the QM energy
and forces do not depend on where the region has diffused to.
The cell must still hold the region with room for its density;
`CPMDC_RECENTER_MARGIN` makes a step fail when an atom comes closer to a face
than that.

# Link atoms
GROMACS cuts a covalent bond between a QM atom and an MM atom and leaves the
valence of the QM atom open; CP2K caps it with a hydrogen that exists in the
QM calculation only.
`libcpmdc_gromacs` does the same for every `&LINK` section of the input, in
the generated input and beside `&CPMDC` in a `-qmi` file:

| Key | Meaning |
|-----+---------|
| `QM_INDEX n` | the QM atom of the bond, a 1-based GROMACS atom number; required |
| `MM_INDEX n` | the MM atom of the bond, a 1-based GROMACS atom number; required |
| `ALPHA_IMOMM alpha` | the bond is scaled by 1/alpha; default 1.38, CP2K's default, the ratio of a C-C to a C-H bond; must exceed 1 |
| `LINK_TYPE IMOMM` | the only scheme implemented; any other value is refused |

Any other key, a `QM_INDEX` that is not a QM atom of the PDB file, an `MM_INDEX`
that is not an MM atom, an atom number outside the system, and a repeated pair
stop `mdrun` with the reason.
GROMACS writes no `ALPHA_IMOMM`, so a generated input uses 1.38;
an input of `-qmi` may set it for each bond.
One QM atom can have several links, and one MM atom can be the end of several.

Each link adds a hydrogen to the atoms of `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`, after
the QM atoms, at the IMOMM position of CP2K,

x_H = x_QM + (x_MM - x_QM) / alpha = (1 - a) x_QM + a x_MM,   a = 1 / alpha

with the nearest image of the MM atom to the QM atom when GROMACS sends a box.
The QM energy is that of the capped region, so the topology must describe the
QM atoms' bonds with the MM atom at the MM level, as GROMACS' preprocessing
does: bonded terms that cross the boundary stay, and bonds, angles, and
dihedrals of QM atoms only go.

The hydrogen moves with the two atoms of its bond, so by the chain rule the
library returns the share `1 - a` of its force to the QM atom and `a` to the
MM atom, the distribution of CP2K's IMOMM link.
The two shares add up to the force on the hydrogen, and the force on the MM
atom joins the other forces GROMACS reads for it.

The virial is the strain derivative of the energy returned, for a strain that
moves every atom and the box, as without links.
With `CELL NONE` the sum `x (x) f` runs over the QM atoms and the hydrogens at
the positions cpmdc used, which equals the sum over the two bonded atoms with
the MM atom at the image the hydrogen used.
With `CELL PERIODIC` cpmdc's stress already treats the hydrogen as an atom
that scales with the cell.

Not implemented: the `PSEUDO` link scheme, a cap other than hydrogen, and any
redistribution of the MM charges around a cut bond other than the one that
Embedding (*Embedding) describes.

# Embedding
GROMACS' CP2K interface assumes electrostatic embedding: grompp zeroes the
charges of the QM atoms, removes the bonds, angles, and dihedrals within the QM
group, excludes QM-QM Lennard-Jones, and keeps QM-MM Lennard-Jones and the
bonded terms that cross the boundary.
The QM-MM Coulomb interaction is then the QM program's job [1].

`libcpmdc_gromacs` provides mechanical embedding.
`EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` adds the Coulomb energy of fixed point charges on the QM
atoms, `QM_CHARGES`, with the MM charges of the PDB file, and its forces on both
sides:

- a periodic box: an Ewald sum with the conventions of GROMACS' PME, the
  real-space term `erfc(alpha r)/r` over every image within `rcut`, the
  reciprocal term over `k` up to the cutoff above, and the neutralizing
  background `-pi Q_QM Q_MM / (V alpha^2)` of a non-neutral QM or MM part; the
  QM-QM and MM-MM sums are not included, since GROMACS' PME already has MM-MM
  and the QM charges are zero in GROMACS;
- no box: the direct sum.

With link atoms, the MM atom of each cut bond sits one bond from a QM charge,
where a pair of point charges is not a model of anything physical.
`EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` therefore deletes the charge of that MM atom from the
QM-MM sum, the Z1 scheme of the QM/MM literature, and keeps the charges of
every other MM atom, including those two bonds away.
The charge is removed from the Coulomb term of the library only; GROMACS still
holds the MM atom's own charge for its classical terms.

The returned energy is the QM energy plus that Coulomb energy; both appear in
`Quantum En.`.
An MD step adds `O(N_k (N_QM + N_MM))` work for the reciprocal sum.

GROMACS saves each QM charge as zero before it writes the generated PDB.
No general rule can recover the original QM topology charges from
`md_cp2k.inp` or `md_cp2k.pdb`.
A generated input with charged MM atoms is therefore refused with a message
naming the missing `QM_CHARGES` key.
Use an explicit `&CPMDC` section to select `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` and provide
`QM_CHARGES`, or explicitly select `EMBEDDING NONE` after deciding that
omitting the QM-MM Coulomb interaction is appropriate.

With `EPSILON_R` (default 1), the mechanical-embedding QM-MM Coulomb energy,
forces, and Ewald virial are divided by `EPSILON_R` while the QM energy, QM
forces, and QM virial stay unscaled, because `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`
takes no dielectric constant.
GROMACS' CP2K QM/MM module (`src/gromacs/applied_forces/qmmm/` in 2024.6,
2025.5, and 2026.4) never reads `t_inputrec` or `t_interaction_const` and passes
neither the `.mdp` `epsilon-r` option (`readir.cpp`, `interaction_const.cpp`) nor
`epsfac` into `md_cp2k.inp`, `md_cp2k.pdb`, or `libcp2k` (`ForceProviderInput`
carries only coordinates, atom count, charges, masses, time, step, box, and the
communication record).
On the explicit `&CPMDC` route, set `EPSILON_R` to match `.mdp`'s `epsilon-r`
whenever `epsilon-r` differs from 1; `EPSILON_R` is refused unless positive,
finite, and paired with `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL`.
On the generated-input route (`PBE` or `BLYP`), any run with charged MM atoms
is already refused for lacking `QM_CHARGES`, so GROMACS' unforwarded
`epsilon-r` cannot enter a mechanical-embedding sum there.

Charge precision across the interface:

- `libcpmdc_gromacs` parses both `QM_CHARGES` and the MM charges in the PDB
  file with `strtod` into `double` (refusing non-finite charges), and
  `cpmdc.gromacs.qmi_input` serializes `qm_charges` with `repr(float)` at full
  IEEE-754 `float64` precision;
- upstream GROMACS (`QMMMInputGenerator::generateCP2KPdb()` in
  `src/gromacs/applied_forces/qmmm/qmmminputgenerator.cpp`) formats every
  charge written to `md_cp2k.pdb` with `%lf` (6 decimal places, rounding MM
  charges to 10^-6 e and writing zero for magnitudes below 5e-7 e) even in a
  double-precision build (`-DGMX_DOUBLE=ON`, where `t_atom::q` is `double`), and
  `QMMMForceProvider::calculateForces()` never forwards `fInput.chargeA_`
  through `libcp2k`;
- the total QM charge (`qmmm-cp2k-qmcharge`, `CHARGE` in `&DFT`, and
  `CPMDCMethodInfo.charge`) is an integer (`int`); `grompp` checks the removed
  classical charge of the QM atoms against it and warns if they differ by more
  than 10^-5 e (`qmmmoptions.cpp`).

Not implemented:

- electrostatic embedding: the MM charges do not polarize the QM density.
  `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` takes no external potential, so
  `EMBEDDING ELECTROSTATIC` is refused.

# QM virial
GROMACS adds the
QM/MM forces through its `ForceWithVirial` buffer, whose forces enter the virial only through `addVirialContribution()`, and the released QM/MM
module never calls it (the GROMACS manual notes the missing virial [1]), so an
unpatched GROMACS reports a pressure without the QM and QM-MM terms.
The patch makes the module call libcp2k's `cp2k_get_stress_tensor()` on each
step that needs the virial, on the main rank only, since GROMACS sums the virial
over ranks, and add

Xi = -0.5 * sigma * V * HARTREE_TO_KJ_PER_MOL

in
kJ/mol, GROMACS' `-0.5 sum r (x) f` convention. `sigma` is CP2K's stress, column-major, in Hartree/Bohr^3,
positive under compression; `sigma V` is the virial
`W = -dE/d(strain)` of the C ABI (file:../reference/c-abi.org) and ASE's
stress is `-sigma`.
`V` is the box volume in Bohr^3.
With no kinetic energy, GROMACS' pressure is then `sigma`.

`libcpmdc_gromacs` returns the strain derivative of the energy it returned, for
a symmetric strain that moves every atom with the box:

- `CELL PERIODIC`: cpmdc's stress for the cell, from
  `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()`;
- `CELL NONE`: the symmetric part of `sum x (x) f` over the QM atoms.
  The QM forces sum to zero, since cpmdc removes the net force of the isolated
  cell, so the sum does not depend on the origin of `x`.
  Without that (`CPMDC_RECENTER=off`) a QM region at `X` with net force `F` adds
  `X (x) F`, which grows as the region drifts and as the barostat scales it away
  from the origin.
  The grid still leaves a small torque, and a symmetric strain does not see the
  antisymmetric part;
- `EMBEDDING MECHANICAL` with a box: plus the strain derivative of the QM-MM
  Ewald sum (its real-space, reciprocal, and background terms), divided by
  `EPSILON_R`.

Link hydrogens are atoms of the QM calculation in the first two cases, as
described in Link atoms (*Link atoms).

It reports the stress as unavailable with no box (`pbc = no`), and with
`CELL PERIODIC` when cpmdc computes no stress: an isolated deck, or
`CPMDC_STRESS=0`.
The patched GROMACS then writes once to `md.log` that the QM program returned no
stress tensor, and the pressure lacks the QM terms; `md_cp2k.out` logs the
outcome of the first request.

# Several ranks
A GROMACS built with `-DGMX_MPI=ON` calls `cp2k_create_force_env_comm` on every
rank, with the Fortran handle of its simulation communicator, and then each step
sends every rank the positions of all atoms and reads the forces of its home
atoms back.
GROMACS refuses separate PME ranks with QM/MM, so every rank of that
communicator makes each call and the library can use collectives on it.
`libcpmdc_gromacs` is built with MPI when Meson finds MPI for C, the same MPI
GROMACS is built with, and then:

- duplicates the communicator, so cpmdc's traffic and error handler stay off
  GROMACS' own;
- reads the input and the PDB file on rank 0 and broadcasts the atom counts, the
  QM atoms, the link atoms, and the `CPMDParams` message;
- hands the duplicate to cpmdc with
  `cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm()` before the first session, with every rank as one calculator (`QM_RANKS ALL`),
  or `MPI_COMM_SELF` on rank 0 (`QM_RANKS 1`).
  It does so on one rank too: GROMACS has started MPI, and OpenCPMD sets up a
  communicator only when it starts MPI itself;
- each step broadcasts rank 0's positions and box, so every QM rank evaluates
  identical input whatever GROMACS' decomposition, builds each link hydrogen
  from those positions, adds the embedding and the link force shares on rank
  0, and broadcasts rank 0's energy and forces.

The forces GROMACS reads are therefore identical on every rank, and domain
decomposition changes which rank applies a force, not its value, including for
QM molecules whose atoms sit in different domains.
With `QM_RANKS 1`, or the reference evaluator, the QM forces are those of a
one-rank run; with OpenCPMD on several ranks they differ from them by the order
of its parallel sums (see
the OpenCPMD runs (file:../explanation/md-engines.org)).
GROMACS reads the energy on its main rank only, so `Quantum En.` counts it once.

A library built without MPI stops a `cp2k_create_force_env_comm` call with the
reason.

# References
1. GROMACS manual,
   Hybrid Quantum-Classical simulations (QM/MM) with CP2K interface (https://manual.gromacs.org/2025.5/reference-manual/special/qmmm.html);
   source `src/gromacs/applied_forces/qmmm/` of GROMACS 2024.6, 2025.5, and
   2026.4.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/lammps.org

Both routes of Run LAMMPS on cpmdc forces (file:../howto/lammps.org),
`cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal` and `pair_style cpmdc`, pass the same numbers to
LAMMPS.
The Python class adapts `cpmdc.Session` to the standard rgpot Python potential
protocol and delegates its LAMMPS mechanics to `rgpot.lammps.FixExternal`.
The plugin remains cpmdc's compiled, LAMMPS-specific route.
This page gives their units, the cell and positions they send, and the virial
they return.

# Units
cpmdc works in Bohr and Hartree.
Both routes convert with the constants of `python/cpmdc` (CODATA 2018, with the
thermochemical calorie, 4.184 J, for `real`):

| LAMMPS `units` | Length per Bohr | Energy per Hartree | Forces | Virial | Pressure |
|----------------+-----------------+--------------------+--------+----------------------+----------|
| `metal` | `BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` Angstrom | `HARTREE_TO_EV` eV | eV/Angstrom | eV | bar |
| `real` | `BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` Angstrom | `HARTREE_TO_KCAL_PER_MOL` kcal/mol | kcal/(mol Angstrom) | kcal/mol | atm |
| `electron` | 1 Bohr | 1 Hartree | Hartree/Bohr | Hartree | Pa |

Any other unit style is refused before the first step with an error that names
the three; `FixExternal` raises `ValueError`.
LAMMPS converts the virial to pressure with its own `nktv2p`.

# Cell and positions
LAMMPS keeps a restricted triclinic box: `a` along x, `b` in the xy plane. cpmdc
takes one lattice vector per row of a row-major 3 by 3 cell, so the cell sent is

| Row | LAMMPS | `domain->h` |
|-----+--------+-------------|
| `a` |  |  |
| `b` |  |  |
| `c` |  |  |

with `lx = xhi - xlo` and the tilt factors `xy`, `xz`, `yz`.
An orthogonal box is the case with zero tilts.
The positions are LAMMPS' Cartesian coordinates unwrapped with the image flags,
`x + ix a + iy b + iz c`, so each atom follows a continuous path across the
boundaries and wavefunction extrapolation sees smooth steps.
The box origin  is not subtracted.
A box with all three axes periodic sends the cell; a box with none sends no
cell, and the `CPMDParams` deck sets the box.
A box with some axes periodic and others not is refused; `FixExternal` raises
`ValueError`.

# Atom IDs
Both routes gather the system and order their call to cpmdc by increasing atom
ID. IDs must be positive and unique, but need not be the consecutive integers
1 through N: deleting atoms without compression leaves holes that are
preserved while each force is returned to its original atom.

Changing the atoms' elemental composition, including by
`delete_atoms ... compress no` or `fix evaporate`, closes the current
cpmdc session before the next
evaluation and opens a new session for the changed topology. An unchanged
composition continues on the existing session.

# Electrostatic QM/MM embedding
Both routes keep their whole-system behavior by default.
For `FixExternal`, pass `qm_types=[...]`; other atom types provide their LAMMPS
`q` values as Gaussian MM charges. `mm_width_angstrom` defaults to 0.30.
For the plugin, write `NULL` for each MM type, for example
`pair_style cpmdc params.bin width 0.30` followed by
`pair_coeff * * O H NULL`.

Element entries are QM and `NULL` entries use the per-atom charge. The energy
includes the QM--MM electrostatic coupling and forces are returned to both
groups. Electrostatic embedding is currently isolated only; a periodic box is
rejected instead of using an incomplete image convention, so the virial
\(-dE/d(\mathrm{strain})\), which needs a cell, is zero on both routes.
`qm_types` must name at least one type, and `mm_width_angstrom` and the
plugin's `width` must be finite and at least 1e-12 Angstrom; a smaller value is
refused when the fix or the pair style is configured.
Both routes send the charges on every step that has MM atoms, and clear them on
the first step that has none after a step that had some, so deleting or
retyping every MM atom leaves no stale charge in the session.

# Virial and pressure
cpmdc returns the virial `W = -dE/d(strain)` in Hartree.
LAMMPS' global virial of a pair style or of `fix_modify virial yes` has the same
sign and units of energy, `W = sum r f` for a pair potential, so both routes
pass `W` times the energy factor, symmetrized, as `xx yy zz xy xz yz`.
The pressure LAMMPS prints is then `P = (sum m v v + W) / V` in its pressure
units; a compressed cell has a positive diagonal of `W` and a positive pressure.
`fix npt` and `fix nph` use it as they use any pair virial.
`compute pressure NULL virial` reports the virial part alone, `W / V` in
pressure units.

# Per-atom quantities
Forces are per atom, and both routes return them for every atom.
The energy and the virial are totals of the whole system, and `pair_style cpmdc`
splits neither:

- A density functional energy is a functional of the electron density, not a sum
  of terms that belong to atoms, so any per-atom share of it would be a choice of
  partition, not a result of cpmdc.
- The virial `-dE/d(strain)` is a derivative with respect to the cell. It holds
  kinetic, Hartree, exchange-correlation, and basis-set (Pulay) parts that are not
  `sum r f` over atoms, so it has no per-atom form that adds up to the pressure.

`pair_style cpmdc` therefore refuses a run in which a compute asks for a split:
`compute pe/atom`, `compute stress/atom`, or `compute centroid/stress/atom`, with
any keywords, even one that is never printed.
The error `pair_style cpmdc computes no per-atom energy or virial (compute ID)`
names the compute and comes from `init_style`, before the first evaluation.
`uncompute ID` removes the request.
`FixExternal` hands LAMMPS one energy and one virial and sets no per-atom values,
so `compute pe/atom` and `compute stress/atom` take nothing from it.
Per-atom forces work with every compute, for example `compute property/atom fx fy fz`.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/pwscale.org

The plane-wave scaffold is declared in `include/cpmdc_pwscale.h` and
implemented in `src/cpmdc_pwscale.c` (CPU and MPI),
`src/cpmdc_pwscale_cuda.cu` (CUDA), and `src/cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_stub.c`
(the CUDA calls of a build without CUDA).
It evaluates one structure-factor sum on a synthetic plane-wave grid so that
threads, ranks, and a GPU can be timed and compared on the same arithmetic.
It is separate from the embed force call and the reference potential, and sits
outside the C ABI of `libcpmdc` (see the C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org)):
the functions use plain C linkage, the header stays in `include/` and is used
from the source tree, and `libcpmdc` exports only the functions of `cpmdc.h`
and `cpmdc_features.h`.
The rank how-to (file:../howto/pwscale-ranks.org) shows how to time it.

# Availability
The scaffold is off in the default build.
`-Dwith_pwscale=true` builds `libcpmdc_pwscale.a`, a static library that is not
installed, together with the `cpmdc-pwscale` harness and the `pwscale` test
suite; it needs OpenMP.
Programs of the source tree include `cpmdc_pwscale.h` and link that archive.
All functions have C linkage, and the header compiles as C and as C++.
None of them writes `cpmdc_last_error()`; the return code is the whole report.

| Function | Needs MPI in the build | Needs CUDA in the build |
|----------+------------------------+-------------------------|
| `cpmdc_pwscale_fill_geometry` | no | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_within` | no | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_sample_check` | no | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_eval` | no | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi` | yes, else `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create` | yes, else `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi_bound` | yes, else `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_free` | compiled in both; does nothing without MPI | no |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_compiled` | no | answers 1 with CUDA, 0 without |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_device` | no | finds a device only with CUDA |
| `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda` | no | yes, else `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOCUDA` |

"MPI in the build" means that Meson found the MPI C compiler wrapper and passed
`-DCPMDC_PWSCALE_HAVE_MPI=1` to `src/cpmdc_pwscale.c`.
"CUDA in the build" means `-Dwith_pwscale_cuda=true`: Meson then needs `nvcc`,
compiles the kernel for `sm_70`, and links `src/cpmdc_pwscale_cuda.cu` in
place of the stub.
A CUDA build on a host without a device still returns
`CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOCUDA` from `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda`.

# Conventions
| Topic | Rule |
|-------+------|
| positions | `double`, Bohr, `3 * natoms` values, atom-major: x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, ... |
| atomic numbers | `int`, `natoms` values; each is used as a weight and is not range-checked |
| forces | `double`, Hartree per Bohr, `3 * natoms` values in the layout of the positions |
| energy | `double` in `stats->energy_h`, Hartree |
| time | `double` seconds from a monotonic clock (CUDA: event time) |
| ownership | the caller owns every array and every `problem` and `stats` struct; no call keeps a pointer past its return |
| scratch | calls allocate their scratch and release it before they return; `cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create` is the one exception, see Binding (*Binding) |
| `stats` | when not `NULL`, a call zeroes it first, so it holds zeros after an error |
| `forces` | an evaluation overwrites the whole array; it does not add to it |
| state | no call keeps state between calls except through a `cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind`, and one binding serves one call at a time |
| OpenMP | `cpmdc_pwscale_eval` and the MPI calls turn OpenMP dynamic adjustment off with `omp_set_dynamic(0)` for the calling thread |

## The sum that is evaluated
A problem has `natoms` atoms in a cubic cell of edge `cell_bohr` and `npw` plane
waves.
Let `n` be the smallest odd integer with `n^3 >= npw`.
Plane wave `k`, for `0 <= k < npw`, has the integer indices
`ix = k mod n - n/2`, `iy = (k / n) mod n - n/2`, and `iz = k / n^2 - n/2`
(integer division), and the wave vector
`G = 2 pi / cell_bohr * (ix, iy, iz)` in inverse Bohr.
So the plane waves are the first `npw` cells of an `n` by `n` by `n` box,
x running fastest; the box is cut short when `npw` is not a cube.
With `G2 = |G|^2` and the position `r` of an atom of atomic number `Z`:

w(G)     = 4 pi / G2 * exp(-G2 / (4 alpha)) * exp(-G2 / (2 sigma^2))
energy   = sum over G != 0, atoms a:  Z_a * w(G) * cos(G . r_a)
force_a  = sum over G != 0:           Z_a * w(G) * sin(G . r_a) * G

The term `G = 0` is visited and adds nothing.
It is visited only when the box that `npw` cuts holds the origin.
With `G` in inverse Bohr, `alpha` is in inverse Bohr squared and `sigma` in
inverse Bohr; the code does not check units.

## How work is split
`CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_PW` gives each worker a contiguous run of plane waves and
every atom; `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_ATOMS` gives each worker every plane wave and a
contiguous run of atoms.
Piece `i` of `p` over `m` items covers `[i * m / p, (i + 1) * m / p)`.
Workers are the OpenMP threads of one call, and in the MPI calls the ranks of
the communicator, each with its own OpenMP team.
With the plane-wave split every thread keeps a private force vector, and the
vectors are summed in thread order.
With the atom split threads write disjoint force entries.

## Agreement
A parallel or MPI result agrees with the serial one when
`cpmdc_pwscale_within` accepts the energy and every force component,
with the tolerance `CPMDC_PWSCALE_RTOL`, and the visit counts are equal.
Bitwise equality is claimed only in the case below.
For a fixed rank count and thread count, every rank holds the same bytes and
repeated runs give the same bytes, because the partial sums are added in rank
order and thread order.
The CUDA path adds with `atomicAdd` on doubles, so its sum order is not fixed.

# Status codes and constants
Every function that returns `int` status returns one of these, except the
predicates `cpmdc_pwscale_within`, `cpmdc_pwscale_sample_check`,
`cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_compiled`, and `cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_device`, which return 1 or 0.

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|----------+-------+---------|
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_OK` | 0 | the call succeeded |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG` | -1 | a pointer is `NULL`, a problem value is out of range, `dist` is unknown, `nthreads` is above 4096, `comm_bytes` is wrong, scratch allocation failed, or an MPI call or another rank failed |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` | -2 | the build has no MPI |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOCUDA` | -3 | the build has no CUDA, or the host has no CUDA device |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_CUDA` | -4 | a CUDA allocation or kernel launch failed |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOFFTW` | -5 | returned by the FFT timing driver `bench/pwscale_fft.c` when built without FFTW, when `fftw_init_threads()` fails, or when FFTW plan creation fails; no function of this header returns it |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_PW` | 0 | split the plane-wave loop |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_ATOMS` | 1 | split the atom loop |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_RTOL` | `1e-8` | relative tolerance of agreement: a gap passes when it is at most `RTOL * max(1, fabs(got), fabs(reference))` |

Codes are negative so that one rank's failure can be taken as the minimum
over ranks.

# Types
## ~cpmdc_pwscale_problem~
One problem.
`cpmdc_pwscale_eval` and the MPI calls reject it with `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG`
unless every limit below holds; a `NaN` fails the three positive tests.
`cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda` applies the same tests except the upper limits.
`cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create` copies it, so the caller's struct may go away
after the call.

| Field | Type | Unit | Allowed values |
|-------+------+------+----------------|
| `natoms` | `int` | atoms | 1 to 1000000 |
| `npw` | `int` | plane waves | 1 to 100000000 |
| `cell_bohr` | `double` | Bohr | greater than 0; the cell is a cube of this edge |
| `alpha` | `double` | inverse Bohr squared | greater than 0 |
| `sigma` | `double` | inverse Bohr | greater than 0 |

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_stats~
Timers and counts of one evaluation.
Every field is zero after an error.
The CPU calls set the fields below; the CUDA call differs where noted.

| Field | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|-------+------+------+---------|
| `energy_h` | `double` | Hartree | the energy of the sum |
| `seconds` | `double` | s | wall time of the evaluated region; see each function |
| `h2d_seconds` | `double` | s | host-to-device copy time; 0 on the CPU path |
| `d2h_seconds` | `double` | s | device-to-host time; 0 on the CPU path |
| `g_visited` | `long long` | plane waves | plane waves visited, `npw` in every successful CPU call |
| `atom_visits` | `long long` | visits | one per atom for each visited plane wave with `G != 0` |
| `alloc_bytes` | `long long` | bytes | scratch counted by the call: per-thread partials (and private force vectors with the plane-wave split); the MPI calls add the buffers of the binding; CUDA counts the device buffers |
| `workers` | `int` | threads | the OpenMP team that ran, from `omp_get_num_threads`, which can be smaller than `nthreads`; 1 on CUDA |
| `mpi_ranks` | `int` | ranks | the communicator size, 1 for `cpmdc_pwscale_eval`; the CUDA call leaves it at 0 |

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind~
An opaque handle declared as `typedef struct cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind`.
It exists only in a build with MPI; without MPI a pointer of this type is always
`NULL`.
See Binding (*Binding) for what it holds.

# Functions
| Function | Result |
|----------+--------|
| `void cpmdc_pwscale_fill_geometry(const cpmdc_pwscale_problem *prob, double *positions_bohr, int *atomic_numbers)` | a deterministic geometry |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_within(double got, double ref)` | 1 when the two values agree under `CPMDC_PWSCALE_RTOL` |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_sample_check(double got_energy, const double *got_forces, double ref_energy, const double *ref_forces, int n3, long long g_got, long long g_ref, long long a_got, long long a_ref, double *max_abs_dE, double *max_abs_dF, int *counts_match)` | 1 when a sample agrees with the reference, with the gaps |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_eval(const cpmdc_pwscale_problem *prob, const double *positions_bohr, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr, int nthreads, int dist, cpmdc_pwscale_stats *stats)` | a status code, forces and stats |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi(const cpmdc_pwscale_problem *prob, const double *positions_bohr, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr, int nthreads, int dist, cpmdc_pwscale_stats *stats, const void *comm, size_t comm_bytes)` | a status code, forces and stats, the same on every rank |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create(const cpmdc_pwscale_problem *prob, int dist, const void *comm, size_t comm_bytes, cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind **out)` | a status code and a binding in `*out` |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi_bound(cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind *bind, const double *positions_bohr, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr, int nthreads, cpmdc_pwscale_stats *stats)` | a status code, forces and stats, the same on every rank |
| `void cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_free(cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind *bind)` | nothing |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_compiled(void)` | 1 when the CUDA scaffold is built in |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_device(char *name, int namelen)` | 1 when a CUDA device exists, and its name |
| `int cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda(const cpmdc_pwscale_problem *prob, const double *positions_bohr, const int *atomic_numbers, double *forces_h_bohr, cpmdc_pwscale_stats *stats)` | a status code, forces and stats |

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_fill_geometry~
Fills `positions_bohr` and `atomic_numbers` for atoms `i = 0 .. natoms - 1`,
with `s = i + 1`:
the position is `(fmod(0.11 s, 0.73), fmod(0.17 s, 0.71), fmod(0.23 s, 0.69))`
times `cell_bohr` and the atomic number is `1 + i mod 8`.
Every position is inside the cell.
The arrays depend only on `natoms` and `cell_bohr` of `prob`.

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `prob` | in | `natoms` and `cell_bohr` are read; `npw`, `alpha`, and `sigma` are ignored |
| `positions_bohr` | out | caller buffer of `3 * natoms` doubles |
| `atomic_numbers` | out | caller buffer of `natoms` ints |

If any pointer is `NULL`, or `natoms` is below 1, nothing is written.
There is no return value.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_within~
Returns 1 when `|got - ref| <= CPMDC_PWSCALE_RTOL * max(1, |got|, |ref|)`, else 0.
The scale is the larger magnitude of the two values and never below 1.
A `NaN` in either argument returns 0.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_sample_check~
Compares one finished sample with the serial reference.
`got_forces` and `ref_forces` each hold `n3 = 3 * natoms` doubles in Hartree per
Bohr.
The energies are in Hartree.
`g_got` and `g_ref` are the plane-wave visit counts, `a_got` and `a_ref` the
atom-visit counts.

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `max_abs_dE` | out | the absolute energy gap `fabs(got_energy - ref_energy)`, not relative |
| `max_abs_dF` | out | the largest absolute force gap over the `n3` values, not relative |
| `counts_match` | out | 1 when `g_got == g_ref` and `a_got == a_ref`, else 0 |

Returns 1 only when `cpmdc_pwscale_within` accepts the energy and every force
component and `*counts_match` is 1.
It returns 0 and writes nothing when `got_forces`, `ref_forces`, `max_abs_dE`,
`max_abs_dF`, or `counts_match` is `NULL`, or `n3` is below 1.
The three outputs are written on every other call, including a failing one.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_eval~
Evaluates the sum on one rank with `nthreads` OpenMP threads.
No MPI is involved, so this works in every build.

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `prob` | in | must hold the limits of the `cpmdc_pwscale_problem` section |
| `positions_bohr` | in | `3 * natoms` doubles, Bohr |
| `atomic_numbers` | in | `natoms` ints |
| `forces_h_bohr` | out | `3 * natoms` doubles, Hartree per Bohr; zeroed, then filled |
| `nthreads` | in | OpenMP team size; a value below 1 means 1, and 1 is the serial loop |
| `dist` | in | `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_PW` or `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_ATOMS` |
| `stats` | out | may be `NULL`; see the `cpmdc_pwscale_stats` section |

Returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_OK`, or `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG` when a pointer other than
`stats` is `NULL`, the problem is out of range, `dist` is unknown, `nthreads` is
above 4096, or scratch allocation fails.
`forces_h_bohr` is untouched for an argument error found before the evaluation,
and is zero when the team fails.
On success `stats->seconds` covers scratch allocation, the arithmetic, and the
ordered sum, and `stats->mpi_ranks` is 1.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi~
Evaluates the sum on every rank of one communicator and gives every rank the
whole result.
It binds a problem, runs one bound call, and frees the binding, on every call.
It is the one-shot form of the binding calls (*Binding).

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `prob`, `positions_bohr`, `atomic_numbers` | in | the same on every rank, with the layout of `cpmdc_pwscale_eval`; each rank passes the whole geometry |
| `forces_h_bohr` | out | `3 * natoms` doubles on every rank; every rank receives the summed forces |
| `nthreads` | in | OpenMP team size inside each rank |
| `dist` | in | the split across ranks: contiguous plane waves or contiguous atoms |
| `stats` | out | may be `NULL`; `mpi_ranks` is the communicator size |
| `comm` | in | `NULL` for `MPI_COMM_WORLD`, else a pointer to an `MPI_Comm` |
| `comm_bytes` | in | `sizeof(MPI_Comm)` when `comm` is not `NULL`; ignored when it is |

The call is collective over the communicator.
Every rank receives the partials of every rank and adds them in rank order, so
every rank ends with the same bytes.
`stats->seconds` runs from the entry of the bound call to the end of the
rank-ordered sum, the Allgather included; the binding step before it is not
timed.
`stats->alloc_bytes` holds `(ranks + 1) * (3 * natoms + 4)` doubles of exchange
buffers plus the scratch of this rank's team.

Returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_OK`, `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` in a build without MPI
(with `stats` zeroed), or `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG`.
The pointers and the problem are checked on the calling rank before any
collective, so a rank that fails that check returns at once without joining.
If every rank passes the same bad argument, every rank returns
`CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG`; if only some ranks do, the others wait in the
collective of the binding step.
A caller whose ranks can fail on their own binds first and uses the bound call,
which reports such a failure on every rank.

## Binding
A binding holds a copy of the problem, `dist`, the rank and size of the
communicator, the handle of the communicator, and the buffers of the exchange
(`(ranks + 1) * (3 * natoms + 4)` doubles).
It saves the checks and allocation of `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi` on every step.
The caller owns a binding from a successful `cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create` until
`cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_free`.
The communicator is not copied, only its handle, so it must outlive the binding.
The bound calls overwrite the buffers of the binding, so one binding serves one
call at a time.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_create~
Binds a problem to a communicator.

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `prob` | in | the problem, the same on every rank; copied |
| `dist` | in | `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_PW` or `CPMDC_PWSCALE_DIST_ATOMS`, the same on every rank |
| `comm`, `comm_bytes` | in | as for `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi` |
| `out` | out | receives the binding, or `NULL` on every failure |

The call is collective: it runs one `MPI_Allreduce` that checks that every rank
holds a valid problem and buffers, and that `npw`, `natoms`, and `dist` match
across ranks.
`cell_bohr`, `alpha`, and `sigma` must match as well, but they are not compared.
On failure after that collective every rank returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG` and
`*out` is `NULL`.
Three failures come before the collective and do not join it:
`out` is `NULL`, `comm_bytes` differs from `sizeof(MPI_Comm)` for a non-`NULL`
`comm`, and a rank or size query of the communicator fails.
A build without MPI returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` and sets `*out` to `NULL`
when `out` is not `NULL`.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi_bound~
One force call on a binding.
It has the arguments and the result of `cpmdc_pwscale_eval_mpi` for the problem
and `dist` of the binding, without `prob`, `dist`, `comm`, and `comm_bytes`.
The geometry arrays are per call.

The call is collective over the bound communicator and runs one
`MPI_Allgather` of each rank's return code, visit counts, energy, and forces.
A failure on one rank, such as a missing array, a team that fails, or
`nthreads` above 4096, is seen by every rank, and every rank returns the lowest
(most negative) code any rank produced; `forces_h_bohr` is untouched then.
A `NULL` `bind` returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG` at once, without the collective.
A build without MPI returns `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOMPI` and zeroes `stats`.

`stats->g_visited` is `npw` with either split, `stats->atom_visits` is the sum
over ranks, `stats->workers` is this rank's team, and `stats->mpi_ranks` is the
communicator size.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_mpi_bind_free~
Releases a binding and its buffers.
The call is local and not collective, and it leaves the communicator alone.
A `NULL` pointer is accepted and does nothing.
The pointer is invalid afterwards.
Without MPI the function does nothing.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_compiled~
Returns 1 when the build compiled `src/cpmdc_pwscale_cuda.cu`, else 0.
It does not look for a device.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_cuda_device~
Reports whether a CUDA device exists and names device 0.

| Argument | Direction | Contract |
|----------+-----------+----------|
| `name` | out | may be `NULL`; else a buffer of `namelen` chars that receives the device name as a NUL-terminated string, cut to fit, and an empty string when there is no device |
| `namelen` | in | size of `name` in chars; `name` is not written when it is 0 or less |

Returns 1 when at least one device exists, else 0.
A build without CUDA always returns 0 and writes an empty string.
`cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda` uses device 0.

## ~cpmdc_pwscale_eval_cuda~
Evaluates the sum on CUDA device 0, with one thread per plane wave.
The arguments are those of `cpmdc_pwscale_eval` without `nthreads` and `dist`,
and the result is the same sum in the same units; `forces_h_bohr` holds
`3 * natoms` doubles.

Returns:

| Code | When |
|------+------|
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_OK` | the evaluation ran |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_ARG` | a pointer other than `stats` is `NULL`, or `natoms`, `npw`, `cell_bohr`, `alpha`, or `sigma` is not positive |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_NOCUDA` | the build has no CUDA, or no device exists |
| `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_CUDA` | a device allocation failed, or the kernel launch reported an error |

A missing build or device writes no timing: `stats` stays zeroed.
On success `stats->seconds` is the event time from before the host-to-device
copies to after the device-to-host copies and the synchronization, so it contains
the copy times.
`h2d_seconds` covers the position and atomic-number copies; `d2h_seconds` runs
from the end of the kernel launch to the end of the call, so it covers the
copies back and any kernel time that is still running.
`g_visited` is `npw`, `workers` is 1, and `mpi_ranks` stays 0.
After `CPMDC_PWSCALE_ERR_CUDA` the contents of `forces_h_bohr` are unspecified.

# Tests
Builds with `-Dwith_pwscale=true` run the `pwscale` suite:

| Test | What it checks |
|------+----------------|
| `pwscale-agreement`, also under 2, 4, and 8 ranks | threads and ranks against the serial loop, and the energy against an independent sum |
| `pwscale-oracle` | the independent sum in `tests/pwscale_oracle.py` |
| `pwscale-collectives-2`, `-4` | the collectives of one call, counted through the PMPI shim, and the bytes of the result |
| `pwscale-mpi-fault` | that a failure on one rank is reported on every rank; `CPMDC_PWSCALE_MPI_FAULT` injects it (see the environment reference (file:environment.org)) |
| `pwscale-logger` | that a timed row carries its own gaps and that a poisoned sample does not pass |
| `pwscale-fft-fail` | that FFT allocation and planning failures return an error instead of using an incomplete plan |
| `pwscale-cuda-include` | the `nvcc` target in `meson.build`, read as text, holds the include directory and the CUDA source name |

The `reference-contract` test fails when a function, type, constant, or struct
field of the header is missing from this page.


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/python.org

# Names
The public names live in `python/cpmdc`.
`Session.energy_forces` and `Potential.evaluate` take positions and cells in Angstrom (`Session.calculate_au` takes Bohr).
`Session` returns Hartree, Hartree/Bohr, and Hartree/Bohr^3 (with the virial in Hartree from `calculate_au`), the native units of the C ABI.
`Potential` returns eV, eV/Angstrom, and eV/Angstrom^3 with the ASE stress sign `(1/V) dE/d(strain)`.
The API contracts (file:contracts.org) page gives each name its signature, units, shape and dtype, ownership, thread behaviour, exceptions and defaults, and the `reference-audit` test keeps it in step with the code.
Importing `cpmdc` does not import ASE.
Import `cpmdc.ase` for `CPMDCCalculator` and its `CalculationFailed`.
Importing `cpmdc.ase` registers `CPMDCCalculator` under `"cpmdc"` with
`ase.calculators.calculator.register_calculator_class` (idempotently), so
`get_calculator_class("cpmdc")` returns `CPMDCCalculator`; `pyproject.toml` also
declares `cpmdc = "cpmdc.ase"` in the `ase.plugins` entry-point group.
The module reads `__ase_plugins__` as a `CalculatorPlugin` set built on first
access, which is empty on an ASE release without `ase._4.plugins`, so importing
`cpmdc.ase` never imports `ase._4` and cannot hide the plugin from ASE's own
discovery.
`cpmdc.ipi` is the `cpmdc-ipi` socket driver; it needs ASE only for
`--structure`.
`cpmdc.lammps` couples a `lammps` object from LAMMPS' Python module. Loading
it uses `rgpot.lammps` when that frontend is installed, and stays importable
when the module is absent. It imports neither LAMMPS nor `mpi4py` until a run
needs them.
`cpmdc.gromacs` writes the grompp `-qmi` input of `libcpmdc_gromacs` and holds
GROMACS' unit factors; it imports nothing outside the standard library.

| Name | Role |
|------+------|
| `HARTREE_TO_EV` | `27.211386245988` eV per Hartree, the constant `CPMDC_HARTREE_EV` in `src/cpmdc.c` |
| `BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` | `0.529177210903` Angstrom per Bohr, the constant `CPMDC_BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` in `src/cpmdc_params.h` |
| `HARTREE_TO_KCAL_PER_MOL` | `627.5094740630558` kcal/mol per Hartree, from CODATA 2018 Hartree energy, the Avogadro constant, and 4184 J per kilocalorie |
| `ATOMIC_NUMBER_MIN`, `ATOMIC_NUMBER_MAX` | `1` and `118` (dimensionless `int`), the range of atomic numbers that `Session` and the C evaluation calls accept |
| `CPMDCError` | `RuntimeError` subclass raised when the library cannot be found or loaded, or when a library call fails; `CPMDCError.code` is the `CPMDCErrorCode` of a library failure and `0` when Python rejected the call or the library predates `cpmdc_last_error_code()` |
| `CPMDCInvalidArgument` | `CPMDCError` subclass for a null handle, a bad buffer, or a value the library refuses, such as a Gaussian width below `1e-12` Angstrom; `CPMDCInvalidArgument.code` is `1` |
| `CPMDCUnavailable` | `CPMDCError` subclass for a backend that is not linked or a link stub; `CPMDCUnavailable.code` is `2` |
| `CPMDCUnsupportedPeriodicEmbedding` | `CPMDCError` subclass for external charges with a periodic cell or a periodic deck; `CPMDCUnsupportedPeriodicEmbedding.code` is `3` |
| `CPMDCEvaluationFailed` | `CPMDCError` subclass for an evaluation that ran and produced no result; `CPMDCEvaluationFailed.code` is `4` |
| `CPMDCDeckExternalPotential` | `CPMDCError` subclass for session charges combined with a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` or `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL ADD`; `CPMDCDeckExternalPotential.code` is `5` |
| `CpmdcError` | deprecated alias of `CPMDCError`, the same class; reading it warns with `DeprecationWarning` |
| `MethodInfo` | `MethodInfo(functional, charge, multiplicity)`: frozen dataclass of the effective method settings decoded from `CPMDParams` (all three fields required) |
| `MethodInfo.functional`, `MethodInfo.charge`, `MethodInfo.multiplicity` | `functional` as the functional token (`str`), `charge` as the total system charge in elementary charges (`int`), and `multiplicity` as the spin multiplicity (dimensionless `int`) |
| `Evaluation` | `Evaluation(energy_h, forces_h_bohr, stress_h_bohr3, dipole_e_bohr=None)`: dataclass of one finished step; it compares and hashes by identity (`eq=False`) |
| `Evaluation.energy_h`, `Evaluation.forces_h_bohr`, `Evaluation.stress_h_bohr3`, `Evaluation.dipole_e_bohr` | `energy_h` in Hartree (`float`), `forces_h_bohr` as an N by 3 `list[list[float]]` in Hartree/Bohr (the negative nuclear gradient), `stress_h_bohr3` as nine row-major Hartree/Bohr^3 values with the OpenCPMD sign `-(1/V) dE/d(strain)` or `None`, and `dipole_e_bohr` as three electron-Bohr values only when OpenCPMD recomputed the dipole for that geometry or `None` |
| `ConstantCutoff` | `ConstantCutoff(cutoff_ry, height_ry=None, width_ry=None)`: frozen dataclass of the constant-cutoff kinetic functional in Rydberg; a field that is not a number (or is `bool`) raises `TypeError`, and one that is not finite and positive raises `ValueError` |
| `ConstantCutoff.cutoff_ry`, `ConstantCutoff.height_ry`, `ConstantCutoff.width_ry` | `E0`, `A`, and `sigma` in Rydberg; `cutoff_ry` is required, `height_ry=None` selects 50 times the deck cutoff for `A`, and `width_ry=None` selects `cutoff_ry / 10` for `sigma` |
| `ConstantCutoff.coerce` | `coerce(value)`: convert `value` (`None`, a `ConstantCutoff`, a mapping of its fields, or `E0` in Rydberg) to a `ConstantCutoff` or `None`; raises `TypeError` or `ValueError` on invalid input |
| `ConstantCutoff.todict` | `todict()`: return `dict[str, float]` of the non-`None` fields in Rydberg as JSON data |
| `Session` | `Session(params, *, library=None, schema=None, constant_cutoff=None)`: one `CPMDCSession` handle and context manager; `params` is serialized `CPMDParams` `bytes` or a file path (required); `library=None` is a `libcpmdc` path or `None` for `find_library`; `constant_cutoff=None` takes what `ConstantCutoff.coerce` takes (in Rydberg) and calls `cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff()`; `schema=None` is deprecated and ignored (`DeprecationWarning` when not `None`); raises `CPMDCError`, `FileNotFoundError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` |
| `Session.energy_forces` | `energy_forces(positions, atomic_numbers, cell=None)`: evaluate one geometry from Angstrom `positions` of shape (N, 3), N integer `atomic_numbers` in 1..118, and optional Angstrom `cell=None` (3x3 or nine row-major floats, encoded as `ForceInput` in process, or `None` for an isolated system); returns `Evaluation` in Hartree, Hartree/Bohr, and Hartree/Bohr^3; raises `CPMDCError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` |
| `Session.calculate_au` | `calculate_au(positions_bohr, atomic_numbers, cell_bohr=None, *, forces=None, virial=None)`: one step through `cpmdc_session_calculate_au()` from `3 * N` Bohr coordinates in `positions_bohr` (flat or N rows), N integer `atomic_numbers` in 1..118, and optional `cell_bohr=None` (nine Bohr values or three rows with one vector per row, or `None`); returns  with `energy_h` in Hartree, `3 * N` forces in Hartree/Bohr, and the nine-component row-major virial `-dE/d(strain)` in Hartree (zero without a cell or stress tensor); C-contiguous `float64` and `int32` inputs pass without a copy, and writable `forces=None` and `virial=None` `float64` buffers are filled in place when given (otherwise new `array('d')` buffers are returned); raises `CPMDCError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` |
| `Session.set_external_charges` | `set_external_charges(positions_angstrom, charges_e, widths_angstrom=None)`: replace the Gaussian MM point charges used by later evaluations; `positions_angstrom` holds `3 * M` Angstrom coordinates, `charges_e` `M` charges in units of the elementary charge, and `widths_angstrom=None` `M` Gaussian standard deviations in Angstrom (the library default, 0.30 Angstrom, when `None`); empty arrays clear the charges; a width below `1e-12` Angstrom raises `CPMDCInvalidArgument` and keeps the previous charges; a non-finite value raises `ValueError`; a library without `cpmdc_session_set_external_charges` raises `CPMDCError` |
| `Session.external_charge_forces_au` | `external_charge_forces_au(n_charges)`: `3 * n_charges` forces on the MM charges of the last successful evaluation, in Hartree/Bohr; raises `CPMDCInvalidArgument` before a successful step or on a wrong count, `CPMDCError` on a library without `cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces`, and `ValueError` for a negative count |
| `Session.select_orbitals` | `select_orbitals(key)`: call `cpmdc_session_select_orbitals()` with signed 64-bit integer `key` (dimensionless); raises `TypeError`, `ValueError`, or `CPMDCError` |
| `Session.copy_orbitals` | `copy_orbitals(from_key, to_key)`: call `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals()` to copy stored orbitals from signed 64-bit integer `from_key` into `to_key` (dimensionless); raises `TypeError`, `ValueError`, or `CPMDCError` |
| `Session.version` | `version()`: return `cpmdc/` and the compiled version string |
| `Session.abi_version` | `abi_version()`: return the numeric ABI generation (`int`) |
| `Session.available` | `available()`: return `True` when OpenCPMD is linked, `False` for the reference evaluator |
| `Session.dipole_possible` | `dipole_possible()`: return `True` when the library provides `cpmdc_session_last_dipole`, OpenCPMD is linked, and the last evaluation did not report the dipole unavailable; return `False` for a library without that symbol, the reference evaluator, after a deck produces no dipole, and on a closed session |
| `Session.close` | `close()`: destroy the handle (idempotent); a later evaluation or orbital call raises `CPMDCError` |
| `Potential` | `Potential(params, *, library=None, schema=None, constant_cutoff=None)`: rgpot-shaped provider and context manager over one `Session`; `params` is serialized `CPMDParams` `bytes` or a file path (required); `library=None` and `constant_cutoff=None` (in Rydberg) go to `Session`; `schema=None` is deprecated and ignored (`DeprecationWarning` when not `None`); raises `CPMDCError`, `FileNotFoundError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` |
