| `Potential.evaluate` | `evaluate(positions, numbers, box=None)`: evaluate one step from Angstrom `positions` of shape (N, 3), N atomic `numbers` in 1..118, and optional Angstrom `box=None` (3x3 or nine row-major floats, or `None` for an isolated system); returns a `dict` with `energy` in eV, `forces` in eV/Angstrom of shape (N, 3), optional nine-component row-major `stress` in eV/Angstrom^3 with the ASE sign `(1/V) dE/d(strain)`, and optional `dipole` in e*Angstrom; raises `CPMDCError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` |
| `Potential.caps` | `caps()`: return `stress` true, `energies` false, and `dipole` as `Session.dipole_possible()` answers |
| `Potential.close` | `close()`: close the owned `Session` (idempotent) |
| `find_library` | `find_library(path=None)`: return the `Path` of `libcpmdc`; tries an explicit `path` first, then `CPMDC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, and `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE` in that order, then `.cpmdc.mesonpy.libs/libcpmdc.so` and `.cpmdc.mesonpy.libs/libcpmdc.dylib` beside the package, then `ctypes.util.find_library("cpmdc")`, then `build/libcpmdc.so` and `build/libcpmdc.dylib` in the working directory; raises `CPMDCError` when not found |
| `find_schema` | `find_schema(path=None)`: return the `Path` of `schema/Potentials.capnp` for `capnp encode` of `CPMDParams` text; tries an explicit `path` first, then `CPMDC_SCHEMA`, then the wheel's `cpmdc/schema/Potentials.capnp`, then `schema/Potentials.capnp` in the working directory; raises `CPMDCError` when not found |
| `params_method` | `params_method(params, *, library=None)`: decode the effective `MethodInfo` from serialized `CPMDParams` `bytes` or a file path through `cpmdc_params_method()` without applying the deck; `library=None` goes to `find_library`; raises `CPMDCError` on an empty buffer, a library without `cpmdc_params_method`, or a failed call |
| `forces_to_ev_per_angstrom` | `forces_to_ev_per_angstrom(forces_h_bohr)`: convert N by 3 forces `forces_h_bohr` from Hartree/Bohr to eV/Angstrom |
| `dipole_to_e_angstrom` | `dipole_to_e_angstrom(dipole_e_bohr)`: convert a three-component molecular dipole from electron Bohr to e*Angstrom; raises `ValueError` unless there are three components |
| `stress_to_ev_per_angstrom3` | `stress_to_ev_per_angstrom3(stress_h_bohr3)`: convert a nine-component row-major tensor `stress_h_bohr3` from Hartree/Bohr^3 to eV/Angstrom^3, keeping the library sign; raises `ValueError` unless there are nine components |
| `CPMDCCalculator` | ASE calculator: `CPMDCCalculator(params=None, *, library=None, constant_cutoff=None, **kwargs)` for `energy` (eV), `free_energy` (eV), `forces` (eV/Angstrom), `stress` (eV/Angstrom^3, Voigt), and `dipole` (e*Angstrom) when available; takes `params`, `library`, and `constant_cutoff` (Rydberg), and ASE's `directory`, `label`, `atoms`, and `parameters`; registered under `"cpmdc"` for `get_calculator_class("cpmdc")` and in `ase.plugins` |
| `CPMDCCalculator.default_parameters` | `params`, `library`, and `constant_cutoff`, all `None`; a `params` or `library` path is stored absolute, resolved against the working directory of the process when it is set; a `constant_cutoff` is stored as E0 in Ry, or as the mapping of `ConstantCutoff.todict` when it sets a height or a width |
| `CPMDCCalculator.implemented_properties` | `energy`, `free_energy`, `forces`, `stress`, and `dipole` |
| `CPMDCCalculator.ignored_changes` | the empty set: a change of `initial_charges` or `initial_magmoms` discards the stored results, because the calculator reads them as the total charge and, through the total moment, the multiplicity |
| `CPMDCCalculator.discard_results_on_any_change` | `True`: a parameter that `set` changes clears the stored results |
| `CPMDCCalculator.calculate` | `calculate(atoms=None, properties=None, system_changes=all_changes)`: one step with `directory` as the working directory; fills `energy`, `free_energy`, `forces`, and any available `stress` and `dipole`; the total of `atoms.get_initial_charges()` is the charge and `abs(total of atoms.get_initial_magnetic_moments()) + 1` is the multiplicity when `params` leaves that setting at its default (a charge of 0, a multiplicity of 1); a nonzero total that differs from a set value of `params`, a total that is not an integer within `n * eps * sum(abs(x))`, and non-collinear moments raise `ValueError`; zero totals change nothing |
| `CPMDCCalculator.set` | `set(**kwargs)`: change `params`, `library`, or `constant_cutoff`, open a new session, clear results, return a dictionary of the changed parameters; `parameters` reads a saved file, and any other key raises `TypeError` |
| `CPMDCCalculator.todict` | `todict(skip_default=True)`: the parameters as JSON data; a `params` buffer of bytes is encoded as standard Base64 under `{"cpmdparams_base64": ...}`, and a `params` or `library` path is absolute, so `CPMDCCalculator(**calc.todict())` reads the same files from any directory |
| `CPMDCCalculator.reset` | `reset()`: clear the stored results; the session stays open |
| `CPMDCCalculator.read` | `read(label)`: always raises `ase.calculators.calculator.ReadError`, because a step stores no file that holds results; `parameters` reads a file written by `Parameters.write` |
| `CPMDCCalculator.potential` | the `Potential` the calculator owns, opened on first use |
| `CPMDCCalculator.close` | `close()`: close that potential; the next step opens a new one |
| `cpmdc.ase.CalculationFailed` | a step that the library rejected; both ASE's `CalculationFailed` and `CPMDCError`, with the step's working directory in the message and the library code in `CPMDCError.code` |
| `cpmdc.ipi.Driver` | `Driver(params, atomic_numbers, *, library=None, cluster=False, log=None)`: answer i-PI protocol requests from one `Session` |
| `Driver.compute` | `compute(positions, cell)`: one step from `3N` Bohr `positions` and the wire's `cell` `h` (lattice vectors as columns, Bohr), in that order; returns Hartree, Hartree/Bohr, and the virial `-dE/d(strain)` in Hartree |
| `Driver.serve` | `serve(sock)`: answer a connected socket until `EXIT` or a closed connection; return the step count |
| `Driver.close` | `close()`: close the session |
| `cpmdc.ipi.ProtocolError` | a `CPMDCError` for a message the driver cannot answer |
| `cpmdc.ipi.connect` | `connect(*, unix=None, host='localhost', port=None, prefix=None, wait=0.0)`: open the UNIX or TCP socket to the server, retrying for `wait` seconds |
| `cpmdc.ipi.species_numbers` | `species_numbers(text)`: atomic numbers from `"O H H"`, `"O,H,H"`, `"OH2"`, or `"8 1 1"` |
| `cpmdc.ipi.unix_socket_path` | `unix_socket_path(name, prefix=None)`: the socket file for an address, with the i-PI and ASE prefix |
| `cpmdc.ipi.HEADER_BYTES`, `cpmdc.ipi.DEFAULT_SOCKET_PREFIX` | the 12-byte width of a protocol header, and the socket-name prefix that i-PI and ASE use |
| `cpmdc.ipi.main` | `main(argv=None)`: the `cpmdc-ipi` command; returns the exit status |
| `cpmdc.lammps.FixExternal` | `FixExternal(lmp, params, elements, *, fix_id='cpmdc', create=True, library=None, comm=None, qm_types=None, mm_width_angstrom=0.30)`: cpmdc as the force engine of a `fix external pf/callback`, delegating the LAMMPS protocol to `rgpot.lammps.FixExternal`; with `qm_types` (atom types evaluated as QM) every other atom is a Gaussian MM charge with its LAMMPS `q` and width `mm_width_angstrom` (finite, at least `1e-12`), on an isolated box only, and the charge set is cleared on the first step that has no MM atom |
| `FixExternal.run` | `run(steps, *keywords)`: run `steps` with LAMMPS keywords; raises `CPMDCError` for a failed step |
| `FixExternal.close` | `close()`: close the session and remove the fixes it added; also on leaving a `with` block |
| `FixExternal.error`, `energy`, `evaluations` | the last failure, the last energy in LAMMPS units, the evaluation count on rank 0 |
| `FixExternal.periodic`, `type_numbers`, `units` | whether the cell is sent, the atomic number of each atom type, the LAMMPS unit style |
| `cpmdc.lammps.UNIT_STYLES` | LAMMPS unit style to (length per Bohr, energy per Hartree) for `metal`, `real`, `electron` |
| `cpmdc.lammps.unit_factors` | `unit_factors(style)`: that pair for one style; `ValueError` for any other |
| `cpmdc.lammps.box_rows` | `box_rows(boxlo, boxhi, xy, yz, xz)`: `boxlo`, `boxhi`, `xy`, `yz`, `xz` to the 3x3 cell with one lattice vector per row |
| `cpmdc.gromacs.qmi_input` | `qmi_input(params, *, cell=None, embedding=None, qm_charges=None, mm_width=None, ewald_rcut=None, ewald_precision=None, epsilon_r=None, qm_ranks=None, charge=0, multiplicity=1)`: text of the grompp `-qmi` file (`embedding` is `"ELECTROSTATIC"`, `"MECHANICAL"`, or `"NONE"`; `mm_width` is the Gaussian width in nm of `"ELECTROSTATIC"` and is refused for any other embedding, below `1e-13` nm, or when not finite; `ewald_rcut` in nm, `qm_ranks` `"ALL"` or `1`); `ValueError` or `TypeError` for a value the library would refuse |
| `cpmdc.gromacs.write_qmi` | `write_qmi(path, params, *, cell=None, embedding=None, qm_charges=None, mm_width=None, ewald_rcut=None, ewald_precision=None, epsilon_r=None, qm_ranks=None, charge=0, multiplicity=1)`: write that text to `path` and return it |
| `cpmdc.gromacs.BOHR_TO_NM`, `HARTREE_TO_KJ_PER_MOL`, `HARTREE_PER_BOHR_TO_KJ_PER_MOL_NM` | GROMACS' QM/MM conversion factors, built as `src/gromacs/math/units.h` builds them |
| `cpmdc.lammps.type_numbers` | `type_numbers(elements, n_types)`: atomic numbers per atom type from `"O H"`, `"8 1"`, or a sequence; `ValueError` unless there are `n_types` |

`free_energy` on `CPMDCCalculator` equals `energy`.
A repeated geometry returns the stored step.
A null or empty input raises; it does not abort the interpreter.
Use cpmdc as an ASE calculator (file:../howto/ase.org) has the property table
and the rules for units, boundaries, caching, the working directory, copies, and
sessions.
Drive cpmdc over the i-PI socket protocol (file:../howto/socket-drivers.org)
covers `cpmdc-ipi`, and Run LAMMPS on cpmdc forces (file:../howto/lammps.org)
covers `cpmdc.lammps`.

# Errors

| Condition | Raised |
|-----------+--------|
| empty or invalid `CPMDParams`, library or schema not found, library load or call failed, closed `Session`, changed atom count or composition | `CPMDCError` |
| a `constant_cutoff` whose E0 + 2 sigma exceeds the deck cutoff, on a message with a raw `&SYSTEM` block or with `system.constantCutoff`, or on a library without `cpmdc_session_set_constant_cutoff` | `CPMDCError` |
| `Session.copy_orbitals` on a library without `cpmdc_session_copy_orbitals`, before any evaluation, or from a key without converged orbitals | `CPMDCError` |
| `Session.set_external_charges` with a width below `1e-12` Angstrom, a null buffer, or a failed charge copy; `Session.external_charge_forces_au` before a successful step or with the wrong count | `CPMDCInvalidArgument` |
| session charges with a periodic cell, or with a periodic deck on a call that passes no cell | `CPMDCUnsupportedPeriodicEmbedding` |
| session charges with a deck `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL` or `EXTERNAL POTENTIAL ADD` | `CPMDCDeckExternalPotential` |
| `Session.set_external_charges` or `Session.external_charge_forces_au` on a library without `cpmdc_session_set_external_charges` or `cpmdc_session_last_external_charge_forces` | `CPMDCError` with code `0` |
| a `CPMDCCalculator` step that the library rejects | `cpmdc.ase.CalculationFailed`, which is a `CPMDCError` and ASE's `CalculationFailed` |
| missing `params` file | `FileNotFoundError` |
| empty or non-3D positions, mismatched `atomic_numbers` or `numbers` length, a cell or box that is not 3x3 or 9 numbers, a `stress_h_bohr3` without 9 components, a non-finite coordinate or cell value, an atomic number outside 1..118, a non-positive or non-finite `ConstantCutoff` field, a whole-number argument that is a fraction such as `14.9`, an orbital key outside the signed 64-bit range | `ValueError` |
| an atomic number, orbital key, `ConstantCutoff` field, or `charge` that is a string, `None`, or `bool`; a coordinate or cell value that is not a real number | `TypeError` |
| `CPMDCCalculator.read` with any label | `ase.calculators.calculator.ReadError`, an ASE `CalculatorError` |
| `atoms.pbc` mixes periodic and open axes, or is periodic and the cell has rank below 3 under the numpy.linalg.matrix_rank cutoff or has a volume below the normal float64 range | `ValueError` |
| a `CPMDCCalculator` step without atoms | `ValueError` |
| stress on free boundaries or an isolated deck; a property outside `implemented_properties` | `ase.calculators.calculator.PropertyNotImplementedError` |
| a keyword to `CPMDCCalculator` or `CPMDCCalculator.set` other than `params`, `library`, `constant_cutoff`, and ASE's own, such as `charge` or `multiplicity`; no `params`, or `params=None` | `TypeError` |
| `schema=` on any class, `restart=` on `CPMDCCalculator` | `DeprecationWarning` |
| a changed atom count, an `INIT` that is not UTF-8 or whose `batch_size` is duplicated or is not the integer 1, a message out of order, a connection closed mid-message, or an unusable periodic cell on the socket | `cpmdc.ipi.ProtocolError` |
| a negative, NaN or infinite `cpmdc.ipi.connect(wait=...)` | `ValueError`, before a socket is opened |
| `Session.calculate_au` with a failed evaluation; positions, numbers, cell, or output arrays of the wrong size, or non-writable or non-contiguous `forces` or `virial` buffers | `CPMDCError`; `ValueError` for the sizes, buffers, non-finite values, and atomic numbers outside 1..118; `TypeError` for non-numeric coordinates or non-integer atomic numbers |
| `FixExternal` on a unit style other than `metal`, `real`, `electron`, on a box with mixed periodicity, with the wrong number of elements, with empty `qm_types`, or with an `mm_width_angstrom` that is not finite or is below `1e-12` | `ValueError` |
| `FixExternal` with unreadable `params`, on several ranks without `mpi4py`, a step with MM atoms on a periodic box or without atom charges, or a failed step in `FixExternal.run` | `CPMDCError` |


## File: docs/orgmode/reference/surface-map.org

A cross-check of the in-process C ABI: every public function against the header,
the inventory, both implementations, and the feature table.
The C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org) documents what each function does; this
page records where each one lives.
The `cpmd-public-abi-inventory`, `stub-abi-symbol-coverage`,
`shared-dlopen-symbol-coverage`, and `c-abi-inventory` tests keep it true.

Protocol adapters are deliberately outside this surface.  Direct callers use
=cpmdc_session_calculate_au()= or the Cap'n Proto result calls; remote callers
normally use rgpot's Cap'n Proto RPC.  An optional i-PI adapter belongs to
rgpot as a frontend over every potential.  In an rgpot build with the RPC
stack, =rgpot-ipi-driver= selects =CPMDPot= for =--pot "CPMD params FILE"=
and for `-m CPMD -o params=FILE`.  Pass =--preserve-open-cell= for CPMD so
a singular cell is passed through instead of padded.  The
i-PI migration status (file:../howto/socket-drivers.org) records that
route.  =cpmdc-ipi= and =cpmdc-ipi-c= remain compatibility fallbacks.

# Sources checked

| Source | Role |
|--------+------|
| `include/cpmdc.h`, `include/cpmdc_features.h` | public declarations |
| `schema/inventory/cpmd_features.json` | `abi_symbols` list and feature rows |
| `src/cpmdc.c` | implementation in the default and OpenCPMD builds |
| `src/cpmdc_stub.c` | implementation in the stub build |
| `src/cpmdc_features.c`, `src/cpmdc_capabilities.c` | discovery functions shared by all builds |
| `libcpmdc` | the `cpmdc_` symbols the built shared library exports |

52 symbols in `abi_symbols`, 52 with every column present.

# Exported symbols
`schema/inventory/surface_map_abi.txt` is generated by
`scripts/abi_inventory.py` from the exported symbols of `libcpmdc` (`nm -D --defined-only`, or `nm -gU` on macOS; `NM` names another `nm`) and the declarations in `include/cpmdc.h`
and `include/cpmdc_features.h`.
It lists the 52 public functions with their header, the ABI generation
(`CPMDC_ABI_VERSION`, 0), and a `@since` column that stays `-` until a
declaration records a later generation.
`libcpmdc` exports exactly those symbols: internal glue is hidden (see the C ABI reference (file:c-abi.org)
for `CPMDC_API` and the export list).

The `c-abi-inventory` test, in the `abi` and `inventory` suites, and the CI stub
job fail when the file differs from what the built library and the headers give,
when a public declaration lacks
`CPMDC_API` or is not exported, or when the library exports any other symbol, internal `cpmdc_`
glue and symbols of the linked static archives alike.
The `shared-dlopen-abi` test also checks that internal C and Fortran glue does
not resolve through `dlsym`.
After changing the surface, regenerate the file with
`meson compile -C build abi-inventory`.

`scripts/abi_baseline.txt` and the `c-abi-baseline` test are separate: they
freeze the exported names so a removal or a rename fails.

# Parser sections
The 25 sections OpenCPMD reads with `inscan('&SECTION')`, recorded in
`opencpmd_inscan_sections` and `schema/inventory/opencpmd_sections.txt`:

ATOM, ATOMS, BASIS, CLAS, CPMD, DFT, EAM, EXTE, HARDNESS, INFO, LINRES,
MOLSTATES, MTS, NLCC, PATH, PIMD, POTENTIAL, PROP, PTDDFT, RESP, SYSTEM, TDDFT,
VDW, VECTORS, WAVEFUNCTION.

QMMM, PROPERTIES, BICANONICAL, and CDFT are `&CPMD` keywords, not sections.


## File: docs/orgmode/tutorials/ase-energy.org

# Run the example
This lesson evaluates the same internal water geometry as the
first tutorial (file:first-energy.org), placed near the origin rather than
at , with the ASE calculator.
The default build's origin-anchored reference well supplies the number.
No OpenCPMD checkout is required.

Build and test the default tree with `pixi run test-stub` (or
`meson setup build -Dwith_tests=true` followed by `meson test -C build` or
`meson compile -C build cpmdc water_params_bin`), as the
build-and-test how-to (file:../howto/quickstart.org) does.
Plain `meson compile -C build` compiles `build/libcpmdc.so` while the test run
or `water_params_bin` target writes the encoded water message
`build/water_blyp_params.bin`.
Point the example at both from the root of the checkout:

export CPMDC_PARAMS=build/water_blyp_params.bin
export CPMDC_LIBRARY=build/libcpmdc.so
export PYTHONPATH=python
python3 examples/python/ase_energy.py

energy_ev=0.059020309570
natoms=3
fmax=0.06513409

`energy_ev` is the reference energy in eV.
`fmax` here is the largest absolute force component in eV/Angstrom; ASE
optimizers compare their `fmax` with the largest force norm instead.
The same geometry without ASE is `examples/python/energy.py`, which prints
Hartree.

With `pip install "cpmdc[ase]"` the package and its library come from the wheel,
so drop `CPMDC_LIBRARY` and `PYTHONPATH` and keep `CPMDC_PARAMS`.

`CPMDCCalculator` keeps one session.
A second `get_potential_energy` on the same atoms does not recompute, and
neither does `get_forces` after it: one step computes both.
`get_forces` returns an array of shape .
Change a position and the next call computes again on the same session, which a
relaxation with `BFGS` and `FixAtoms` relies on.
`energy` is in eV and `forces` in eV/Angstrom, matching ASE's unit system and
converted from Hartree and Bohr with `cpmdc.HARTREE_TO_EV` and
`cpmdc.BOHR_TO_ANGSTROM` (CODATA 2018).
`tests/python/test_ase_conformance.py` checks those units, the cache, and the
errors of the calculator with ASE's own tools, against the same reference well.
Use cpmdc as an ASE calculator (file:../howto/ase.org) lists every property,
the units, the boundary rules, and the working directory, and shows how to relax
a structure and its cell with an ASE optimizer.


## File: docs/orgmode/tutorials/eon-rgpot.org

This tutorial relaxes the water molecule of the
first tutorial (file:first-energy.org) with eOn's minimiser, with every force
call going through `rgpot` into `libcpmdc` inside the `eonclient` process.
It reuses `water.params.bin` from that tutorial and runs against either build
of `libcpmdc` that the tutorial made: the default build in `$CPMDC/build`, and
the OpenCPMD build in `$CPMDC/build-cpmd`.
The default build evaluates the reference well, finishes in about a second, and
needs no OpenCPMD and no pseudopotentials.
The OpenCPMD build computes a BLYP energy and takes about a minute.
Each build has its own transcript below.
Run every command in the Pixi shell that the first tutorial opened.

# What connects to what
eOn's `RGPOT` potential loads rgpot's `CPMDPot`, which opens `libcpmdc.so` with
`dlopen` and keeps one `CPMDCSession` for the life of the client. eOn hands each
geometry to `CPMDPot`, `CPMDPot` turns it into a `ForceInput`, and `cpmdc` runs
the SCF in the same process, starting every call after the first from the
previous orbitals.
The method comes from a `CPMDParams` message file that eOn reads through
`[RgpotPot] params_path`.

You need an `eonclient` built with RGPOT support whose `[RgpotPot]` section
reads `params_path`; eOn lists the key under `RgpotPot` in `eon/config.yaml`.
Without
`params_path`, eOn builds `CPMDParams` from four scalar keys (`functional`, `cutoff_ry`,
`charge`, `multiplicity`).
A positive cell is then periodic: symmetry 1 when the edges are equal, symmetry
8 when they are not, and `CELL VECTORS` with no symmetry line when the box is
tilted.
A zero cell stays `SYMMETRY 0` with the Hockney solver.
To keep a molecule isolated, the message has to ask for it.
This run uses `water.params.bin`, which sets `poissonSolver = "HOCKNEY"`, and
stays isolated.

# Build eonclient
This section builds rgpot and eOn into one prefix with the compilers and
libraries of cpmdc's Pixi environment. eOn's own `pixi.toml` does not load under
Pixi 0.84.2: its task `mkeon` depends on an environment `eon` that the file does
not define. cpmdc's environment has no Eigen, and eOn needs Eigen 3.4.
Install it as a separate Pixi environment:

pixi global install 'eigen>=3.4,<3.5'

Work in the directory that holds the cpmdc checkout and `cpmdc-tutorial`:

cd "$CPMDC/.."
export EON_PREFIX=$PWD/eon-prefix
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$EON_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$HOME/.pixi/envs/eigen/share/pkgconfig

`$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig` is on the list because Meson can pick a system
`pkg-config` that does not search the Pixi environment.
Build rgpot with MPI and install it:

git clone https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgpot.git
cd rgpot
git checkout 5fec533f
meson setup bbdir --prefix="$EON_PREFIX" --libdir=lib \
  -Dwith_rpc=true -Dwith_mpi=enabled -Dwith_fortran_pots=enabled \
  -Dwith_expr=true -Dwith_tests=false
meson install -C bbdir
cd ..

`with_rpc` builds `CPMDPot`.
`with_mpi` builds `librgpot_mpi`, which rgpot loads only when the client runs
under `mpirun`. eOn's configure stops when the installed rgpot has no Fortran
potentials.
`with_expr` matches the rgpot that eOn builds when it finds none installed.
Then build eOn against the installed rgpot:

git clone https://github.com/TheochemUI/eOn.git eon
cd eon
git checkout 579738a93
meson setup bbdir --prefix="$EON_PREFIX" --libdir=lib -Dwith_mpi=enabled
meson install -C bbdir
cd ..
export PATH=$EON_PREFIX/bin:$PATH

Meson reports `rgpot found: YES 3.7.0` and uses the installed rgpot instead of
its own copy.
`-Dwith_mpi=enabled` makes eOn build `librgpot_pot_mpi`, which starts MPI for the calculator groups and ends it at exit. eOn builds that library when `rgpot.pc` defines `RGPOT_HAS_MPI` or when its own `with_mpi`
is on. rgpot 5fec533f puts the define in `rgpot-mpi.pc` instead, so `with_mpi`
is the switch that works here.
The same `eonclient` runs on one rank without `mpirun`.

# Prepare the run directory
Start in the directory that holds `cpmdc-tutorial`, the one `cd "$CPMDC/.."`
chose above:

mkdir -p eon-water
cd eon-water
cp ../cpmdc-tutorial/water.params.bin .

Save the starting geometry as `pos.con`, eOn's structure format.
It is the water molecule of the first tutorial, in the same 10 Angstrom box,
oxygen first:

Generated for the cpmdc eOn tutorial

10.000000 10.000000 10.000000
90.000000 90.000000 90.000000


2
1 2
15.999000 1.008000
O
Coordinates of Component 1
5.000000 5.000000 5.117300 0 1
H
Coordinates of Component 2
5.000000 5.757200 4.530800 0 2
5.000000 4.242800 4.530800 0 3

eOn lists each element in one component.
`cpmdc` also accepts a step whose atoms of one element are split: it places
positions into CPMD's species blocks and returns forces in the order of the
input.

Save the eOn settings as `config.ini`:

[Main]
job = minimization

[Potential]
potential = rgpot

[RgpotPot]
backend = cpmdc
params_path = water.params.bin

`backend = cpmdc` selects rgpot's `CPMDPot`.
`params_path` is read relative to the directory `eonclient` runs in.
`RGPOT_PARAMS_PATH` in the environment overrides it.

# Run the minimisation
`eonclient` finds `libcpmdc.so` through the environment.
rgpot tries `[RgpotPot] engine_path` first, then `CPMDC_LIBRARY`,
`RGPOT_CPMDC_ENGINE`, and `RGPOT_CPMD_ENGINE`, then `libcpmdc.so` on the loader
path.
Run the client once on each build, in the `eon-water` directory.
The second run overwrites `min.con`, `results.dat`, and `run.log` of the first.

## Run on the default build
The reference evaluator reads no pseudopotentials, so `CPMDC_LIBRARY` is the
only variable to set:

export CPMDC_LIBRARY=$CPMDC/build/libcpmdc.so
eonclient > run.log
sed -n '/^RgpotPot:/,/^Final Energy:/p' run.log

The `sed` command prints eOn's own lines of the run, from the line that names
the backend to the final energy.
The lines before it name the eOn version, the build time, the host, and the
process; the lines after it are timings.
The transcript is under Default build in the next section.

## Run on OpenCPMD
Point CPMD at the pseudopotentials as well:

export CPMDC_LIBRARY=$CPMDC/build-cpmd/libcpmdc.so
export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=$PWD/../cpmdc-tutorial/Regtests/tests/PP_LIBRARY
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
eonclient > run.log
grep -E '^\[Matter\]|^Minimization|^Final Energy' run.log

CPMD writes its output for each force call to the client's standard output, so
`run.log` holds it, and the `grep` keeps only the lines of eOn's minimiser.
The first call starts from atomic orbitals; later calls start from the previous
call's orbitals and need fewer SCF iterations.
This `awk` command prints the call number, the number of SCF iterations, and the
converged energy in Hartree of each force call:

awk '/^ NFI/ {ncall++; scf=1}
     NF==6 && $2 ` /E[-+]/ && $1 ` /^[0-9]+$/ {iters[ncall]=$1}
     /TOTAL ENERGY/ && scf {e[ncall]=$(NF-1); scf=0}
     END {for (i=1;i<=ncall;i++) printf "%d %d %s\n", i, iters[i], e[i]}' run.log

The transcripts are under OpenCPMD build in the next section.

When a run ends, the directory holds:

| File | Contents |
|------+----------|
| `min.con` | the relaxed structure |
| `results.dat` | the termination status, the potential name, the number of force calls, the final energy in eV, and build provenance |
| `run.log` | the standard output of the client |

eOn works in eV and Angstrom; rgpot converts from the Hartree and Hartree/Bohr
values that `cpmdc` returns.

# Expected output
These versions produced the output below:

| Component | Version |
|-----------+---------|
| cpmdc | 0.7.0, this tree |
| OpenCPMD | `062582b` with the patches of the archive how-to (file:../howto/opencpmd-archive.org), OpenCPMD build only |
| rgpot | `5fec533f`, version 3.7.0 |
| eOn | `579738a93`, version 3.6.0 |
| OpenCPMD Regtests | `b2b2c64`, OpenCPMD build only |
| Toolchain | Pixi 0.84.2, GCC 14.3.0, Open MPI 5.0.10, Cap'n Proto 1.4.0, OpenBLAS 0.3.34, Eigen 3.4.0 |

Every transcript below comes from a run of the commands above on one rank, in a
fresh clone of this tree, with the builds above.
A repeat run printed the same digits in both builds.
Built with the same options and the same eOn commit, rgpot `84119ca2`, the head
of its `develop` branch when this page was written, gave the same force-call
counts and final energies in both builds.
Each `[Matter]` row lists the iteration, the step size in Angstrom, the force
norm in eV per Angstrom, and the energy in eV.
eOn's `[Optimizer]` defaults apply: the conjugate-gradient optimiser stops
when the force norm falls below `converged_force`, 0.01, and moves no atom
more than `max_move`, 0.2 Angstrom, in one step.
Both runs made one force call before the first iteration and two per iteration.

## Default build
This is the default build of `libcpmdc`, so the energies come from the
reference well and mean nothing physically, as in the
first tutorial (file:first-energy.org).
The minimisation took 39 iterations and 79 force calls.
The step stayed at the 0.2 Angstrom limit for the first 37 iterations.

## What to expect
- Default build: the run is deterministic arithmetic.
  Expect `GOOD`, 39 iterations, 79 force calls, and a final energy within
  1e-6 eV of 10.63288405405.
- OpenCPMD build: expect `GOOD`, a final force norm below 0.01 eV/Angstrom, and
  a final energy within 1e-4 eV of -464.1301944953.
  The test below does not compare SCF iteration counts or timings.
- A run that stops with a termination status other than 0, prints no
  `[Matter]` rows, or reports an energy outside these bounds did not
  reproduce this page.

`tests/test_tutorials_run.py` runs this page's `pos.con` and `config.ini` through
`eonclient` and compares `results.dat` and the `[Matter]` rows with the transcript
for the build under test: the default-build transcript for a default library,
and the OpenCPMD transcript for a library that links OpenCPMD when
`CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR` is set.
It skips this check when no `eonclient` is on `PATH`; set `EONCLIENT` to the
path of one to run it.

# Change the method
Edit `water.params.txt`, encode it again, and rerun; eOn needs no other change:

capnp encode "$CPMDC/schema/Potentials.capnp" CPMDParams \
  < ../cpmdc-tutorial/water.params.txt > water.params.bin

To see what CPMD receives, set
`CPMDC_DECK_OUT=$PWD/deck.inp` before `eonclient` (see [[file:../howto/debug-deck.org][debugging
a deck]]).
For a periodic system or a larger cluster, write the message as the
CPMDParams how-to (file:../howto/write-cpmdparams.org) shows, and choose the
optimiser for warm starts with the
optimiser how-to (file:../howto/wavefunction-optimiser.org).

# Run on several ranks
Start `eonclient` under `mpirun` to let CPMD spread each SCF over the ranks:

mpirun -np 4 eonclient

Every rank runs the whole client. rgpot binds the four ranks into one calculator
and hands its communicator to `cpmdc_adopt_calculator_comm()`.
Only CPMD's parent rank holds the calculator's result. eOn broadcasts that
result to every rank, and rgpot finalizes MPI at exit.
Running under mpirun (file:../howto/mpi.org) explains these rules.

With the build above and the same files, CPMD split each SCF over four
processors, and only the parent rank printed.
Each call took as many SCF iterations as on one rank.
`results.dat` again reported `GOOD` and 7 force calls, with
`-4.641301944941e+02 potential_energy`, 1.2e-9 eV from the one-rank energy.
`mpirun` returned 0.

Before cpmdc accepted an adopt while a session had not evaluated yet, every rank
stopped here, because rgpot creates its session before it binds the ranks:

eonclient: fatal error: RGPOT(cpmdc): ranks_per_image=0 does not divide the MPI world into calculator groups

With rgpot and eOn built without MPI, the four ranks finished the minimisation,
but they exited without `MPI_Finalize` and `mpirun` returned 1.


## File: docs/orgmode/tutorials/first-energy.org

This tutorial starts from a fresh checkout and ends with the energy and forces
of a water molecule from the `cpmdc` C application programming interface (API).
You first run it against the default build, which needs no OpenCPMD, and then
against a build that links OpenCPMD, where the same program returns a BLYP
(Becke, Lee, Yang, Parr) density functional energy.

# Build the default library
Clone the repository and build it with the checked-in Pixi environment:

git clone https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/cpmdc.git
cd cpmdc
pixi run test-stub
export CPMDC=$PWD

The last lines of the test run report no failures.
The build directory `build/` now contains `libcpmdc.so` and the example program
`example_host_step`.
`CPMDC` remembers the checkout for the commands below.

# Describe the method and the geometry
`cpmdc` takes two messages: `CPMDParams` for the method, written once, and
`ForceInput` for each geometry.
Work in a directory outside the checkout, and open a shell in the Pixi
environment so that `capnp` and the compilers are on the path:

mkdir -p ../cpmdc-tutorial
cd ../cpmdc-tutorial
pixi shell --manifest-path "$CPMDC/pixi.toml"

Save the method as `water.params.txt`.
It asks for BLYP at a 50 Ry cutoff, an isolated molecule in a 10 Angstrom box,
and names one pseudopotential per element:

(
  functional = "BLYP",
  cutOffRy = 50.0,
  inputSections = [
    ( cpmd = ( optimizeWavefunction = true, convergenceOrbitals = 1.0e-5,
        maxIter = 100, centerMoleculeOff = true ) ),
    ( dft = ( functional = "BLYP" ) ),
    ( system = ( symmetry = 0, angstrom = true, cutOffRy = 50.0,
        cell = [10.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        poissonSolver = "HOCKNEY" ) ),
    ( atoms = ( pseudopotentials = [
        ( element = "O", path = "O_MT_BLYP.psp", lmax = 1 ),
        ( element = "H", path = "H_CVB_BLYP.psp", lmax = 0 )
      ] ) )
  ]
)

Save the geometry as `water.step.txt`, with the molecule at the centre of the
box:

(
  pos = [
    5.0, 5.0, 5.1173,
    5.0, 5.7572, 4.5308,
    5.0, 4.2428, 4.5308
  ],
  atmnrs = [8, 1, 1],
  box = [10.0, 0.0, 0.0,  0.0, 10.0, 0.0,  0.0, 0.0, 10.0],
  lengthUnit = "angstrom",
  energyUnit = "eV"
)

Encode both into the binary form the C API reads:

capnp encode "$CPMDC/schema/Potentials.capnp" CPMDParams \
  < water.params.txt > water.params.bin
capnp encode "$CPMDC/schema/Potentials.capnp" ForceInput \
  < water.step.txt > water.step.bin

# Run the example host
`example_host_step` creates a session from the first file, evaluates the second,
and prints a summary:

"$CPMDC/build/example_host_step" water.params.bin water.step.bin

energy_h=0.958703877646
potential_result_size_bytes=792
message=ok
ener_com_etot=0.958703877646
ener_com_ekin=0.000000000000
ener_com_exc=0.000000000000
ener_com_eht=0.000000000000

The default build evaluates a deterministic reference function instead of
density functional theory.
That function is a harmonic well scaled by the atomic numbers.
Its numbers exercise the API and mean nothing physically, which is why the
energy is positive and the components other than `etot` are zero.

# Write your own host
Save this program as `first_forces.c`.
It creates a session, evaluates one `ForceInput`, and prints the energy and the
force on each atom:

#include <cpmdc.h>

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static unsigned char *slurp(const char *path, size_t *size) {
  FILE *fp = fopen(path, "rb");
  if (!fp)
    return NULL;
  fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);
  long len = ftell(fp);
  rewind(fp);
  unsigned char *buf = malloc((size_t)len);
  *size = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)len, fp);
  fclose(fp);
  return buf;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  if (argc != 3) {
    fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s params.bin step.bin\n", argv[0]);
    return 2;
  }
  size_t params_size = 0, step_size = 0;
  unsigned char *params = slurp(argv[1], &params_size);
  unsigned char *step = slurp(argv[2], &step_size);
  if (!params || !step)
    return 2;

  printf("%s available=%d\n", cpmdc_version(), cpmdc_available());
  CPMDCSession *session = cpmdc_session_create(params, params_size);
  if (!session) {
    fprintf(stderr, "cpmdc_session_create failed\n");
    return 1;
  }

  double forces[9]; /* three atoms, x y z each, Hartree/Bohr */
  CPMDCResult r =
      cpmdc_session_calculate_forces(session, step, step_size, forces, 9);
  if (!r.ok) {
    fprintf(stderr, "step failed: %s\n", r.message);
    return 1;
  }
  printf("energy_h=%.8f\n", r.energy_h);
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i)
    printf("force[%d] = %10.6f %10.6f %10.6f\n", i, forces[3 * i],
           forces[3 * i + 1], forces[3 * i + 2]);

  cpmdc_session_destroy(session);
  cpmdc_finalize();
  free(params);
  free(step);
  return 0;
}

The link step comes next.
The default build links the Message Passing Interface (MPI) library whenever
Meson finds one.
The Pixi environment provides OpenMPI, so `libcpmdc.so` needs `libmpi`.
Compile with the MPI C wrapper and link with the MPI Fortran wrapper.
The Fortran wrapper adds the MPI library and the Fortran runtime for `libcpmdc`.

mpicc -c first_forces.c -I "$CPMDC/include"
mpif90 first_forces.o -L "$CPMDC/build" -lcpmdc \
  -Wl,-rpath,"$CPMDC/build" -o first_forces
./first_forces water.params.bin water.step.bin

# [[[cog
# import re
# version = open("version.txt").read().strip()
# cog.out(re.sub(r"^cpmdc/\S+", f"cpmdc/{version}", cog.previous, flags=re.M))
# ]]]
cpmdc/0.7.0 available=0
energy_h=0.95870388
force[0] =  -0.053992  -0.053992  -0.055259
force[1] =  -0.006749  -0.007771  -0.006116
force[2] =  -0.006749  -0.005727  -0.006116
# [end]

`available=0` means this library is not linked to OpenCPMD.
The energy in that transcript is the reference spring, a harmonic function of
the positions, and it is not a plane-wave total energy.

`cpmdc_session_calculate_forces()` returns the energy in Hartree and the forces
in Hartree/Bohr, whatever units the `ForceInput` names; the units of the message
apply to the serialized `PotentialResult` path.

# Switch to OpenCPMD
The same program and the same two messages now run against the Car-Parrinello
Molecular Dynamics (CPMD) code itself.
Three things change: the library, the pseudopotential files, and one environment
variable.

1. Build a patched OpenCPMD archive with `-fPIC`, as the
   archive how-to (file:../howto/opencpmd-archive.org) describes, into
   `/path/to/opencpmd-build`.
2. Link `cpmdc` against it, with the MPI compiler wrappers that built OpenCPMD:

   #+begin_src bash
   cd "$CPMDC"
   CC=mpicc FC=mpif90 meson setup build-cpmd \
     -Dwith_cpmd=true -Dcpmd_root=/path/to/opencpmd-build -Dwith_tests=false
   meson compile -C build-cpmd
   cd ../cpmdc-tutorial
   #+end_src

When OpenCPMD was built with OpenMP and FFTW3, pass the same libraries to the
link, for example with `LDFLAGS="-fopenmp -lfftw3_omp -lfftw3"` in front of
`meson setup`.
3. Fetch the two pseudopotentials from the OpenCPMD regression tests:

   #+begin_src bash
   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/OpenCPMD/Regtests.git
   export CPMDC_PSEUDO_DIR=$PWD/Regtests/tests/PP_LIBRARY
   #+end_src

Relink the program against the new library and run it on one rank:

mpicc -c first_forces.c -I "$CPMDC/include" -o first_forces_live.o
mpif90 first_forces_live.o -L "$CPMDC/build-cpmd" -lcpmdc \
  -Wl,-rpath,"$CPMDC/build-cpmd" -o first_forces_live
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ./first_forces_live water.params.bin water.step.bin

The program prints its version line, now with `available=1`.
CPMD then prints its usual output, which ends with the self-consistent field
(SCF) iterations and the energy breakdown.
The program prints the energy and forces last:

# [[[cog
# import re
# version = open("version.txt").read().strip()
# cog.out(re.sub(r"^cpmdc/\S+", f"cpmdc/{version}", cog.previous, flags=re.M))
# ]]]
cpmdc/0.7.0 available=1
 ...
 NFI      GEMAX       CNORM           ETOT        DETOT      TCPU
   1  4.082E-02   5.185E-03     -16.731578    0.000E+00      0.58
 ...
  13  4.114E-06   6.390E-07     -17.055834   -1.331E-08      0.58
 ...
 (K+E1+L+N+X)           TOTAL ENERGY =          -17.05583351 A.U.
 ...
energy_h=-17.05583351
force[0] =   0.000000   0.000000   0.023856
force[1] =  -0.000000   0.012501  -0.011928
force[2] =  -0.000000  -0.012501  -0.011928
# [end]

The SCF reached -17.05583351 Hartree at iteration 13.
The forces are those of an off-equilibrium water geometry: zero along `x`, the
direction normal to the molecular plane, and mirror-symmetric in `y`.
The `x` components round to zero at six decimals, and two keep their minus sign.
They also sum to zero: cpmdc moves the molecule to the middle of its isolated
cell before each evaluation and removes the net force the fixed cell would
otherwise add;
atoms in an isolated cell (file:../explanation/isolated-cells.org) explains
why, and the environment reference (file:../reference/environment.org) lists
the `CPMDC_RECENTER` settings.
The iteration timings in the `TCPU` column depend on the machine.

# What you built
- a `CPMDParams` message and a `ForceInput` message, encoded with `capnp`;
- a C host that creates a session and evaluates a step;
- the same host running against the default evaluator and against OpenCPMD.

A library force call writes no `RESTART.1`, `LATEST`, `GEOMETRY`, or
`GEOMETRY.xyz`.
The pseudopotential directory is unchanged.
To evaluate many geometries, call `cpmdc_session_calculate_forces()` again on
the same session.
On an OpenCPMD build, a call starts from the stored orbitals when the
functional, deck, cell, cutoff, charge, multiplicity, and elemental
composition match and the geometry lies within `CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` (default
`0.15` Angstrom root-mean-square distance per atom) of the stored geometry;
beyond `CPMDC_WARM_RMSD` it skips full setup and starts from the deck's guess
instead (see
wavefunction state between calls (file:../explanation/wavefunction-state.org)).
A new session with that same basis starts from those orbitals under the same
distance rule, including when the atomic numbers are reordered.
The eOn tutorial (file:eon-rgpot.org) drives exactly that loop from a
minimiser, and running under mpirun (file:../howto/mpi.org) spreads each SCF
over several ranks.
